# Documentation index

Use [AGENTS](../AGENTS.md) as the sole authoritative agent and contributor guide. Detailed implementation, validation and release rules are maintained by the linked topic documents. **Current behavior** is described by the code and the maintained documents below. Historical release claims and source-diff inventories are not product contracts.

| Topic | Maintained document |
| --- | --- |
| Coding standards and approved agent workflow | [Agent guide](../AGENTS.md), [Coding standards](engineering/coding-standards.md), [Release rules](build-deployment/release-naming.md) |
| Current implementation, proven passes and unverified gates | [Current](project-management/current.md) |
| Active unfinished work and triage | [Tasks](project-management/tasks.md), [legacy unresolved acceptance ledger](archive-history/LEGACY_ACCEPTANCE_LEDGER.md) |
| Prioritized engineering debt and verification gates | [Technical debt](project-management/technical-debt.md) |
| Grammar course authoring and structural validation | [Courses authoring](engineering/courses-authoring.md) |
| Product overview and UX | [Product](product-ux/product.md), [UX](product-ux/ux.md) |
| Future Courses mosaic and grammar assessments | [Courses mosaic spec](learning-practice/courses/courses-mosaic.md) |
| Statistics 2.0 dashboard design and implementation plan | [Statistics product design](product-ux/pages/learning-statistics-preview.md), [Statistics architecture](architecture/modules/statistics-dashboard.md), [Statistics acceptance](testing-quality/e2e/statistics-dashboard-design-acceptance.md) |
| Prospective Knowledge Points scoring policy and unresolved decisions | [Knowledge Points](learning-practice/pedagogy/knowledge-points.md), [scoring engine architecture](architecture/modules/knowledge-scoring.md) |
| Planned session evidence and legacy proficiency requirements | [Learning evidence](learning-practice/practice/learning-evidence.md) |
| Practice setup, storage and persisted translation | [Practice builder](learning-practice/practice/practice-session-builder.md), [Practice session storage](architecture/modules/practice-session-storage.md), [Sentence translation](learning-practice/translation/translate-sentence.md) |
| Word Sets, Browse, writing, games | [Dictionary Browse](dictionary-data/dictionary-browse.md), [Write Hanzi](learning-practice/hanzi/write-hanzi-activity.md), [Cloud Match](games/cloud-match.md) |
| Private data, backup and personal database status | [Personal data](dictionary-data/personal/personal-data-storage.md), [personal schema](dictionary-data/schema/personal-data.md) |
| Historical source-to-documentation evidence | [Archived source reconciliation](archive-history/audits/SOURCE_RECONCILIATION.md), [release engineering review history](archive-history/audits/release-engineering-review-history.md) |
| System architecture and dependencies | [Architecture](architecture/architecture.md), [UI architecture](architecture/ui-architecture.md) |
| Translation and AI responsibilities | [Sentence exercises](architecture/modules/sentence-exercises.md), [AI client](architecture/modules/ai-client.md) |
| Dictionary schema, generator and runtime | [DB index](dictionary-data/schema/db.md), [regeneration](dictionary-data/schema/regeneration.md), [runtime](dictionary-data/schema/runtime.md) |
| Testing strategy and E2E implementation | [Testing](testing-quality/acceptance/testing.md), [Chrome E2E](testing-quality/e2e/overview.md), [E2E architecture](testing-quality/e2e/e2e-architecture.md) |
| Decision provenance | [Decisions](project-management/decisions/index.md) |
| Historical-to-current editorial disposition | [Editorial reconciliation](project-management/editorial-reconciliation.md) |
| Accepted historical outcomes | [Completed](archive-history/completed/), [release history](archive-history/RELEASE_HISTORY.md), [root release notes](../RELEASE_NOTES.md) |
| Current UI visual direction | [Visual and interaction review](product-ux/references/ui-screenshot-review.md), [visual reference status](product-ux/references/reference-mockups.md) |

## Physical documentation sections

These are the twelve physical first-level sections under `docs/`. Topic subdirectories provide a second level of grouping; individual articles form the third level. The Docs reader uses the same directory hierarchy.

| Directory | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| `getting-started/` | Onboarding and first-run orientation |
| `product-ux/` | Application behavior, navigation, visual design and accessibility |
| `learning-practice/` | Practice, pedagogy, courses and language exercises |
| `games/` | Game-specific rules and interaction contracts |
| `dictionary-data/` | Dictionary, schema, vocabulary and personal data |
| `architecture/` | System architecture, components and state boundaries |
| `engineering/` | Coding standards, authoring and contributor engineering guides |
| `testing-quality/` | Test requirements, acceptance criteria, E2E and evidence |
| `build-deployment/` | CI, asset preparation, packaging and deployment |
| `project-management/` | Active work, decisions and unresolved requirements |
| `archive-history/` | Frozen completed records, audits and release history |
| `issues/` | Issue reports and visual evidence |

The root `docs/README.md` is the documentation index, not an additional category. Moving an article changes its Docs reader URL; old article paths are not retained as compatibility aliases.

## Documentation rules

- The source tree takes precedence for describing implementation; an approved product decision may describe an intended behavior not yet implemented. Label these distinctly.
- Maintain a **single current** description for each area. Do not create a new `R###_*` document for every checkpoint or re-copy outdated test statistics into permanent specs.
- Historical decisions and completed outcomes may be retained for provenance, but are never silent compatibility obligations.
- Report observed Windows/browser results separately from authored Rust test code and Node source-contract checks.
- Avoid stale paths such as `crates/web/` and removed scripts such as `crates/zipeek-e2e/fixtures/ai-server.cjs`.
- Unresolved work belongs in [Tasks](project-management/tasks.md); finalized choices belong in authoritative specifications and [Decisions](project-management/decisions/index.md).

Future learning evidence and seven-day proficiency E2E requirements: [learning evidence](learning-practice/practice/learning-evidence.md) and [E2E contract](testing-quality/e2e/learning-evidence-e2e.md).

## Docs reader navigation

The in-app Docs reader uses the twelve physical documentation directories as its navigation sections. The classification in `crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/system/docs/model.rs` follows those directory paths. The curated sections are Getting started, Product & UX, Learning & Practice, Games, Dictionary & Data, Architecture, Engineering, Testing & Quality, Build & Deployment, Project Management, Archive & History, and Issues. Within each section, related articles appear under a topic. The Markdown path is the article URL identity, and the navigation resolves against the new physical directories.

Historical completed records are displayed under Archive & History and are not current product instructions. The retired pending-decision scratchpad is no longer published or indexed.

New defects and design requests are tracked in the [issue library](issues/README.md), with per-issue screenshots and acceptance checklists. [Open issues](issues/OPEN.md) provides the active list. The old [issue register](project-management/user-reported-issues.md) redirects to the canonical library.

When docs Markdown changes, regenerate the `crates/zipeek-web/static/docs/index.json` using the project's docs publishing command before shipping. Keep that generated manifest consistent with Markdown paths and titles.

## Visual evidence

The Issues section publishes reports from `docs/issues/` and images from `docs/issues/assets/screenshots/`. Keep the corresponding static images under `crates/zipeek-web/static/docs/issues/assets/screenshots/` in sync so screenshot links resolve in the deployed Docs reader. Issue IDs remain stable when an issue changes status.

## Modular reference pages

These topic pages contain the original approved specification text relocated from the broad overview documents. Original section headings remain as links to preserve entry points. The underlying contracts are unchanged.

| Domain | Topic pages |
| --- | --- |
| Practice presentation | [Setup](product-ux/practice/ux-practice-setup.md), [Matching](product-ux/practice/ux-match.md), [Multiple choice](product-ux/practice/ux-mcq.md), [Summary](product-ux/practice/ux-summary.md) |
| Dictionary and accessibility | [Browse](product-ux/pages/ux-browse.md), [Accessibility](product-ux/foundation/ux-accessibility.md) |
| Appearance | [Theme and dark mode](product-ux/foundation/ux-appearance.md) |
| Practice domain behavior | [Current Practice overview](learning-practice/practice/practice-overview.md) |
| UI state architecture | [State ownership](architecture/ui-state-ownership.md), [Browse state](architecture/ui-browse-state.md) |
| Rust/WASM browser interoperability | [Browser boundary and thin wrappers](architecture/modules/rust-wasm-interop.md) |

Use the [documentation validation script](../scripts/docs-validate.cjs) to check source links, image references, navigation index freshness and prohibited typography before packaging.

## Current approved product requirements

The following are authoritative **target-behavior** specifications. They do not imply successful builds, implemented features, or completed browser acceptance. Historical narrative in older documents remains available for provenance, but must not override these current requirements.

| Responsibility | Authoritative specification |
| --- | --- |
| Shared exercise frame and typed outcomes | [Practice exercise foundation](learning-practice/practice/shared-exercise-foundation.md) |
| Header and long dragon progress | [Header and dragon](product-ux/foundation/header-and-dragon.md) |
| Nonblocking vocabulary count | [Eligibility counting](dictionary-data/vocabulary/eligibility-counting.md) |
| Credits and acknowledgements | [Credits](product-ux/credits.md) |
| E2E evidence review workflow | [Developer and Codex review](testing-quality/e2e/review-workflow.md) |
| Practice verdicts, summary and Skip and Replace | [Practice outcomes](learning-practice/practice/practice-outcomes.md) |
| Pedagogical selection, visitation and global exclusions | [Vocabulary selection](dictionary-data/vocabulary/vocabulary-selection.md) |
| Portable saved Practice profiles | [Profile JSON portability](learning-practice/practice/practice-profile-portability.md) |
| Unified vision recognition canvas and privacy | [AI Hanzi recognition](learning-practice/hanzi/ai-hanzi-recognition.md) |
| Copy, theme, startup recovery, SEO and engineering policy | [Interface and platform policy](product-ux/foundation/interface-and-platform-policy.md) |
| Shared local visitation architecture | [Visitation boundaries](dictionary-data/vocabulary/vocabulary-visitation.md) |
| Sentence Relay stages, interaction and contextual correction | [Sentence Relay](games/sentence-relay.md) |
| Application screenshot-driven UI requirements | [Visual and interaction review](product-ux/references/ui-screenshot-review.md) |
| Testable requirements | [Acceptance criteria](testing-quality/acceptance/approved-behavior-acceptance.md) |

Unresolved decisions and implementation gaps remain in [tasks](project-management/tasks.md) and [issues](issues/OPEN.md). Historical release records are not current product requirements.

The [E2E requirements-to-test matrix](testing-quality/e2e/e2e-requirements-matrix.md) distinguishes authored browser scenarios from executed, verified evidence.

## Editorial ownership and filenames

Maintained article filenames use lowercase kebab-case, except conventional `README.md` entry points. Article titles should identify a specific responsibility, and similarly named files must have distinct ownership. Topic subfolders are allowed; do not introduce deeper nesting without a demonstrable navigation need. Historical and issue filenames retain identifiers when necessary for provenance. Avoid release identifiers in maintained titles and body text.

Overlapping contracts: the current [UX overview](product-ux/ux.md) and [Practice overview](learning-practice/practice/practice-overview.md) are navigation entry points, not duplicate authorities. E2E [recording workflow](testing-quality/e2e/e2e-recording.md) is operational guidance; the [video evidence contract](testing-quality/e2e/e2e-video-recording.md) governs recording metadata and validity. Historical implementation chronicles are stored in archive-history/audits.

For ongoing editorial and implementation verification gaps, see [documentation quality](project-management/documentation-quality.md).

# Architecture

Workspace architecture overview. Current package membership must be confirmed against the root Cargo manifest. This file describes code boundaries, not older proposals or historical release snapshots. Approved future behavior is documented in [Product](../product-ux/product.md), [UX](../product-ux/ux.md) and [Tasks](../project-management/tasks.md).

## Workspace

The root Cargo workspace contains:

| Package | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `zipeek-web` | Yew CSR application, router, shell, components, browser services and orchestration |
| `zipeek-core` | Shared vocabulary types and deterministic round-domain primitives |
| `zipeek-exercises` | Practice definitions, validated setup drafts and pure exercise/session domains |
| `zipeek-ai-protocol` | Authored prompts and validation of model responses, including sentence analysis and generated exercise contracts |
| `zipeek-ai-core` | New provider-neutral generation request, validation and streamed event contract; no backend connected yet |
| `zipeek-ai-server` | Injectable HTTP chat-completion transport with JSON/SSE and restricted CORS; executable/model runtime still unimplemented |
| `zipeek-ai-client` | OpenAI-compatible HTTP transport for native and WASM clients |
| `zipeek-db` | Native/WASM database infrastructure, typed queries and personal-storage probe |
| `zipeek-db-gen` | Native generator for the read-only DuckDB dictionary and manifest |
| `zipeek-ui`, `zipeek-browser` | UI and browser-specific reusable functionality |
| `zipeek-hanzi-writing` | Pure Hanzi stroke/ink geometry |
| `zipeek-themes` | Theme providers and resolution |
| `zipeek-e2e` | Managed Chrome E2E harness, scenarios and in-process Rust AI fixture |
| `zipeek-image-server` | Optional local image service |
| `zipeek-cli` | Clap command orchestration, asset preparation, source pack/unpack, dictionary publication tooling |
| `zipeek-static-server` | Tokio/Axum server for already-built static Trunk assets, supporting root and Pages prefixes |

`Cargo.toml` is authoritative for current members. Tool/version pins are enforced by manifests and lockfiles, not historical documentation.

## Source audit boundary

The installed dictionary manifest currently declares 120,970 `words` rows, `v2.0.0` engine and storage compatibility, and a generated database file that is **not included in the complete source ZIP**. Older HSK source reading counts are not dictionary row counts. See [database metadata](../dictionary-data/schema/db.md) and [source verification](../project-management/source-accuracy-audit.md). Runtime readiness and browser persistence still require a working application build and evidence.

## Grammar learning ownership

`zipeek-pedagogy::grammar` is the authoritative static Grammar catalogue, slug mapping and region plan for 100 draft courses. `zipeek-exercises::grammar_learning` provides pure step, recall and answer-transition rules without Yew dependencies. `zipeek-web` maps these to a local reducer, route-specific learning components and browser-local progress persistence, while both course engines reuse `GrammarLessonScaffold`. The web layer has no generated Grammar curriculum tables. Two separate pedagogical lesson engines remain; no mastery inference or HSK verification has been added. Rust/WASM/browser acceptance is pending.

Browser functionality follows the [Rust/WASM interoperability contract](modules/rust-wasm-interop.md): Rust owns application state and lifecycle, `zipeek-browser` owns reusable browser bindings, Yew owns presentation, and permitted JavaScript stays a thin vendor/host boundary.

## Runtime

`crates/zipeek-web/index.html` supplies the static loading shell and packaged asset references. Trunk builds the Yew/WASM app, which mounts the router and providers. Shared global state includes theme, dictionary readiness, Word Sets and exercise contexts. The app uses the `/#/` hash router for static hosting and `/zipeek/` as the Pages base path.

The database transport loads the generated compressed/verified artifact under `crates/zipeek-web/static/`. DuckDB-WASM opens it read-only and serves typed queries to Browse and Practice. Debug reads typed storage statistics through the database service and, in development builds only, offers an Overview/DuckDB/SQL tabbed view with a 100-row bounded SELECT terminal against the packaged read-only dictionary. Its SQL parser guardrails are not a security sandbox and it never connects to personal OPFS data. The displayed generator storage-compatibility version is manifest metadata, not proof of the WASM engine's default physical file storage version. Native generator and browser engine versions are distinct from manifest storage compatibility metadata.

## Practice and AI data flow

The learner selects Practice options in the four-step setup. `zipeek-exercises::practice_draft` validates choices. Every supported Practice start creates a UUID v7 session in `PracticeSessionStore`, then navigates to `/practice/session/:id`. The only Practice routes are `/practice` and `/practice/session/:id`. The session stores a shared typed configuration map and per-step configuration references; old standalone exercise routes have been intentionally removed. `practice_generated.rs` generates a validated sentence using Settings-owned AI endpoint/model and saved direction; `pages/practice/generated_session.rs` renders its tiles, obtains model evaluation and sends a scored result to the host. `pages/practice/local_session.rs` manages advancement, interruption, restoration and completion cleanup.

The generation request carries a reproducible sampled vocabulary pool of at most ten entries. Model output is a Chinese and English sentence pair; Zipeek constructs sentence tiles and their canonical answer metadata. Other exercise families retain their dedicated runtime boundaries where applicable. The standalone sentence generation route and the free-text translator are not the same as UUID-backed Practice.

## Storage boundaries

- Generated dictionary: immutable/read-only DuckDB asset, manually regenerated and installed.
- Preferences and non-secret AI settings: `zipeek.preferences.v1` localStorage.
- Personal Word Sets/course progress/exclusions: separate localStorage categories with JSON backup and explicit deletion.
- Unfinished UUID Practice: `zipeek.practice.session.v1.*`, removed after finishing.
- Optional API key: tab-memory only.
- Personal OPFS/DuckDB: diagnostics/snapshot/probe and an unverified opt-in Practice-outcome writer; the latter is not yet browser-verified.

## Testing and deployment

The Rust E2E harness owns test servers, isolated Chrome sessions and a Rust AI fixture. The separate [native AI transport](modules/ai-server.md) is not yet a running model service. Test cases cover concrete routes under local root and Pages base paths. `cargo make e2e-full` compiles WASM and test targets before Chrome execution. See [E2E](../archive-history/audits/e2e.md), [data flow](modules/data-flow.md), [DB](../dictionary-data/schema/db.md) and [current acceptance](../project-management/current.md).

### Practice setup boundaries

`pages/practice/setup/page.rs` coordinates the setup reducer and page panels. Its sibling `validation.rs` computes launch eligibility without UI state changes, `launch.rs` owns route and session launch effects, `profiles.rs` owns the Yew profile controls while delegating persistence to `services/practice_profiles.rs`, and `session_recovery.rs` renders the existing-session recovery screen. The authoritative duplicate-session check remains in `PracticeSessionStore::create()`. This source-level refactor still requires WASM compilation and Chrome journey acceptance.

## Component and module ownership

Cloud Match has a feature entry point at `crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/learning/games/cloud_match/mod.rs`; its private HUD and vocabulary-loading helpers are now `games/cloud_match/game/hud.rs` and `games/cloud_match/vocabulary.rs`. The `games/mod.rs` facade exports `CloudMatchPage`, not those implementation helpers. The vocabulary helper still calls the shared game-pair mapper in `games/pairs.rs`; data loading, reducer ownership, and runtime behavior have not deliberately changed.

Cloud Match E2E probes reside in `crates/zipeek-e2e/tests/cloud_match_scripts.rs` and are used by `game_interactions.rs`. The JavaScript behavior probes have standalone Node regression checks in `scripts/cloud-e2e-probes.test.cjs`. The existing `tests/suites` modules remain shared through multiple integration-test parents and have not been migrated into the library, since that requires Rust target-level compilation. Practice-session schema validation is now implemented in `services/practice_session_store/validation.rs`, with the session model, transitions, codec, inventory rules and browser storage adapter in `services/practice_session_store/`. The generation transition methods share a finished-step guard. The extraction has source-contract coverage but still requires Rust compilation plus serialized-schema and revision/recovery acceptance before separating persistence.

## pedagogical domain foundation

The newly approved `zipeek-pedagogy` crate houses a source-only, pure Rust recognition acquisition projection for future Dragon Progression. It currently has no dependencies or runtime integrations. Its 10×7 rules are documented in [pedagogy](../dictionary-data/schema/pedagogy.md). The existing the historical source multi-skill learning engine remains in `zipeek-exercises`; no authoritative personal DuckDB, `/stats` route or browser worker has been activated by this change. The domain and browser worker execution host are intentionally separate boundaries.

## pedagogy analysis coordinator (WIP)

`zipeek-pedagogy::worker` now provides a platform-neutral job state machine. Requests carry a stable ID and an assessment as-of UTC timestamp; duplicate IDs with different payloads are rejected. The coordinator reads committed recognition history through the existing `EvidenceJournal` boundary and publishes only successful `RecognitionProjection` calculations. Retry attempts are capped at three, with due-time scheduling and a visible failure state; explicit retry is required after exhaustion. Disabling processing pauses queued work.

This is **not** the browser Web Worker implementation. A separate WASM worker host must initialize the Rust runtime in a worker context, establish typed messaging, coordinate with the existing DuckDB-WASM worker, and recover a durable queue. There is no new database schema, runtime dependency, automatic evidence collection or UI attachment in the source reviewed for this contract.

## Statistics dashboard boundary (WIP)

The `/stats` route is a dictionary-independent Yew page with Overview, Hanzi, Skills, History and Insights sections. It currently renders an explicit unassessed state and a link to personal storage Settings. It does not read personal DuckDB, initialize the Rust/WASM worker, infer recognition proficiency from game outcomes, or publish acquisition awards. Future authoritative projections require verified committed evidence, host-side consent, single-tab ownership and the existing learning-domain acceptance gates before attaching live data.

## Rust browser worker monitor boundary

`zipeek-pedagogy::monitor` is the platform-neutral read-only health-request state machine; it verifies version, correlation, expiry, health fields and shutdown without using browser APIs. `zipeek-browser::pedagogy_worker` owns the temporary module Worker, event listeners, timeout and termination. Yew Settings calls the Rust browser adapter directly. `static/pedagogy-worker/worker.mjs` is only the WASM loader, buffering requests until initialization and returning correlated startup errors. The separate Rust/WASM worker binary owns the permanent `DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope` message listener, request decoding, single disabled-by-default `WorkerEndpoint`, and response serialization; the browser host remains a read-only diagnostic client. The separate worker is built cross-platform via `zipeek-cli build pedagogy-worker` (exact wasm-bindgen 0.2.130, locked release build); Pages CI runs this before Trunk copies `static/`. The monitor exposes only `get_health` and is not the evidence analysis coordinator. The main application's worker status button does not consent to tracking, connect to OPFS, persist jobs, or award learning progress. Real browser and WASM acceptance remain pending.

## typed worker binary and first-run diagnostics

`zipeek-web` now declares `[[bin]] pedagogy_worker` with an explicit `src/bin/pedagogy_worker/mod.rs` path. `browser.rs` is the only module depending on browser globals; `runtime.rs` validates and dispatches the Rust endpoint; `wire.rs` holds Serde v1 envelopes and stable health/result/error codes; `error.rs` defines typed errors; `evidence.rs` converts recognition DTOs without treating caller-supplied `snapshot_verified` as a proof of durability. The browser JS loader is unchanged. Rust worker still starts disabled. Do not activate analysis based on first-run preferences alone.

The first-run landing form chooses one of the six existing theme presets and stores an inert, default-off pedagogical opt-in preference. Settings permits changing/revoking that preference. Neither UI writes recognition evidence, enables the worker nor alters OPFS ownership. The debug-only dictionary SQL terminal is bounded and read-only, with a tabular result and CSV export of the displayed (at most 100) rows. A fresh WASM database storage-version probe is **not implemented**: the loaded dictionary's manifest compatibility value and engine `version()` are not equivalent to independently reading a newly created database file's physical storage format.

## Vocabulary curriculum ownership

`zipeek-pedagogy::curriculum` now owns the static 100-region Vocabulary catalogue and typed region identity, domain and membership fields. The existing `zipeek-web` course route consumes it through the workspace dependency already present. `zipeek-exercises` continues to own exercises, not region metadata; the dictionary lookup and personal Word Set provider remain in the web application. This is a code ownership change, **not** completed thematic or HSK coverage. A pinned-source audit script reports gaps; the future fully authored curriculum needs entry-level identities and semantic review before coverage claims. No dependencies, stored browser format, or data generator inputs changed.

## exhaustive HSK Vocabulary source membership

`zipeek-pedagogy::curriculum::VOCABULARY_REGIONS` is a deterministic generated Rust catalogue holding 100 distinct region definitions, 11,494 pinned HSK source indices, 12,188 distinct (Hanzi, numeric-pinyin) keys, unique simplified spellings and per-region source HSK counts. The pinned fingerprint and the last recorded assignment audit are retained in `docs/learning-practice/VOCABULARY_COVERAGE.json`; the former Python generators were removed previously and require a native replacement before source changes; machine-classification exceptions are recorded in `docs/learning-practice/VOCABULARY_REVIEW_QUEUE.csv`. Source coverage and semantic editorial acceptance are separate.

`zipeek-web` resolves each region through batched parameterized `Database::words_by_simplified` queries, validates complete unique dictionary IDs and exposes up to 200 words per personal Word Set. The browser Word Sets limit is 250; its serialized structure is unchanged. Dictionary acquisition now matches both simplified spelling and numeric pinyin, so distinct source readings remain independently acquirable. Dictionary runtime matching still needs live verification against the generated bundle. No new dependencies or generated dictionary bundle were introduced.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/architecture-architecture.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.

# Speaking capture, waveform and contextual targets

**Status:** browser microphone capture, live amplitude visualization, local playback,
and discard are implemented on the experimental `#/practice/speaking` route.
No pronunciation assessment, persistence, or upload exists. The
`zipeek-exercises::definition::SPEAKING` contract is reserved for the future scored exercise.

## Domain boundaries

- `zipeek-exercises`: speaking exercise definition/instance and future pronunciation evidence; a waveform is not a pronunciation score.
- `zipeek-browser/src/microphone/`: browser permission, capture, MediaRecorder, Web Audio analysis, 30-second limit, playback URL, generation checks and release of tracks. This is Rust using `web-sys`; no JavaScript recorder module remains.
- `zipeek-web/src/components/audio/speaking_recorder/`: Yew controls, status, errors, playback UI and callback lifetimes. The bindings adapter passes callback functions to `zipeek_browser::microphone::MicrophoneRecorder` and disposes it on unmount.
- Future opt-in speech assessment is outside this local-only recorder.

The recorder is a single-field tuple struct wrapping shared Rust lifecycle state.
The Rust implementation is divided into `recorder.rs` (public API), `state.rs`
(resource ownership and callbacks), `capture.rs` (MediaRecorder and permission
flow), `waveform.rs` (frame sampling), and `error.rs` (browser error mapping).
`mod.rs` exports the recorder without implementing all of those concerns.
The lifecycle phase is a typed `RecordingPhase` enum internally, converted to
legacy status strings only when invoking the Yew callback.
`BlobEvent::data()` returns `Option<Blob>` in the pinned `web-sys`; missing or
empty blobs are ignored rather than unwrapped before adding chunks. It retains the original `idle`, `requesting`, `recording`, `processing`, `ready` and `error` states. The permission request starts only from a user gesture. Late permission grants are rejected using an increasing generation token; tracks from obsolete grants are stopped immediately. Unmount/discard releases MediaRecorder handlers, audio context, animation frame, deadline and object URL.

The previous `crates/zipeek-web/src/services/microphone.js` has been removed. `scripts/translation.test.cjs` asserts the Rust contracts; actual permission denial, capture and stop/discard behavior still need browser validation.

## Microphone-to-waveform pipeline

1. Ask for microphone access only after pressing Record; support permission
   denial, unavailable devices, insecure origins and concurrent recording.
2. Attach the `MediaStream` to a Web Audio `AudioContext` and `AnalyserNode`
   with a small FFT window. Sample time-domain data with
   `getFloatTimeDomainData`; calculate windowed RMS or peak amplitude.
3. At `requestAnimationFrame` cadence, append an amplitude observation to a
   bounded ring buffer. Render vertical bars centered on a baseline, with
   approximate 20-40 updates per second. This is an **amplitude waveform**,
   not an FFT/spectrogram (frequency visualization is different).
4. Capture audio separately through `MediaRecorder`, with runtime MIME support
   detection and a bounded recording duration. `MediaRecorder` and Web Audio
   may share the same `MediaStream`, but their lifecycles are independent.
5. On Stop, navigate-away or component unmount, stop media tracks and release
   the recorder/audio context/animation frame. Do not assume cancelling a
   visualizer also stops a microphone recording.
6. Preserve the last amplitude bars with browser-native playback controls after
   recording. A player may seek through the captured audio; amplitude bars are
   purely presentational and must not be treated as a measure of speaking skill.
   Elapsed-time display and waveform seeking are follow-up tasks.

## UI and accessibility

A SoundCloud-like row of centered vertical bars can visualize the user's
speech. Provide visible Record, Stop, Play and Discard controls plus elapsed
recording time and a textual status for screen readers. Use a neutral idle
waveform, respect reduced motion, display a clear recording/permission state,
and provide a fallback when Web Audio is unsupported. Always distinguish
**recorded** from **evaluated**; never imply that a decorative waveform is an
assessment. Avoid autoplay and automatic cloud uploads.

## API / dependency policy

No Rust crate, npm package, `web-sys` feature flag, or dependency pin was added.
The Rust browser adapter uses `web-sys` browser APIs and the existing
`wasm-bindgen` dependency. Chromium browser and wasm32
compilation still require local verification. Extract a separate audio crate
only if reusable signal processing and capture-domain contracts warrant it;
`zipeek-exercises` must not depend on microphone APIs.

`crates/zipeek-web/src/components/audio/audio_waveform.rs` remains a presentational 40-bar
SVG renderer with clamped amplitude input. Microphone samples are never stored
as vocabulary proficiency evidence, and there is no implicit speech upload.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/architecture-audio-recording.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.

## Native Mandarin engine boundary

`zipeek-tts-stt` is a separate loopback-only native service, not a web microphone provider. Its eSpeak NG synthesis emits PCM16 mono WAV. When eSpeak writes to stdout, it cannot seek back to update WAV length fields; the service verifies the returned format, sample rate and bounded audio payload, then writes actual RIFF/data sizes before serving the file. Corrupt or empty audio is rejected. Whisper recognition is restricted to bounded 16 kHz mono PCM16 WAV; results must contain a nonempty, bounded transcript without control characters. Transcript text is not a pronunciation score.

Every HTTP endpoint, including health and capability checks, requires a localhost/127.0.0.1 Host and rejects browser Origin requests. Responses carry `Cache-Control: no-store`. The existing browser capture, TTS providers and microphone permissions remain independent. A desktop bridge needs a separate approved security design; do not expose the native server directly to hosted pages.
title: Speaking capture, waveform and contextual targets

# Experimental Live STT binary protocol

R687 replaces the R686 JSON/text WebSocket messages with a single compact binary protocol. This is a development-phase break, not a backward-compatible negotiation. The endpoint remains `ws://127.0.0.1:8799/v1/stt/live`, restricted by the existing loopback and Origin checks.

Each WebSocket **binary message** is one complete application frame. The first byte is its kind. Integer fields are little-endian. The client sends 16 kHz, mono, signed PCM16 without a WAV header. No JSON, Base64 or serializer crate is involved. UTF-8 is used only for transcript content.

| Direction | Kind | Payload |
|---|---|---|
| Client to server | `0x01` | `u32` sample rate, must be 16000 |
| Client to server | `0x02` | No fields; finish utterance |
| Client to server | `0x03` | 2 to 6400 bytes of interleaved little-endian PCM16 samples, mono |
| Server to client | `0x81` | `u32` rate 16000, `u16` maximum seconds 30, `u8` mode 1 for Qwen snapshot recognition |
| Server to client | `0x82` | No fields; ready for PCM |
| Server to client | `0x83` | `u32` cumulative sample count, followed by UTF-8 partial transcript |
| Server to client | `0x84` | `u32` cumulative sample count, followed by UTF-8 final transcript |
| Server to client | `0x85` | One byte error code |

Error codes: 1 no speech; 2 inference unavailable; 3 recognition task failed; 4 session timeout; 5 invalid session transition; 6 unexpected message type; 7 session audio limit; 8 invalid audio frame; 9 other rejected session. The server then sends a WebSocket close frame.

Limits: two concurrent sessions, 30 seconds audio per session, 45-second session timeout, and one in-flight snapshot transcription per session. Recognition is still periodic Qwen3-ASR on accumulated snapshots, not a checkpoint-compatible true Zipformer streaming encoder.

The Yew Live tab uses an `AudioWorklet` to transfer PCM blocks off the audio rendering thread, incrementally resamples to 16 kHz and sends bounded 100 ms frames. It flushes the AudioWorklet pending block before sending Finish, then stops capture. It also stops capture when leaving the tab, on explicit cancellation, or when replaced. If the socket's `bufferedAmount` exceeds 64 KiB, the browser reports an error rather than silently dropping arbitrary speech. The live audio is not saved to disk by the new transport.

This protocol has no compatibility with the earlier R686 JSON messages. The client and server must both come from R687. The `AudioWorklet` uses a generated local blob module and needs a browser/WebView security-policy check; the hosted `/zipeek/` deployment cannot connect to the localhost speech server from an untrusted origin.

## Acceptance

Run `cargo check --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt`, `cargo test --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt --test live_stt_websocket`, `cargo check --locked -p zipeek-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo test --locked -p zipeek-browser` and `cargo test --locked -p zipeek-web` on the Windows development machine. Start the localhost speech service with a Qwen ASR checkpoint and `ZIPEEK_STT_DEVICE=cuda`. In the local app, open `#/record`, select Live, start the microphone, verify real PCM waveform and partial transcripts, finish and verify the final transcript. Repeat cancellation, no speech, wrong origin, reconnect, closed socket, and mode switching. Verify browser and Tauri WebView CSP support for the worklet module.
title: Experimental Live STT binary protocol

# AI client boundary

`zipeek-ai-client` is a native-and-browser-WASM OpenAI-compatible HTTP client implemented in Rust with `reqwest =0.13.5`. `lib.rs` only declares modules and re-exports the public API. Internals are split by responsibility:

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `src/client.rs` | `AiClient(ClientConfig)`; HTTP POST, SSE response assembly, configurable progress callback, native five-minute total deadline, and connection diagnostics |
| `src/config.rs` | URL validation, `/v1/chat/completions` construction, credential and insecure-remote-HTTP safeguards |
| `src/protocol.rs` | Serde request and response wire types |
| `src/stream.rs` | Incremental SSE parser handling network chunk and UTF-8 boundaries, completion markers, output limits and malformed streams |
| `src/prompts.rs` | Translation directions, source checks, translation and connection-test messages |
| `src/error.rs` | Status-specific errors, provider JSON parsing, bounded/redacted diagnostic text |

There is **no JavaScript HTTP transport**, wasm-bindgen HTTP binding or platform-specific stub. `reqwest` uses browser Fetch on WASM and the native async HTTP stack on desktop. AI settings and tab-memory API-key storage live in `zipeek-browser/src/ai_configuration.rs`; `zipeek-web/src/services/ai/mod.rs` passes the key per request without storing it in `AiClient`. The API key remains in tab memory and is never persisted.

`zipeek-ai-protocol` is the pure sentence-analysis contract owner: it builds structured-analysis prompts, parses returned JSON, validates vocabulary and grammar against exact source/translation spans, and builds repair prompts. The web service still orchestrates the structured request, one repair, and plain-translation fallback when a provider rejects structured output with HTTP 400/422. No analysis fields or SQL have moved into the HTTP client.

## Endpoint and browser restrictions

The Rust client rejects non-HTTP(S) URLs, URL-embedded credentials, query/fragment in the base URL, and API-key transmission over non-loopback HTTP. Native builds configure a five-minute overall request deadline on `reqwest::Client` to allow slow local model generation. **The browser reqwest adapter does not expose `ClientBuilder::timeout` on wasm32**: the browser client therefore does not enforce that five-minute deadline. Streaming progress still works, but a separate target-independent timeout/cancellation design is needed before promising bounded browser requests. Native builds use an explicit no-redirect policy. The WASM `reqwest` adapter does not offer the same redirect configuration: browser Fetch may follow redirects; the client rejects responses whose final URL differs from the requested URL, but this is an **after-the-request check**, not a guarantee that the browser did not forward a request. Prefer a direct trusted `/v1/` endpoint. Standard browser CORS, mixed-content, and HTTPS rules still apply.

The default request contract uses `stream: true` and consumes `text/event-stream` using `reqwest::Response::bytes_stream`. A provider that returns a conventional JSON completion despite requesting streaming is also accepted without an extra model call. SSE frames are bounded and must terminate with `[DONE]` or a `finish_reason`; an incomplete response is rejected. The client exposes `complete_streaming(messages, api_key, on_delta)` for progress-aware consumers and retains `complete()` as the assembled-text wrapper. The web translation page and sentence-translation exercise now consume streaming progress. An accessible status widget displays the current phase and observed character count; it does not invent a completion percentage. During structured analysis, partial JSON and private model reasoning are never displayed as final learning content. Models that emit `reasoning_content` can report activity before any answer text appears.

Provider HTTP errors are translated to bounded readable messages. If a provider supplies JSON `error.message` and `error.code`, the message is sanitized, truncated and redacted against the supplied API key and common bearer patterns. Raw HTML and unrecognized error bodies are not shown. The actual configured model may still reject structured analysis because of context length, token budget, or provider capability: a successful plain fallback is not proof that analysis succeeded.

## Deterministic integration fixtures

`tests/fixtures/complex_zh_en.json` and `complex_en_zh.json` include complex concessive/conditional sentences with expected translation, two grammar explanations and three vocabulary items each. These are **hand-authored fixture expectations, not model evaluations**. `tests/http_integration.rs` launches a local TCP HTTP server and checks real reqwest request serialization, authorization headers, HTTP status handling, translation responses and `zipeek_ai_protocol::sentence_analysis::parse` validation for both directions. It exercises a structured HTTP 400 followed by a successful plain translation. These tests run without a live AI model.

`tests/live_model.rs` is ignored by default and invokes a real configured model for both fixture sentences. The detailed analysis uses streaming and prints incremental deltas to stdout with `--nocapture`, so lengthy generation shows progress before completion. It asserts nonempty plain translation and complete schema-valid analysis; it does not claim semantic equivalence to the hand-authored reference translation. A failure here may indicate the model cannot comply with the structured contract even if plain translation succeeds.

### Windows validation

```powershell
cargo test -p zipeek-ai-client --locked
cargo test -p zipeek-ai-client --test http_integration --locked
cargo check -p zipeek-ai-client --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --locked
cargo check -p zipeek-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --locked
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

To exercise your local OpenAI-compatible model (example LM Studio endpoint), from PowerShell:

```powershell
$env:ZIPEEK_AI_ENDPOINT = "http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1/"
$env:ZIPEEK_AI_MODEL = "your-loaded-model-id"
# Optional: $env:ZIPEEK_AI_KEY = "your-key"
cargo test -p zipeek-ai-client --test live_model --locked -- --ignored --nocapture
```

Afterward run the existing managed Chrome Translate Sentence fixture scenarios from `zipeek-e2e`, and manually check the screenshot's structured-analysis rejection against the actual model. Node source tests do not validate Rust compilation or live browser behavior.

## Streaming browser acceptance

The managed E2E AI fixture now accepts both `stream: true` SSE and legacy JSON completions. `translator-streaming` intentionally sends a reasoning delta before delivering a fragmented structured-analysis response, giving the Chrome scenario time to assert the accessible `data-ai-stream-progress` status before the final result. Generation and evaluation fixtures also return SSE to match the real Rust HTTP contract. The fixture's private reasoning text is never displayed by the UI; only its length is surfaced. These Chrome scenarios still require actual Chrome/WebDriver execution.

## typed protocol and structured-analysis contract

`zipeek-ai-client/src/message.rs` defines serializable/deserializable `ChatMessage` and `ChatRole` for ordinary translation and connection tests. The HTTP request and non-streaming response are typed; the SSE decoder deserializes typed per-choice deltas, including opaque reasoning activity counts. The public generic completion entry points continue accepting existing serializable message collections while callers migrate away from `serde_json::Value`.

`zipeek-ai-protocol/src/sentence_analysis/prompt.rs` owns the deliberately explicit translation and linguistic-evidence prompt; `schema.rs` owns the strict provider JSON Schema, and `sentence_analysis.rs` owns the `SentenceAnalysis` domain types and semantic evidence checks. All ten top-level fields are required, including empty enrichment arrays; unknown properties and ungrounded vocabulary/grammar fragments are rejected. The schema requires nested item objects to contain only their declared fields. `estimated_hsk` remains an estimate and may be null.

The Translate Sentence workflow requests OpenAI-compatible `response_format: {type: "json_schema", json_schema: {name: "sentence_analysis", strict: true, schema: ...}}` with streaming. If the provider rejects that format with HTTP 400/422, Zipeek retries the existing pedantic prompt without provider-side schema enforcement, then retains its plain-translation fallback. Partial structured JSON remains hidden until `SentenceAnalysis::parse` succeeds, and a single bounded repair attempt is still supported.

**Limits:** Neither JSON Schema nor substring matching proves correct pinyin or linguistic interpretation. The live Qwen test provided by the user passed both fixture directions in 182.64 seconds on an earlier version; the historical source's stricter contract and schema negotiation need a fresh native/WASM and live-model run. Dictionary-backed reading verification is a separate future enhancement. Browser provider support for strict JSON Schema varies; schema rejection is not the same as translation failure.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/architecture-modules-ai-client.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.

## R532 image recognition request boundary

`RecognizeHanziPage` uses the existing generic serializable chat message interface to send a multimodal OpenAI-compatible `image_url` data URL only after pressing Recognize. Images are composited to a bounded 768 by 480 canvas, not persisted; the web controller validates model candidates independently of model-supplied meanings or pinyin and checks exact dictionary entries. The E2E fixture redacts image data from captured request records. The client does not currently advertise a vision-capability probe or provide a cross-platform abort signal, so production acceptance must verify the selected model and cancellation behavior. No new dependency is introduced.

R537: Hanzi recognition parses candidate responses with category and JSON line/column diagnostics and logs safe structural metadata on failure. It does not log model text or image data. The workspace samples theme surface/ink colors at paint time and repaints on appearance changes.


## AI Settings diagnostic lifecycle

`crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/system/settings/ai/` owns the Settings AI page (`page.rs`), callback and asynchronous request orchestration (`controller.rs`), request-ticket reducer (`state.rs`) and diagnostic display (`diagnostics.rs`). Synchronous request gating prevents a rapid second test from launching before Yew rerenders; reducer ticket checks discard stale completions after edits, saves, dismissal, restart or unmount. **Dismiss test** invalidates display publication; it does **not** abort an already-started HTTP call. Verify with locked Rust/WASM and browser tests before claiming acceptance. This is diagnostic connectivity, not R608 evaluator evidence or mastery scoring.
title: AI client boundary

# Local AI server boundary

The native `zipeek-ai-server` executable now starts a real `llama-cpp-2` GGUF inference backend, not the fixture provider. It requires an explicitly selected local model. The executable accepts `--bind 127.0.0.1:1430` and rejects non-loopback binds. The service is managed by the existing Tauri Services manager as the `ai` sidecar.

## Model selection

Set `ZIPEEK_AI_MODEL_PATH` to the GGUF file before starting Tauri, or install exactly one `.gguf` file under `models/ai` relative to the process working directory or executable directory. Multiple GGUF candidates require an explicit environment variable to avoid nondeterministic model selection. Startup fails if the file is missing. `ZIPEEK_AI_GPU_LAYERS` selects GPU offload (default 0), and `ZIPEEK_AI_CONTEXT` selects the context window (default 4096, accepted 512–131072).

The server advertises model ID `local-gguf` and retains one loaded model for the process lifetime. A per-request llama.cpp context is created on a blocking worker. Requests are serialized by the Axum semaphore, tokens are generated with the checkpoint's own embedded chat template, streaming output is bounded, and cancellation is checked during prompt and generation loops. Sampling uses the requested temperature and a fixed seed for repeatable diagnostics. Request cancellation is cooperative and can only interrupt between native decode calls.

The existing Axum OpenAI-compatible endpoints remain `/health`, `/v1/models`, and `/v1/chat/completions`; generation supports text chat with SSE or JSON output. Structured provider-side JSON Schema is not implemented here; the web translation workflow retains its prompt-enforced fallback when structured requests are rejected. This is a text-only backend, not a vision-capable model. The in-memory deterministic `FixtureBackend` remains compiled only in `#[cfg(test)]` so HTTP unit tests do not require a GGUF; no fixture-mode executable is shipped.

## Security and lifecycle

The process only binds to loopback. The server only authorizes known browser origins, including development localhost. The model file and user prompts remain on this computer when Local AI is selected. The model itself is not included in source ZIPs or Tauri bundles. Services settings control process startup; AI settings select the provider and model, without duplicating process actions.

LM Studio uses the configured HTTP-compatible endpoint and model discovered through `/v1/models`. The default proposal is `http://192.168.1.148:1234/v1/`, but the user can edit it. In browser/WebView mode the existing reqwest/WASM transport remains subject to CORS and mixed-content rules; a native Tauri HTTP proxy is not yet integrated. Credentials are not persisted; the client rejects transmitting keys over non-loopback unencrypted HTTP.

## Acceptance still required

The Rust and WASM builds, native DLL linkage, model loading, true GGUF inference and SSE with an installed model have not been run in the packaging environment. On Windows, use `cargo check --locked -p zipeek-ai-server -p zipeek-app`, `cargo test --locked -p zipeek-ai-server -p zipeek-ai-client`, and `cargo check --locked -p zipeek-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. Rebuild the sidecar explicitly with `cargo make desktop-sidecars-rebuild`; the development staging task can reuse stale executables. Then start AI from Settings > Services and test both Local AI and LM Studio in Settings > AI. Test the external model list with GET `/v1/models` and a short translation; verify SSE and model failure recovery.
title: Local AI server boundary

## Implemented boundaries

- [`zipeek-db/src/wasm/`](../../../crates/zipeek-db/src/wasm) owns the DuckDB-WASM bridge, local worker asset resolution, manifest validation, transport and connection lifetime. It is not a separate `zipeek-db-wasm` crate.

- [`zipeek-web/src/components/browse/`](../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/components/browse) drives Browse searches and pagination; [`services/database/browse_queries.rs`](../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/services/database/browse_queries.rs) implements the active normalized Browse query. This is **not** an unconnected future query proposal.
- [`zipeek-db/src/wasm/probe.rs`](../../../crates/zipeek-db/src/wasm/probe.rs) is a separate writable personal-data **probe**, not a production learner-history database.

## Runtime and artifact facts

Current web npm pin: **`@duckdb/duckdb-wasm@1.33.1-dev114.0`**; native generator engine `v2.0.0`, explicit disk compatibility `v2.0.0`. The browser engine must be read from the live runtime, not inferred from native versions. The installed manifest declares **120,970** dictionary rows, not the earlier HSK source count or 12,100-row snapshot. See [runtime](../../dictionary-data/schema/runtime.md) and [installed artifact](../../dictionary-data/schema/db.md) for evidence and the difference between historical decisions and the current installed source policy.

The dictionary uses the packaged local JS/WASM worker and Arrow assets. Source preparation is explicit (`zipeek-cli`/Cargo Make); Trunk deploys prepared assets and loads the timestamped compressed dictionary below the correct `/` or `/zipeek/` base. The dictionary itself is opened read-only and is never the destination for learner outcomes. Browser readiness is owned by the database provider and boundary, with a retry path for failures.

## Real Browse behavior and test boundaries

`BrowseSearchForm` and `BrowseResults` render the active query UI. The service applies typed filters to normalized dictionary tables and orders pages by word ID. Pagination uses the presence of an extra result to establish Next rather than inventing a total count. User-reported Windows E2E results passed Browse word-set discovery, membership, accessibility, empty search, live search and pagination on the earlier source; they do not certify every combination of category/PoS filters in the latest UUID translation build.

An optional future adapter-crate extraction and index/FTS redesign are proposals in [target architecture](target-architecture.md) and [schema review](../../dictionary-data/schema/review.md). Do not present historical A13/A22 or the historical source plans as current limitations in conflict with an implemented Browse query.

See [database schema](../../dictionary-data/schema/schema.md), [E2E](../../archive-history/audits/e2e.md), [current validation state](../../project-management/current.md).

# Native dictionary generator

The implemented native generator is [`crates/zipeek-db-gen`](../../../crates/zipeek-db-gen), not the retired `crates/db-gen` path. Its Cargo package, CLI commands and dependency pins are defined by its current Cargo manifest, `src/cli.rs` and `src/policy.rs`.

## Source-verified pipeline

1. `inputs/` verifies the pinned HSK and CC-CEDICT bytes and associated notices and hashes.
2. `database.rs` opens `duckdb-neo`, requiring engine `v2.0.0` and explicit writable compatibility `v2.0.0`.
3. `schema.sql` creates compatibility `words` plus normalized senses, memberships, characters, identity candidates, controlled categories/PoS and classification relations.
4. [`generator.rs`](../../../crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/generator.rs) parses HSK, applies CC-CEDICT gloss fallback and expands additional CC-CEDICT readings, retaining explicit character-reading data. `import/storage.rs` writes the relational representation.
5. `artifact/writer.rs` stages the native output, copies tables, validates logical snapshots and a reopened read-only database, and publishes only on success. Optional approved classification cache data can be applied before snapshotting.
6. `artifact/report.rs` writes the manifest, provenance, diagnostic counts and per-file hashes. The installed manifest is found under [`zipeek-web/static`](../../../crates/zipeek-web/static/hanzi.manifest.json).

The output is read-only browser dictionary data. It is not a writable personal store or a pedagogical observation ledger. Do not treat an old HSK-only A02/A03 count as the installed dictionary.

## Source and manifest consistency

The installed manifest declares 120,970 `words` rows, engine `v2.0.0`, storage `v2.0.0`, and DuckDB-WASM `1.33.1-dev114.0`. These match `src/policy.rs`, `artifact/writer.rs` and web `package.json`. Older storage-version decisions are historical, not a description of this checked-in generator. Do not change dependency or format pins without explicit approval.

**Artifact verification gate:** `character_readings` is included in the manifest table list and generated SQL, but the source ZIP omits the actual DuckDB binary. Do not claim the table was physically opened or queried until the artifact is present and verified with the native/browser runtime. Source inspection does not certify the user's current Windows build.

## Entry points and further detail

- [Regeneration and installation](../../dictionary-data/schema/regeneration.md)
- [Physical schema](../../dictionary-data/schema/schema.md)
- [Artifact evidence](../../dictionary-data/schema/artifacts.md)
- [Inputs and provenance](../../dictionary-data/schema/sources.md)
- [Current acceptance](../../project-management/current.md)

## Generation performance review (R528 WIP)

The artifact writer currently specifies `BLOCK_SIZE 262144` (256 KiB). Increasing the storage block size is not an established optimization for this workload. The import operates in a transaction with reusable prepared statements but performs individual executes for words, senses and character readings; the artifact writer then bulk-copies the in-memory tables, builds English FTS, checkpoints and verifies the reopened file. Benchmark these phases separately before changing bulk ingestion, schema/index ordering or database layout. Expected gloss pipe normalization diagnostics remain preserved in the structured artifact, but no longer emit WARN per occurrence.

## Batched ingestion (R529 WIP)

The main `words`, `word_senses`, and `character_readings` imports now use parameterized multi-row inserts in chunks of 256, reducing query executions for large dictionaries. Sense display derivation, qualifier and relation extraction, and character enrichment keep their existing per-row logic and transactional boundaries. Small word inserts retain their individual error attribution. The artifact still uses DuckDB's maximum supported 256 KiB block size, and logical snapshot/reopen verification remains mandatory. Benchmark and run the generator's import tests locally before considering the optimization accepted.

# Hanzi stroke reference and guided tracing -

## Architecture

The original reference viewer remains available. The Hanzi Writing workspace now uses the same packaged glyph data to validate handwriting one stroke at a time. It no longer treats every pointer release as a successful stroke.

- `zipeek-hanzi-writing::matching` samples the reference median and candidate trace by arc length. In addition to uniform samples, original reference and candidate vertices are checked against the opposite polyline at matching arc-length fractions, so short hooks and tight curves cannot hide between samples. It checks starting position, ending position, direction (including folded stroke reversals), stroke length, average geometric deviation, and peak deviation in the same normalized canvas coordinates. It deliberately does not independently normalize the two stroke shapes because that would ignore positional errors.
- `zipeek-hanzi-writing::session` owns accepted stroke count, mistakes, rejection reasons, and completion. A rejected stroke does not advance progress. Undo removes one accepted stroke, and Clear resets the session.
- `hanzi_references.rs` owns the shared, once-per-session aggregate fetch and single-character lookup, while `hanzi_writing/practice/stroke_loading.rs` constructs the validated writing session. Requests from a previous character are invalidated on selection changes and stale results are rejected by character identity in the reducer.
- `hanzi_writing/practice/canvas_input.rs` is a pointer-event adapter: it captures/releases pointers and dispatches typed begin, move, finish and cancellation actions. `practice/controller.rs` is the single reducer owning ink, selected character, guide preference, loading status and graded session. Only its finish transition can submit a trace to the pure Rust session. `practice/board.rs` renders the canvas/overlay; `practice/controls.rs` renders action buttons using callbacks owned by the coordinator. A completed pointer gesture is not accepted by itself.
- `HanziWriting` renders the active pen trace on a canvas. An SVG overlay renders canonical stroke outlines. Accepted strokes snap to the exact sourced outline; the next expected outline and its starting point are highlighted when the guide is on. Missing or malformed reference data disables handwriting acceptance.

This is geometric guided tracing against canonical data, not optical recognition of arbitrary handwritten Chinese characters, recognition of alternative stroke order, or a trained handwriting model. The default matching thresholds are engineering starting values and need calibration with real mouse, touch, and stylus input to determine false acceptance and rejection rates.

## Reference data and licensing

The source-only checkpoint deliberately excludes the licensed upstream Hanzi Writer Data distribution and generated `characters.json` reference bundle from pack/unpack; install those assets separately. To regenerate it from the vendored upstream distribution, run from the repository root:

```text
cargo run --locked -p zipeek-cli -- hanzi prepare-references <upstream-json-directory> crates/zipeek-web/static/hanzi-strokes <path-to-ARPHICPL.TXT>
```

For repeatable local setup, run `cargo make prepare-hanzi`; it reuses an existing valid `characters.json` bundle with its manifest and licence. Otherwise `zipeek-cli hanzi prepare` uses `external/hanzi-writer-data/data` and `external/hanzi-writer-data/ARPHICPL.TXT`, cloning a sparse checkout of Hanzi Writer Data with Git when the source directory is absent. Git must be installed and the initial download requires network access. If an incomplete source directory already exists, the command rejects it rather than overwriting it. The Git subprocess runs with the project root as its working directory and a relative checkout destination to avoid Windows extended-length (`\\?\`) destination paths. Clone and final checkout run quietly, suppressing normal Git progress while preserving stderr diagnostics and failure status; sparse-checkout does not request a quiet option. Use `cargo run --locked -p zipeek-cli -- hanzi prepare --force` to regenerate an existing bundle. Source-only ZIPs exclude the licensed upstream inputs and generated stroke bundles.

The Rust importer validates every glyph before writing the single `characters.json` bundle keyed by lower-case Unicode code point, copies the unmodified licence and a modification notice, and writes a manifest with per-glyph and whole-bundle SHA-256 hashes. On a successful write it removes only legacy hex-named per-character JSON assets. Trunk copies `static/hanzi-strokes` into the site. Both browser consumers use the relative `hanzi-strokes/characters.json` URL, cache one shared in-flight fetch for the browser session, and select individual glyphs in memory. A single initial download is approximately 30.7 MB uncompressed for 9,574 glyphs; enable Brotli/gzip at the hosting layer. The browser does not verify SHA-256 at runtime; the manifest is for package integrity verification.

The runtime does not download character data from a third-party CDN. Without packaged data it shows an unavailable state and does not accept strokes. Successful aggregate loads remain cached, while failed aggregate requests are evicted and may be retried from the handwriting workspace. Concurrent requests still share one in-flight fetch.

## Verification

Run `cargo test --locked -p zipeek-hanzi-writing`, `cargo check --locked -p zipeek-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, and `cargo test --locked -p zipeek-e2e --test writing_interactions -- --nocapture` on Windows, after preparing the relevant assets. Inspect stroke orientation and pointer behavior in Chrome. The new E2E scenario also verifies the unavailable-data state if no assets were packaged.

Pure Rust regression tests cover near-correct curves, reverse direction, translated strokes, truncated strokes, unrelated curvature, stroke order, undo, and reset. Browser and real-device calibration is outstanding.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/architecture-modules-hanzi-stroke-references.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.

# Hanzi writing domain crate -
`crates/zipeek-hanzi-writing` is the domain-only foundation for a future Hanzi Drawing exercise. It has no third-party dependencies and does not reference Yew, `web_sys`, HTML canvas, browser events, fonts, or stroke-dataset formats.

## Boundary

- `geometry`: validated two-dimensional points, ordered strokes, extents, CSS-client-to-normalized canvas coordinates, normalized-to-backing coordinates (including high-DPI canvases), deterministic arc-length resampling and translation/uniform-scale normalization.
- `input`: pointer-specific pen capture, duplicate sample suppression, completion, cancellation, undo and clear. It deliberately does not capture pointer events or assign pressure/touch semantics.
- `comparison`: a deterministic order-sensitive geometric distance diagnostic for equal stroke counts. Results are **not** correctness scores, HSK evidence, stroke-order certification, or a basis for grading without calibrated reference data and evaluated thresholds.

## Browser adapter (not implemented)

A Yew component should use a canvas element and pointer events. Read `getBoundingClientRect`, CSS dimensions, and drawing buffer dimensions, then create `CanvasTransform`. Call `client_to_normalized` for samples, record them using `InkCapture`, and on redraw map the normalized values back to backing pixels. Apply pointer capture and handle `pointercancel`, `lostpointercapture`, resize, and device pixel ratio changes. Prevent unwanted touch scrolling only on the drawing surface. Canvas rendering and hit-testing must not become core crate dependencies.

## Future test strategy

Rust unit tests cover pointer lifecycle and coordinate geometry using numeric fixtures, including invalid dimensions, NaN input, duplicate samples, wrong pointers, cancel, resampling, and reversible navigation state. Browser E2E should later verify pointer capture, touch-action, resize/DPR scaling, rendering and undo using controlled pointer events. Real stroke-order assessment needs a separately approved, licensed dataset and measured false-positive/false-negative rates. No DB schema changes are needed for the domain crate.

## Browser drawing workspace

- Added `/practice/hanzi-writing` as a separate, explicitly **unscored** preview accessible from Practice; the route does not require DuckDB. Character samples are temporary UI fixtures, **not** licensed reference stroke trajectories.
- `crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/hanzi_writing.rs` owns canvas drawing only. It uses `CanvasTransform` to map pointer client coordinates into normalized positions, and `InkCapture` for pointer ownership, duplicate suppression, completion, cancellation, undo, and clear. All completed and active strokes are redrawn from the same model.
- Rendering keeps the 2D backing resolution proportional to device pixel ratio (capped at 2048 pixels) and redraws on window resize, model changes, guide changes, or character selection. Pointer capture keeps a stroke connected when the pointer exits the drawing area. `touch-none` applies only to the writing surface.
- Known follow-ups: browser E2E for pointer capture, lost capture, DPI/resize, and touch; live dictionary vocabulary target selection; sourced stroke datasets, stroke-order feedback and independently validated assessment. Changing the target clears prior ink. No grades, scores, or session ledger writes are produced.

## Current guided handwriting display

The guided-writing route has a Yew reducer for the active character, in-progress ink, and sequential grading session. The `WritingBoard` owns the rendering surface, while a visual-only `DirectionGuide` previews 25% of the next canonical median using arc-length interpolation, growing to 35% and 50% after successive rejections of the same stroke. A static fading amber stroke replaces the former start dot, and a small start anchor remains. The reducer counts per-stroke rejections and resets the count after acceptance, Undo, Clear or character loading. This overlay is suspended during drawing and playback, does not modify matching thresholds, and does not animate. Browser acceptance and touch/stylus calibration remain pending.

## Recognition and prompt boundary

`matching.rs` validates endpoint placement, net direction and plausible length before calling `elastic.rs` for constrained dynamic-time-warp alignment and symmetric robust path coverage. The latter relaxes timing/vertex alignment, not stroke identity. `session.rs` checks candidate scores against later reference strokes to give stroke-order feedback; indistinguishable overlaps advance in supplied canonical order. The web reducer exposes `StrokeRejection::message()` without leaking matcher internals into views. No handwriting input leaves the browser.

`WriteHanziOptions` in `zipeek-web` owns three independently persisted boolean prompt flags. `practice_exercise_settings/writing.rs` configures them; `write_hanzi_exercise.rs` renders dictionary-sourced word title metadata and reuses `ListenButton` / `SpeechService` for user-initiated `zh-CN` playback. The `HanziWriting` canvas and stroke loading remain isolated from word metadata. The new strict options format intentionally has no old-format reader.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/architecture-modules-hanzi-writing.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.

# Knowledge scoring architecture (R612 WIP)

The R608 Knowledge Points product rules are consolidated in [Knowledge Points](../../learning-practice/pedagogy/knowledge-points.md). The pure Rust candidate is `zipeek_pedagogy::knowledge`. It is not connected to live Practice, AI, storage or Statistics.

| Module | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `model.rs` | Fixed categories, category-specific dimensions, scoring target state, reading sets and retained observations |
| `policy.rs` | Default seven-day/ten-success policy, bounded debt constants, configurable days/quota/eligibility |
| `engine.rs` | Chronological event transitions, context uniqueness, daily quota lock, balanced reading coverage, debt and relapse |
| `evidence.rs` | Manifest-aware evidence validation, cue/modality authorization and unscorable outcome filtering |
| `ledger.rs` | All-or-nothing in-memory validated-event batches and cross-target attempt replay protection |
| `projection.rs` | Integer-ratio score aggregation, category-specific 1-point entities and mixed-category normalization |
| `tests.rs` | Focused authored tests for core transitions and category scoring |

`AssessmentEvent` is an already-validated domain observation, **not** raw untrusted AI output. The engine cannot determine whether a translation demonstrates a character or whether generated context families are semantically distinct. The pure validator covers authorization and modality, while semantic context-equivalence certification and fixed catalogue membership remain upstream responsibilities.

`KnowledgeState.observations` retains accepted target observations and `seen_attempts` enforces target-scoped replay protection. These structures are in-memory only: a durable store and atomic write of the entire ledger remain to be integrated. One shared attempt may authorize different targets, but a target may only count the attempt once.

Polyphonic Hanzi requires `required_readings` to be supplied from the fixed curated catalogue before scoring Pronunciation; each successful event must identify its required reading. The quota must be covered by an evenly distributed subset (base `floor(quota/readings)` for each, remainder from distinct readings). Extra earlier successes for one reading cannot substitute for missing coverage.

R612 source review does not establish Cargo, WASM, Clippy, E2E or persistence acceptance. Run locked Rust tests and verification before promoting the candidate.

## R612 validated evidence and Comeback core

The pure `knowledge::evidence` module validates manifest-authorized targets, dimension compatibility, modality, independent demonstration, cue leakage, required reading keys and per-attempt target uniqueness before producing `AssessmentEvent` values. A manifest must be built from trusted exercise-generation metadata and the fixed catalogue; the standalone validator does not itself verify catalogue membership or certify semantic context equivalence.

`knowledge::ledger` applies whole validated batches against a cloned ledger and commits only if every target transition succeeds. It tracks completed attempt IDs across scoring targets; the owner must durably persist the entire ledger as one atomic write before making the updated state authoritative. This module itself is in-memory and does not claim IndexedDB transaction or cross-tab coordination.

`Transition::Comeback` occurs only when a disqualified target reaches 100 consecutive distinct eligible successes on the same day; the transition is the UI notification signal and the day may qualify on the same event. The streak is never user-visible. An active severe relapse prevents Comeback.
title: Knowledge scoring architecture (R612 WIP)

# Practice session persistence and lifecycle boundaries

**Current source boundaries:** `crates/zipeek-web/src/services/practice_session_store/`, `pages/practice/local_session/` and `pages/practice/generated_session/`. These modules do not yet constitute a verified end-to-end browser acceptance. This architecture concerns temporary Practice session state, **not** authoritative R608 pedagogical evidence.

## Local session ownership

`local_session/mod.rs` exports the route-keyed component; `page.rs` composes Yew state and effects; `restore.rs` recovers stored sessions; `generation.rs` reconciles generation attempts; `persistence.rs` writes retries, progress and completion; `history.rs` owns finalization; `exercise.rs` renders validated steps. Route-keyed mounting and stale-result checks prevent some old-session result publication; they do **not** cancel external generation requests. A persisted `PracticeSession` remains authoritative.

Generated Practice isolates translation in `generated_session/translation.rs`, image vocabulary in `image.rs`, and deterministic tile ordering in `order.rs`. Separate child lifecycle state does not provide transport-level cancellation.

## Persistence and concurrency

`practice_session_store/mod.rs` exposes the store contract. `codec.rs` validates persisted JSON, `inventory.rs` validates recoverable record membership and cleanup, and `persistence.rs` owns browser storage and revisions; other modules own model, transitions, generation and invariants.

The recoverable-session inventory snapshots and sorts storage keys, reads the named records and checks a second key snapshot. This detects **some** concurrent key-set changes. It is **not** atomic cross-tab compare-and-swap: a value can change while the key set remains the same, and load-then-save remains optimistic. Never claim write serializability or collision freedom.

A completed practice outcome may be finalized into optional personal history. Session-history recording and R608 assessed-knowledge evidence are distinct contracts; one cannot substitute for the other.

## Acceptance still required

Run locked native/WASM tests and Chrome E2E for rapid route navigation, stale generation, restart/restore, completion/history idempotency, quota errors, invalid saved records, two-tab writes and inventory changes. Failed storage commits must not silently discard the last recoverable record.

Historical R602-R606 source-review detail is preserved in [release engineering history](../../archive-history/audits/release-engineering-review-history.md).
title: Practice session persistence and lifecycle boundaries
