## R661 WIP: Persistent native inference workers

The `speech_workers` module now owns two independent thread-backed inference loops. Each holds an optional persistent Candle engine, accepts bounded requests through Tokio MPSC, and responds through oneshot channels. The HTTP-facing `Speech` coordinator retains the eSpeak subprocess fallback, WAV processing and the two capacity semaphores, but no longer owns mutable neural models or locks over inference. A queued or running request transfers its owned permit to the worker, preventing premature admission after an HTTP timeout. Dropped requests use cooperative cancellation; the worker does not promise preemptive interruption of a GPU kernel.

The neural model status machine distinguishes not installed, installed, loading, warming, ready and failed, using an atomic snapshot for nonblocking capabilities reads. TTS startup still runs actual `你好` synthesis; ASR startup loads weights without a waveform forward pass. The capabilities boolean is true only when a neural model is ready, or when the selected eSpeak fallback is usable in the absence of complete neural assets. Checkpoint presence remains separately queryable. Model failure invalidates the worker's cached engine and a later neural request can attempt reinitialization. Device names are validated at service construction. Backend error details are logged but not returned verbatim to HTTP clients.

This is authored, uncompiled R661 source, not Windows/CUDA acceptance. In particular, confirm backend failure recovery and shutdown with actual checkpoints before claiming production reliability. The earlier R660 sampling-path behavior was not intentionally modified.

## R637 Zipeek-owned Qwen3-TTS acoustic-code and waveform inference

R637 replaces the former placeholder with a native Candle source path for Mandarin CustomVoice/Vivian speech synthesis. The Qwen3-TTS talker now runs a bounded greedy acoustic-code generation loop; the five-layer predictor emits 15 residual codebooks per frame, and the waveform decoder reconstructs all 16 quantizers, runs the published eight-layer sliding-window codec Transformer and causal convolutional upsampling/vocoder network. Its synthesis endpoint is designed to return 24 kHz mono PCM16 WAV, with the existing Opus response negotiation unchanged. No external neural TTS crate, system eSpeak dependency or additional Rust dependency is required by this neural code path. Existing eSpeak fallback remains separately available when model assets are absent.

This is **unverified source**, not proven audio synthesis: Cargo/rustfmt and the local 1.8 GB Qwen3-TTS weights are not available in the authoring environment. `NEURAL_WAVEFORM_DECODER_READY` selects the implementation when local model assets exist, but asserts **architecture wiring**, not runtime readiness or quality. The ignored `neural_tts.rs` test must execute with downloaded model files and save a non-silent `target/speech-e2e/mandarin_qwen3_tts.wav` before claiming working TTS. The codec mapping and output must be checked numerically against the upstream tokenizer; an inference error must not be reported as success. Text input support remains limited to uninterrupted Mandarin Hanzi, not general-purpose segmentation or full Unicode tokenization. GPU memory, latency, caching and reference-speech accuracy are not accepted.

The previous R634 narrative below describes the historical, now-removed `talechime-qwen3-tts` integration. It is not the current implementation or dependency.

## R634 native Qwen3-TTS CustomVoice synthesis integration

When the complete local Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-CustomVoice directory is available under `models/speech`, `/v1/tts` now selects a native Rust/Candle inference backend: Qwen text tokenization, autoregressive talker, acoustic code predictor and neural audio-token decoder. It uses Mandarin (`Language::Chinese`) and preset speaker Vivian, converts the resulting finite non-silent 24 kHz mono waveform to PCM16 WAV, and keeps the existing Ogg Opus HTTP response negotiation. `ZIPEEK_QWEN_TTS_MODEL` accepts a checkpoint override; `ZIPEEK_TTS_DEVICE` accepts `cpu` (default) or `cuda` when the `qwen-tts-cuda` feature is built. Inference failures return explicit errors rather than silently falling back. eSpeak NG remains an optional fallback **only if** complete Qwen3-TTS assets are absent. Kokoro native inference remains a separate unfinished backend.

This integration introduces pinned `talechime-qwen3-tts =0.4.1` and a feature-gated CUDA path. Dependency approval and root lockfile resolution remain blocking before release acceptance, and Rust compilation, actual model output and spoken Mandarin quality have not been validated in the authoring environment. The `neural_tts.rs` ignored acceptance test must save a non-silent, 24 kHz waveform from real weights before the neural backend is considered working. Long-running blocking synthesis is held behind a single-job semaphore. In this checkpoint the large model is loaded for each request; caching, cancellation, memory limits and warm-up performance require subsequent runtime work.

## R630 pure-Rust audio codec integration

The native speech server now has an `audio_codec` module. It decodes MP3/FLAC with pinned Symphonia and Ogg Opus with pinned `opus-pure`, without linking native codec libraries. Decoded material is downmixed to mono, checked for finite samples and bounded to 30 seconds, then linearly resampled to the 16 kHz PCM required by Qwen3-ASR. RIFF PCM16 WAV remains the strict canonical regression and model-input format. Input `Content-Type` is required and explicitly allowlisted: `audio/wav`, `audio/x-wav`, `audio/mpeg`, `audio/flac`, `audio/x-flac`, `audio/ogg`, or `audio/opus`.

`POST /v1/tts` retains its PCM16 WAV default. Clients can request `Accept: audio/ogg` to obtain a mono 48 kHz Ogg Opus file generated using the pure-Rust `opus-pure` encoder with 24 kb/s voice settings, actual encoder pre-skip and end-trim. This is compression of the existing eSpeak output; it does not implement Kokoro or Qwen3-TTS. Unsupported explicit Accept values receive HTTP 406. There are no FFI codec bindings. For continuous work, the current linear resampler should be evaluated against a bandlimited resampler before high-fidelity audio requirements are considered accepted.

The new crates must be resolved into the existing workspace `Cargo.lock` on a machine with Cargo and crates.io access before `cargo --locked` can work. The authoring environment lacks Cargo and internet package resolution, so the source is a WIP checkpoint, not a compiled/locked release. Run `cargo check -p zipeek-tts-stt` once to update the root lockfile, then `cargo test --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt --test audio_codecs`, and the existing suite. Run the strict real speech tests independently. Existing WAV fixtures are unchanged; new small MP3/FLAC fixtures test decoding only, not lexical transcription correctness.

## R625 acoustic encoder implementation scope

R625 adds `candle_stt/encoder.rs`, with the published 0.6B audio tower's 18 noncausal Transformer layers, 14 attention heads (64 channels each), 3,584-channel GELU feed-forward path, pre-attention and pre-FFN LayerNorm, post-encoder LayerNorm and a two-stage 896-to-1,024 acoustic projector. The existing 100-Mel-frame convolution chunks feed independent eight-second attention windows; no attention crosses those window boundaries. The exact weight prefixes follow `thinker.audio_tower` and the upstream encoder layers. A checkpoint-backed ignored Rust test provides an explicit opt-in path to exercise the complete encoder on CPU. The normal library/test startup does not load weights or enable STT.

The user supplied an R624 Windows log with 44 passing Rust unit tests. This establishes R624 compile/test success, not R625 or actual weight execution. Numerical parity, tokenizer, Qwen3 text decoder and Mandarin transcription remain pending. Qwen3-TTS asset validation now requires the codec's checkpoint, configuration and preprocessing metadata, but actual TTS remains eSpeak NG; Kokoro's PyTorch format remains a separate conversion/loader requirement. No model downloads or dependencies were added.

## R619 approved Candle-native speech architecture

Candle (`candle-core`, `candle-nn`, `candle-transformers`, `candle-kernels`, pinned to 0.11.1) remains the neural execution stack. `whisper-rs` and whisper.cpp are not permitted. The primary Mandarin STT research target is **Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B** (audio encoder plus language-model decoder); SenseVoiceSmall is an evaluation candidate, not a second production backend. The practical first Mandarin TTS target is **hexgrad/Kokoro-82M-v1.1-zh**; **Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-CustomVoice** is a later neural codec-based TTS research target. Each model requires a distinct architecture and correct text/audio preprocessing. R620 updates the audio frontend to Qwen3-ASR's published 128-band, 16 kHz, 400-point FFT and 160-sample hop contract; coefficient parity, padding/masking semantics and encoder integration are still unverified.

`src/runtime/device.rs` supplies a CPU/CUDA Candle initialization and small tensor-operation check. `src/runtime/models.rs` identifies chosen published model repositories and verifies Qwen TTS assets. `src/candle_stt/assets.rs` validates the Qwen3-ASR distribution layout; `src/candle_tts/assets.rs` validates the **actual upstream Kokoro distribution** (`kokoro-v1_1-zh.pth`, `config.json`, `voices/zf_007.pt`). The published Kokoro `.pth` and `.pt` files are PyTorch serialized assets, **not** ready-to-load Candle safetensors. Conversion or a native compatible loader, verified against trusted weight names/shapes and reference outputs, is a separate milestone. Never load untrusted pickle files in the application or assume an arbitrary file rename converts their format.

R621 replaces fixed-length input with a 128-band F32 tensor padded to 100-Mel-frame multiples (up to `[1, 128, 3000]`); `candle_stt/weights.rs` probes the Qwen3-ASR safetensors checkpoint using memory-mapped Candle `VarBuilder`. R622 adds a three-Conv2D projection stem. R624 runs convolution over each complete zero-padded 100-frame chunk and adds non-interleaved sinusoidal positions resetting at each chunk before trimming invalid output tokens. Neither checkpoint tensor-shape verification nor numerical parity with upstream is complete; there is still no end-to-end encoder/decoder. `candle_tts/waveform.rs` prepares finite bounded neural PCM samples as RIFF PCM16 WAV, but it is not neural waveform generation. These new primitives do not change the exposed endpoint readiness flags. Only load model assets from trusted local sources.

The model registry is preflight/architecture groundwork only. No complete Qwen3-ASR encoder/decoder, Qwen3-TTS audio-token decoder, Mandarin Kokoro synthesis, pronunciation scoring or automatic model downloading is implemented. `/v1/stt` remains unavailable and `/v1/tts` still uses eSpeak NG. Do not use successful asset checks or a Candle tensor allocation as evidence of usable speech inference.

### Model downloads (external to source archives)

Recommended local directories beneath the native executable's `resources/` tree:

- `qwen3-asr-0.6b/`: snapshot of `https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B` including `model.safetensors`, `config.json`, `generation_config.json`, `preprocessor_config.json`, `vocab.json`, `merges.txt` and tokenizer metadata. This is the primary STT checkpoint.
- `kokoro-zh/`: snapshot of `https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M-v1.1-zh` including `kokoro-v1_1-zh.pth`, `config.json`, and the `voices/` directory, at least `zf_007.pt`. This is the first TTS target. The upstream checkpoint format needs a safe conversion/load strategy before any Candle inference.
- `qwen3-tts-0.6b/`: optional later snapshot of `https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-CustomVoice` including the entire `speech_tokenizer/` subdirectory and root safetensors/config/tokenizer files. It is **not** required for the current milestone.

Snapshot whole repositories using `hf download <repository> --local-dir <directory>` from the installed Hugging Face CLI, rather than choosing a single weights file. Model directories are local runtime assets; do not put several gigabytes of weights in the project source ZIP. Review each repository's licence and download a pinned revision for reproducible development.

`ZIPEEK_CANDLE_STT_MODEL` defaults to the Qwen model path under the native executable's `resources/`. `ZIPEEK_CANDLE_TTS_MODEL` selects the Chinese Kokoro checkpoint; its current default is a project-relative path. `ZIPEEK_CANDLE_DEVICE=cpu|cuda` is recognized by the new explicit runtime device API, but no model request yet invokes it. GPU errors should be reported, never silently treated as successful CUDA execution.

### Implementation stages

1. Validate local snapshots and choose/initialize a Candle device without loading untrusted Python-pickle assets.
2. Port Qwen3-ASR-specific audio frontend, feature shapes, weight naming, encoder, tokenization and incremental decoder with reference parity tests on Mandarin samples. Keep speech transcription separate from tone/pronunciation assessment.
3. Build the Kokoro Chinese phonemizer (word segmentation, polyphonic readings, tone sandhi), establish a verified checkpoint-conversion workflow, port neural model/voice/vocoder and synthesize PCM WAV with reference parity tests.
4. Investigate Qwen3-TTS neural speech-token generation and `speech_tokenizer` codec as an alternative later backend. Benchmark latency and peak VRAM on the user's 16 GB GPU before selecting a production configuration.
5. Enable native endpoints only after locked Rust compilation, actual model inference, Mandarin audio correctness, resource and security checks and native loopback acceptance.

## R615 Candle transition status

`whisper-rs` was explicitly rejected. The current source no longer imports Whisper.rs or expects a GGML Whisper.cpp checkpoint. `ZIPEEK_CANDLE_STT_MODEL` selects the Qwen3-ASR safetensors checkpoint under `resources/qwen3-asr-0.6b/`; asset validation and the explicit mapping probe do not establish inference readiness. There is no Candle inference pipeline yet, so `/v1/stt` returns a transparent service-unavailable error even when a checkpoint file is present. WAV input validation remains enabled. Do not advertise a speech-recognition capability until the Candle frontend, encoder/decoder, tokenizer and inference have been implemented and evaluated.

TTS still runs through the pre-existing eSpeak NG native adapter as a temporary development path; Candle Mandarin TTS has not yet replaced it. The four Candle 0.11.1/CUDA dependencies already existed in the manifest. No new crates or model binaries were added. The speech model architecture, checkpoints, Mandarin text processing, licensing, CUDA build support and real inference acceptance remain open implementation tasks.

## R618 native Candle research checkpoint

The native speech crate now contains a standalone Whisper-compatible *candidate* audio frontend at `src/candle_stt/frontend.rs`, with bounded 16 kHz mono PCM input, a 400-point radix-2/5 Fourier transform, periodic Hann window, 160-sample hop, Slaney-style triangular Mel filters, 80-by-3000 output and log-energy normalization. `speech::prepare_stt_features` connects strict WAV decoding to this frontend for model integration. The implementation includes deterministic numerical and input-validation tests, but has **not** been compared to a reference Whisper feature extractor on real Mandarin audio. Such comparison is required before it can be treated as numerically compatible with the selected model. This is not transcription or a pronunciation assessor.

`src/candle_tts/` adds two separate prerequisites for a future Chinese Kokoro implementation: bounded Mandarin punctuation-aware segmentation, and a local safetensors model/voice/vocabulary asset contract. These are experimental interfaces, **not** evidence that a published Kokoro Chinese checkpoint has exactly those files or that it is loadable by the current code. Real model loading, checkpoint conversion where necessary, text-to-phoneme mapping, tone sandhi, voice selection, prosody/acoustic inference and waveform synthesis remain unimplemented. The live `/v1/tts` service continues to use eSpeak NG.

The `ZIPEEK_CANDLE_TTS_MODEL` environment variable can select the experimental checkpoint path for asset diagnostics. Neither model weights nor voices are bundled, and no downloads occur at runtime. The current CUDA-only Candle dependency selection is unchanged.

Native verification remains required: `cargo check --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt`, `cargo test --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt`, comparison of log-Mel coefficients against a reference Whisper implementation, and native Mandarin speech/model tests. Do not advertise `/v1/stt` as available based on asset checks or successful frontend numerical tests alone.

# Local Mandarin speech service

`zipeek-tts-stt` is a native, loopback-only speech process. It does not expose a public network listener, ship eSpeak/Whisper binaries or models, or automatically enable a browser provider. The approved D56 browser/local provider selection and microphone UX remain separate integration work.

## Runtime

Start with `cargo run --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt`. The listener binds to `127.0.0.1:8799`; `ZIPEEK_SPEECH_PORT` may select another nonzero TCP port. Network-facing bind addresses are intentionally not configurable.

Resource paths can be selected with `ZIPEEK_ESPEAK_BIN`, `ZIPEEK_ESPEAK_DATA`, and `ZIPEEK_CANDLE_STT_MODEL`. Otherwise resources are located beside the executable under `resources/`. The `espeak-ng-data` directory must reside under the configured data root. Candle STT inference is not yet implemented. The service must not silently install/download third-party models. Verify their licenses separately.

Native HTTP endpoints:

| Endpoint | Method | Request | Response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/health` | GET | None | `ok` |
| `/v1/capabilities` | GET | None | Plain-text availability flags and `zh-CN` |
| `/v1/tts` | POST | `text/plain; charset=utf-8`, max 4 KiB | `audio/wav` |
| `/v1/stt` | POST | `audio/wav`, mono 16 kHz PCM16, max 30 s | UTF-8 transcript |

The speech engine uses eSpeak NG Mandarin (`cmn`) for TTS; STT is currently unavailable. Requests do not award pronunciation mastery. Each engine admits one job at a time and returns HTTP 429 while busy. Missing resources return HTTP 503. Malformed input returns HTTP 400. Engine errors return HTTP 500. WAV is parsed and strictly bounded before model loading. Text and audio are neither logged nor persisted.

Native speech POST requests require a `Host` header naming `localhost` or `127.0.0.1` (with an optional nonzero port) and do not permit requests carrying a browser Origin header. It is **not** an approved web-audio endpoint or a remote transport. A future trusted desktop bridge must perform microphone permission handling, provider selection, interruption handling, and source-origin enforcement before exposing the capability to frontend consumers. Never connect it directly to a hosted browser page without an approved security design.

## Verification

Run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt`, and `cargo test --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt`. Runtime acceptance additionally requires licensed local eSpeak NG assets, a Candle model implementation and checkpoint, a Mandarin audio fixture, and an explicit reviewer check that the service binds only to loopback. Tests and runtime acceptance were not run in the archive-authoring environment.

## R534 native protocol hardening

The POST endpoints reject non-loopback `Host` headers, malformed or missing hosts, and any browser `Origin` header before engine invocation. This is a defense against cross-site browser access and misleading Host routing, not a substitute for desktop-bridge authentication. Do not weaken these checks to make hosted Pages clients call the native service.

Synthesis now fails promptly when a child process emits output beyond the configured bound. The process is terminated and reaped on any failed or timed-out synthesis operation rather than waiting for a blocked stdout pipe. Tests cover malformed audio framing and HTTP handler error statuses without requiring external speech models.

## R536 trusted local development bridge

The browser bridge is intentionally restricted to the local Zipeek development origin
`http://localhost:1420`, `http://localhost.:1420` or `http://127.0.0.1:1420`. The process still binds to loopback only.
Remote hosting, other local ports and cross-origin web pages are rejected. An exact-origin
CORS preflight allows only POST and the Content-Type header for `/v1/tts` and `/v1/stt`.
The browser never receives credentials; local-provider selection is an explicit, in-memory
choice in Settings and resets on page reload. Browser speech remains the default.

The bridge transmits text to local eSpeak and samples from a five-second microphone
capture as mono 16 kHz PCM16 WAV to local Whisper. Audio is not persisted. Recording
is initiated explicitly, and tracks are stopped after capture, cancellation or errors.
The backend validates WAV. Hosted `/zipeek/` cannot use this bridge. This remains a
**development-only** connection, not a general desktop security boundary.

Run `cargo run --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt`, open `http://localhost:1420`,
choose Local Mandarin speech in Settings, and confirm capabilities before tests.
This integration requires Windows/browser acceptance and review of browser private
network access behavior, microphone capture, cancellation, and audio playback.

Existing practice recordings may be explicitly transcribed with **Transcribe locally**
when the user has opted in to the local speech provider. This decodes the
browser's in-memory blob, mixes up to two channels, resamples to mono 16 kHz
PCM16 and sends only to the loopback service. A transcript does not award
pronunciation mastery. Existing recording/playback controls remain unchanged.

## R538 local browser speech Rust/WASM migration

The browser-side speech bridge is now implemented in `zipeek-browser/src/local_speech/` using `wasm-bindgen`, `js-sys` and browser APIs, with standalone PCM16 WAV encoding and native unit tests in `zipeek-browser/src/speech_wav.rs`. `zipeek-web` Settings, the shared speech service and Speaking Recorder call this Rust API directly instead of the old JavaScript module. Browser speech remains the default, and local service use requires explicit in-memory opt-in from only `http://localhost:1420`, `http://localhost.:1420`, or `http://127.0.0.1:1420`. `zipeek-web` passes the origin from `AppEnvironment.window` during application setup; `zipeek-browser` caches only the trusted/untrusted decision, not an independently retrieved global Window.

The new browser capture path uses MediaRecorder followed by AudioContext decoding and Rust channel mixing/resampling. Object URLs, microphone tracks and abort controllers are owned by the Rust state. Hosted origins remain blocked; no credentials, recorded audio or transcript history are persisted. This remains development-only, and needs Chrome/Firefox microphone permission, cancellation and engine integration acceptance before release.

## R594 native client API boundary

`zipeek-tts-stt-client` is a separate dependency-free native library for the existing loopback HTTP protocol. It exposes `SpeechClient` (`health`, `capabilities`, `synthesize`, `transcribe`), typed capability and error values, a configurable nonzero port, and a bounded timeout. The transport connects only to `127.0.0.1`; it does not accept remote addresses, credentials, arbitrary URLs, or a browser Origin. HTTP response framing and content lengths are bounded, and protocol responses are checked before passing data to callers. This is a **blocking native client**; callers must not run it on a browser UI thread or within asynchronous executor tasks without an appropriate blocking boundary.

The existing `zipeek-browser/src/local_speech/` WASM microphone and browser HTTP bridge remains the browser implementation. It is not replaced by the native client, which deliberately depends on no `reqwest`, `tokio`, `web-sys`, `whisper-rs` or other external crate. The server does not require a third-party dependency change or a new network listener. The new crate has local protocol and loopback mock tests, but the actual Windows server, eSpeak engine, Whisper model and browser integrations still require runtime acceptance. No speech recording or transcript is persisted by the native client.

Build checks: `cargo test --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt-client -p zipeek-tts-stt`, `cargo check --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt-client`, and the existing speech server/Chrome acceptance matrix. These commands were not executable in the R594 authoring environment.

## R595 native client protocol verification boundary

The native `zipeek-tts-stt-client` now checks successful HTTP `Content-Type` against the endpoint contract, rejects duplicate or absent success media-type headers, and strips control characters from bounded service-error text. The client checks full WAV RIFF size, PCM16 format, mono channel count, rate and byte alignment rather than trusting magic bytes; STT uploads are restricted to mono 16 kHz and at most 30 seconds. Framing arithmetic for chunked responses is checked for overflow. Server-side validation remains authoritative. This is protocol validation of bytes returned by a loopback process, not proof of model quality or audio permissions.

Run `cargo test --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt-client -p zipeek-tts-stt` and use a real native service for GET and POST acceptance. The existing browser bridge remains a separate permission-controlled integration, and neither native model assets nor Chrome microphone tests are supplied by this checkpoint.


## Native speech client validation boundary

The native loopback speech client validates endpoint-specific HTTP Content-Type, WAV RIFF framing, PCM16 mono parameters, sample alignment, nonempty data and bounded error text. STT additionally requires 16 kHz input and no more than 30 seconds of samples. Chunked-length arithmetic is checked. This is a blocking, native `127.0.0.1` client and does not govern browser microphone permissions or make external model/runtime availability claims. Locked native tests and end-to-end audio validation remain required.

## R617 native Whisper/Candle model preflight

The local service now requires a nonempty `model.safetensors` checkpoint, `config.json`, and `tokenizer.json` alongside the checkpoint before its model-assets diagnostic reports a complete bundle. This preflight does not parse or instantiate the model, validate model/tokenizer compatibility, generate log-Mel audio features, or enable transcription. `recognition_available` remains false and the STT endpoint returns unavailable. Native Candle inference, a tested Windows CUDA toolchain and a properly verified checkpoint bundle are pending. The current eSpeak TTS path is unchanged.


## R621 Qwen3-ASR variable-length acoustic input

The STT acoustic frontend has been corrected from R620's fixed `[1, 128, 3000]` tensor to a variable-length Candle tensor `[1, 128, padded_frames]` and an accompanying `[1, padded_frames]` U32 attention mask. Audio shorter than 8,000 samples receives zero sample padding before features are extracted. The Mel time axis is right-padded to a multiple of 100 frames, without replacing the observed sample duration with an artificial 30-second input. Only valid frames participate in spectral normalization; post-feature padding is zero.

The encoder layout maps each 100-frame Mel chunk to 13 output tokens, and partitions tokens into attention windows of no more than eight chunks. `candle_stt/layout.rs` contains a deterministic, separately testable window plan. Neither the convolutional encoder nor neural decoding is integrated. These boundaries must be checked against Hugging Face reference tensor values and attention masks before implementing acoustic layers. See https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/model_doc/qwen3_asr and https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/qwen3_asr/feature_extraction_qwen3_asr.py.


## R622 WIP Qwen3-ASR convolutional stem

`candle_stt/stem.rs` introduces a checkpoint-backed Candle Conv2D stem for the 0.6B model: three 3x3 convolutions with stride 2, padding 1 and GELU, followed by a bias-free 7680-to-896 linear projection. The loader uses the published `thinker.audio_tower.conv2d1`, `conv2d2`, `conv2d3` and `conv_out` weight namespaces. A chunk is processed separately for every 100 valid Mel frames, with a short final chunk cropped to its actual valid frame count before convolution. The returned embeddings have shape `[token_count, 896]`; a short 50-frame chunk yields 7 tokens, not 13. The window planner now accepts **valid frames** rather than padded frames, so final attention-window lengths agree with the convolution's output. The right-padded Mel features and input mask remain available to the rest of the pipeline.

This is not yet a usable Qwen3-ASR audio encoder: the sinusoidal per-chunk positional embedding, 18 Transformer encoder blocks, final projections, decoder and tokenizer are not implemented. The new stem has not been tested with a real safetensors checkpoint or compiled on the required toolchain. This WIP does not enable the STT endpoint. Reference: https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-ASR/blob/main/qwen_asr/core/transformers_backend/modeling_qwen3_asr.py.

## Local speech model discovery (R631 WIP)

The native speech server uses `models/speech` under the working directory, or searches ancestor directories of the executable to find an existing `models/speech` directory. This supports a source checkout started from `C:\repos\zipeek` and a binary under `target/debug/deps`. The packaged eSpeak executable and voice-data defaults remain executable-adjacent `resources`, independent of neural checkpoint discovery.

Default checkpoint paths are `models/speech/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B/model.safetensors` for recognition and `models/speech/Kokoro-82M-v1.1-zh/kokoro-v1_1-zh.pth` for planned neural synthesis. `ZIPEEK_CANDLE_STT_MODEL` and `ZIPEEK_CANDLE_TTS_MODEL` explicitly override those defaults. An existing model directory alone does not demonstrate inference readiness; model asset validation and real checkpoint execution remain separate gates.

# Browser vendor asset lifecycle

## Ownership and boundaries

The browser application consumes, but does not generate, local third-party runtime
assets. `zipeek-cli web` prepares these files explicitly. npm remains the only
installer for packages described by `crates/zipeek-web/package-lock.json`.
Trunk copies the prepared `vendor/` directory into the site; its watch/rebuild
pipeline must not install dependencies or regenerate vendor assets.

## Commands (repository root)

| Task | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo make setup` | Locked npm install followed by preparation and verification |
| `cargo make web-install` | Run `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund` explicitly |
| `cargo make prepare-assets` | Prepare DuckDB/Arrow and Chart.js summary assets if stale |
| `cargo make prepare-duckdb` | Prepare only the pinned DuckDB-WASM/Arrow bundle |
| `cargo make prepare-summary` | Prepare only the pinned esbuild/Chart.js bundle |
| `cargo make verify-assets` | Read-only version, input hash, output hash and file checks |
| `cargo make serve` | Verify once, then run `trunk serve`; no preparation hook |

The `zipeek-cli` implementation is split across `web/inputs.rs` (locked module
inputs), `web/fingerprint.rs` (hashes and verification), `web/prepare.rs`
(staged preparation and publication), and `web/install.rs` (explicit npm install).
The parent `web.rs` remains the CLI-facing API for these operations.

The `zipeek-cli` commands are also available as `cargo run -p zipeek-cli
--locked -- web <install|prepare|verify|prepare-duckdb|prepare-summary>`.

## Reproducibility and failure handling

Preparation checks installed npm package versions against the currently pinned
manifest values. For DuckDB, Rust copies the Base WASM and worker, rewrites all bare
Apache Arrow module imports (the pinned DuckDB build may contain more than one), and copies the approved local Arrow adapter and
license/notice files. For the summary bundle, Rust invokes the pinned esbuild
script only during explicit preparation. No npm install is triggered during
preparation or verification.

Each vendor directory contains a generated `.zipeek-prepared.json` stamp with a
preparation format version, source SHA-256 hashes and generated file hashes.
The stamp is created only after the staged output has been published. A matching
stamp allows a repeated prepare request to skip copying; verification never
updates the stamp. The prepared vendor directories and stamps are generated
output and must not be shipped as source archive inputs.

Generated files are prepared in temporary sibling directories; a failed build
leaves the previous published asset directory intact. Once preparation has
succeeded, the prepared directory replaces the old one. CI and Pages deployment
must explicitly prepare after `npm ci` and before invoking Trunk.

If verification fails after unpacking, run `cargo make setup` from the root.
For a stale input with existing `node_modules`, run `cargo make prepare-assets`.
Do not use `cargo clean` to resolve missing JavaScript assets. Browser runtime
loading, worker lifetime, and dictionary database integrity remain owned by the
WASM database integration, not the vendor build step.

## DuckDB Arrow import regression

The installed `@duckdb/duckdb-wasm@1.33.1-dev114.0` may expose two `from`
references to `apache-arrow`. Asset preparation must rewrite **every** matching
import specifier to `./arrow.mjs` rather than requiring exactly one occurrence.
Zero matching references remain a hard error because that suggests upstream
module output changed incompatibly. This is a vendor preparation check, not a
request to remove imports or reinstall packages.

## Practice progress creatures

The six source WebP illustrations live in `crates/zipeek-web/static/practice/` and have stable creature names: `dragon.webp`, `qilin.webp`, `phoenix.webp`, `white-tiger.webp`, `crane.webp`, and `deer.webp`. They are preserved by the CLI source archive unpacker alongside the authored Courses and brand assets. Trunk copies `static/` into the deployed site. The shared Practice progress component renders the corresponding `/practice/<creature>.webp` URL in root development or `/zipeek/practice/<creature>.webp` on GitHub Pages. Image bytes are never embedded in WASM and no Blob URLs are created.

The existing Animato tween changes the bottom-up reveal; image decoding and asset responses are checked in the focused Chrome scenarios. Unpacker tests verify these authored assets are installed instead of skipped.

## R538 retained Chart.js through a typed Rust boundary

D35 and the pinned Chart.js/esbuild build-only packaging remain in force. `scripts/summary.mjs` now exports only a minimal Chart constructor after importing/registering Chart, DoughnutController and ArcElement. `zipeek-browser::charts` resolves the prepared local module. The Rust `src/services/charts.rs` owns summary/course ring datasets, options and an opaque ChartInstance with idempotent destruction.

The previous `course_charts.js` and `summary.js` wrappers had no active Rust callers and are removed. No live Yew components mount the new chart handle yet. D35 numeric counters, reduced-motion transitions and async unmount lifecycle require an integrated frontend implementation and browser review before being called complete.

## Chart.js WASM interop (R540 WIP)

The pinned Chart.js bundle remains built from `crates/zipeek-web/scripts/summary.mjs` using the existing explicit preparation pipeline. `zipeek-browser::charts` resolves `vendor/summary/summary.mjs` against the document base URI and uses a narrow `wasm-bindgen(inline_js)` dynamic import before constructing Chart.js through its exported factory. A Rust `ChartInstance` newtype owns `destroy` and cleanup. `zipeek-web::services::charts` owns summary/course-specific datasets and presentation options. The old `chart_bridge.js` shim has been removed. Browser acceptance for both `/` and `/zipeek/` remains pending.

## R541 application browser interop

AI configuration, Hanzi clipboard behavior and Recognize Hanzi canvas state are now owned by `zipeek-browser`. The recognition workspace uses typed Rust event handlers, a small `wasm-bindgen(inline_js)` theme observer adapter, and existing Yew DOM events for workspace status. The old `recognition_workspace.js`, AI config shim and unused clipboard shim are removed. The Chart.js vendor entrypoint, esbuild bundle generation, and Node asset tooling remain build-only resources under D35.

The Rust/WASM and browser acceptance gates for these changes are pending.

## Full local installation

`cargo make install` is the explicit all-assets setup entrypoint. It runs `setup-all`, regenerates/compresses/installs the dictionary using its verified native pipeline, fetches/audits/builds the pinned local AreaCity Province Quest geography, prepares the pedagogy Worker, and executes `preflight-deploy` after those dependencies complete. `cargo make geo-install` provides the geography-only sequence. `cargo make serve` remains the fast read-only vendor verification and Trunk startup path.

AreaCity boundary redistribution rights are unresolved. Geography generated by this installation is for local testing only until legal provenance and licensing acceptance is separately recorded. The asset-integrity audit does not certify legal redistribution. Network access and 7z/7zz are required on a cold geography setup; cached validated source data can be reused.

## Tauri frontend assets

`cargo run --locked -p zipeek-cli -- desktop-frontend --prepare-only` verifies the shared Chart.js/background assets and generates `crates/zipeek-web/index.desktop.html` from the maintained browser HTML. It removes dictionary and manifest preload links and substitutes filtered `.desktop-assets/static` and `.desktop-assets/vendor` copy inputs. Shared Docs, styles, illustrations, notices, attribution, Hanzi assets and the pedagogy worker remain available. Desktop vendor staging includes Chart.js, excluding DuckDB-WASM and Arrow. The native DuckDB license is copied independently from the maintained `scripts/duckdb-LICENSE.txt` to `notices/DUCKDB-LICENSE.txt`. The generated HTML, staging and `dist-desktop` are ignored by Git and excluded from source snapshots.

`desktop-frontend` builds to `dist-desktop` at base `/`, `--release` produces release frontend assets, and `--serve` uses localhost:1421. The production output is checked for browser database artifacts. Restart the desktop frontend command after changing staged static/vendor inputs or browser HTML so those staged inputs are refreshed; Rust/CSS development continues through Trunk. The browser `index.html`, `dist` and `/zipeek/` build remain separate. Dictionary generation and vendor preparation remain explicit, never implicit build operations.

Native dictionary bytes are staged separately under the Tauri `binaries/dictionary` resource path by `desktop-sidecars`, using the verified installed manifest. They are not copied into the desktop frontend. No DuckDB dependency or data migration is introduced.
title: Browser vendor asset lifecycle

# Web shell and startup boundaries

This page describes the checked-in Rust/Yew implementation. Approved changes that have not been implemented are kept in [interface and platform policy](../../product-ux/foundation/interface-and-platform-policy.md), [visual review](../../product-ux/references/ui-screenshot-review.md) and [tasks](../../project-management/tasks.md).

## Bootstrap and theme

`crates/zipeek-web/index.html` provides the static loading shell before WASM mounts. [`src/setup.rs`](../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/setup.rs) applies the stored theme and appearance preferences before rendering [`src/app.rs`](../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/app.rs). A static bootstrap failure must be distinguished from a dictionary initialization failure after Yew starts.

## Database ownership

[`DatabaseProvider`](../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/components/providers/database_provider.rs) owns database state and retry commands. [`DatabaseBoundary`](../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/components/providers/database_boundary.rs) renders loading, ready, and failure states; the failure state includes a retry action. [`route.rs`](../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/route.rs) applies this boundary to database-dependent routes only. Docs, Settings, Stats, courses and several game routes are explicitly exempt, so the approved policy of blocking **the entire application** on essential dictionary failure is **not yet implemented**. A browser test is required before claiming startup recovery is complete.

## Navigation and practice shell

[`AppShell`](../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/components/shell/app_shell/mod.rs) owns the shared header, sidebar, footer, session reminder and route-specific layouts. Active local Practice sessions use a dedicated immersive shell; course lessons also use a dedicated layout. The general shell still computes and passes a centered route title to its header. Removing it to make space for the approved long dragon progress indicator is future work, not current source behavior.

## Other-tab detection

[`OtherTabIndicator`](../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/components/shell/app_shell/other_tab/mod.rs) uses a [`BroadcastChannel` coordinator](../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/components/shell/app_shell/other_tab/coordinator.rs) with periodic peer heartbeats. Its current UI is a bottom-right informational warning when peers exist. The coordinator observes presence, not ordered exclusive ownership, and the source does not implement the approved first-tab-wins full-screen blocking protocol. Do not claim multi-tab write exclusivity or crash takeover safety based on this warning.

## Deployment and verification

The hash router runs at local root and the hosted `/zipeek/` prefix. Static source checks establish file wiring, not successful boot, database loading, browser storage persistence or layout. Verify relevant startup and navigation journeys at both base paths with an actual build and browser test.

## Source provenance

Older descriptions are preserved in [historical architecture audits](../../archive-history/audits/SOURCE_RECONCILIATION.md) and release history. They do not establish current runtime acceptance.
title: Web shell and startup boundaries

# AI prompts and inference boundaries

The former `crates/zipeek-ai/` prompt owner has been extracted to `crates/zipeek-ai-protocol/`. Prompt generation, structured sentence analysis, classification and exercise-output validation remain domain contracts, not HTTP or model-runtime implementation. `zipeek-web` and `zipeek-db-gen` depend on this protocol crate.

`zipeek-ai-client` owns OpenAI-compatible HTTP transport for native and browser clients. It currently works with a configured provider endpoint, including LM Studio. `zipeek-ai-core` now defines transport-neutral chat messages, a generation request with bounded validated options, generation events, shared cancellation, errors, and an asynchronous `GenerationBackend` streaming callback contract. The core interface does not yet replace the client's established public wire types.

`zipeek-ai-server` is a separate native crate. Its copied `llama_cpp` source references a missing `model_runtime` module; that copied code is intentionally not exposed by the crate entry points and cannot yet be considered an operational inference server. Connecting and testing the backend requires implementing runtime ownership, cancellation, model loading and OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoints, without weakening deterministic test fixtures.

The deterministic E2E AI fixture remains in `zipeek-e2e/src/harness/ai_fixture.rs`. It is independent of both LM Studio and the unfinished native AI server and must remain the default for reproducible E2E assertions.
title: AI prompts and inference boundaries

# zipeek-core module

Shared domain types and pure logic: Word/WordId, HSK and PoS enums, comparison-only
pinyin normalization, practice URL state, and the deterministic round builder.
Part of the [architecture overview](../architecture.md). Approved shared-crate
decision in [D01](../../project-management/decisions/foundations.md#d01-shared-crate).

## Constraints

`zipeek-core` must compile on both `wasm32-unknown-unknown` and native targets,
and must not import `web_sys`, `js_sys`, or `wasm_bindgen`. It holds types and
pure logic only; queries take data as arguments, never a database handle. Public
API is versioned by the repository, not semver; breaking changes are acceptable
during development (D10). The only dependency is approved `rand` 0.10.3 with
`chacha` (D17).

## Shared domain modules (A02)

`hsk.rs` holds distinct `Hsk2Level` and `Hsk3Level` enums, `HskSystem` and a
tagged `HskLevel`. Checked integer conversions reject invalid levels; `SevenToNine`
stores 7. `HskSystem::label()` and `levels()` are the canonical standard names and supported typed level catalogs; `HskLevel::label()` and `badge_label()` preserve the combined HSK 3.0 7-9 display. `HskLevel::try_from((system, number))` validates source selections without accepting out-of-system levels. Browse, Practice and translation must not copy the supported-level arrays. `word.rs` holds the ten-field `Word` representation and `WordId`, checked
against positive SQL INTEGER row-number bounds. Optional metadata stays optional;
empty PoS vectors represent SQL NULL. `Word` is a transport record; the A03 importer
enforces nonblank labels, at least one membership, grouping and conflict policies
before insertion.

`part_of_speech.rs` exposes strict canonical-token parsing separately from
case-insensitive source-code mapping. `from_source_codes` rejects the entire list
on an unknown code, deduplicates recognized values and sorts by canonical token.
The A03 importer catches the error and logs/drops the entire source entry before
grouping or IDs. A08 implements tolerant URL filtering in `practice/query.rs`. No
serde or database library was added to the shared crate.

Six unit tests include the 42-row mapping fixture; native schema fixtures test
exact columns, constraints and both indexes (schema test lives in db-gen, not
here).

## Comparison and fallback boundary (A04)

`normalize_for_comparison` is dependency-free logic in the shared crate, reused
by A07 label comparison. It lowercases, maps umlaut/`u:` to `v`, converts tone
marks to trailing numbers, and removes a neutral 5 only from a vowel-containing
syllable. Numeric digit boundaries are processed before removing separators,
preserving `r5`/`ng5`. Spaces and apostrophe/hyphen syllable separators do not
enter the key. Common decomposed tone/umlaut marks are supported. Marked
concatenated syllables use a fixed syllable vocabulary and longest complete
segmentation; unknown marked chunks retain their mapped letters/marks rather than
guessing a valid syllable. Stored transcriptions and exact primary grouping keys
never use this function.

`CedictIndex` validates UTF-8 and dictionary line structure and keeps source order
within simplified/normalized-reading keys. `apply_cedict_fallback` parses the
index only when any row lacks primary English, ignores `variant of` entries, and
uses the first matching entry with usable glosses. It shares gloss serialization
with the primary importer and returns filled/unresolved/skipped-variant counts.
Unknown matches remain NULL with warnings; IDs, memberships and transcriptions
stay fixed. Fallback diagnostics identify WordIds and include CC-CEDICT line
numbers where available. `ImportDiagnostic.entry` is the source entry number for
primary events and WordId for fallback events (including fallback pipe
replacements); the detail and diagnostic kind identify the context. Primary
`MissingEnglish` events describe the earlier primary-selection stage, not the
final post-fallback outcome.

## Practice URL boundary (A08)

The dependency-free practice module separates:

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `types.rs` | Six approved variants, filters and modes |
| `query.rs` | Decoded pairs and diagnostics |
| `normalize.rs` | Word lookup, authoritative exclusions and seed disposition |
| `canonical.rs` | v1 formatting and FNV-1a |
| `state.rs` | Offset, exclusion union and Fixed progress |

Canonical `query_pairs` returns decoded values for the router to serialize once.
Loading a URL has no saved-exclusion input and does not rewrite browser history.

`web/services/practice_url.rs` uses the existing router decoder; Practice logs
diagnostics only in debug builds. A21 supplies dictionary-backed ID lookup
and calls normalization before loading ordered candidate views. `RecoveryRequired` is an A07 builder input,
not an RNG operation: original URL seed/filter stay canonical and the builder
owns the single recovery/generation stream.

Normalization accepts a pure `Word` lookup, supplied by A21 from validated
browser dictionary rows. `RecoveryRequired` retains the original seed/filter at
offset zero; A07 performs recovery and generation with its single RNG stream.
The published canonical golden remains `0xa0e531d76df62844`.

## Pure round builder (A07)

`round/builder.rs` owns one `ChaCha12Rng` and orchestration; `pool.rs` validates
ordered, nested, exclusion-clean and context-correct views; `recovery.rs` handles
bounded recovery and effective seed context; `labels.rs` handles first-gloss
display and right-label keys; `selection.rs` handles windows, partners and reserve
requests; `content.rs` performs only the final successful layout shuffles;
`error.rs` contains actionable errors. No database, browser, clock or ambient
randomness enters them.

`RoundCandidates` borrows initial views, original seed metadata, ordered recovery
rows and `ContextPool` entries keyed by recovered filter. A06 must supply these
as pure data, including views for possible recovered contexts when recovery is
needed. Ready seeds use their own context; canonical hashing always uses original
normalized URL state. Missing or inconsistent data fails rather than silently
substituting filters or sorting rows. `RoundContent` exposes only playable cards;
`BuildTrace` separately records internal reserves and requests for diagnostics.

`tests/support` loads a small TSV fixture and produces 18 full-round cases shared
by native tests and the `replay_vectors` wasm example. The Node runner compares
the wasm digest with the checked-in native fixture and rejects any host call.
It needs no added dependency. Web has no exercise UI or DB connection yet at the
time A07 landed.

### Module map

| File/module | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `round/builder.rs` | RNG ownership and orchestration |
| `round/pool.rs` | CandidatePool validation |
| `round/recovery.rs` | Bounded seed recovery, effective context |
| `round/labels.rs` | First-gloss display, right-label keys |
| `round/selection.rs` | Windows, partners, reserve requests |
| `round/content.rs` | Final layout shuffles |
| `round/error.rs` | `BuildError` variants |

### Builder API

`build_round(RoundCandidates, ExerciseVariant, &NormalizedPracticeQuery)` returns
`Result<Round, BuildError>`. `RoundCandidates` borrows an initial `CandidatePool`,
the original seed row if retained, ordered/exclusion-clean recovery rows and
`ContextPool` entries for possible recovered contexts. For a Ready seed, initial
views must use its HSK/PoS context; unseeded views use the URL filter. Recovery
prefers HSK 3.0 membership and derives the seed's canonical PoS set, then selects
the supplied views for that context. It never performs a query or rehashes.
The original seed/filter remain canonical even when effective context changes.

The builder rejects unordered/duplicate IDs, inconsistent or nonnested rows,
excluded rows, wrong-system/level/PoS views and missing seed/context data with
actionable errors. It validates caller ordering rather than sorting the views.
SQL construction and exclusion binding remain A06 responsibilities.

## What zipeek-core is not

- **Not a database client.** No `web_sys`, no `js_sys`, no DuckDB bindings.
- **Not a UI library.** No Yew, no `Html`, no components.
- **Not a domain-model owner.** That is `web`'s `models` module for UI-facing
  types; `zipeek-core` types are the shared domain layer used by both `web` and
  `db-gen`.
- **Not an importer.** The importer lives in `db-gen`; core supplies shared types
  and pure algorithms (pinyin normalization, gloss serialization helpers).
title: zipeek-core module

# `zipeek-themes` - visual context and background providers

The approved `zipeek-themes` crate is a dependency-free domain boundary for
resolving category/topic hints to a visual theme and loading background asset
metadata. The crate must not depend on Yew, exercise sessions, AI language
clients, HTTP image-generation SDKs, or the dictionary runtime.

`ThemeRequest` carries canonical topic/category labels and a seed. The resolver
counts recognized hints and selects a dominant theme; ties use the seed, while
unrecognized inputs select Neutral. This is deliberately independent of the
practice round-seed format `zipeek-round-v1`.

`StaticBackgroundProvider::load` is asynchronous and currently returns the
existing bundled `public/background.webp` for every theme. No image generation,
image caching, remote call, privacy transfer, or per-category artwork is claimed.
`web/components/themed_background.rs` performs the asynchronous request, ignores
late results after request changes/unmount and renders a fallback asset while
loading. The image is decorative, beneath content, and never blocks interaction.

Future image-generation integration should implement a provider adapter outside
the pure domain crate, with explicit consent, retention/cache policy, accessibility
and error handling. A stable topic should ordinarily be chosen at session start.
title: `zipeek-themes` - visual context and background providers

# Native streaming ASR: R682 checkpoint-specific head and cache contract

R682 uses the **user-supplied Windows ONNX inventory** from the cloned `pkufool/zipformer-small-streaming` `chunk-32-left-128` files. This is checkpoint inspection evidence, not a model execution or verified pinned upstream commit. The existing Qwen3-ASR and TTS production paths are untouched.

The encoder declares 77 input frames with 80 mel bins per invocation, a 512-wide output, twelve attention/cache groups, embedding state `[N,128,3,19]` and processed lengths `int64[N]`. The new `zipformer32.rs` module describes and validates 12 groups of keys, nonlinear attention, values and convolution histories. The group sizes are **not uniform**. Initial cache states allocate zero tensors on the selected Candle device. The model-specific encoder operations, graph output-to-cache transfers and exact frontend remain outstanding.

The checkpoint's decoder exports `[N,2]` int64 contexts, `[N,512]` output, embedding `[11661,512]`, grouped convolution `[512,4,2]`, and projection `[512,512]`. The joiner exports `Add -> Tanh -> Gemm` and only the `[11661,512]` output projection, not the three projections assumed by the earlier generic prototype. `checkpoint_head.rs` is a separate checkpoint-shaped Candle implementation; it has not established numeric parity with ONNX, including exact ReLU placement and token preprocessing. The generic prototype is retained separately for its synthetic-pipeline tests, not represented as compatible.

Weight conversion to safetensors requires the model files in the local `models/speech` checkout. Neither weights nor the 1.77 GiB Hugging Face clone are bundled in releases. Before enabling recognition, record the cloned commit hash, verify frontend parity, run ONNX vs Candle decoder/joiner logits on fixed tokens and encoder features, implement the complete Zipformer2 encoder/cache updates and test streaming Mandarin transcription. Do not add a WebSocket service or Live tab until those pass.

## Previous R680 checkpoint integration preparation

The `candle_streaming_stt` subsystem remains a non-production experimental module. It does not replace native Qwen3-ASR, and it has no HTTP/WebSocket endpoint or UI route. R679 provided incremental 16 kHz PCM framing, provisional Fbank extraction, a token-vocabulary reader and a streaming pipeline with a synthetic encoder. R680 adds a strict ONNX checkpoint inspector and a data-only embedded-initializer exporter so the actual encoder, decoder, joiner and cache interfaces can be mapped before implementing checkpoint-specific Candle math.

The provisional model is `pkufool/zipformer-small-streaming`. The upstream repository lists Chinese/English streaming models under Apache-2.0 and separate transducer encoder/decoder/joiner ONNX components for chunk 16/left 64, with a `data/tokens.txt` file. The upstream `model.pt` / TorchScript files are not parsed or executed. No model weights have been acquired or bundled in R680. Actual immutable revision, asset checksums and licensing provenance remain to be recorded locally.

See [checkpoint preflight](native-streaming-checkpoint-preflight.md) for local inspection/export commands, strict file-format limitations and the remaining acceptance path.

## Supported implementation

- R678: bounded PCM queue, transducer decoding state, native Candle predictor/joiner prototypes and generic attention-cache primitive.
- R679: incremental provisional Fbank, strict dense token-map parser, and test-injected encoder pipeline.
- R680: dependency-free, bounded protobuf inspection of ONNX metadata (graph ports, symbolic dimensions, operator inventory and initializer shapes/dtypes), component-set preflight, and byte-checked export of supported embedded initializers to safetensors.

## Critical limitations

- No Zipformer2 checkpoint-backed encoder is implemented. The generic attention cache is not a Zipformer layer.
- The decoder/joiner namespaces remain provisional and are not mapped to verified upstream initializer names.
- Exporting weight bytes is not equivalent to converting an ONNX computation graph into Candle operators.
- R679 feature extraction is not verified to match the upstream online Fbank.
- An ONNX graph inventory is an engineering input, not numerical parity evidence.
- Rust compilation, unit tests, checkpoint conversion and CUDA validation have not run in this authoring environment.

The next release should consume a pinned checkpoint inventory and target exact encoder modules and cache conventions. Do not add WebSocket transport or Live UI before genuine incremental model inference works.

## R683: checkpoint-backed decoder and joiner parity gate

R683 corrects the checkpoint decoder convolution to `conv1d_no_bias`. The exported decoder contains `decoder.conv.weight` `[512,4,2]` and **no** `decoder.conv.bias`, so a bias-requiring Candle constructor cannot load the real checkpoint. The existing grouping (128) and kernel (2) are preserved.

The new `streaming_head_parity` command maps the converted safetensors through Candle, evaluates three fixed token contexts, and compares all 512 decoder outputs and all 11,661 joiner logits against an ONNX Runtime-generated JSON fixture. The reference-generation script is optional developer tooling and uses a separately installed Python `numpy` and `onnxruntime`; neither is added to the Rust dependency graph or production application.

Run from the repository root in PowerShell, after installing the optional Python packages in a dedicated local environment:

```powershell
$checkpoint = 'models/speech/zipformer-small-streaming'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force target/zipformer-parity | Out-Null
cargo run --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt --bin streaming_checkpoint_inspect -- --export "$checkpoint/decoder-chunk-32-left-128.onnx" target/zipformer-parity/decoder.safetensors
cargo run --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt --bin streaming_checkpoint_inspect -- --export "$checkpoint/joiner-chunk-32-left-128.onnx" target/zipformer-parity/joiner.safetensors
python scripts/zipformer-head-reference.py "$checkpoint/decoder-chunk-32-left-128.onnx" "$checkpoint/joiner-chunk-32-left-128.onnx" target/zipformer-parity/reference.json
cargo run --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt --bin streaming_head_parity -- target/zipformer-parity/decoder.safetensors target/zipformer-parity/joiner.safetensors target/zipformer-parity/reference.json
```

The export command refuses to overwrite existing output, so remove or rename only the **generated** target/zipformer-parity files before repeating. The parity command fails on missing tensors, malformed or nonfinite reference values, or mismatched decoder vectors or joiner logits. Its tolerances (decoder `2e-4 + 2e-4 * abs(reference)`; joiner `2e-3 + 5e-4 * abs(reference)`) are initial CPU tolerances, not a claim of verified numeric equivalence. Explicitly capture the console output and checkpoint SHA-256 hashes. The experimental pipeline cannot transcribe until the encoder and streaming-state transfer are fully implemented.


## R686 experimental WebSocket transport

`GET /v1/stt/live` is an experimental localhost-only WebSocket route backed by the persistent Qwen3-ASR worker for best-effort partial/final transcripts. It does **not** use the unfinished Zipformer encoder. See root `RELEASE_NOTES.md` for the frame protocol, limits and initial acceptance commands. This represents a deliberate, separately approved transport milestone before full native model parity; the R682 historical warning against enabling an unverified Zipformer model remains valid. The R685 embedding source and parity tools have been restored into the Tauri mainline, but remain unverified on Windows.
title: Native streaming ASR: R682 checkpoint-specific head and cache contract

# Native streaming ASR checkpoint preflight (R680)

This document specifies the inspection boundary for the provisional `pkufool/zipformer-small-streaming` model. The published repository lists separate `encoder-chunk-16-left-64.onnx`, `decoder-chunk-16-left-64.onnx`, `joiner-chunk-16-left-64.onnx` files and `data/tokens.txt`. The upstream page currently lists an Apache-2.0 license, but the full revision SHA, each downloaded file hash, and any redistributed assets must be verified before packaging. The model repository contains TorchScript artifacts flagged as suspicious by the hosting service. **Do not deserialize or execute untrusted `.pt`/pickle files for this workflow.** The first conversion path uses data-only ONNX initializers.

Reference:
- https://huggingface.co/pkufool/zipformer-small-streaming/tree/main
- https://huggingface.co/pkufool/zipformer-small-streaming/tree/main/data

## Windows local acquisition and inventory

Download the chosen ONNX exports and `data/tokens.txt` from a pinned repository revision using a trusted Hugging Face download workflow. Do not place them under packaged web assets or commit them to the source archive. Preserve the exact source revision and record all SHA-256 hashes (for example, `Get-FileHash path -Algorithm SHA256`). The directory names and archive layout are not a checkpoint loader contract.

Run the new source-local inspection program:

```powershell
cargo run --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt --bin streaming_checkpoint_inspect -- `
  "C:\models\zipformer\encoder-chunk-16-left-64.onnx" `
  "C:\models\zipformer\decoder-chunk-16-left-64.onnx" `
  "C:\models\zipformer\joiner-chunk-16-left-64.onnx" `
  "C:\models\zipformer\data\tokens.txt" 0 `
  *> target\zipformer-r680-inventory.txt
```

The optional last argument is the blank token ID; 0 is a diagnostic starting value, **not** a verified model fact. Confirm the upstream tokenizer's blank convention. The inspector reads protobuf metadata without invoking an ONNX execution engine or deserializing PyTorch objects. It reports graph input/output shapes (including symbolic cache dimensions), operator counts, initialized tensor names, shapes, and types. It rejects missing or malformed graphs, external initializers, incompatible ONNX IR revisions across the three components and an inconsistent fixed joiner-vocabulary dimension. The inspector does not prove an executable Candle graph.

For each ONNX component, a data-only conversion can be attempted:

```powershell
cargo run --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt --bin streaming_checkpoint_inspect -- `
  --export "C:\models\zipformer\encoder-chunk-16-left-64.onnx" `
  "C:\models\zipformer\encoder.safetensors"
```

Repeat for decoder and joiner with distinct output paths. The exporter copies supported, uncompressed, embedded `TensorProto.raw_data` bytes into the safetensors format, validates every shape/byte count, and refuses an existing output filename. It refuses external data, unsupported dtypes and tensors stored only as typed protobuf fields. This converter does **not** convert graph operations, fold constants, implement Zipformer layers or validate numeric parity. Large or nonstandard ONNX exports may require a separately approved conversion procedure. Never pass an ONNX graph directly to Candle's `VarBuilder`.

## Engineering milestones still blocked by model artifacts

1. Run the inventory against actual files and retain the report, exact SHA-256 hashes, model revision and applicable notices.
2. Determine which graph initializers represent trained weights versus constants, and map their exact namespaces to Candle modules. Use initializer inventory and graph operators rather than guessing an architecture from filenames.
3. Implement the selected checkpoint's convolutional subsampler, per-stack Zipformer encoder layers and streaming-cache tensors with exact cache sizes and offsets.
4. Establish frontend parity against the model's online Kaldi/Fbank implementation, especially `snip_edges`, framing, scale, dither and final padding.
5. Use the same PCM samples to compare reference ONNX and Candle intermediate tensors and token emissions. Quantify absolute/relative error and check multiple chunk partitions.
6. Only after parity and Mandarin decoding tests pass, connect persistent streaming model sessions to bounded transport and the experimental Live tab.

R680 supplies model-file inspection and conversion primitives only. It does **not** claim a working Zipformer recognizer, an implemented checkpoint-compatible encoder, or runtime equivalence with ONNX.
title: Native streaming ASR checkpoint preflight (R680)

# UI architecture and state ownership

## Ownership principles

The root application owns durable cross-route services and readiness boundaries. A feature owns its transient interaction state unless it must be shared across routes or persisted. Use pure domain transitions and focused reducers where multiple fields must change consistently. Do not introduce a global provider for each local control.

- Root state includes theme preference, dictionary/database readiness and shared session-level services where source code confirms them.
- Route and feature state includes browse queries, Word Set selection, wizard drafts, lesson navigation and exercise-local drafts.
- Persistence services own browser data writes; UI components should not independently derive mastery counters or duplicate final outcomes.
- Async requests, animation timers and event listeners are scoped to their owners, cancelled or invalidated on navigation, and protected from stale completions.

Read [state ownership](ui-state-ownership.md), [Browse state](ui-browse-state.md), [system architecture](architecture.md) and [shared Practice exercise foundation](../learning-practice/practice/shared-exercise-foundation.md) before changing providers.

## Practice composition

A session host owns session identity, persistence, scheduling, navigation and aggregate progress. A shared exercise frame owns common presentation, accessibility, actions and feedback. Each exercise owns its domain interaction rules and emits typed attempts/outcomes to the host. Do not make an oversized component that switches on every exercise type. Skip and Replace does not count as an exercise verdict. See [Practice outcomes](../learning-practice/practice/practice-outcomes.md).

## Layout and motion

Use the current Tailwind/theme infrastructure and shared accessible control styles. The global header should not repeat page or exercise titles. The long dragon-shaped header visual reflects persisted pedagogical evidence, not completion or a floating percentage. Motion must preserve accessibility and honor reduced motion. Avoid implicit animation ownership shared between unrelated components; stop frame tasks on component unmount or content change.

## Verification and source boundaries

Implementation should be checked against the actual Yew provider tree, `crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/`, and the responsible domain crates before refactoring. Names in this document are conceptual boundaries, not claims that every shared component already exists. Validate both root and hosted routing, keyboard access, browser storage and in-flight work cancellation.

Older checkpoint observations, including source descriptions of Tailwind, Grammar and course adapters, are preserved in [the archived UI architecture snapshot](../archive-history/audits/superseded-maintained/architecture--ui-architecture-source.md). They are not evidence of current compilation or acceptance.

## Statistics dashboard architecture

The approved Statistics 2.0 UI uses a feature reducer and scoped context only for genuinely shared dashboard state. Heavy read-only projections are separate from UI selection state; typed IDs, stable paging, explicit provenance and Rust-owned Chart.js lifecycle are planned in the [Statistics architecture specification](modules/statistics-dashboard.md). This remains a design target, not the implemented R564 state-management structure.

## Record feature ownership (R670 WIP)

The Record reference and replay panels read `currentTime / duration` from the active local browser audio element to render a progressing PCM waveform and offer accessible seeking; the reference text highlights progressively by character index. This highlight approximates timing and does not represent forced speech alignment. Playback progress is transient component state, not the reducer or persistent learning data.

The `/record` route is composed within `crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/record/`. `mod.rs` mounts the feature controller and typed child views. `state.rs` owns target and workflow transitions, with a `RecordingId` identifying the current captured utterance. `audio.rs` owns the transient microphone WAV and its PCM-derived waveform. `controller.rs` owns local TTS/STT callbacks, cancellation, stale-request invalidation and the audio resource lifecycle. Target selection, reference, microphone, waveform and transcription panels render from typed properties and emit callbacks; they do not independently own speech requests or WAV buffers. The recorded payload is never in a Yew render-state value, and no audio persists beyond the route lifecycle. This is an authored, not yet WASM/browser-verified source boundary.
title: UI architecture and state ownership

# Ui Browse State

## Browse feature state

Browse is composed in `pages/browse.rs`; it no longer owns dictionary queries,
Word Set persistence, or form editing state. Its child components live in
`components/browse/`: `search_form.rs` owns automatic search controls,
`results/mod.rs` selects the status component and owns result-list wiring;
`results/status.rs` renders loading/empty/error states,
`results/word_card.rs` renders typed vocabulary entries, and
`results/pagination.rs` renders page navigation;
`word_set_panel.rs` owns the create/rename/delete/backup input fields.

`BrowseProvider` owns the route-scoped `BrowseState` reducer and abortable
DuckDB query effect. Search requests carry generation IDs, and superseded
responses cannot replace the latest state. Search and Retry both validate the
current saved-set boundary. Missing required Yew provider contexts are treated
as developer invariant violations and unwrapped; storage, query and user-data
failures remain recoverable results.

`WordSetsProvider` owns `WordSetsState` with the saved collection, selected
management target and a single success-or-error feedback state. Its callback
executes validated mutations through `services/word_sets.rs`, writes storage
before committing reducer state, and dispatches a failure without discarding
the previous collection if persistence fails. Delete/import invalidate Browse
rather than automatically displaying unrestricted results. An active saved-set
toggle updates the exact candidate list and resets Browse pagination.

Both providers currently mount only for Browse. Practice Setup still reads the
same localStorage key independently when it mounts; a future cross-route
Word Set provider requires a separately reviewed lifecycle and storage-sync
design. Do not describe this route-local provider as app-global.

The source Browse UI is a pragmatic dropdown/card implementation. It does **not**
implement the D45/A37 canonical chips, strategy control, URL-authoritative
query or numbered-page contracts. D45 approves the modern card/sidebar layout
and preserves the A37 query/URL semantics. A13 retains
that product discrepancy as open implementation work.

### Route composition and component imports

Browse's route branch imports `BrowseProvider`, `WordSetsProvider`, and
`DatabaseBoundary` explicitly at module scope. The route uses multiline nested
Yew tags for its provider composition; the providers remain scoped to Browse,
not the entire app. The Browse page and word-card component use readable
multiline callback and optional-action expressions. These edits are source
readability changes only: no provider ownership, event behaviour, or URL
contract is altered. A Node source-layout regression check covers the route
shape; Rust/Chrome checks remain local validation steps.

### Browse results component boundaries

The Browse input form observes query text, filter values and saved-set snapshots. Typing cancels the previous 320 ms debounce; filter changes and initial mount run immediately. Refresh explicitly reissues the current search, Clear resets the filter input state, and the reducer generation discards stale database responses. Word Set deletion clears the removed selection and reruns the query without an obsolete manual Search step. `BrowseResults` computes a `status_component` from the reducer state before its outer `html!` block. `BrowseLoading`, `BrowseEmpty`, and `BrowseError` are presentational status views; `BrowseWordCard` (now rendered as a compact single-column row) and `BrowsePagination` receive focused props/callbacks. The container alone resolves the required search and Word Set contexts and dispatches actions. `data-component` values and the older `data-browse-*` hooks remain stable. Do not fold these separate views back into nested match expressions inside `html!`. This source refactor still requires local Rust/Chrome validation.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/architecture-ui-browse-state.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.
title: Ui Browse State
