# Ui State Ownership

> **Current approved target behavior:** [Shared visitation boundaries](../dictionary-data/vocabulary/vocabulary-visitation.md). Older implementation descriptions below record prior contracts and may not match the latest approved behavior or verified source.


## State ownership

| State | Authority and lifetime | Access and status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Theme | App lifetime; existing approved saved preference | Implemented ThemeProvider, read/command hooks and persistence effect |
| Motion preference | App lifetime; live prefers-reduced-motion value | MotionProvider publishes a small preference snapshot; no new saved setting proposed |
| Database client | One app-owned runtime session | Implemented stable Dictionary context; typed read-only Database facade |
| Database readiness | App lifetime, independent of routes | Implemented status context, typed Retry command and pure reducer |
| HSK, PoS, mode, count, seed, offset and URL exclusions | Current URL, normalized by A08 | Route adapter produces immutable typed inputs; no second writable global filter store |
| Saved and pending exclusions | Explicit user actions, approved D13 lifecycle | A11 local setup hook validates saved IDs and exposes Retry/Reset; generation only, never union into loaded URLs. Shared feature commands can follow their first consumers. |
| Browse request/results/pagination | Browse feature scope | Feature reducer plus cancellable query effect; URL authority follows approved UX |
| Practice round, guesses, mistakes and progress | Practice session scope | Feature reducer; A07 builds round data, core FixedProgress tracks completion |
| Drawer expansion | AppShell; current reload-reset behaviour | Keep local unless another component actually needs shared commands |
| Hover, temporary focus and individual animated values | Owning component/controller | Local state/refs; never broadcast every frame through app context |

Do not create one application-wide reducer containing every result list, input
and animation tick. A provider belongs at the nearest shared ownership boundary.
Use props for leaf inputs such as a card label, selected state or click callback.
Components that need a shared service or feature state consume its hook directly;
intermediate layout components must not relay those values through several levels.

## Hanzi recognition feature ownership (R545 WIP)

The `recognize_hanzi` feature reducer owns input classification, Undo availability, request status, errors, candidate results, and the monotonic request generation. The page owns scoped async orchestration and workspace mounting; child components receive typed props. The browser crate owns canvas, pointer, upload and clipboard resources. Candidate parsing remains a pure feature module. Browser verification is pending.

## Statistics explorer ownership (R586 source-only WIP)

The Statistics page owns one route-scoped `DashboardState` reducer for shared filters, paging, selection sets and active Grammar detail. The query hook owns asynchronous request lifecycle, including stale-response protections. History timeline entry expansion stays local to its own row. `history/{day,entry,table_row}.rs`, `grammar/{detail,items}.rs`, `explorer/row.rs` and shared `stats/pagination.rs` receive typed properties and report selection/navigation through callbacks. They do not create new contexts or independent copies of shared state.

The parent explorers remain responsible for search/filter toolbars, bulk selection and query orchestration; a further boundary review is outstanding. This source-only checkpoint does not establish browser or WASM acceptance.

## R587 Statistics composition correction (source-only WIP)

`stats/mod.rs` owns route providers, preview activation and top-level selection review. Feature directories use `mod.rs` only for module declarations and exports; each page controller lives in `page.rs`. Settings catalogue search/category state is local, while persisted metric visibility and tile ordering stay in one route reducer. Settings children emit typed preset/metric/tile actions. Skills and Insights aggregation is pure and independently testable. History toolbar and Grammar view selector emit typed intent to their parent pages. Selection-review resolution is pure, and preview IDs still must not be transferred to Practice/Word Sets.

`state/mod.rs` retains atomic shared transitions and request phase invariants. `state/metrics.rs` and `state/filters.rs` only own types and local operations; they are not independent writable stores. History/Grammar/Vocabulary async pages retain query hooks and guarded bulk selection. No result of this source-only refactor should be treated as compiled or browser-accepted until the locked gates pass.

## R587 shared Statistics record snapshots (source-only WIP)

Read-only demo snapshots and section projections now use typed `WordRecords`, `GrammarRecords` and `SessionRecords` newtypes backed by `Rc<[T]>`, with construction from owned vectors and cheap shared clones. Each type exposes read-only slice operations, while bounded asynchronous query pages continue to use their own `Vec<T>` plus pagination metadata. The collection API does not expose mutation or mutable references, and no new context or reducer has been added. Locked WASM and browser acceptance remain outstanding.
title: Ui State Ownership

# R318 server architecture checkpoint

Current implementation was verified against the R317 source. Documentation and pending tests do not establish that a browser journey passes.

## Exercise coverage status

- Speaking: target switching, accessible selection, and permission-denial recovery have E2E scenarios. Successful microphone capture, discard, retry, playback, and cleanup are not verified.
- Listening choice: sufficient-vocabulary gating and a configured session-and-restore journey exist; audible playback was not verified here.
- Audio dictation: the browser suite contains playback gating, answering, and restoration; browser execution remains required.
- Image Vocabulary: mode selection has browser coverage; a full image generation, approval, selection, scoring, and completion scenario is still absent.
- Translation and sentence transformation: deterministic fixture and exercise interactions exist; the harness does not yet run the native AI-server process for those scenarios.

## New owned servers

- `zipeek-static-server::StaticServer::run(ServerConfig)` binds and serves a built Trunk dist tree, returns its actual address, and supports graceful stop.
- `zipeek-image-server::ImageServer::run(ImageServerOptions)` binds a loopback endpoint, starts the placeholder or SDXL backend, returns its actual address, and supports graceful stop. Placeholder mode needs no external model.
- `zipeek-e2e` declares dependencies on all three server crates. Static, Image and AI have owned server lifecycle tests, but compilation and runtime acceptance remain pending.

Both APIs return owned handles that initiate graceful shutdown on drop. Explicit `.stop().await` waits for task termination. These tests must be compiled and run on the target Rust toolchain before acceptance.

## Implemented in the continuing R318 checkpoint

- The image server now accepts an explicit list of strictly validated loopback HTTP origins in `ImageServerOptions.allowed_origins`. The legacy local development origins remain accepted. E2E passes its actual dynamically allocated browser origin instead of disabling CORS.
- `Harness::start` launches and owns a placeholder `ImageServer`, passes its URL to `ScenarioContext`, stores image files under suite artifacts, and awaits shutdown in `Harness::finish`.
- A non-ignored browser scenario selects Picture Vocabulary from Advanced Practice, checks the selection state, configures the placeholder image endpoint, and performs real browser-origin health, job submission, job polling, and generated-image retrieval requests. It does **not** complete the Image Vocabulary Yew answer workflow yet.
- `page_objects/audio_probes.rs` verifies that silent-mode speech recorded a Mandarin `speak` event, not merely that a listen button was clicked. Listening-session coverage now invokes the play control and verifies the service event.
- The existing microphone-permission denial fixture counts `getUserMedia` attempts. The Speaking browser test verifies both attempts reached the microphone API. It does not prove successful capture, MediaRecorder stop/discard, or audio fidelity.
- Added service-level Rust regression checks for allowed image origins and invalid origins, plus a deterministic image-server preflight test. Browser tests remain unexecuted until Windows Chrome acceptance.

## Next integration steps

1. Implement a full Image Vocabulary browser scenario with dynamically valid AI scene composition for the selected HSK words, image review and approval, answer submission, scoring, and regeneration. The standalone placeholder image backend and browser CORS boundary are now testable.
2. Add a deterministic `getUserMedia`/`MediaRecorder` fixture that produces a non-empty recording and exposes stream-track cleanup, then verify stop, retry, discard, and recorder unmount. The current denial fixture only proves acquisition attempts and failure handling.
3. Verify actual audible output and microphone capture on a supported device. Silent speech event capture proves service invocation, not sound reproduction.
4. The native `AiServer::run(address)` now returns `RunningAiServer` with graceful stop. Its HTTP health/models/CORS fixture test is written; migrating browser translation scenarios still requires the custom fixture's request-record/reset controls. Run model-backed acceptance only when explicitly configured.
5. Root suites now use owned `StaticServer::run` after `trunk build`. The Pages `/zipeek/` fixture adapter remains unchanged; verify both hosting paths in Chrome.
6. Execute Cargo check, tests and managed Chrome suites; investigate any new errors without interpreting Node source contracts as compiler or browser acceptance.

## Known limitations

There is no local Rust toolchain in the authoring environment. No Rust or Chrome pass is claimed. The image-server dependency includes the existing CUDA-enabled Candle stack and may increase the build burden of the E2E crate. No third-party package versions were modified.

## Continuing R318 static and AI-server lifecycle work

- Root `Harness::start` retains `trunk build` for compiling assets and uses an
  owned `StaticServer` instead of `trunk serve`. Startup allocates a dynamic
  loopback port, uses that origin for the Image Server CORS configuration, and
  reports static-server shutdown errors during `Harness::finish`.
- `server::BuiltWeb` makes the built distribution and adapter URL explicit;
  Pages still use the Node fixture adapter and `/zipeek/` public URL.
- `AiServer::run(address)` returns `RunningAiServer`, an owned fixture-capable
  server with ephemeral-port binding and graceful stop. New HTTP integration
  assertions check health, model listing, approved/disallowed browser origins,
  and port release after stop. Existing translation fixture remains active.
- Added static hosting tests for index, asset, 404, missing build root and
  cleanup. None have been executed under Cargo in this environment.
title: R318 server architecture checkpoint

# R451 UI and integration source audit

This is a source-level review against user-supplied Chrome screenshots, not a passed visual acceptance report. The inspected baseline was the full R450 working tree. Source evidence describes implementation, while the screenshots establish the user-observed defects.

| Area | Confirmed baseline finding | R451 action | Remaining validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Grammar mosaic | Source illustration was a screenshot of an earlier Zipeek UI, visible through gaps | Replaced with detailed original autumn painting; versioned asset path and unpack/preflight checks | Verify screenshot contains no UI at all, real browser loading |
| Vocabulary mosaic | 50 regions had 98.5% cover, leaving rich garden invisible; only four have authored curricula | Use subdued theme-aware cover, mark authored regions, clarify unpublished selection | Visual test at 0% and responsiveness |
| Pinyin mosaic | Six enormous solid-blue regions covered faint artwork | Reduce cover, preserve all six lessons, improve page layout | Art is still low-detail; a replacement illustration must be approved/visually validated before adoption |
| Course layout | Full-viewport constraints in AppShell and track components stretched/clipped details | Remove Courses viewport lock and independent panel stretch; use natural page scrolling | Browser heights 600, 768, 900 and mobile |
| Grammar details | Repetitive messages about unavailable mastery dominated panels | Reduce noise; keep the real lesson player and explicit unpublished states | Verify interactive player |
| Practice setup | Exercise list scroll relied on desktop flex sizing; selection contrast under theme backgrounds was weak | Explicit max-height scroll area, strong selected card/path/format styling and theme-aware action tones | Actual pointer/keyboard interaction across presets |
| Practice session | Dedicated shell exists in baseline but user screenshot showed global chrome and stale Matching copy | Preserve dedicated branch, make it self-contained, add R451 marker; add in-session step progress | Establish which bundle Chrome serves; run shell E2E |
| Matching | Selected and matched states had UI labels but failed user-visible acceptance; MCQ lacked a selected style | Larger standalone quiz card, clearer selected MCQ controls, consistent state feedback and progress | Verify actual pairs by clicks and keyboard; partial answers remain in local component state |
| Browse | Headword undersized, flexible row columns produced poor alignment, meaning controls overly spaced | Prominent Hanzi and compact two-column rows with responsive fallback; compact meaning control | Long meanings and mixed scripts in Chrome |
| Home/onboarding | Theme selection preview and card spacing were implemented but different screens used fixed blue actions | Theme-specific primary and hover palette; consistent spotlight controls | Confirm preview rollback, storage and wallpaper provisioning |
| Pinyin lesson | Example presentation compact and mixed script label assigned to entire mixed-language string | Better card typography and responsive spacing | Pronunciation pedagogy and audio assessment not in this UI batch |
| Testing | Existing browser tests still inspect obsolete direct Practice URLs; previous course opacity assertions stale | Updated focused tests and authored visual workflows; retained legacy scenarios in task register | Large migration still required for pre-R444 test suites |

## Source and build blockers

The full source contains `static/courses` illustrations, but `crates/zipeek-web/public` and `vendor` are not included. These are explicitly prepared by repository-owned commands and remain out of a source archive; do not introduce generated/vendor binaries into the source by hand. A fresh environment requires explicit `cargo make setup` and asset verification before Trunk.

The provided environment lacks `cargo`, `rustfmt`, the WASM target, a running frontend and a Chrome harness. No successful compilation, dynamic testing, screenshots or browser acceptance can be claimed. Archive integrity only establishes that the source is distributable, not that the changes compile or behave correctly.

The app retains no fake course mastery from region selection, no manual Pinyin completion, only two Practice routes, and no backward compatibility aliases. Full per-exercise answer-state persistence and verified pedagogical evidence remain separate future work.
title: R451 UI and integration source audit

## Matching feedback and ambiguous entries

The user considers the green success checkmark unnecessary and requests its
removal from matching cards. Keep an understandable matched/disabled state;
the exact replacement, including whether background feedback alone is enough,
belongs to A54's implementation review. This request does not remove MCQ
feedback icons or change scoring. Current matching still renders the checkmark.

The supplied screenshot shows `井` twice: `jǐng` and `Jǐng`. The pinned primary
dataset has both readings: the lowercase form starts with “a well”; the
capitalized form starts with the Chinese astronomy constellation gloss and
also includes the surname gloss. These are distinct imported reading rows,
not evidence that a dictionary row should be deleted or merged.

Current hanzi-to-English uniqueness compares normalized right-column English
labels, not left-column hanzi. Thus both can appear in one round despite
nearly identical learner-facing prompts. Pinyin capitalization is a weak cue.
The user approved avoiding duplicate simplified hanzi within a matching round
(D42). The four target pairs must not represent different readings sharing the
same simplified hanzi; the two cards belonging to one pair still represent that
one word as usual. Preserve both source readings for other rounds. This does
not authorize sense labels or change MCQ duplicate policy. A55 owns the change.
Do not silently case-fold source reading identity. Any builder selection/RNG
change needs the explicit replay compatibility review required by
[ROUND_GENERATION](../../games/round-generation.md) and AGENTS; no replay break is approved
by recording this policy.

## Local AI category enrichment

The user added AiMux/LM Studio scaffolding to `db-gen` to use a local model
for classification. The goal is category tags associated with an entry and
later filtering by those tags. User examples:

- Medicine or medical usage.
- Idioms.
- Technical or specialist usage.
- Poetry/literary usage.
- Very rare usage.

These examples are a starting vocabulary, not an approved exhaustive taxonomy.
“Rare” may be a usage/frequency attribute while “medicine” is a domain and
“idiom” is a form; do not force them into one exclusive class without review.
Preserve specialist entries in the dictionary; classification alone does not
authorize excluding them from all practice.

A56 must refine whether tags apply to a reading row, an individual sense or a
shared headword, allow multiple tags, define stable tag IDs and filter behavior,
and propose the exact storage/query/export changes for schema approval.
Suggested review topics include unclassified entries, manual overrides,
classification provenance/model/prompt identity, caching and reproducibility,
failed responses and confidence/review policy. These are design proposals.
Existing WordIds and source data remain authoritative until explicitly amended.

Classification belongs to an explicit generator/enrichment workflow, not a
Trunk rebuild or an implicit runtime dependency. Current checked-in data has
no category-tag schema or classifier output. See
[db-gen notes](../../architecture/modules/db-gen.md#user-added-local-llm-scaffold).

## Practice setup category and part-of-speech filters

User request and refinement recorded 2026-10-29 (D44 / A61): Practice setup
needs a richer filter section so a session can use only words from chosen
categories and/or parts of speech, alongside the existing HSK selection.

Approved combination rule: **OR within each group, AND across groups**. For
example, (medical OR technical) AND (noun OR verb) AND the selected HSK level.
An empty category or PoS group adds no restriction for that group. Each selected
exercise still applies its own existing eligibility requirements. The selected
session filters should apply throughout a mixed-type session.

Proposed UI for the implementation review: searchable multi-select category
and PoS controls, removable chips for active selections, Clear filters, and an
eligible-word count to help avoid unusably small pools. Exact layout, mobile
interaction, count semantics and insufficient-pool handling remain open.
The word "fancy" expresses a request for a richer usable filter experience,
not approval of a particular widget/library or new dependency.

Current practice URL/core query types already support PoS, but setup currently
constructs an empty PoS selection and exposes no PoS picker. PoS UI can therefore
be scoped independently. Category filters depend on A56's approved taxonomy,
tag data and schema/query design; current artifacts contain no such tags.
Practice filtering should use generated tags rather than classify words with
a live AI call whenever a session starts.

A61 must define how filters survive Start, mixed transitions, Play again and
Reset, plus any URL encoding/sharing changes. Do not invent a category URL
parameter or modify v1 canonical replay inputs in this documentation task.
Document schema/replay impacts and obtain their required approval before code.

## Settings route and audio interaction

The user requests a future Settings route with theme selection and an audio
preference. `/settings` is the proposed app-relative path, preserving the Pages
base `/zipeek/`; the current router has no Settings route.

Requested audio mode: hide the audio icon and automatically play pronunciation
when the user clicks a word/card. This is user-triggered speech, not automatic
speech on route load. Explicit icon mode remains the current behavior.
A57 must define default mode, persistence, which surfaces/clicks speak, replay
and cancellation behavior, keyboard equivalence, unsupported-speech fallback,
and whether the existing topbar theme control remains available too.
Card selection must still perform its exercise action; the preference must
not create a second scoring action or nested interactive controls.

## Experimental pronunciation and listening exercises

The user clarified that these are two distinct future exercise types (D43):

- **Pronounce a word:** the learner speaks into a microphone. Recognition,
  acceptable pronunciation, grading/feedback and microphone failure behavior
  remain to be defined under A58.
- **Listen and choose:** the app speaks a word and the learner identifies it
  from exactly three options. Option representation (hanzi, meaning or another
  label), retries/feedback and progression remain to be defined under A60.

Both are experimental and must be independently toggleable in Settings. They
should only be offered in setup/mixed-session selection when their Settings
option is enabled. Default enablement, preference persistence and behavior if
a previously enabled type is disabled while selected remain open. Current
six-type setup/URL behavior is unchanged by this future requirement.

The user reports that speech synthesis does not pronounce the Chinese word
for "2" (二, èr) reliably. Record this as a reported speech-quality issue, not
as an inherent inability to pronounce that character in every voice/browser.
Speech synthesis and microphone speech recognition are separate capabilities.
Qualification for one does not prove the other works.

Eligibility is required for the audio exercises, but its source is undecided:
a curated allowlist, voice/browser qualification, per-reading pronunciation
metadata, or another reviewed policy. Evaluate both exercises separately, and
include the reported 二 / èr case in future synthesis evaluation. Do not exclude
entries from unrelated exercises as a consequence.

## Translate sentence exercise

The user proposes querying 20 random words and asking AI to make a sentence
for a translation exercise. They approved using a useful subset of that
20-word candidate pool; the model does not have to use all 20. This exercise
is experimental and must be enabled in Settings. Enabling it exposes AI
connection configuration; it is usable only with a working configured endpoint.
A59 must define:

- Translation direction and how the learner submits an answer.
- Difficulty/HSK/category filters, grammar constraints and sense selection.
- Expected translation, acceptable alternatives, grading and feedback.
- Browser connection to the user-configured AI endpoint, initially targeting
  local LM Studio. GitHub Pages/browser compatibility still needs a practical
  spike; generator-side AiMux does not run inside the static browser app.
- How to handle unavailable AI, malformed/unsuitable sentences, latency,
  caching and word/sentence provenance.

No specific model, hosted provider/service, new route, exercise URL/replay
format or dependency is selected here. Current v1 round determinism remains intact.


### AI connection in Settings

User refinement recorded 2026-10-29: sentence translation joins the two audio
exercises as an experimental Settings-gated feature. Settings needs an AI
connection section. Proposed fields: API base URL, model identifier, an API
key/token when required by the chosen server, and Test connection. Exact layout,
validation and endpoint/token persistence are still implementation choices.

For the first local-development target, LM Studio supports an OpenAI-compatible
API base such as http://localhost:1234/v1 and model discovery. Its authentication
is optional by default; if Require Authentication is enabled, requests need
a bearer API token. Browser calls from Zipeek's localhost:1420 to port 1234
are cross-origin, so LM Studio must permit CORS. These are documented platform
capabilities, not a claim that a Zipeek connection has been tested. See
[LM Studio compatibility](https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/openai-compat),
[server settings](https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/core/server/settings) and
[authentication](https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/core/authentication).

GitHub Pages is static hosting; the browser would contact the user's endpoint
directly. A localhost endpoint means the visitor's own machine. Pages does not
run LM Studio/db-gen or provide a secret-hiding backend. A public HTTPS page
may reach a local server in supporting browsers with the relevant local/loopback
permission and CORS, but browser support/policy and connection failure behavior
must be tested before claiming hosted support. Local development is the first
validation target; unsupported hosted connections need a clear unavailable
state rather than a guaranteed fallback. See [GitHub Pages](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/what-is-github-pages)
and [Chrome local network access](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance/guides/security/local-network-access).

Use a user-supplied token when needed; never embed a shared application secret
in the static bundle, route URL or generated dictionary. Session-only versus
remembered credential storage remains open. No endpoint call, token collection,
new dependency or remote service is introduced by these notes.


## Schema and query review prerequisite

The user requests a schema review covering indexes, additional tables and
full-text search support in WASM. A62 evaluates those choices against the real
word/filter/search workload, including A56 tags and A61 setup filters. See
[the review brief](../../dictionary-data/schema/review.md). Official WASM support for
the fts extension is documented; Zipeek's pinned version/read-only artifact
compatibility is still untested. No extra table/index or ranked-search change
is selected merely by recording this request.

# Product Practice

> **Current approved target behavior:** [Practice outcomes](../../learning-practice/practice/practice-outcomes.md), [vocabulary selection and exclusions](../../dictionary-data/vocabulary/vocabulary-selection.md), and [profile portability](../../learning-practice/practice/practice-profile-portability.md). Older implementation descriptions below record prior contracts and may not match the latest approved behavior or verified source.


## Practice

### HSK filters

Treat HSK system and level/tier as separate concepts. HSK 2.0 has levels 1-6;
HSK 3.0 has levels 1-6 plus a combined advanced tier 7-9. These are distinct word
lists. A word can have different levels in each, belong to both, or belong to only
one. For example, a word may be level 2 in HSK 2.0 and level 3 in HSK 3.0.
Missing membership is not a level or an inferred equivalence between systems.

The HSK 3.0 advanced band has one domain value, `Hsk3Level::SevenToNine`, stored
and canonically encoded as integer `7`. Values 8 and 9 are not separate levels.
Accept `level=7-9` as an alias for HSK 3.0 and normalize to `level=7`. Display
"HSK 7-9", never three separate level buttons (A22 amendment, 2026-10-27). HSK 2.0 still
accepts only 1-6. Missing/invalid levels default to 1 in the selected system (D15),
never all levels. Invalid values produce a debug-only warning, not a page error.

The setup screen's initial filter scope is HSK system + level. URL filtering
already supports PoS; adding a setup PoS picker later does not change the URL scheme.

### Round generation (D02: approved)

The visible round has exactly **four cards on the left and four on the right**:
eight labels total. The user matches four corresponding pairs.

Internally, the builder uses four correct pairs plus up to four distractor
candidates per side: up to eight candidates per column before selection. Extra
candidates never render and are discarded after the four winners are chosen.
Each visible left card must retain its corresponding right match; candidate
sampling must not turn the visible exercise into an unmatchable set.

1. Choose four correct pairs from the filtered HSK + PoS pool. D02 originally
   specified random selection; D13 supersedes that for unseeded practice with
   deterministic ordered slices at the URL's offset. Random still chooses its
   initial variant/seed randomly, then must rebuild deterministically from its URL.
2. Draw distractor candidates from the same PoS and HSK pool. D13 requires any
   random-looking candidate choices to reproduce from the URL inputs (D12).
3. No two entries in a round may share the visible right-column label for the
   selected variant. Deduplicate candidates and resample to achieve uniqueness.
4. If the deduplicated pool cannot supply eight candidates, widen HSK to the
   selected level plus or minus one, then drop the PoS filter if still too small.
   Reaching the duplicate-resampling retry limit also triggers this widening.
5. If no candidate view can supply four correct pairs plus four distinct-label
   reserves, return D12's insufficient-pool error and show the distinct-words
   message with level/exclusion recovery controls.

The four additional candidates are internal reserves, never extra visible cards.
D12 specifies the pure CandidatePool builder, canonical seed string, portable
ChaCha12Rng, SQL ordering/exclusions, bounded sliding/rejection, and system-clamped
widening in [ROUND_GENERATION](../../games/round-generation.md). Unseeded windows slide past
duplicate right labels; widened views start at zero. Seeded rounds never slide.

### Practice modes (D03: approved)

The user picks the mode on `/practice`:

- **Endless:** infinite rounds with a Next round button between rounds. No
  summary and no score persistence. Show an in-session streak and cumulative
  correct count; a wrong attempt/answer resets the streak. Show a flame at ≥ 3.
  Matching also shows `N / 4` locally; Fixed adds `Round N of M` to its header.
- **Fixed:** choose N rounds up front. After round N, show First-attempt,
  Mistakes, Time and Highest streak with an accuracy ring, Play again and Back
  to setup actions (D35). Offer
  exactly three round-count buttons: **5 / 10 / 20**, default **10**. No custom-N
  input in v1 (D13).

### Random shortcut (D04: approved)

Random reuses the practice round generator with randomized inputs. It ignores
setup-screen HSK/PoS filters and always starts Endless mode.

1. Pick a variant randomly from `eng-pinyin`, `pinyin-hanzi`, and `hanzi-eng`.
2. Pick a seed word randomly from the entire database, without setup filters.
3. Select the seed plus three other correct pairs matching its PoS and HSK
   membership, with distractor candidates from the same pool. Apply D02's widening
   and duplicate-label rules unchanged.
4. Navigate directly to the selected practice variant with `mode=endless`, `seed`,
   and the seed's `hsk`/`level` context, plus exclusions if nonempty (D13 below).
5. Retry a seed with no HSK membership up to ten times, then use the first ordered
   word with a membership. Prefer HSK 3.0 when both exist. If the three candidate
   views still fail, report D12's typed insufficient-pool error. D12 replaces the
   older unfiltered-round escape hatch.

The seed's attributes become the effective filter. There is no separate
Random-specific round-building implementation; all deterministic selection uses
the shared builder. Normalize seeded offset to zero before forming its seed string.

### Practice URLs and replay (D13: approved)

Unseeded practice from setup uses this query contract (bracketed parts optional):

```text
/practice/<variant>?mode=<endless|fixed>&rounds=<5|10|20>&hsk=<2.0|3.0>&level=<1..7>[&pos=<noun,verb>][&exclude=<id,id,id>][&offset=<n>]
```

Canonical URLs include mode, hsk, and level. Include rounds iff
mode=fixed; in Endless it is ignored. Defaults for missing/invalid values are
mode=endless, rounds=10, hsk=3.0, level=1, offset=0.

hsk and level identify the active filter across all rounds and on deep links.
HSK 2.0 allows 1-6; HSK 3.0 also allows 7 for the combined advanced tier.
Missing/invalid level uses 1 in the selected system, including values such as
99, abc, or level 7 with HSK 2.0. Never broaden an invalid level to all levels.

Optional pos is a comma-separated set of canonical lowercase enum strings
(for example pos=verb,noun). Include words whose PoS is in the set. Omitted
or empty means all parts of speech; do not emit pos=. Drop unrecognized
entries while retaining recognized entries; if none remain, use no PoS filter.
The DB and query layer share the vocabulary documented in
DB.

exclude contains comma-separated integer WordIds. Apply only the router's
normal query serialization; no additional encoding pass. Omit empty exclusions
entirely, rather than emitting exclude=. No new serialization dependency is
approved merely by this contract.

offset is a nonnegative index into the filtered, ordered pool, not a word ID.
Every candidate-view query uses ORDER BY id ASC, after exclusions in SQL.

Parse values strictly and fall back to defaults for unknown/malformed values;
malformed links must never panic. Canonical output requirements do not prevent
safe defaults when parsing incomplete input.

Random seed replay uses a distinct contract:

text
/practice/<variant>?mode=endless&seed=<word_id>&hsk=<2.0|3.0>&level=<1..7>&pos=<seed_pos>[&exclude=<ids>]
The seed anchors one of the four correct pairs. The Random tile writes the seed's
HSK system/level and canonical PoS into the URL so reload uses those same attributes.
For example, a verb seed emits pos=verb. HSK 3.0 advanced seeds use level=7.
Retained seeded rounds require Endless. If a URL combines Fixed with a seed,
ignore the seed, warn only in debug, and run normal Fixed with its original
filter/offset. Offset is zeroed only after a seed is validated and retained.

URL normalization and fallbacks (D15: approved)
Normalize input deterministically in memory; malformed URLs must not panic or
error the page. Preserve the current URL until an explicit new URL is generated.

A08 implements pure parsing/normalization helpers. A21 connects dictionary-backed
normalization and ordered candidate views to A07's single-stream builder.
RecoveryRequired retains original canonical inputs; the builder owns recovery
draws. All six practice routes now have playable controls under A09/A10. URL loading
never reads saved exclusions or rewrites the entered link.

Parse mode/count, HSK system/level, PoS, exclusions, and entered offset using
the defaults above. The URL's exclusions are authoritative, not saved browser
exclusions. Invalid levels use 1 with a warning only in debug builds.

If mode is Fixed, ignore any seed before seed lookup or offset-zeroing. Keep
Fixed, its count, the same filter, and the entered offset; emit a debug warning.

Otherwise, an absent/malformed seed, nonexistent ID, or seed excluded by this
URL falls back to an unseeded round with the same filter and entered offset.
An ID excluded only in localStorage must not invalidate a shared URL's seed.

An existing, nonexcluded seed with neither HSK membership uses deterministic
recovery: up to ten ChaCha draws from the ordered, exclusion-clean pool, then
the first eligible word by id. No ambient randomness on URL loads. Keep the
original bad seed in the URL; recovery is internal and reproducible.

Only a retained/resolved seed normalizes offset to zero before canonical RNG
input construction. A rejected seed must not erase the unseeded fallback's
entered offset. See ROUND_GENERATION for the two seed-selection paths.

The same URL and database snapshot must reproduce the same round, including
candidate choices and label layout. Later resampling/shuffling must therefore be
deterministic from the canonical inputs; using ambient randomness on reload would
violate replay. D12's round-generation specification defines
the algorithm; D17 selects rand's ChaCha feature and D19 fixes the sole v1
format and single-stream recovery/selection/shuffle order. Golden-round
implementation checks remain future work.
The database is committed in Git, but regeneration may change it; the development
policy does not promise compatibility or identical rounds across database changes.

Word exclusions (D13: approved)
Marking a word "don't show again" adds its WordId to the pending next-round
exclusion set and the saved set persisted in localStorage through gloo storage.
Do not change the current round's URL, active candidate set, cards, or matches
mid-round. Apply the new exclusion only when generating the next practice URL.
A suggested storage key is zipeek.excluded_words; the exact key is not fixed.
Persisting WordIds does not persist hash state or practice scores.

Exclusions have two distinct lifecycle rules:

Generate a URL (setup, Random, Next round): serialize the union of the
saved set and the current round/per-round exclusions. Saved state contributes
here; the emitted URL carries the complete set and is self-contained.

Read a URL (page load, deep link, reload): the round's set is exactly the
query's exclusions. Never union saved exclusions into a loaded URL or rewrite
it implicitly. An absent exclude means the empty set, even if localStorage
contains saved exclusions. A recipient's saved set cannot alter a shared round.

Read saved IDs for URL generation (and display their count in setup), not to
augment loaded rounds. Write saved IDs only on an explicit don't-show-again action
or the explicit Reset action. Loading a shared link must not persist its IDs.
Deduplicate IDs, ignore unknown integer IDs, and drop noninteger entries with a
debug-only warn!. Omit the query parameter when the effective set is empty.

Filter excluded IDs before choosing correct pairs and distractor candidates,
including after each D02 widening step. If fewer than eight candidates remain
after widening, show "not enough words after exclusions - reset exclusions?"
with a button that clears the set. The setup screen also shows
"Excluded words: N · Reset". Clicking Reset on setup clears saved and pending
exclusions and generates a new practice URL with exclude omitted. It does not
silently rewrite an in-progress round when a word is marked.

Offset progression (D13: approved)
New unseeded Fixed and Endless sessions from setup default to offset 0. Without
wrapping, a fresh session's zero-based round r uses offset = r * 4: displayed
round 1 starts at 0, round 2 at 4. Deep links/reloads retain their entered offset
even when in-memory progress restarts. Next round advances nominal offset by four.
Fixed stops after the selected number of
rounds and shows the summary; Play again starts at a fresh random in-pool offset
under D35. Endless continues.

If offset + 4 > pool_size, wrap to offset 0 and show a small
"pool exhausted, looping" hint once. Strict slices without sliding are distinct
until exhaustion. D12's duplicate-label sliding and widened-view offset-zero
fallback can overlap correct sets even before wrapping. The eight-candidate minimum
and visible-label rules still apply. Fixed completion must track completed rounds
separately from the wrapping offset, as specified below.

Fixed progress, reload, and seeded Next round (D15)
Fixed mode keeps completed/current-round progress and total rounds in memory.
Initialize completed progress to zero (display round 1/N); stop after N completed
rounds. Do not persist progress. Reload resets that counter while honoring the
URL's pool offset: a bookmarked offset 40 does not imply round 11. Wrapping the
pool to offset zero mid-session leaves progress unchanged, such as round 4/5.

For seeded Endless, Next round clears seed, retains the same filter, and
generates an unseeded URL. All v1 variants match four pairs, so advance by 4:
the seeded normalized offset is zero and Next starts at 4, subject to normal
pool-exhaustion handling. Do not advance by one for v1. Freshly generated URLs
fold in saved/pending exclusions per D13; the current seeded URL is unchanged
until that navigation.

MCQ practice (D20: approved)
D20 is approved on 2026-10-26. Each question presents one prompt and exactly
three answer options: one correct answer and two distractors (N=2).

Variant token	Prompt	Answer label
hanzi-to-meaning	Simplified hanzi	First English gloss
meaning-to-hanzi	First English gloss	Simplified hanzi
meaning-to-pinyin	First English gloss	Display pinyin
Routes are /practice/mcq/<variant> as listed above. A21 declares all three paths
and connects their preparation/loading pipeline; gameplay remains A10.

Use the same HSK/PoS filtering, exclusions, deterministic URL principles, and
D02/D12 widening/answer-label uniqueness rules, adapted to two distractors.
All three variants require English, so apply D18 eligibility rules. D19 fixes
MCQ prompt selection, two distractor samples, and final option shuffle on one
continuous RNG stream. A07 implements all six variants' pure round data and
native/wasm golden tests; A21 declares MCQ routes, while controls/gameplay remain A10 work.

Support Endless and Fixed. Fixed offers 5/10/20 questions, default 10, with
session progress kept independently of the pool offset. Advance the nominal
offset by one per question; matching continues to advance by four per round.
Endless has no Fixed summary. UX-MCQ01 now specifies immediate feedback, one
locked selection, number-key badges/shortcuts, Continue gating and adaptive
answer layout; see [UX](UX.md#mcq-interaction-ux-mcq01). These are A10
implementation requirements. The first A10 milestone implements them for all
three Endless variants, including the in-session streak/correct counters,
secondary traditional text, Listen and offset/seed progression. Fixed MCQ and
its summary are now implemented under D35. Fixed progress uses completed/total
above the prompt, independently of the pool offset. The last Continue captures
completion instead of navigating to an extra question. First-attempt is correct
first selections / total questions; Mistakes counts each locked wrong selection.
Time runs from first render to final Continue without pausing when hidden and
freezes on completion; Highest streak records the session maximum. All four stats
are DOM text beside the local Chart.js accuracy ring. Play again retains mode,
count/filter/exclusions at a fresh random offset; Back to setup restores defaults.
Leaving/reloading loses scores/progress without confirmation or resume.

Landing and theme
Show exactly three navigation tiles: Practice, Browse, Random.

Random starts the approved shortcut described above (D04).

Show a Word of the Day card using the approved selection below (D05).
The field order is HSK/PoS badges, large simplified hanzi, muted traditional
hanzi, accent pinyin and first English gloss; add Listen near hanzi/pinyin.
Daily and practice pronunciation uses browser speech synthesis (D32), reading
the represented word's simplified hanzi with zh-CN under the supplied fallback
rule. Voice availability/quality varies; there are no new DB fields/audio assets.
Match cards and MCQ hanzi/pinyin surfaces offer the same control.
See [UX](UX.md#pronunciation-d32) for surface and accessibility requirements.

Use the shared left sidebar, theme controls, and footer described below.

App shell, theme selection, and footer
Provide a collapsible left drawer and permanent top panel across routes (D25).

Dark is the preferred/default theme when the user has no saved selection.
Offer an explicit dark/light toggle at the top-right of the top panel (D25).
Restore a saved choice ahead of the default and persist changes in localStorage
using the existing boolean storage key and browser storage facilities.

Apply the same selected theme to the static HTML loading shell, Yew's initial
loading view, and the ready app. Avoid a light flash during startup or route changes.

A22 shell amendment (2026-10-27): move the existing GitHub icon from the drawer
to the footer, linking to https://github.com/Jozefpodlecki/zipeek. Retain its
"Zipeek repository on GitHub" accessible name, target="_blank",
rel="noopener noreferrer", simple_icons icon and existing licence notice.
Navigation links show labels only: no numbers or visual active-route decoration;
keep aria-current="page" as the sole active indication.

Include a footer with Jozef Podlecki and the copyright symbol/year, for
example © 2026 Jozef Podlecki. Use the current year when implementing it.
Copyright, dictionary attribution and GitHub icon form one dot-separated footer
row. A35 implements the row with the user-approved attribution wrapping inside
its item on narrow screens; the app does not force the full text onto one line.

D24/A27 implements the slate/blue shell; D25/A28 adds the permanent top panel
and collapsible drawer, removes decorative headers and fixes accidental overflow.
A29 removes decorative tile arrows, reduces panel/footer height and makes the
theme control borderless, retaining its visible keyboard-focus indication.
D26/A30 keeps the existing landscape behind loading and ready views in both
themes, with translucent readable surfaces and a centered loading panel.
The shell retains
saved theme and attribution footer. HTML and Yew use dark by default and honor
saved light. The landing arrangement and navigation tiles are present; the
daily-word area uses the agreed unavailable copy until A06/A12 supplies actual
selection data. A11 implements the six-activity setup and canonical Start links.
A21 prepares deterministic practice rounds from dictionary
queries; playable controls are implemented by A09/A10. Browse
and Random remain feature placeholders without their feature queries.

When dictionary data is served, show this attribution in the visible site footer,
with links to the project and licence:

Chinese dictionary data from CC-CEDICT (cc-cedict.org), licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

See DB for primary/fallback source notices
and the pinned import rules. D16 supplies PoS and frequency when available;
genuinely missing metadata remains NULL. D18's complete, case-insensitive
source-code mapping defines canonical PoS tokens; entries with unknown codes are
excluded during import with a warning. Do not infer missing values or display raw
source codes as app enum tokens.

No unresolved default in DECISIONS is an implementation requirement yet.

Word of the Day (D05: approved)
Select deterministically from the full word pool, independently of practice
HSK/PoS filters. Read the browser's local calendar date using js_sys::Date and
format it as yyyy-mm-dd; do not substitute a UTC calendar date.

Count the full word pool using COUNT(*).

If the count is zero, show the neutral placeholder "No word available".
Do not compute modulo zero or panic.

Hash the UTF-8 date string and reduce the hash modulo the word count.

Pick that offset in a deterministically ordered result. D07 uses synthetic
IDs, so use ORDER BY simplified, pinyin, whose unique natural key resolves
ties. This is D05's generic hanzi ordering mapped to the physical schema.
Never use LIMIT 1 OFFSET n without deterministic ordering.

The same local date, pool, ordering, and hash implementation produce the same
selection. Data regeneration may change the pool or ordering and thus the word.

Use 64-bit FNV-1a over the UTF-8 date bytes (D14): initialize h to offset
basis 0xcbf29ce484222325; for each byte, apply h ^= byte as u64 then
h = h.wrapping_mul(0x100000001b3). Implement as a small dependency-free Rust
const fn. Use u64, not
usize, for hash arithmetic and modulo reduction so 32-bit and 64-bit builds
agree; convert only the bounded result where indexing requires it.

DefaultHasher is allowed only for ephemeral in-session use such as a HashMap.
It is forbidden for Word of the Day and any value that must reproduce across
builds or upgrades. Do not persist hash state anywhere. No hash dependency is needed.

If the DB fails to load, show the same "No word available" placeholder plus a
retry button. An empty successfully loaded pool does not require the failure-only
retry state.

For reproducible e2e, support the testing-only override /?wotd=2026-10-26 to force
that local calendar date. Gate date-override behaviour behind
#[cfg(debug_assertions)]; debug e2e can use cfg!(debug_assertions) consistently.
Release builds may parse the query string but ignore wotd entirely: it has zero
behavioural effect in Pages deploys. No testing Cargo feature is needed for v1;
introducing one for release testing later requires a separate approved change.

Validate exact yyyy-mm-dd formatting, calendar validity, and supported date range.
An invalid override, such as 2026-13-40, silently falls back to the real browser
local date. Do not panic or show a page error. An optional warn! is allowed only
in debug builds. Use the valid override to assert a specific word in e2e. No Clock
trait is required.

# Source-to-documentation reconciliation

**Inspection date:** 2026-11-09. **Baseline:** `zipeek-R282-WIP-documentation-consolidation-20261109-153451.zip`. This is a source-to-documentation review, not a Rust/Chrome execution report.

## Method and precedence

Implementation statements were checked against relevant Rust/JS source, `Cargo.toml`, `package.json`/lockfiles, `schema.sql`, `Makefile.toml` and the installed JSON manifest. Earlier release contracts are preserved as historical rationale, not reinterpreted as present runtime behavior. For product intent, pending decisions remain explicitly proposals. ## Resolved documentation drift

- Replaced original HSK-only/single-table claims with the normalized generator schema and CC-CEDICT expansion.
- Replaced historical 12,100-row artifact figures in current guides with the **installed manifest's declaration of 12,188 words**. Previous run counts remain historical evidence.
- Corrected runtime package documentation to the installed **`1.33.1-dev114.0`** pin, without changing dependencies or silently amending approved policy.
- Restored the current six Settings tabs and nine-field serialized preferences contract instead of the old five-tab design.
- Replaced R54 model-authored word-bank claims with application-owned canonical answer tiles and the UUID translation Practice workflow.
- Updated current Browse documentation: the normalized search endpoint is connected; the “not yet connected” statement was obsolete.
- Removed current-facing use of retired `crates/db-gen` paths in generator/testing docs; old paths remain only in historic decisions and completion logs.
- Rewrote personal-storage documentation to distinguish `localStorage`, JSON backups and OPFS probes from non-existent persistent pedagogical history.
- Separated root/Pages browser acceptance evidence from the latest unexecuted translation integration.

## Unresolved issues requiring code/artifact or policy decisions

1. **DuckDB-WASM pin reconciled (2026-11-09):** the user explicitly approved `1.33.1-dev114.0`. D08 and AGENTS now name the exact installed version; the former `1.32.0` pin is retained only as historical provenance. No dependency or artifact bytes were changed in this documentation pass.
2. **Manifest table inventory:** `crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/schema.sql` declares `character_readings` and `src/artifact/writer.rs` bulk-copies it; the checked-in manifest `tables` list lacks this table. Verify the actual binary (and manifest report generator) before claiming an installed `character_readings` query is supported. Do not regenerate or alter the database solely for documentation.
3. **Acceptance gap:** Latest translation-only UUID Practice integration and the full root/Pages E2E matrix lack user-provided Windows passing results for that exact source. Previous Windows results cover the 31 E2E library unit tests, accessibility, Browse and an older standalone live AI translation path. Do not carry them forward as proof of the new journey.
4. **Architecture proposals:** Remaining unapproved technical choices are tracked in [active tasks](../../project-management/tasks.md). Retired UX requests are not active specifications.
5. **Legacy archived records:** `docs/process/completed/`, `docs/process/decisions/`, `docs/archive-history/RELEASE_HISTORY.md`, and dated mockups describe their own historical state. Their old paths, counts and dependency choices are retained for traceability, never treated as active contracts.

## Verification scope

This pass updates documentation only. It does not change Rust, JS, Cargo, manifest, DuckDB or E2E source. Link and repository checks are recorded below; tests listed in source were not executed by this audit. **Completeness boundary:** this mapping covers major implemented features and known contracts, but is not a formal proof that every line of every historical product document exactly matches runtime code. Where a discrepancy could not be settled by source inspection, it remains openly listed here.


Final documentation scan: 709 local Markdown links checked, 0 missing targets. Node source suite: 661 passed, 14 pre-existing failures (675 total). Source comparison against the input ZIP: 28 modified Markdown/release-note files, 1 new Markdown files, 0 removed files and 0 non-document byte changes.

## Additional product-direction reconciliation (2026-11-09)

The [Courses mosaic specification](../../learning-practice/courses/courses-mosaic.md) defines the target behavior. The older concept image has been retired because it no longer represents the current UI. The specification is approved future requirements, **not current shipped features**. Current source [`pages/learning/courses/listing.rs`](../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/learning/courses/listing.rs) still presents a card catalogue and `progress_store.rs` (retired location) stores a list of completed Pinyin lesson slugs. Course-point assessments, mosaic geometry and permanent grammar-cell reveal are not there.

The user also approved the direction of [session-first pedagogical history](../../learning-practice/practice/learning-evidence.md): derived per-Hanzi, exercise, category, HSK and grammar observations, a minimum seven-day observation window, ten encounters across multiple sessions and demonstrated recognition/listening/speaking/sentence-use. The current implementation does not write these records. Detailed scoring, number of distinct sessions, audio reliability and retention rules remain unresolved. The source-to-documentation audit treats these policies as future design, not implemented runtime contracts.

## R526 source map follow-up

The earlier source mapping above contains references to modules that no longer exist at their original paths. The old `zipeek-ai` crate has been split, and Courses progress implementation has moved. The associated behavioral assertions are historical and require a dedicated source reconciliation before being treated as current evidence.
