# Architecture

Current architecture overview for the R285 WIP source tree. This file describes code boundaries, not older proposals or historical release snapshots. Approved future behavior is documented in [Product](../../../product-ux/product.md), [UX](../UX.md) and [Tasks](../../../project-management/tasks.md).

## Workspace

The root Cargo workspace contains:

| Package | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `zipeek-web` | Yew CSR application, router, shell, components, browser services and orchestration |
| `zipeek-core` | Shared vocabulary types and deterministic round-domain primitives |
| `zipeek-exercises` | Practice definitions, validated setup drafts and pure exercise/session domains |
| `zipeek-ai-protocol` | Authored prompts and validation of model responses, including sentence analysis and generated exercise contracts |
| `zipeek-ai-core` | New provider-neutral generation request, validation and streamed event contract; no backend connected yet |
| `zipeek-ai-server` | Injectable HTTP chat-completion transport with JSON/SSE and restricted CORS; executable/model runtime still unimplemented |
| `zipeek-ai-client` | OpenAI-compatible HTTP transport for native and WASM clients |
| `zipeek-db` | Native/WASM database infrastructure, typed queries and personal-storage probe |
| `zipeek-db-gen` | Native generator for the read-only DuckDB dictionary and manifest |
| `zipeek-ui`, `zipeek-browser` | UI and browser-specific reusable functionality |
| `zipeek-hanzi-writing` | Pure Hanzi stroke/ink geometry |
| `zipeek-themes` | Theme providers and resolution |
| `zipeek-e2e` | Managed Chrome E2E harness, scenarios and in-process Rust AI fixture |
| `zipeek-image-server` | Optional local image service |
| `zipeek-cli` | Clap command orchestration, asset preparation, source pack/unpack, dictionary publication tooling |
| `zipeek-static-server` | Tokio/Axum server for already-built static Trunk assets, supporting root and Pages prefixes |

`Cargo.toml` is authoritative for current members. Tool/version pins are enforced by manifests and lockfiles, not historical documentation.

## Grammar learning ownership (R492 WIP)

`zipeek-pedagogy::grammar` is the authoritative static Grammar catalogue, slug mapping and region plan for 100 draft courses. `zipeek-exercises::grammar_learning` provides pure step, recall and answer-transition rules without Yew dependencies. `zipeek-web` maps these to a local reducer, route-specific learning components and browser-local progress persistence, while both course engines reuse `GrammarLessonScaffold`. The web layer has no generated Grammar curriculum tables. Two separate pedagogical lesson engines remain; no mastery inference or HSK verification has been added. Rust/WASM/browser acceptance is pending.

## Runtime

`crates/zipeek-web/index.html` supplies the static loading shell and packaged asset references. Trunk builds the Yew/WASM app, which mounts the router and providers. Shared global state includes theme, dictionary readiness, Word Sets and exercise contexts. The app uses the `/#/` hash router for static hosting and `/zipeek/` as the Pages base path.

The database transport loads the generated compressed/verified artifact under `crates/zipeek-web/static/`. DuckDB-WASM opens it read-only and serves typed queries to Browse and Practice. Debug reads typed storage statistics through the database service and, in development builds only, offers an Overview/DuckDB/SQL tabbed view with a 100-row bounded SELECT terminal against the packaged read-only dictionary. Its SQL parser guardrails are not a security sandbox and it never connects to personal OPFS data. The displayed generator storage-compatibility version is manifest metadata, not proof of the WASM engine's default physical file storage version. Native generator and browser engine versions are distinct from manifest storage compatibility metadata.

## Practice and AI data flow

The learner selects Practice options in the four-step setup. `zipeek-exercises::practice_draft` validates choices. Every supported Practice start creates a UUID v7 session in `PracticeSessionStore`, then navigates to `/practice/session/:id`. The only Practice routes are `/practice` and `/practice/session/:id`. The session stores a shared typed configuration map and per-step configuration references; old standalone exercise routes have been intentionally removed. `practice_generated.rs` generates a validated sentence using Settings-owned AI endpoint/model and saved direction; `pages/practice/generated_session.rs` renders its tiles, obtains model evaluation and sends a scored result to the host. `pages/practice/local_session.rs` manages advancement, interruption, restoration and completion cleanup.

The generation request carries a reproducible sampled vocabulary pool of at most ten entries. Model output is a Chinese and English sentence pair; Zipeek constructs sentence tiles and their canonical answer metadata. Other exercise families retain their dedicated runtime boundaries where applicable. The standalone sentence generation route and the free-text translator are not the same as UUID-backed Practice.

## Storage boundaries

- Generated dictionary: immutable/read-only DuckDB asset, manually regenerated and installed.
- Preferences and non-secret AI settings: `zipeek.preferences.v1` localStorage.
- Personal Word Sets/course progress/exclusions: separate localStorage categories with JSON backup and explicit deletion.
- Unfinished UUID Practice: `zipeek.practice.session.v1.*`, removed after finishing.
- Optional API key: tab-memory only.
- Personal OPFS/DuckDB: diagnostics/snapshot/probe and an R283 opt-in Practice-outcome writer checkpoint; the latter is not yet browser-verified.

## Testing and deployment

The Rust E2E harness owns test servers, isolated Chrome sessions and a Rust AI fixture. The separate [native AI transport](../../../architecture/modules/ai-server.md) is not yet a running model service. Test cases cover concrete routes under local root and Pages base paths. `cargo make e2e-full` compiles WASM and test targets before Chrome execution. See [E2E](../e2e.md), [data flow](../../../architecture/modules/data-flow.md), [DB](../../../dictionary-data/schema/db.md) and [current acceptance](../../../project-management/current.md).

### Practice setup boundaries (R286 WIP)

`pages/practice/setup/page.rs` coordinates the setup reducer and page panels. Its sibling `validation.rs` computes launch eligibility without UI state changes, `launch.rs` owns route and session launch effects, `profiles.rs` owns the Yew profile controls while delegating persistence to `services/practice_profiles.rs`, and `session_recovery.rs` renders the existing-session recovery screen. The authoritative duplicate-session check remains in `PracticeSessionStore::create()`. This source-level refactor still requires WASM compilation and Chrome journey acceptance.

## Source grouping update (2026-11-10 WIP)

Cloud Match has a feature entry point at `crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/learning/games/cloud_match/mod.rs`; its private HUD and vocabulary-loading helpers are now `games/cloud_match/game/hud.rs` and `games/cloud_match/vocabulary.rs`. The `games/mod.rs` facade exports `CloudMatchPage`, not those implementation helpers. The vocabulary helper still calls the shared game-pair mapper in `games/pairs.rs`; data loading, reducer ownership, and runtime behavior have not deliberately changed.

Cloud Match E2E probes reside in `crates/zipeek-e2e/tests/cloud_match_scripts.rs` and are used by `game_interactions.rs`. The JavaScript behavior probes have standalone Node regression checks in `scripts/cloud-e2e-probes.test.cjs`. The existing `tests/suites` modules remain shared through multiple integration-test parents and have not been migrated into the library, since that requires Rust target-level compilation. Practice-session schema validation is now implemented in `services/practice_session_store/validation.rs`, with the session model, transitions, and browser storage adapter still in `services/practice_session_store.rs`. The generation transition methods share a finished-step guard. The extraction has source-contract coverage but still requires Rust compilation plus serialized-schema and revision/recovery acceptance before separating persistence.

## R333 WIP: pedagogical domain foundation

The newly approved `zipeek-pedagogy` crate houses a source-only, pure Rust recognition acquisition projection for future Dragon Progression. It currently has no dependencies or runtime integrations. Its 10×7 rules are documented in [pedagogy](../../../dictionary-data/schema/pedagogy.md). The existing R259 multi-skill learning engine remains in `zipeek-exercises`; no authoritative personal DuckDB, `/stats` route or browser worker has been activated by this change. The domain and browser worker execution host are intentionally separate boundaries.

## R336 pedagogy analysis coordinator (WIP)

`zipeek-pedagogy::worker` now provides a platform-neutral job state machine. Requests carry a stable ID and an assessment as-of UTC timestamp; duplicate IDs with different payloads are rejected. The coordinator reads committed recognition history through the existing `EvidenceJournal` boundary and publishes only successful `RecognitionProjection` calculations. Retry attempts are capped at three, with due-time scheduling and a visible failure state; explicit retry is required after exhaustion. Disabling processing pauses queued work.

This is **not** the browser Web Worker implementation. A separate WASM worker host must initialize the Rust runtime in a worker context, establish typed messaging, coordinate with the existing DuckDB-WASM worker, and recover a durable queue. There is no new database schema, runtime dependency, automatic evidence collection or UI attachment in R336.

## R344 Statistics dashboard boundary (WIP)

The `/stats` route is a dictionary-independent Yew page with Overview, Hanzi, Skills, History and Insights sections. It currently renders an explicit unassessed state and a link to personal storage Settings. It does not read personal DuckDB, initialize the Rust/WASM worker, infer recognition proficiency from game outcomes, or publish acquisition awards. Future authoritative projections require verified committed evidence, host-side consent, single-tab ownership and the existing learning-domain acceptance gates before attaching live data.

## R346 WIP: Rust browser worker monitor boundary

`zipeek-pedagogy::monitor` is the platform-neutral read-only health-request state machine; it verifies version, correlation, expiry, health fields and shutdown without using browser APIs. `zipeek-browser::pedagogy_worker` owns the temporary module Worker, event listeners, timeout and termination. Yew Settings calls the Rust browser adapter directly. `static/pedagogy-worker/worker.mjs` is only the WASM loader, buffering requests until initialization and returning correlated startup errors. The separate Rust/WASM worker binary owns the permanent `DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope` message listener, request decoding, single disabled-by-default `WorkerEndpoint`, and response serialization; the browser host remains a read-only diagnostic client. The separate worker is built cross-platform via `zipeek-cli build pedagogy-worker` (exact wasm-bindgen 0.2.130, locked release build); Pages CI runs this before Trunk copies `static/`. The monitor exposes only `get_health` and is not the evidence analysis coordinator. The main application's worker status button does not consent to tracking, connect to OPFS, persist jobs, or award learning progress. Real browser and WASM acceptance remain pending.

## R349 WIP: typed worker binary and first-run diagnostics

`zipeek-web` now declares `[[bin]] pedagogy_worker` with an explicit `src/bin/pedagogy_worker/mod.rs` path. `browser.rs` is the only module depending on browser globals; `runtime.rs` validates and dispatches the Rust endpoint; `wire.rs` holds Serde v1 envelopes and stable health/result/error codes; `error.rs` defines typed errors; `evidence.rs` converts recognition DTOs without treating caller-supplied `snapshot_verified` as a proof of durability. The browser JS loader is unchanged. Rust worker still starts disabled. Do not activate analysis based on first-run preferences alone.

The first-run landing form chooses one of the six existing theme presets and stores an inert, default-off pedagogical opt-in preference. Settings permits changing/revoking that preference. Neither UI writes recognition evidence, enables the worker nor alters OPFS ownership. The debug-only dictionary SQL terminal is bounded and read-only, with a tabular result and CSV export of the displayed (at most 100) rows. A fresh WASM database storage-version probe is **not implemented**: the loaded dictionary's manifest compatibility value and engine `version()` are not equivalent to independently reading a newly created database file's physical storage format.

## R470 WIP: Vocabulary curriculum ownership

`zipeek-pedagogy::curriculum` now owns the static 100-region Vocabulary catalogue and typed region identity, domain and membership fields. The existing `zipeek-web` course route consumes it through the workspace dependency already present. `zipeek-exercises` continues to own exercises, not region metadata; the dictionary lookup and personal Word Set provider remain in the web application. This is a code ownership change, **not** completed thematic or HSK coverage. A pinned-source audit script reports gaps; the future fully authored curriculum needs entry-level identities and semantic review before coverage claims. No dependencies, stored browser format, or data generator inputs changed.

## R471 WIP: exhaustive HSK Vocabulary source membership

`zipeek-pedagogy::curriculum::VOCABULARY_REGIONS` is a deterministic generated Rust catalogue holding 100 distinct region definitions, 11,494 pinned HSK source indices, 12,188 distinct (Hanzi, numeric-pinyin) keys, unique simplified spellings and per-region source HSK counts. The pinned fingerprint and the last recorded assignment audit are retained in `docs/learning-practice/VOCABULARY_COVERAGE.json`; the former Python generators were removed in R493 and require a native replacement before source changes; machine-classification exceptions are recorded in `docs/learning-practice/VOCABULARY_REVIEW_QUEUE.csv`. Source coverage and semantic editorial acceptance are separate.

`zipeek-web` resolves each region through batched parameterized `Database::words_by_simplified` queries, validates complete unique dictionary IDs and exposes up to 200 words per personal Word Set. The browser Word Sets limit is 250; its serialized structure is unchanged. Dictionary acquisition now matches both simplified spelling and numeric pinyin, so distinct source readings remain independently acquirable. Dictionary runtime matching still needs live verification against the generated bundle. No new dependencies or generated dictionary bundle were introduced.

# Speaking capture, waveform and contextual targets (R66)

**Status:** browser microphone capture, live amplitude visualization, local playback,
and discard are implemented on the experimental `#/practice/speaking` route.
No pronunciation assessment, persistence, or upload exists. The
`zipeek-exercises::definition::SPEAKING` contract is reserved for the future scored exercise.

## Domain boundaries

- `zipeek-exercises`: speaking exercise definition/instance and future pronunciation evidence; a waveform is not a pronunciation score.
- `zipeek-browser/src/microphone/`: browser permission, capture, MediaRecorder, Web Audio analysis, 30-second limit, playback URL, generation checks and release of tracks. This is Rust using `web-sys`; no JavaScript recorder module remains.
- `zipeek-web/src/components/audio/speaking_recorder/`: Yew controls, status, errors, playback UI and callback lifetimes. The bindings adapter passes callback functions to `zipeek_browser::microphone::MicrophoneRecorder` and disposes it on unmount.
- Future opt-in speech assessment is outside this local-only recorder.

The recorder is a single-field tuple struct wrapping shared Rust lifecycle state.
The Rust implementation is divided into `recorder.rs` (public API), `state.rs`
(resource ownership and callbacks), `capture.rs` (MediaRecorder and permission
flow), `waveform.rs` (frame sampling), and `error.rs` (browser error mapping).
`mod.rs` exports the recorder without implementing all of those concerns.
The lifecycle phase is a typed `RecordingPhase` enum internally, converted to
legacy status strings only when invoking the Yew callback.
`BlobEvent::data()` returns `Option<Blob>` in the pinned `web-sys`; missing or
empty blobs are ignored rather than unwrapped before adding chunks. It retains the original `idle`, `requesting`, `recording`, `processing`, `ready` and `error` states. The permission request starts only from a user gesture. Late permission grants are rejected using an increasing generation token; tracks from obsolete grants are stopped immediately. Unmount/discard releases MediaRecorder handlers, audio context, animation frame, deadline and object URL.

The previous `crates/zipeek-web/src/services/microphone.js` has been removed. `scripts/translation.test.cjs` asserts the Rust contracts; actual permission denial, capture and stop/discard behavior still need browser validation.

## Microphone-to-waveform pipeline

1. Ask for microphone access only after pressing Record; support permission
   denial, unavailable devices, insecure origins and concurrent recording.
2. Attach the `MediaStream` to a Web Audio `AudioContext` and `AnalyserNode`
   with a small FFT window. Sample time-domain data with
   `getFloatTimeDomainData`; calculate windowed RMS or peak amplitude.
3. At `requestAnimationFrame` cadence, append an amplitude observation to a
   bounded ring buffer. Render vertical bars centered on a baseline, with
   approximate 20-40 updates per second. This is an **amplitude waveform**,
   not an FFT/spectrogram (frequency visualization is different).
4. Capture audio separately through `MediaRecorder`, with runtime MIME support
   detection and a bounded recording duration. `MediaRecorder` and Web Audio
   may share the same `MediaStream`, but their lifecycles are independent.
5. On Stop, navigate-away or component unmount, stop media tracks and release
   the recorder/audio context/animation frame. Do not assume cancelling a
   visualizer also stops a microphone recording.
6. Preserve the last amplitude bars with browser-native playback controls after
   recording. A player may seek through the captured audio; amplitude bars are
   purely presentational and must not be treated as a measure of speaking skill.
   Elapsed-time display and waveform seeking are follow-up tasks.

## UI and accessibility

A SoundCloud-like row of centered vertical bars can visualize the user's
speech. Provide visible Record, Stop, Play and Discard controls plus elapsed
recording time and a textual status for screen readers. Use a neutral idle
waveform, respect reduced motion, display a clear recording/permission state,
and provide a fallback when Web Audio is unsupported. Always distinguish
**recorded** from **evaluated**; never imply that a decorative waveform is an
assessment. Avoid autoplay and automatic cloud uploads.

## API / dependency policy

No Rust crate, npm package, `web-sys` feature flag, or dependency pin was added.
The Rust browser adapter uses `web-sys` browser APIs and the existing
`wasm-bindgen` dependency. Chromium browser and wasm32
compilation still require local verification. Extract a separate audio crate
only if reusable signal processing and capture-domain contracts warrant it;
`zipeek-exercises` must not depend on microphone APIs.

`crates/zipeek-web/src/components/audio/audio_waveform.rs` remains a presentational 40-bar
SVG renderer with clamped amplitude input. Microphone samples are never stored
as vocabulary proficiency evidence, and there is no implicit speech upload.
title: Speaking capture, waveform and contextual targets (R66)

# AI client boundary (R208)

`zipeek-ai-client` is a native-and-browser-WASM OpenAI-compatible HTTP client implemented in Rust with `reqwest =0.13.5`. `lib.rs` only declares modules and re-exports the public API. Internals are split by responsibility:

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `src/client.rs` | `AiClient(ClientConfig)`; HTTP POST, SSE response assembly, configurable progress callback, native five-minute total deadline, and connection diagnostics |
| `src/config.rs` | URL validation, `/v1/chat/completions` construction, credential and insecure-remote-HTTP safeguards |
| `src/protocol.rs` | Serde request and response wire types |
| `src/stream.rs` | Incremental SSE parser handling network chunk and UTF-8 boundaries, completion markers, output limits and malformed streams |
| `src/prompts.rs` | Translation directions, source checks, translation and connection-test messages |
| `src/error.rs` | Status-specific errors, provider JSON parsing, bounded/redacted diagnostic text |

There is **no JavaScript HTTP transport**, wasm-bindgen HTTP binding or platform-specific stub. `reqwest` uses browser Fetch on WASM and the native async HTTP stack on desktop. The already-existing web `services/ai/config.js` remains solely for settings and tab-memory API-key storage; `zipeek-web/src/services/ai/mod.rs` passes the key per request, without storing it in `AiClient`.

`zipeek-ai-protocol` is the pure sentence-analysis contract owner: it builds structured-analysis prompts, parses returned JSON, validates vocabulary and grammar against exact source/translation spans, and builds repair prompts. The web service still orchestrates the structured request, one repair, and plain-translation fallback when a provider rejects structured output with HTTP 400/422. No analysis fields or SQL have moved into the HTTP client.

## Endpoint and browser restrictions

The Rust client rejects non-HTTP(S) URLs, URL-embedded credentials, query/fragment in the base URL, and API-key transmission over non-loopback HTTP. Native builds configure a five-minute overall request deadline on `reqwest::Client` to allow slow local model generation. **The browser reqwest adapter does not expose `ClientBuilder::timeout` on wasm32**: the browser client therefore does not enforce that five-minute deadline. Streaming progress still works, but a separate target-independent timeout/cancellation design is needed before promising bounded browser requests. Native builds use an explicit no-redirect policy. The WASM `reqwest` adapter does not offer the same redirect configuration: browser Fetch may follow redirects; the client rejects responses whose final URL differs from the requested URL, but this is an **after-the-request check**, not a guarantee that the browser did not forward a request. Prefer a direct trusted `/v1/` endpoint. Standard browser CORS, mixed-content, and HTTPS rules still apply.

The default request contract uses `stream: true` and consumes `text/event-stream` using `reqwest::Response::bytes_stream`. A provider that returns a conventional JSON completion despite requesting streaming is also accepted without an extra model call. SSE frames are bounded and must terminate with `[DONE]` or a `finish_reason`; an incomplete response is rejected. The client exposes `complete_streaming(messages, api_key, on_delta)` for progress-aware consumers and retains `complete()` as the assembled-text wrapper. The web translation page and sentence-translation exercise now consume streaming progress. An accessible status widget displays the current phase and observed character count; it does not invent a completion percentage. During structured analysis, partial JSON and private model reasoning are never displayed as final learning content. Models that emit `reasoning_content` can report activity before any answer text appears.

Provider HTTP errors are translated to bounded readable messages. If a provider supplies JSON `error.message` and `error.code`, the message is sanitized, truncated and redacted against the supplied API key and common bearer patterns. Raw HTML and unrecognized error bodies are not shown. The actual configured model may still reject structured analysis because of context length, token budget, or provider capability: a successful plain fallback is not proof that analysis succeeded.

## Deterministic integration fixtures

`tests/fixtures/complex_zh_en.json` and `complex_en_zh.json` include complex concessive/conditional sentences with expected translation, two grammar explanations and three vocabulary items each. These are **hand-authored fixture expectations, not model evaluations**. `tests/http_integration.rs` launches a local TCP HTTP server and checks real reqwest request serialization, authorization headers, HTTP status handling, translation responses and `zipeek_ai_protocol::sentence_analysis::parse` validation for both directions. It exercises a structured HTTP 400 followed by a successful plain translation. These tests run without a live AI model.

`tests/live_model.rs` is ignored by default and invokes a real configured model for both fixture sentences. The detailed analysis uses streaming and prints incremental deltas to stdout with `--nocapture`, so lengthy generation shows progress before completion. It asserts nonempty plain translation and complete schema-valid analysis; it does not claim semantic equivalence to the hand-authored reference translation. A failure here may indicate the model cannot comply with the structured contract even if plain translation succeeds.

### Windows validation

```powershell
cargo test -p zipeek-ai-client --locked
cargo test -p zipeek-ai-client --test http_integration --locked
cargo check -p zipeek-ai-client --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --locked
cargo check -p zipeek-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --locked
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

To exercise your local OpenAI-compatible model (example LM Studio endpoint), from PowerShell:

```powershell
$env:ZIPEEK_AI_ENDPOINT = "http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1/"
$env:ZIPEEK_AI_MODEL = "your-loaded-model-id"
# Optional: $env:ZIPEEK_AI_KEY = "your-key"
cargo test -p zipeek-ai-client --test live_model --locked -- --ignored --nocapture
```

Afterward run the existing managed Chrome Translate Sentence fixture scenarios from `zipeek-e2e`, and manually check the screenshot's structured-analysis rejection against the actual model. Node source tests do not validate Rust compilation or live browser behavior.

## Streaming browser acceptance

The managed E2E AI fixture now accepts both `stream: true` SSE and legacy JSON completions. `translator-streaming` intentionally sends a reasoning delta before delivering a fragmented structured-analysis response, giving the Chrome scenario time to assert the accessible `data-ai-stream-progress` status before the final result. Generation and evaluation fixtures also return SSE to match the real Rust HTTP contract. The fixture's private reasoning text is never displayed by the UI; only its length is surfaced. These Chrome scenarios still require actual Chrome/WebDriver execution.

## R208 typed protocol and structured-analysis contract

`zipeek-ai-client/src/message.rs` defines serializable/deserializable `ChatMessage` and `ChatRole` for ordinary translation and connection tests. The HTTP request and non-streaming response are typed; the SSE decoder deserializes typed per-choice deltas, including opaque reasoning activity counts. The public generic completion entry points continue accepting existing serializable message collections while callers migrate away from `serde_json::Value`.

`zipeek-ai-protocol/src/sentence_analysis/prompt.rs` owns the deliberately explicit translation and linguistic-evidence prompt; `schema.rs` owns the strict provider JSON Schema, and `sentence_analysis.rs` owns the `SentenceAnalysis` domain types and semantic evidence checks. All ten top-level fields are required, including empty enrichment arrays; unknown properties and ungrounded vocabulary/grammar fragments are rejected. The schema requires nested item objects to contain only their declared fields. `estimated_hsk` remains an estimate and may be null.

The Translate Sentence workflow requests OpenAI-compatible `response_format: {type: "json_schema", json_schema: {name: "sentence_analysis", strict: true, schema: ...}}` with streaming. If the provider rejects that format with HTTP 400/422, Zipeek retries the existing pedantic prompt without provider-side schema enforcement, then retains its plain-translation fallback. Partial structured JSON remains hidden until `SentenceAnalysis::parse` succeeds, and a single bounded repair attempt is still supported.

**Limits:** Neither JSON Schema nor substring matching proves correct pinyin or linguistic interpretation. The live Qwen test provided by the user passed both fixture directions in 182.64 seconds on an earlier version; R208's stricter contract and schema negotiation need a fresh native/WASM and live-model run. Dictionary-backed reading verification is a separate future enhancement. Browser provider support for strict JSON Schema varies; schema rejection is not the same as translation failure.
title: AI client boundary (R208)

# Browser dictionary adapter and query ownership

## Implemented boundaries

- [`zipeek-db/src/wasm/`](../../../../crates/zipeek-db/src/wasm) owns the DuckDB-WASM bridge, local worker asset resolution, manifest validation, transport and connection lifetime. It is not a separate `zipeek-db-wasm` crate.
- [`zipeek-web/src/services/database/`](../../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/services/database) owns application-facing typed read-only queries, result projection and metadata. Its runtime SQL remains private; Debug uses `Database::storage_statistics()`.
- [`zipeek-web/src/components/browse/`](../../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/components/browse) drives Browse searches and pagination; [`services/database/browse_queries.rs`](../../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/services/database/browse_queries.rs) implements the active normalized Browse query. This is **not** an unconnected future query proposal.
- [`zipeek-db/src/wasm/probe.rs`](../../../../crates/zipeek-db/src/wasm/probe.rs) is a separate writable personal-data **probe**, not a production learner-history database.

## Runtime and artifact facts

Current web npm pin: **`@duckdb/duckdb-wasm@1.33.1-dev114.0`**; native generator engine `v2.0.0`, explicit disk compatibility `v1.4.0`. The browser engine must be read from the live runtime, not inferred from native versions. The installed manifest declares **12,188** reading rows, not the original 12,100-row snapshot. See [runtime](../../../dictionary-data/schema/runtime.md) and [installed artifact](../../../dictionary-data/schema/db.md) for evidence and the outstanding approval-policy mismatch.

The dictionary uses the packaged local JS/WASM worker and Arrow assets. Source preparation is explicit (`zipeek-cli`/Cargo Make); Trunk deploys prepared assets and loads the timestamped compressed dictionary below the correct `/` or `/zipeek/` base. The dictionary itself is opened read-only and is never the destination for learner outcomes. Browser readiness is owned by the database provider and boundary, with a retry path for failures.

## Real Browse behavior and test boundaries

`BrowseSearchForm` and `BrowseResults` render the active query UI. The service applies typed filters to normalized dictionary tables and orders pages by word ID. Pagination uses the presence of an extra result to establish Next rather than inventing a total count. User-reported Windows E2E results passed Browse word-set discovery, membership, accessibility, empty search, live search and pagination on the earlier R282 source; they do not certify every combination of category/PoS filters in the latest UUID translation build.

## Not yet a supported contract

An optional future adapter-crate extraction and index/FTS redesign are proposals in [target architecture](../../../architecture/modules/target-architecture.md) and [schema review](../../../dictionary-data/schema/review.md). Do not present historical A13/A22 or R12 plans as current limitations in conflict with an implemented Browse query.

See [database schema](../../../dictionary-data/schema/schema.md), [E2E](../e2e.md), [current validation state](../../../project-management/current.md).
title: Browser dictionary adapter and query ownership

# Hanzi stroke reference and guided tracing - R319 WIP

## Architecture

The original reference viewer remains available. The Hanzi Writing workspace now uses the same packaged glyph data to validate handwriting one stroke at a time. It no longer treats every pointer release as a successful stroke.

- `zipeek-hanzi-writing::matching` samples the reference median and candidate trace by arc length. In addition to uniform samples, original reference and candidate vertices are checked against the opposite polyline at matching arc-length fractions, so short hooks and tight curves cannot hide between samples. It checks starting position, ending position, direction (including folded stroke reversals), stroke length, average geometric deviation, and peak deviation in the same normalized canvas coordinates. It deliberately does not independently normalize the two stroke shapes because that would ignore positional errors.
- `zipeek-hanzi-writing::session` owns accepted stroke count, mistakes, rejection reasons, and completion. A rejected stroke does not advance progress. Undo removes one accepted stroke, and Clear resets the session.
- `hanzi_references.rs` owns the shared, once-per-session aggregate fetch and single-character lookup, while `hanzi_writing/practice/stroke_loading.rs` constructs the validated writing session. Requests from a previous character are invalidated on selection changes and stale results are rejected by character identity in the reducer.
- `hanzi_writing/practice/canvas_input.rs` is a pointer-event adapter: it captures/releases pointers and dispatches typed begin, move, finish and cancellation actions. `practice/controller.rs` is the single reducer owning ink, selected character, guide preference, loading status and graded session. Only its finish transition can submit a trace to the pure Rust session. `practice/board.rs` renders the canvas/overlay; `practice/controls.rs` renders action buttons using callbacks owned by the coordinator. A completed pointer gesture is not accepted by itself.
- `HanziWriting` renders the active pen trace on a canvas. An SVG overlay renders canonical stroke outlines. Accepted strokes snap to the exact sourced outline; the next expected outline and its starting point are highlighted when the guide is on. Missing or malformed reference data disables handwriting acceptance.

This is geometric guided tracing against canonical data, not optical recognition of arbitrary handwritten Chinese characters, recognition of alternative stroke order, or a trained handwriting model. The default matching thresholds are engineering starting values and need calibration with real mouse, touch, and stylus input to determine false acceptance and rejection rates.

## Reference data and licensing

The source-only R319 checkpoint deliberately excludes the licensed upstream Hanzi Writer Data distribution and generated `characters.json` reference bundle from pack/unpack; install those assets separately. To regenerate it from the vendored upstream distribution, run from the repository root:

```text
cargo run --locked -p zipeek-cli -- hanzi prepare-references <upstream-json-directory> crates/zipeek-web/static/hanzi-strokes <path-to-ARPHICPL.TXT>
```

For repeatable local setup, run `cargo make prepare-hanzi`; it reuses an existing valid `characters.json` bundle with its manifest and licence. Otherwise `zipeek-cli hanzi prepare` uses `external/hanzi-writer-data/data` and `external/hanzi-writer-data/ARPHICPL.TXT`, cloning a sparse checkout of Hanzi Writer Data with Git when the source directory is absent. Git must be installed and the initial download requires network access. If an incomplete source directory already exists, the command rejects it rather than overwriting it. The Git subprocess runs with the project root as its working directory and a relative checkout destination to avoid Windows extended-length (`\\?\`) destination paths. Clone and final checkout run quietly, suppressing normal Git progress while preserving stderr diagnostics and failure status; sparse-checkout does not request a quiet option. Use `cargo run --locked -p zipeek-cli -- hanzi prepare --force` to regenerate an existing bundle. Source-only ZIPs exclude the licensed upstream inputs and generated stroke bundles.

The Rust importer validates every glyph before writing the single `characters.json` bundle keyed by lower-case Unicode code point, copies the unmodified licence and a modification notice, and writes a manifest with per-glyph and whole-bundle SHA-256 hashes. On a successful write it removes only legacy hex-named per-character JSON assets. Trunk copies `static/hanzi-strokes` into the site. Both browser consumers use the relative `hanzi-strokes/characters.json` URL, cache one shared in-flight fetch for the browser session, and select individual glyphs in memory. A single initial download is approximately 30.7 MB uncompressed for 9,574 glyphs; enable Brotli/gzip at the hosting layer. The browser does not verify SHA-256 at runtime; the manifest is for package integrity verification.

The runtime does not download character data from a third-party CDN. Without packaged data it shows an unavailable state and does not accept strokes. Successful aggregate loads remain cached, while failed aggregate requests are evicted and may be retried from the handwriting workspace. Concurrent requests still share one in-flight fetch.

## Verification

Run `cargo test --locked -p zipeek-hanzi-writing`, `cargo check --locked -p zipeek-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, and `cargo test --locked -p zipeek-e2e --test writing_interactions -- --nocapture` on Windows, after preparing the relevant assets. Inspect stroke orientation and pointer behavior in Chrome. The new E2E scenario also verifies the unavailable-data state if no assets were packaged.

Pure Rust regression tests cover near-correct curves, reverse direction, translated strokes, truncated strokes, unrelated curvature, stroke order, undo, and reset. Browser and real-device calibration is outstanding.
title: Hanzi stroke reference and guided tracing - R319 WIP

# Hanzi writing domain crate - R106

`crates/zipeek-hanzi-writing` is the domain-only foundation for a future Hanzi Drawing exercise. It has no third-party dependencies and does not reference Yew, `web_sys`, HTML canvas, browser events, fonts, or stroke-dataset formats.

## Boundary

- `geometry`: validated two-dimensional points, ordered strokes, extents, CSS-client-to-normalized canvas coordinates, normalized-to-backing coordinates (including high-DPI canvases), deterministic arc-length resampling and translation/uniform-scale normalization.
- `input`: pointer-specific pen capture, duplicate sample suppression, completion, cancellation, undo and clear. It deliberately does not capture pointer events or assign pressure/touch semantics.
- `comparison`: a deterministic order-sensitive geometric distance diagnostic for equal stroke counts. Results are **not** correctness scores, HSK evidence, stroke-order certification, or a basis for grading without calibrated reference data and evaluated thresholds.

## Browser adapter (not implemented)

A Yew component should use a canvas element and pointer events. Read `getBoundingClientRect`, CSS dimensions, and drawing buffer dimensions, then create `CanvasTransform`. Call `client_to_normalized` for samples, record them using `InkCapture`, and on redraw map the normalized values back to backing pixels. Apply pointer capture and handle `pointercancel`, `lostpointercapture`, resize, and device pixel ratio changes. Prevent unwanted touch scrolling only on the drawing surface. Canvas rendering and hit-testing must not become core crate dependencies.

## Future test strategy

Rust unit tests cover pointer lifecycle and coordinate geometry using numeric fixtures, including invalid dimensions, NaN input, duplicate samples, wrong pointers, cancel, resampling, and reversible navigation state. Browser E2E should later verify pointer capture, touch-action, resize/DPR scaling, rendering and undo using controlled pointer events. Real stroke-order assessment needs a separately approved, licensed dataset and measured false-positive/false-negative rates. No DB schema changes are needed for the domain crate.

## R107 - Browser drawing workspace

- Added `/practice/hanzi-writing` as a separate, explicitly **unscored** preview accessible from Practice; the route does not require DuckDB. Character samples are temporary UI fixtures, **not** licensed reference stroke trajectories.
- `crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/hanzi_writing.rs` owns canvas drawing only. It uses `CanvasTransform` to map pointer client coordinates into normalized positions, and `InkCapture` for pointer ownership, duplicate suppression, completion, cancellation, undo, and clear. All completed and active strokes are redrawn from the same model.
- Rendering keeps the 2D backing resolution proportional to device pixel ratio (capped at 2048 pixels) and redraws on window resize, model changes, guide changes, or character selection. Pointer capture keeps a stroke connected when the pointer exits the drawing area. `touch-none` applies only to the writing surface.
- Known follow-ups: browser E2E for pointer capture, lost capture, DPI/resize, and touch; live dictionary vocabulary target selection; sourced stroke datasets, stroke-order feedback and independently validated assessment. Changing the target clears prior ink. No grades, scores, or session ledger writes are produced.

## R319 - Current guided handwriting display

The guided-writing route has a Yew reducer for the active character, in-progress ink, and sequential grading session. The `WritingBoard` owns the rendering surface, while a visual-only `DirectionGuide` previews 25% of the next canonical median using arc-length interpolation, growing to 35% and 50% after successive rejections of the same stroke. A static fading amber stroke replaces the former start dot, and a small start anchor remains. The reducer counts per-stroke rejections and resets the count after acceptance, Undo, Clear or character loading. This overlay is suspended during drawing and playback, does not modify matching thresholds, and does not animate. Browser acceptance and touch/stylus calibration remain pending.

## R510 WIP - Recognition and prompt boundary

`matching.rs` validates endpoint placement, net direction and plausible length before calling `elastic.rs` for constrained dynamic-time-warp alignment and symmetric robust path coverage. The latter relaxes timing/vertex alignment, not stroke identity. `session.rs` checks candidate scores against later reference strokes to give stroke-order feedback; indistinguishable overlaps advance in supplied canonical order. The web reducer exposes `StrokeRejection::message()` without leaking matcher internals into views. No handwriting input leaves the browser.

`WriteHanziOptions` in `zipeek-web` owns three independently persisted boolean prompt flags. `practice_exercise_settings/writing.rs` configures them; `write_hanzi_exercise.rs` renders dictionary-sourced word title metadata and reuses `ListenButton` / `SpeechService` for user-initiated `zh-CN` playback. The `HanziWriting` canvas and stroke loading remain isolated from word metadata. The new strict options format intentionally has no old-format reader.
title: Hanzi writing domain crate - R106

# Target architecture

**Proposal archive, not the actual module map.** This document retains an older extraction plan with former package paths and pin assumptions. The implemented package map is [Architecture](../../../architecture/architecture.md), the current browser adapter is [browser-db](../../../architecture/modules/browser-db.md), and current dependency drift is in [source reconciliation](../SOURCE_RECONCILIATION.md).

Current and proposed workspace/crate structure, the A33 crate extraction
proposal, and the runtime data-flow summary. Part of the
[architecture overview](../../../architecture/architecture.md). Proposed extraction in
[D30](../../../project-management/decisions/process-and-infra.md#d30-extract-browser-database-adapter-proposed).

## Implemented workspace and dependency direction (R69 audit)

The workspace currently contains the following packages:

| Package | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `zipeek` (`crates/web`) | Yew presentation, browser services, local interaction and request lifecycle |
| `db-gen` | Native dictionary importer, offline classification and artifact publication |
| `zipeek-core` | Shared lexical types, deterministic rounds and pure tile operations |
| `zipeek-ai` | Sentence-generation/evaluation contracts and versioned interactive prompts |
| `zipeek-exercises` | Exercise definitions, learner-visible instances, sessions and evidence |
| `zipeek-themes` | Domain-neutral theme resolution and asynchronous asset provider contract |
| `e2e` | Browser acceptance harness and managed test infrastructure |

The intended direction is from application/adapters to domain crates, not the
reverse. The core domain must not depend on Yew, DuckDB, the browser bridge or
LM Studio. `zipeek-exercises` owns the cross-exercise contracts; `zipeek-ai`
uses them for simulated-learner input without becoming the exercise-session
owner. `zipeek-themes` is independent of the quiz engine and image-generation
networking.

Current application adapters include `web/services/translation_instance.rs`
for browser-side tile randomisation and safe exercise-instance projection,
`zipeek-browser/src/microphone/` for permission-gated capture, and
`web/components/audio_waveform.rs` for amplitude presentation. This boundary
keeps source solutions out of AI learner-visible exercise data.

### Deferred browser database extraction

A33 / D30 propose a future `zipeek-db-wasm` crate. **It is not present in the
workspace or approved for implementation by R67.** The proposal remains below
for dependency/feature approval before any relocation. It must preserve the
pinned DuckDB-WASM browser version and existing JS asset packaging.

## Proposed browser database crate extraction (A33)

The A06 services/database module is a reasonable extraction boundary now that
it owns transport, typed decoding and SQL independently of Yew. Unlike an earlier
suggestion of another generic shared-logic crate, this isolates a concrete browser
runtime dependency. Proposed crate: crates/zipeek-db-wasm, package
zipeek-db-wasm. The name, manifest moves and extraction are proposed, not
approved or implemented.

The detailed ownership mapping (current module → proposed owner) lives at
browser-db.md. Summary constraints
from D30:

Retain the existing narrow typed Database facade; move the API first, without
redesigning query semantics or replay.

DatabaseOptions explicitly carries database URL, asset base and relevant
timeouts; the library must not hard-code the app's hosting prefix, inspect
routes or silently select a CDN.

The crate owns resource cleanup and failed-open disposal; the app provider owns
the lifetime of one client and its retry policy. Review an explicit awaited
shutdown operation; Drop alone cannot await cleanup. Do not silently close a
live shared client when one consumer releases its reference.

Keep the library free of Yew, Animato, localStorage, page loading components
and application-global context.

Native gates must still work: worker/JS code is wasm-only, and native open
returns a typed unsupported-target error. Never silently fake a working DuckDB
connection.

The npm dependency stays exactly @duckdb/duckdb-wasm@1.32.0 in web. The crate
does not run npm or copy assets from build.rs. Keep application-controlled
packaging and license notices, and verify wasm-bindgen resolves the relocated
bridge from the new crate's manifest directory.

The existing browser smoke probe's private snippet discovery must be replaced
by an explicit adapter-test entry point, as described in A15.

Before implementation, inventory the exact dependencies needed by the new crate:
zipeek-core, serde, serde_json, thiserror, log, wasm-bindgen,
wasm-bindgen-futures, js-sys and serde-wasm-bindgen as applicable. Keep the
current resolved versions/features. Some remain direct dependencies of web for
other uses; do not blindly move or delete them. Prefer target-specific JS
dependencies where the chosen facade allows it. Any testing/mock dependency must
be named in the plan; no async-trait or general DI framework is approved by
this proposal.

Migration order (proposed)
Complete A15 isolation and preserve a reproducible browser baseline.

Approve the crate name, public facade, exact dependency additions/moves and
native-target strategy; add workspace/path wiring and update Cargo.lock.

Move transport/decoding/private SQL with tests; leave a temporary web re-export
only if useful while callers migrate. Avoid maintaining two implementations.

Keep providers and feature commands in web, injecting the extracted client.
Remove the old service modules after callers use the new boundary.

Run native gates, typed query tests, real worker/read-only/full-file checks,
loading/retry, and actual /zipeek/ build tests. Preserve artifact checksums,
package pins, query ordering and all A07 replay vectors.

The benefit is dependency/test isolation and a stable client boundary; it is not
needed to share pure logic already in core. The cost is another manifest, target
configuration and JS asset integration boundary. Keep it proposed until the user
approves those concrete changes; feature work can use the existing facade meanwhile.

Practice and rounds boundary
Practice state, query state, and component ownership should be documented here
when approved and implemented. Practice setup selects HSK system/level and
Endless or Fixed mode. PoS filtering is supported in URLs; its setup picker is
future work. Practice and Random share one round generator; Random supplies a
whole-DB seed and always uses Endless. Internal candidate reserves never render:
the visible round remains four matched cards per side. See
PRODUCT.

D13 makes unseeded rounds deterministic ordered slices selected by URL offset;
seeded replay instead uses the seed and its HSK context. Canonical URL state carries
mode, Fixed round count when applicable, HSK context, optional canonical PoS set,
exclusions, and either offset or seed. Random emits the seed's PoS. The setup
count choices are 5/10/20 with default 10. Fixed completion tracking must remain
independent of offset wrapping.

Word exclusions are a localStorage-persisted set of WordIds through gloo
storage, serialized into round URLs and applied before generation. Creating a
URL unions saved/current-round exclusions; loading a URL uses only its set, with
absence meaning empty. Persist IDs only on explicit user actions, not on link
load. Marking a new exclusion changes saved/pending state for the next generated
URL, leaving current-round cards, active inputs, and URL unchanged. Setup Reset
clears saved/pending sets and generates a new URL without exclude. This state
is distinct from transient scores and forbidden persisted hash state.

D15 fixes level default 1, rejects malformed/missing/excluded seeds into unseeded
inputs with the same filter/offset, and ignores seeds for Fixed. Validate those
cases before zeroing the offset of a retained seed. Fixed progress is in-memory,
resets on reload, and is independent of the URL's pool position or wrap. Seeded
Next clears its anchor and advances by four as an unseeded Endless round.

ROUND_GENERATION owns the approved D12
algorithm and resolved D19 single-stream/v1 replay contract. The pure build
pipeline owns its one RNG; recovery helpers borrow that stream, and
generation/shuffling continue from its resulting position. The caller supplies
original URL metadata and ordered data, not an independently recovered seed and
newly seeded RNG. A07 supplies full-round native/wasm vectors.

The wasm caller builds three exclusion-clean CandidatePool views with SQL
ORDER BY id ASC; a pure native-testable builder performs all deterministic
selection. URL parsing normalizes seeded offsets to zero. A hand-written ASCII
seed string prefixed zipeek-round-v1 feeds FNV-1a then rand::rngs::ChaCha12Rng
from the existing rand 0.10.3 dependency with its approved chacha feature (D17).
An existing URL whose seed lacks membership uses deterministic, bounded ChaCha
recovery followed by the first eligible id; never the ambient RNG used for a fresh
Random click. Preserve the original seed URL and retain recovery in effective state.
The builder does not touch database, localStorage, clock, or ambient RNG. Sliding
and fallback affect only internal window starts. The approved rand chacha
feature is enabled in zipeek-core after the approved A07 dependency move; the
builder and portable full-round vectors are implemented. Do not add
a separate rand_chacha dependency.

Shared domain crate in the workspace
zipeek-core (D01) provides Word, ExerciseVariant, HSK domain types, and
query types used by web and db-gen. Its scaffold and workspace/path wiring
exist. Word/WordId, HSK system/levels and all 42 PartOfSpeech values are
implemented; practice variants/URL state and the pure round builder are
implemented. SQL query and playable exercise integration remain future work.

The HSK domain distinguishes system from level/tier and supports independent
memberships for HSK 2.0 and HSK 3.0. A single universal integer level cannot
represent that requirement. Hsk3Level::SevenToNine maps the advanced tier to
integer 7 in storage/canonical URLs; 8 and 9 are not separate levels. Remaining
database-query types remain to be designed; SQL storage uses D07's separate
nullable hsk2_level and hsk3_level columns in words.

During development, breaking code/data changes and regeneration are acceptable;
backward compatibility and application/database versioning are not required.
This does not authorize changing pinned dependencies without approval (D10).

Related
Browser database module: browser-db.md.

Shared crate: zipeek-core.md.

Runtime data flow: data-flow.md.

Architecture overview: ARCHITECTURE.md.

## R69 boundary review: shared sessions and authoritative outcomes

`zipeek-exercises` owns domain invariants for sessions and results; the
app-level Yew provider should orchestrate delivery, not duplicate score
validation. R69 adds an atomic completed-result operation to the domain crate.

There are three distinct identities which must not be collapsed:

- **Exercise definition**: versioned input/output contract independent of a question.
- **Exercise instance**: one concrete visible question; may be repeated in later sessions.
- **Submission event**: a unique finalized attempt at an instance within a session;
  retries of the same event must not be counted again.

The current shared provider generates a sequential instance ID at receipt time.
That keeps recorded instance IDs unique, but does not prove event idempotency.
A follow-up needs an explicit source event ID and a submission acknowledgement
before navigation. Until then, the session is a completed-result ledger,
not a durable planner, scheduler or exactly-once delivery queue.

The aggregate `earned/possible` currently mixes Matching pair counts with MCQ
question and Translation evaluation counts. Interpret these as **scored units**,
not a proven cross-exercise proficiency percentage; authoritative per-skill
evidence remains unwired. Browser recording is not a scored exercise.

# Ui Browse State

## Browse feature state (2026-11-04, R41 source refactor)

Browse is composed in `pages/browse.rs`; it no longer owns dictionary queries,
Word Set persistence, or form editing state. Its child components live in
`components/browse/`: `search_form.rs` owns automatic search controls,
`results/mod.rs` selects the status component and owns result-list wiring;
`results/status.rs` renders loading/empty/error states,
`results/word_card.rs` renders typed vocabulary entries, and
`results/pagination.rs` renders page navigation;
`word_set_panel.rs` owns the create/rename/delete/backup input fields.

`BrowseProvider` owns the route-scoped `BrowseState` reducer and abortable
DuckDB query effect. Search requests carry generation IDs, and superseded
responses cannot replace the latest state. Search and Retry both validate the
current saved-set boundary. Missing required Yew provider contexts are treated
as developer invariant violations and unwrapped; storage, query and user-data
failures remain recoverable results.

`WordSetsProvider` owns `WordSetsState` with the saved collection, selected
management target and a single success-or-error feedback state. Its callback
executes validated mutations through `services/word_sets.rs`, writes storage
before committing reducer state, and dispatches a failure without discarding
the previous collection if persistence fails. Delete/import invalidate Browse
rather than automatically displaying unrestricted results. An active saved-set
toggle updates the exact candidate list and resets Browse pagination.

Both providers currently mount only for Browse. Practice Setup still reads the
same localStorage key independently when it mounts; a future cross-route
Word Set provider requires a separately reviewed lifecycle and storage-sync
design. Do not describe this route-local provider as app-global.

The source Browse UI is a pragmatic dropdown/card implementation. It does **not**
implement the D45/A37 canonical chips, strategy control, URL-authoritative
query or numbered-page contracts. D45 approves the modern card/sidebar layout
and preserves the A37 query/URL semantics. A13 retains
that product discrepancy as open implementation work.

### Route composition and component imports (R43 - R45)

Browse's route branch imports `BrowseProvider`, `WordSetsProvider`, and
`DatabaseBoundary` explicitly at module scope. The route uses multiline nested
Yew tags for its provider composition; the providers remain scoped to Browse,
not the entire app. The Browse page and word-card component use readable
multiline callback and optional-action expressions. These edits are source
readability changes only: no provider ownership, event behaviour, or URL
contract is altered. A Node source-layout regression check covers the route
shape; Rust/Chrome checks remain local validation steps.

### Browse results component boundaries (2026-11-04)

The Browse input form observes query text, filter values and saved-set snapshots. Typing cancels the previous 320 ms debounce; filter changes and initial mount run immediately. Refresh explicitly reissues the current search, Clear resets the filter input state, and the reducer generation discards stale database responses. Word Set deletion clears the removed selection and reruns the query without an obsolete manual Search step. `BrowseResults` computes a `status_component` from the reducer state before its outer `html!` block. `BrowseLoading`, `BrowseEmpty`, and `BrowseError` are presentational status views; `BrowseWordCard` (now rendered as a compact single-column row) and `BrowsePagination` receive focused props/callbacks. The container alone resolves the required search and Word Set contexts and dispatches actions. `data-component` values and the older `data-browse-*` hooks remain stable. Do not fold these separate views back into nested match expressions inside `html!`. This source refactor still requires local Rust/Chrome validation.
title: Ui Browse State

# CI and validation targets

The authoritative CI workflows are `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `deploy.yml`; the authoritative local build tasks are in `Makefile.toml`. Historical release commands referring to `crates/web`, a package named `zipeek`, or `web/dist` should not be copied into new verification instructions.

## Local gates

From the workspace root:

```powershell
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo check --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p zipeek-web

Native/WASM compilation, Chrome interaction checks, and deployment-path verification are required; the legacy Node source-contract suite was removed in R392. For documentation-only tasks, validate local links and consistency with source, without claiming an unexecuted Rust gate.

The newest UUID translation integration and current full suite have not yet been accepted on that evidence. # CI and deployment

Local commands and prerequisites live in [testing/TESTING.md](../../../testing-quality/acceptance/testing.md).
A16 implements the workflow migration on 2026-10-28. Configuration and local
validation are recorded here; GitHub-hosted execution is not claimed by a local run.

A10 adds exact chart.js 4.6.1 and dev-only esbuild 0.28.2 under D35.
CI runs locked npm installation, then `cargo run -p zipeek-cli --locked -- web prepare`
to prepare DuckDB/Arrow and the tree-shaken summary bundle with licenses.
Trunk never regenerates these files on each Yew rebuild. Both root/Pages
Chrome builds and the standalone Pages gate consume prepared vendor files.

## Entry points and validation

.github/workflows/ci.yml handles pushes to master, pull requests and manual runs.
Its Windows validate job selects Rust 1.97.1 with rustfmt, Clippy and the wasm32
target, Node 22 and the existing Trunk installation action. It verifies installed
Chrome, prints tool versions and installs web assets from crates/zipeek-web/ using
npm ci --ignore-scripts, then runs explicit Rust CLI vendor preparation before any Trunk build or browser test.

The current `.github/workflows/ci.yml` does **not** run the retired Node source-contract suites. Its Windows validation job installs locked npm browser assets, prepares vendor assets through the Rust CLI, runs Rust formatting, Clippy and locked workspace tests, checks the AI client and web WASM targets, builds documentation and builds the `/zipeek/` Trunk bundle. Rust/Chrome E2E coverage is exercised by configured Rust test targets; successful source inspection is not a substitute for execution. D36 permits focused local validation for routine work; it does not change the current workflow:

```powershell
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p zipeek-web --locked
```

```powershell
# From crates/zipeek-web/
trunk build --public-url /zipeek/
```

Workspace tests include the owned root and Pages Chrome suites. Each harness
build uses its own directory and dynamic server ports. Trunk must serve HTTP
200 before Chrome starts; a regression fixture covers initial 404 responses.
No external server or
separate ChromeDriver setup is used. Thirtyfour manages its matching driver.
The GitHub Windows image supplies installed Chrome; the prerequisite check fails
explicitly if it is absent. See the official
[runner image inventory](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/blob/main/images/windows/Windows2025-Readme.md).
Network/cache access is needed for managed driver and pinned native neo prebuilt
library downloads, in addition to Rust/npm/Trunk tool setup. The neo revision's
own .duckdb-release selects native v2.0.0; do not substitute a runner DuckDB.
Existing native tests enforce that engine and v1.4.0 storage compatibility.

## Validation-gated Pages

Only a non-PR master run with successful validate calls the local reusable
.github/workflows/deploy.yml. Other-branch manual runs validate without deploying.
Manual deployment starts from the CI workflow on master. deploy.yml has only a
workflow_call trigger, preventing an independent push/manual path from bypassing
validation or testing a different commit. Local reusable calls use the caller's
checkout context; see [GitHub reusable workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/reuse-automations/reuse-workflows).

The reusable Ubuntu build installs Rust 1.97.1/wasm32, matching wasm-bindgen-cli
0.2.130, the existing Trunk selection and Node 22. It installs locked npm assets
from crates/zipeek-web/, then runs:

```sh
trunk build --release --public-url /zipeek/
```

That command runs from crates/zipeek-web/. Trunk handles the pinned Tailwind tool and copies already prepared
DuckDB and summary assets; no vendor preparation hook or DB generation runs. actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3 uploads crates/zipeek-crates/zipeek-web/dist/.
The dependent deploy job uses actions/deploy-pages@v4 and the github-pages
environment, publishing its page_url output. Existing repository Pages publishing
must be configured for GitHub Actions; this change does not modify remote settings.
A separate configure-pages step is unnecessary for the explicitly configured
Trunk public URL and existing Pages site. Deployment permissions, environment and
build dependency follow [GitHub's custom workflow requirements](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/using-custom-workflows-with-github-pages).

PR validation has contents: read only. The caller Pages job grants contents: read,
pages: write and id-token: write to the reusable call; its deployment job requests
only Pages/OIDC writes. A PR cannot enter that job. Validate has a 45-minute bound,
release build 30 minutes and deploy 10 minutes. Superseded PR validation can cancel;
master validation and an active Pages deployment are not cancelled by a newer run.
The Pages concurrency group serializes active deployments using GitHub's normal
pending-run handling.

## Caches and tool selections

Cargo caches registry/Git sources and target/, keyed by OS, Rust 1.97.1, the
root Cargo.lock, workspace manifests, rust-toolchain.toml, crates/zipeek-web/Trunk.toml and web
package lock. Pages release uses a separate key. Cargo executables are not cached:
restoring old binaries must not replace selected tools. setup-node caches npm's
package cache using crates/zipeek-web/package-lock.json; node_modules and vendor outputs are installed/prepared explicitly before Trunk;
dist output is rebuilt by Trunk.

Existing action versions are retained: checkout v6, CI cache v5, Pages cache v4,
setup-node v4, trunk-action v0.5.0, upload-pages-artifact v3 and deploy-pages v4.
No new package, Cargo feature or action version is introduced. Rust is corrected
to the already-approved 1.97.1. Trunk remains latest as in the previous deployment
workflow: no exact version is approved by A16, and this remains an explicit
reproducibility limitation. Local evidence uses installed Trunk 0.22.0.

## Tooling advisory review

The preserved lockfile contains picomatch 2.3.1 through micromatch. The original
A06 audit and the A16 locked npm install report one high-severity dependency.
The reviewed upstream advisories cover
[extglob ReDoS](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c2c7-rcm5-vvqj) and
[POSIX character-class method injection](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3v7f-55p6-f55p),
with 2.3.2 as the patched 2.x release. These concern processing attacker-controlled
glob patterns; here the dependency belongs to build tooling, not browser search
input. PR source is already executable build input. Under [D33](../../../project-management/decisions/process-and-infra.md#d33-accept-build-tool-picomatch-advisories),
the user accepts both advisories under that build-tool-only input condition.
Do not add an override, run npm audit fix or refresh the lockfile for them.
Reassess if untrusted application patterns reach this dependency. Acceptance is
not remediation; audit output may persist. An independently approved future
Trunk/Tailwind upgrade may bring a fixed version naturally. A39 is retired.

## Validation limits

Local checks cover YAML structure, triggers/permissions/needs, cache/input paths,
gate commands, all five actual code gates and the release artifact contents.
Root/Pages Chrome run locally. The Actions service, fresh hosted Windows/Ubuntu
images, remote permissions/environment approval and actual Pages publication
cannot be exercised by this workspace. No push, dispatch, remote setting change
or deployment was performed. Confirm the first hosted run after these changes
are committed/pushed; do not describe local success as a hosted deployment.

## Release ZIP installation

For numbered hand-off ZIPs accepted by the legacy PowerShell `unpack.ps1`,
use `zipeek-R<number>-<description>-YYYYMMDD.zip`. The native Rust CLI
uses `target/zipeek-source-<version>-<UTC-timestamp>.zip` for pack snapshots. See
[RELEASE_NAMING.md](../../../build-deployment/release-naming.md) for the distinction and checks.


The supported `unpack.ps1` mirrors `crates/*/src`, `docs`, and `scripts` as **managed directories**. Each old directory is moved into `.unpack-backups` before the new release copy is installed; this removes retired source, release-note, and script files. It preserves `.git`, target caches, and local configuration outside these managed directories. Installing this release using an older unpacker that only mirrors `src` will **leave old docs/scripts behind**. Replace your local unpacker with the version included in R173 once. The installer itself is excluded from installation to avoid overwriting the running script.

# Release archive naming and installation

## Numbered source handoffs

The current native `zipeek-cli` unpack discovery accepts two timestamped forms:

```text
zipeek-R<number>-<description>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.zip
zipeek-R<number>-WIP-<description>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.zip
```

A WIP checkpoint is not an accepted major release. Use a real UTC packaging timestamp, a positive decimal release number and a lowercase hyphen-separated description. Check the latest established release before incrementing the number.

Examples:

```text
zipeek-R285-native-ai-server-20261109-221530.zip
zipeek-R285-WIP-ai-transport-20261109-221530.zip
```

`cargo make unpack` searches Downloads for the highest numbered native release or checkpoint. When both a completed release and a WIP checkpoint have the same number, the completed release has priority. An explicit archive path avoids relying on Downloads selection:

```powershell
cargo run -p zipeek-cli --locked -- unpack C:\path\to\archive.zip
```

Before delivering an archive, validate that its filename is recognized by the actual parser in `crates/zipeek-cli/src/command.rs`. Check the ZIP structure for `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `AGENTS.md`, the `crates/`, `docs/` and `scripts/` trees at the ZIP root, with no wrapper directory. The CLI also validates required source files before modifying the checkout. Preserve local edits and backups before unpacking.

The legacy `unpack.ps1` expects an older date-only naming format. The current time-stamped handoff contract is authoritative for `cargo make unpack`; do not assume legacy PowerShell acceptance. Do not silently rename an old archive to a higher release number.

## Native source snapshots

`cargo make pack` produces a different archive under `target/`:

```text
zipeek-source-<workspace-version>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.zip
```

A source snapshot does not use the numbered handoff naming convention. To restore it, supply the path explicitly to the CLI. Review excluded generated assets and source completeness before using any archive as a release handoff.

## Numbered major-release acceptance

The following **major-release-only** gate does not apply to routine tasks, WIP checkpoints, documentation-only changes or native `cargo make pack` snapshots. A numbered major release requires purposeful improvements to at least **20 distinct `.rs` paths**, compared against the agreed baseline. Count each qualifying path once from the final diff; generated code, placeholders, wrappers without meaningful behavior, renames, formatting-only edits, comments and non-Rust files do not qualify.

Do not inflate the count by splitting modules, adding hypothetical features or modifying unrelated code without approval. If the planned work reaches fewer than 20 qualified files, report the shortfall and propose additional valuable changes with risks, validation and expected affected paths **before** expanding scope. If not approved, retain an incomplete or unverified candidate rather than calling the major release accepted.

Before delivering an accepted numbered major release, provide a file-by-file qualifying Rust inventory, separate non-Rust/filtered counts, the actual final diff baseline, applicable test commands and results, unresolved verification, known failures, data-loss implications and archive layout validation. With unavailable build/browser tooling label the output **unverified release candidate**, not a tested release.

# Image service scaffold (R180)

The standalone native crate `crates/zipeek-image-server` is **not used by the Yew frontend yet**. It runs an Axum server bound to `127.0.0.1:1431` and uses a deterministic **SVG placeholder** backend, not Candle or a diffusion model. A trait in `src/inference` is the future inference integration point. Generated placeholders are **not valid image questions** and must not be used as learner-facing assessment content.

## Build and launch

On first install, run `cargo check -p zipeek-image-server` **without** `--locked` to update Cargo.lock for the new dependencies. Commit the generated lockfile, then use `--locked` in CI. This release could not regenerate Cargo.lock because no Rust toolchain is available in its packaging environment. Do not run `cargo generate-lockfile` blindly if preserving existing pinned dependency resolutions matters.

```powershell
cargo check -p zipeek-image-server
cargo test -p zipeek-image-server
cargo make image-server
```

### API

- `GET http://127.0.0.1:1431/health` returns the backend identifier.
- `POST /v1/images` with `{ "prompt": "red apple on a table", "width": 512, "height": 512 }` returns HTTP 202 and an in-memory job ID.
- `GET /v1/jobs/{uuid}` returns `queued`, `running`, `completed` or `failed`, and `image_url` on completion.
- `GET /v1/images/{uuid}` serves the persisted SVG.

Job statuses are process-local; image bytes and their metadata survive restart in `target/zipeek-images`. A restart does not restore old job statuses. Queue admission is capped at four pending/running tasks, with one active generator. IDs are parsed as UUIDs; request bodies, dimensions and prompt length are bounded. There is no public-bind or authentication support, and no configured cross-origin access.

This is an architecture scaffold. Production work must add a real inference implementation, GPU feature-gating, output image validation, review/approval, durable queue state, retention/cleanup, authentication if remote exposure is needed, and image-exercise planning and scoring in `zipeek-exercises`.
title: Image service scaffold (R180)
