# R183: Local SDXL Base inference

The `zipeek-image-server` is a native, loopback-only Axum service.
The default backend remains the deterministic SVG placeholder. Select `sdxl`
explicitly to generate actual PNG images using Candle 0.11.1 and CUDA.

## Local model assets

The SDXL backend reads files **only** from disk, with no automatic downloads.
Default root: `<Cargo workspace>/models/sdxl` (resolved from the image-server crate manifest, independent of the launch directory). Set `ZIPEEK_IMAGE_MODEL_DIR` to override.

```text
sdxl/
  base/
    unet/diffusion_pytorch_model.fp16.safetensors
    text_encoder/model.fp16.safetensors
    text_encoder_2/model.fp16.safetensors
  vae/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors
  clip/tokenizer.json
  clip2/tokenizer.json
```

The VAE file is from `madebyollin/sdxl-vae-fp16-fix`; the tokenizers are
from `openai/clip-vit-large-patch14` and
`laion/CLIP-ViT-bigG-14-laion2B-39B-b160k`. These match Candle's SDXL
Stable Diffusion example. Download and review model licences separately.

Direct file sources (download only any files you do not have):
- SDXL FP16 base weights: https://huggingface.co/stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0/tree/main
  (`unet/diffusion_pytorch_model.fp16.safetensors`, `text_encoder/model.fp16.safetensors`,
  `text_encoder_2/model.fp16.safetensors`). The unqualified UNet file without `.fp16.`
  is **not** the expected FP16 file and is much larger.
- VAE: https://huggingface.co/madebyollin/sdxl-vae-fp16-fix/blob/main/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors
- CLIP 1 tokenizer: https://huggingface.co/openai/clip-vit-large-patch14/blob/main/tokenizer.json
- CLIP 2 tokenizer: https://huggingface.co/laion/CLIP-ViT-bigG-14-laion2B-39B-b160k/blob/main/tokenizer.json

The first two encoder weights already on disk can be reused; only download missing
files. The image server validates its six required files at startup and reports a
structured `SdxlSetupError` when any is missing, empty, or not a regular file.

**Prompt length (R401):** The Rust backend accepts up to 300 content tokens
per tokenizer. Each CLIP encoder processes repeated windows of up to 75 content
tokens plus its two special tokens, preserving the model's 77-position context.
All encoded windows are concatenated along the sequence dimension and passed to
the U-Net, with the two SDXL encoders and unconditional guidance aligned to the
same window count. This avoids the old silent 77-token truncation and needs no
new weights. A prompt beyond 300 content tokens fails explicitly.

Long prompts are a conditioning technique rather than equivalent to a model
trained with a longer attention context. Semantics may weaken across chunks and
VRAM/latency increase with prompt length. The live CUDA smoke test remains
opt-in; no runtime inference or image-quality acceptance has been completed in
this packaging environment.

```powershell
cargo test --locked -p zipeek-image-server clip_chunks_preserve_all_250_content_tokens
cargo test --locked -p zipeek-image-server sdxl_generates_png_from_250_token_prompt -- --ignored --nocapture
```

## Run on Windows PowerShell

The PNG encoder uses `flate2` and `crc32fast`, both already present in
the uploaded workspace lockfile. R183 updates the image-server lockfile entry
to include them and `tokenizers`. Validate the pinned dependency graph:

```powershell
cargo check -p zipeek-image-server
cargo test -p zipeek-image-server
cargo make image-server-sdxl
```

For a custom model directory or step count:

```powershell
$env:ZIPEEK_IMAGE_MODEL_DIR = "C:\zipeek-models\sdxl"
$env:ZIPEEK_IMAGE_STEPS = "20"
cargo make image-server-sdxl
```

Send a request from another terminal:

```powershell
$job = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post `
  -Uri http://127.0.0.1:1431/v1/images `
  -ContentType application/json `
  -Body '{"prompt":"A red apple on a plain wooden table, product photograph, no text","width":512,"height":512}'
$job
do {
  Start-Sleep -Seconds 3
  $status = Invoke-RestMethod "http://127.0.0.1:1431/v1/jobs/$($job.id)"
  $status
} while ($status.status -in @("queued", "running"))
if ($status.status -eq "completed") {
  Invoke-WebRequest "http://127.0.0.1:1431$($status.image_url)" -OutFile "$PWD\sdxl-test.png"
}
```

`GET /health` reports `backend: sdxl` when selected.

## Limits and known caveats

- **Not CUDA verified in the release-build environment**: compile and generate
  on the Windows RTX 5080 laptop before considering inference operational.
- One concurrent generator; four total queued/running jobs. Inference is run on
  a Tokio blocking worker; it does not block the web executor.
- The initial implementation reconstructs Candle weights for each request,
  keeping the architecture simple at the cost of warm-up time. Model lifetime
  caching can be added after an actual CUDA memory profile.
- It uses the official Candle SDXL dual-CLIP, DDIM, UNet and VAE path,
  with FP16 UNet/VAE, CLIP inference in F32 and guidance 7.5.
- CUDA generation can exhaust VRAM, especially at 768px. Start with 512px,
  batch 1, and unload large language models first.
- Jobs are in memory across server restarts; completed images and metadata
  persist in `ZIPEEK_IMAGE_DATA_DIR` as `.png` or `.svg` plus `.json`.
- Prompts and images are local. No remote model/API calls occur.
- Image exercise answer correctness and visual validation are separate work.
title: R183: Local SDXL Base inference

# Dictionary Browse - design and implementation status

Approved 2026-11-04. The design reference is the dark-theme Dictionary mockup.

## Responsibilities

Browse is for **finding, hearing, inspecting and collecting words**, not for
choosing quiz types or launching an ambiguous one-word quiz. Any selected Word
Set can be handed off to Practice with its identity preserved. Practice then
chooses exercise types, mode and any relevant specialized configuration.

## Results presentation (R79 implemented)

- Five visible rows per page; issue the database query with one lookahead row
  so Next is enabled only if another page exists. Keep Previous/Next inside
  the result panel and show the current page number. No synthetic total count.
- Each list row places simplified hanzi and pinyin **on the same line** when
  horizontal space allows; traditional characters remain supplemental.
  Meanings wrap. Long definitions do not force horizontal page overflow.
- Each row has an accessible **Listen** icon using the existing `ListenButton`
  and Web Speech synthesis `zh-CN`, plus Add/Remove from the chosen Word Set.
  Do not imply TTS provides authoritative tone/reading validation for
  heteronyms; speech synthesis uses simplified word text and device voices.
- No generic per-word Practice action, and no bottom-of-Browse “Translate
  selected vocabulary” button that might mean either word translation or
  exercise generation. The selected Word Set panel offers a named, disabled-
  when-empty “Use <name> in Practice” action instead.
- Search is automatic with a short debounce for text; filters change
  immediately. Refresh uses a Lucide icon with an accessible name. Clear
  resets filters. The underlying reducer/query contract is retained.

## Later (not yet implemented)

- Row details disclosure with sense/reading provenance, usage examples,
  full meanings and an explicit pronunciation target if disambiguated.
- Optional bulk selection and Save selected rows, with clear scope semantics
  (current page versus complete filtered result set). No implicit “all”
  operation across undisplayed pages.
- A full URL-authoritative Browse state codec and history handling remain
  separate work. Current route-local reducer does not implement that design.
- Additional numbered page navigation only after a trustworthy total-count
  query exists; do not invent “Page N of M”.

## Dictionary Word Set destination (R518 WIP)

The current Word Set selection is the default destination for Dictionary Add/Remove actions, as clarified by the user. Selecting a set in Word Sets or Dictionary updates a separate browser-local preference. On reload the selection is validated against existing Word Set IDs; if the set no longer exists, the first available set is selected. The preference does not change the Word Set backup format and does not override Practice vocabulary selection.

## E2E acceptance

Verify 5 rows per page, independent next/previous, query lookahead,
state-cancelled searches, keyboard search/refresh, row Listen accessibility,
selected-set Add/Remove, empty saved-set start disabled, and route handoff with
saved-set preselection. Run at 320, 768 and 1440 px in both themes. Speech
synthesis calls may be mocked at the browser boundary for deterministic CI;
voice quality is a device test, not an automated correctness assertion.

## Structured filter suggestions

Browse separates free-text search from structured filter suggestions for HSK system and level, category and part of speech. Active chips can be removed independently, and Clear returns to the unfiltered query. The result list is capped at five visible rows with lookahead pagination. Do not resurrect the obsolete release-specific autocomplete contract or infer unverified AI categories from text.
title: Dictionary Browse - design and implementation status

# Personal learner data and storage

## Existing browser storage

Zipeek uses a generated read-only DuckDB dictionary and separate learner-owned browser storage. The dictionary must not be described as the writable destination for learning results.

- `zipeek.preferences.v1`: consolidated appearance/character preferences, explicit default-off Practice-history recording consent (`learning_history_enabled`), and non-secret AI endpoint/model configuration. The optional AI API key is memory-only.
- `zipeek.user_word_sets.v1`: personal Word Sets. Sets acquired through Courses carry an optional typed `source` with one-based `region_id` and `set_index`. Only this source identity establishes acquisition; matching display names are not proof of acquisition. Renaming or editing words preserves the source, deletion removes acquisition. Pre-existing source-less sets remain personal but are not automatically attributed to courses.
- `zipeek.excluded_words`: vocabulary exclusions.
- `zipeek.crosswords.rotation.v1`: optional browser-local crossword variety history. Contains the 100 most recently used distinct Hanzi answers with usage sequence/count and the 10 most recent puzzle word lists and session IDs; assists seed selection but does not change restored crossword solutions or Practice learning evidence. Separate from `zipeek.crosswords.v5.<session-id>` puzzle snapshots. This key is not included in Word Set personal-data exports.
- `zipeek.practice.session.v1.<uuid-v7>`: temporary session JSON containing one configuration per exercise type, ordered step instances with ISO start/finish timestamps, and session lifecycle timestamps. Finished records are removed after successful optional learning-history handling. Existing records with an incompatible JSON shape are not migrated; they fail current-session validation and must be cleared explicitly if they block new sessions.

The Settings Data & Storage panel supports a versioned JSON personal-data backup/import for Word Sets and exclusions, plus selective deletion. This does **not** imply backups include temporary Practice records or an authoritative learning-history database. Existing importer validation and deletion confirmation remain application features.

Pinyin modules now persist passed **written recognition checks** in `zipeek.courses.progress.v1` after two correct answers. Opening a lesson or listening to an example never marks a module as passed. The same browser-local key saves Grammar step checkpoints and best draft assessment scores, but **never** awards full listening/speaking competence, independently verified grammar mastery or mosaic completion. This category is not included in the current Word Set/exclusions backup/export interface; clearing browser site data can remove it. Browser storage failures are surfaced in the lesson UI. No old manual-completion key is read or written.

## Personal OPFS/DuckDB status

The R283 unverified checkpoint adds an opt-in personal DuckDB Practice-outcome writer with commit/readback-before-cleanup behavior, separate from the diagnostics and snapshot/probe functionality. A browser-local OPFS snapshot is a point-in-time backup, not a live transactional learning store. Do not claim real-world persistence until a browser-verified commit and readback succeed. The completion view only reports success after that operation returns successfully.

The Practice completion screen now distinguishes recorded, disabled and retryable failure outcomes; recording defaults to off. The **approved future direction** is session-first pedagogical evidence with derivation of per-Hanzi/word, exercise, HSK/category and grammar observations. The eligibility floor is seven distinct active dates and ten qualifying scored encounters over at least three sessions with a per-session cap, plus separately assessed recognition, listening, speaking and sentence use; this does **not** constitute a running proficiency algorithm. See [learning evidence](../../../learning-practice/practice/learning-evidence.md). The new default-off opt-in and minimal v1 outcome table are source-implemented but not browser-verified; retention, portable export/import, migrations and durability acceptance remain open.

## Data risks and planned acceptance

Browser-local storage can be deleted by site-data clearing and may fail due to quotas or browser restrictions. JSON export is the user-controlled portability path for the categories that it actually exports. OPFS and future personal DuckDB adoption require close/reopen, reload, cross-tab, quota, corrupt-record, export/import and deletion coverage.

See [schema design](../../../dictionary-data/schema/personal-data.md), [current implementation](../../../project-management/current.md) and [open tasks](../../../project-management/tasks.md).
title: Personal learner data and storage

# Dictionary generation and published artifacts

This is the **current** generator pipeline, as implemented in [`crates/zipeek-db-gen`](../../../../crates/zipeek-db-gen) and described by the installed [`hanzi.manifest.json`](../../../../crates/zipeek-web/static/hanzi.manifest.json). Task-by-task historical snapshot sizes, temporary checksums and former pre-expansion counts belong in [release history](../../RELEASE_HISTORY.md), not in current generator specifications.

## Inputs and preparation

`inputs/` validates the pinned HSK and CC-CEDICT source files, declared license notices, paths, lengths and SHA-256 hashes. [`generator.rs`](../../../../crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/generator.rs) calls `prepare()` to verify sources and open the engine-guarded in-memory schema. Native `duckdb-neo` must report `v2.0.0`; the writer explicitly uses storage compatibility `v2.0.0`.

`import_primary()` parses HSK, applies CC-CEDICT gloss fallback where required, expands valid CC-CEDICT-only readings and preserves explicit character readings. This is no longer an HSK-only, fallback-on-missing-glosses-only pipeline. See [import rules](../../../dictionary-data/schema/import-rules.md) and the actual [`import/`](../../../../crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/import) modules.

## Schema, enrichment and output

[`schema.sql`](../../../../crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/schema.sql) defines the `words` compatibility table, normalized senses/characters/identities, classification tables, memberships, constraints, indexes and controlled taxonomy. The generator may apply validated AI classification cache data if supplied; a table existing does not mean every sense is classified.

[`artifact/writer.rs`](../../../../crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/artifact/writer.rs) writes a staging directory, attaches an explicitly compatible native DuckDB file, bulk-copies generated tables, compares logical snapshots, checkpoints/detaches, reopens read-only and validates again before publishing. Failed stages do not publish a partial output. [`artifact/report.rs`](../../../../crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/artifact/report.rs) records manifest, diagnostics, source/artifact provenance and table metadata.

## Current installed bundle

| Property | Value from manifest |
| --- | --- |
| Readings / words | **12,188** |
| Character occurrences | **23,900** |
| Identity candidates | **12,188** |
| Diagnostic events | **467** |
| Native engine | `v2.0.0` |
| Storage version | `v1.4.0` |
| Browser package | `@duckdb/duckdb-wasm@1.33.1-dev114.0` |
| Data artifact | `hanzi-20261108-183418.duckdb` (plus compressed `.gz`) |

These are manifest **declarations** read from the supplied source, not an independent native replay or validation of every row. To inspect the actual asset filenames and hashes, read the installed manifest directly. Do not use the original 12,100-row, 514-diagnostic HSK-only export as the current count.

## Browser integration and boundaries

The [`zipeek-db` WASM adapter](../../../../crates/zipeek-db/src/wasm) verifies and opens the installed read-only dictionary; the app supplies a local worker and asset bundle. The manifest's required generator/storage fields are distinct from the live browser engine version and Debug's runtime storage metrics. A new generated dictionary requires native output verification plus browser/Pages tests. It is **not** a writable user database.

See [regeneration](../../../dictionary-data/schema/regeneration.md), [runtime](../../../dictionary-data/schema/runtime.md), [reproducibility](../../../dictionary-data/schema/reproducibility.md) and [provenance testing](../../../testing-quality/e2e/provenance.md).

## R464 English full-text indexing

Generation explicitly sets `BLOCK_SIZE 262144` on the new `artifact` database.
After copying dictionary data and validating its logical snapshot, the native
generator installs and loads DuckDB `fts` and creates an immutable BM25 index
on `words.id` / `words.english`. This requires the DuckDB 2.0 `fts` extension
to be available to the native generator. A missing extension fails generation
rather than publishing an artifact without the declared index. The generator
verifies the index schema and executes a BM25 query during generation and
read-only reopening. FTS-owned auxiliary tables are excluded from the canonical
logical dictionary snapshot, which still compares all dictionary relations.

The read-only `Database::english_full_text_search` provides a standalone ranked
query. Browse also exposes `English relevance (FTS / BM25)` as an explicit
field selection. It uses the persisted `fts_main_words` index, sorts by BM25
score, and retains HSK, part-of-speech, category, Word Set and pagination
filters. Ordinary English substring search and Hanzi/Pinyin search remain
separate modes.

On browser dictionary initialization, the DuckDB-WASM connection attempts
`INSTALL AND LOAD fts;`. The extension is fetched dynamically by the versioned
WASM runtime. If it cannot be loaded, the dictionary remains available but
ranked queries will report an error instead of quietly changing to substring
search. The browser compatibility and offline behavior require actual Chrome
verification with a regenerated DuckDB 2.0 bundle at both `/` and `/zipeek/`.
title: Dictionary generation and published artifacts

# Personal learning evidence: phase 0 and independent foundations

**Phase-zero design record, not a deployed personal database.** The historical WASM 1.32.0 validation constraint is superseded as an installed-runtime fact by [runtime](../../../dictionary-data/schema/runtime.md); policy approval remains unresolved. See [personal data](../../../dictionary-data/schema/personal-data.md) for current storage authority and migration gates.

Status: design checkpoint, not an active writable DuckDB schema. The current personal learning records remain browser-local as described in `personal-data.md`. No user database was created or reset.

This checkpoint follows `Zipeek_Personal_Learning_Schema_Implementation_Spec(1).md`, but does not activate its DDL. The proposed tables must first be checked against the pinned DuckDB-WASM 1.32.0 runtime, including UUID, TIMESTAMPTZ, foreign-key and uniqueness behavior, OPFS persistence, export/import, locking and recovery.

## Source observations

- `crates/zipeek-exercises/src/evidence.rs` currently exposes six historical evidence categories: recognition, listening, pronunciation, recall, writing and usage. These are **not** equivalent to the spec's four independent vocabulary competency axes and two grammar assessment modes. Do not blend results from the older ledger into verified mastery.
- `crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/schema.sql` identifies dictionary words by generated integer IDs and a `(simplified, pinyin)` unique pair. Neither is sufficient to prove stable, reading- and sense-aware identity across regenerated dictionaries.
- `crates/zipeek-db/src/wasm/probe.rs` exercises a disposable OPFS DuckDB probe. A successful one-session probe does not establish browser-restart durability or suitability as the live personal-record store.
- R258 UUID practice sessions are localStorage records. A session record is not an authoritative, target-specific assessment event log.

## Implemented, not yet wired into persisted user records

The `zipeek-exercises::learning` module contains typed attempts and independent vocabulary/grammar target observations, a conservative validity gate, an in-memory append-once journal, explicit correction events, and raw per-skill observed metrics. It refuses to treat pinyin-only transcription as Hanzi typing, copying as recall, playback or self-report as acoustic pronunciation, and non-obligatory grammar patterns as assessed. It does not award learned/mastered statuses or produce scientifically unverified retention probabilities.

The new code neither replaces the existing `evidence.rs` ledger nor automatically promotes saved practice sessions into skill mastery. Actual assessment integration requires provenance of the stimulus, stable dictionary lexical identity, evaluator/rubric versions and privacy decisions.

## Product-owner decisions required before schema activation

1. Do all four applicable skills define the final `fully_learned` claim, with verified pronunciation unavailable until trustworthy scoring exists? Alternative: show only per-skill states and `receptively_learned` initially.
2. Is Hanzi input through an IME sufficient to assess practical typing, with handwriting treated as optional additional evidence?
3. Does graduation require seven **distinct successful local dates**, a delayed success separated by at least seven days, and an optional 14-day higher tier? Specify what constitutes delayed retention when daily reviews continue uninterrupted.
4. Will pronunciation be objectively scored by a qualified model/human or remain explicitly `self_reported` / `not_assessed` initially?
5. Which authored grammar definitions and evaluator rubrics are the source of truth for obligatorily elicited targets and accepted alternatives?
6. What opt-in, expiry and export/deletion rules apply to recordings, strokes, raw typed text and generated sentence responses?

The user must approve these decisions and the sense-aware lexical identity/reconciliation policy before mastery production logic or a live personal DuckDB begins writing learning records. No backward-compatibility code is proposed. A reset of existing personal data would require a separately approved, explicit user action.

## Next implementation gates

1. Confirm decisions and stable lexical keys, versioned context-suitability and acceptance policies. Add deterministic reconciliation fixtures for homographs and changed dictionary IDs.
2. Implement event schema and transactionally insert an attempt, all observations and any correction with a stable submission key. Test duplicate concurrent submissions and partial failure against actual pinned DuckDB-WASM.
3. Prove writable OPFS durability and cross-tab coordination, export/import and error recovery before making a personal DB authoritative. Keep current user-owned data untouched throughout verification.
4. Derive reproducible projections and scheduling from committed events. Display four independently assessed skill states; never infer verified pronunciation or Hanzi typing from unrelated exercises.
title: Personal learning evidence: phase 0 and independent foundations

# Pedagogy: recognition acquisition foundation (R333 WIP)

## Status and authority

This design records the user's 2026-11-11 decisions for **historical Hanzi recognition acquisition**. The source-only R333 checkpoint introduces `zipeek-pedagogy`, a pure Rust domain crate with deterministic, in-memory projections. It does **not** activate automatic assessment capture, a persistent personal-data authority, a worker, `/stats`, or dragon awards in the UI. Those remain separately gated.

It deliberately does not replace R259 `zipeek-exercises::learning::MasteryPolicy`, which continues to represent its older multi-skill vocabulary projection until an approved migration of domain ownership and reconciliation of its separate definitions. Dragon acquisition and full multi-skill proficiency are not interchangeable.

## Recognition acquisition contract

- Each individual Hanzi independently earns a historical recognition award after **seven consecutive qualifying local dates**.
- Each qualifying day requires **ten correct, eligible, unassisted recognition observations**, across **at least three completed sessions**. At most **four** correct observations from any one session count toward the daily ten.
- The maximum mistakes before daily qualification is **0, 1, or 2**, default 0. The allowance is frozen in the submitted evidence for each item and local date. An inconsistent allowance within one day is an error, not a retroactive adjustment.
- An additional eligible incorrect observation that exceeds the allowance **fails that day immediately** and resets the active acquisition streak. Earlier attempts are not deleted.
- Once a day qualifies it **locks immediately**. Later mistakes that day do not alter that qualification; they remain available for subsequent retention analysis.
- Qualifying days must be **consecutive local calendar dates** with **at least 24 elapsed hours** between the moments each day qualifies. A missed date resets the active streak.
- Later recall failures can change a separate retention status. They do not revoke the timestamp of a historical acquisition award.
- The full HSK 1-9 learning pool is accessible regardless of acquisition progress. Dragon achievements count distinct acquired Hanzi in the selected dictionary-HSK target; words and readings have independent evidence identities and do not automatically award character recognition.

## Evidence boundary

All games may submit scored observations, but game scoring is not itself an acquisition decision. Recognition events have stable attempt/session identities, submission time, local date and zone context, assessment version and evaluator provenance. Invalid dates, inconsistent local dates/UTC offsets, duplicate IDs with conflicting content, and evidence from the future are rejected.

Independent recognition assessments qualify when unassisted and complete. Multiple-choice recognition requires a validated assessment proof from a separate gate: the R333 `ValidatedChoice` type carries a non-empty validation identifier, but **this crate cannot verify its content**. This is a provisional domain API, not permission for production games to fabricate validation IDs. Hinted, incomplete, unvalidated-choice and general exposure events are recorded as supporting-only evidence. No production game is wired to this API yet.

**Outstanding correctness requirements before persistent mastery:** define the authoritative choice-validation gate (prompt/distractor diversity and independent recall), fixed-zone behaviour across travel, trustworthy item identity through dictionary refresh, recovery of clock anomalies, and atomic persistence with one active tab. R333's projection must not be the sole source of durable mastery until those gates pass.

## Crate boundaries

`zipeek-pedagogy` is independent of Yew, JS, DuckDB and all third-party crates. `zipeek-exercises` continues to own game outcomes and the existing R259 learning contract. The future adapter validates outcomes and passes independent evidence to pedagogy. The existing database crate owns authoritative writes after persistence acceptance. A Rust/WASM browser worker is an execution host in existing browser infrastructure, not a reason to put learning rules in `zipeek-worker`.

The new crate includes its own pure calendar-date validation because no dependency direction between the existing learning calendar module and this new domain was approved for R333. Consolidating identical calendar functionality is a follow-up refactoring task before production integration.

## Scheduled stages

1. **R333:** pure evidence and recognition projection plus deterministic tests. WIP until compiled and reviewed.
2. **Later:** validated game-to-evidence adapter, historical policy readback, OPFS DuckDB durability/atomicity, and consent gating. Schema changes require separate approval.
3. **Later:** background WASM worker host, pending-work recovery, single-tab ownership and Settings diagnostics.
4. **Later:** `/stats`, separate skill and retention views, dragon colour progression, HSK-target denominator and accessible UI.
5. **Later:** optional advanced AI insights with external-transfer consent and independently validated generated exercises.

Do not imply the app is collecting pedagogical data, awarding character mastery, or using a running analysis worker until these integrations and tests are completed.

## R334 verified evidence-journal boundary (WIP)

`zipeek-pedagogy::EvidenceJournal` is a synchronous pure-Rust port for reading
recorded recognition events and atomically appending a batch. `append_and_verify`
first validates candidate evidence against the existing journal, requests the
append, then rereads stored records and refuses to return a learning projection
unless the candidate events are present and unchanged. `project_committed`
computes only from journal readback. Replayed identical attempt identifiers are
idempotent; conflicting IDs are rejected before append.

The port contract requires an adapter to provide **atomic, durable** append,
consistent readback, and exclusive single-writer coordination. Those
requirements are **not** implemented by this port itself. Test doubles model
write failures, discarded writes, altered readbacks, and duplicate retries. The
existing Practice session JSON table is not automatically equivalent to a
character-level assessment event journal, and cannot be used without approved
schema and provenance work.

No worker, browser persistence adapter, production capture, award writes, or
`/stats` view was activated in R334. The independent choice-validation gate,
learner timezone authority, consent controls, and authoritative OPFS durability
remain prerequisites to production integration.
title: Pedagogy: recognition acquisition foundation (R333 WIP)

# Personal-data storage: implemented state and proposed database

## Current authority

The application uses `localStorage` for settings, personal Word Sets, Pinyin-course progress, exclusions and temporary UUID Practice records. The keys and backup boundary are documented in [Personal Data](../../../dictionary-data/personal/personal-data-storage.md). `PracticeSessionStore` saves unfinished work under `zipeek.practice.session.v1.<uuid-v7>`; completion removes that temporary record. The R283 unverified checkpoint introduces a dedicated OPFS DuckDB outcome ledger, gated by a default-off recording preference. This requires browser validation before durability claims.

The Settings Personal Data page implements category-based JSON backup/preview/import/delete. It also exposes isolated OPFS/snapshot diagnostics and a writable DuckDB-WASM persistence **probe**. The probe uses its own database and does not migrate or replace user Word Sets, exclusions, course progress or Practice records. See [`zipeek-db/src/wasm/probe.rs`](../../../../crates/zipeek-db/src/wasm/probe.rs) and [`zipeek-web/src/services/personal_data/`](../../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/services/personal_data).

## Not yet production-accepted

The R283 checkpoint has an initial `zipeek-personal-learning-v1.duckdb` outcome table, a default-off opt-in and an exclusive Web Lock. There is still no production-accepted pedagogical-history writer, completed migration model, verified cross-tab locking and durable exercise-evidence schema beyond completed Practice outcome records. A successful OPFS probe does not imply any of those capabilities. Attempts/events in [`zipeek-exercises`](../../../../crates/zipeek-exercises/src) are domain/test structures, not automatically persisted browser records.

## R335 recognition evidence table (approved WIP, not activated)

The user explicitly approved a dedicated recognition-evidence table and Rust/WASM
adapter on 2026-11-12. The WIP adapter is implemented in
`zipeek-db/src/wasm/recognition_history.rs` and uses the existing personal OPFS
DuckDB file, the same exclusive Web Lock, and the existing DuckDB-WASM bridge.
The table is created lazily on the first explicit append:

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS recognition_evidence (
    attempt_id VARCHAR PRIMARY KEY,
    evidence_json VARCHAR NOT NULL
);
```

The versioned JSON payload includes `schema_version: 1`, `attempt_id`, a single
`character`, session `session_id` and `completed`, `occurred_at_utc_ms`,
`timezone_iana`, `timezone_offset_minutes`, `local_date`, `mistake_allowance`
(0, 1 or 2), `evaluator_id`, `assessment_version`, `correct`, `assisted`, and
`format` (tagged object: `independent_recall`, `validated_choice` with
`validation_id`, or `supporting_only`). The adapter rejects inconsistent
identities, invalid fields, oversized records/batches and conflicting duplicate
IDs. It inserts an entire batch in a transaction, checkpoints, reopens the
database and verifies the exact stored JSON by attempt ID. Exact-match retries
are idempotent. `PersonalLearningHistory::erase` now drops both learning
history tables in one transaction.

The API provides `PersonalRecognitionHistory::append_verified` and `read_all`.
The latter is bounded to two million records and is intended for replay and
verification, not repeated per-render dashboard queries. Aggregate SQL and
pagination will be needed before high-volume dashboard adoption.

**Not activated:** This adds neither opt-in collection wiring nor a production
`RecognitionEvent` serializer, browser worker, `/stats` UI or authoritative
acquisition projection. The personal DuckDB migration is additive and lazy;
existing `practice_sessions` records remain untouched until the user explicitly
requests deletion. Browser transaction/OPFS/restore/consent acceptance is
pending; do not treat source-level tests as durability proof.

## Design gates before adoption

1. Implement the approved session-first scored observations in a personal DuckDB with explicit recording consent; finalize opt-in defaults and raw audio/text retention before production collection.
2. Select versioned vocabulary identity keys that remain valid when the read-only dictionary changes; generated integer WordIds alone are not portable.
3. Define append-only attempt semantics, stable exercise/step IDs, schema versions, deletions, backup/import/rollback and a quota/retention policy.
4. Prove write, checkpoint, restart, cross-tab lock, failure recovery, export/import and corruption handling in real browsers for the approved DuckDB-WASM package.
5. Only after durable-write verification, show a success confirmation; when disabled show a privacy notice, and on real write errors show an explicit failure.

Historical R117-R119 exploratory steps and proposed tables are recorded in [completed history](../../completed) and [release history](../../RELEASE_HISTORY.md). They must not be read as a deployed learner database specification.

## Approved pedagogical evidence direction (not implemented)

Persist Practice sessions as the evidence authority; derive attempt and skill observations linked to their original session/step, normalized word/Hanzi IDs, exercise kind, HSK/category labels and assessed grammar point. The approved eligibility floor is **seven distinct active local calendar days**, **at least ten qualifying scored encounters over three or more distinct Practice sessions**, a per-session counting cap, and separately successful evidence for recognition, listening, assessed speaking and sentence use. The per-session cap, exact modality thresholds, learner timezone policy and audio privacy/retention remain undecided; never grant mastery automatically on the tenth encounter. Inject a test clock so E2E can advance dates without altering the OS clock. Preserve a distinct irreversible grammar course-completion record once all required grammar-point assessments pass. See [learning evidence](../../../learning-practice/practice/learning-evidence.md) and [future Courses spec](../../../learning-practice/courses/courses-mosaic.md).
title: Personal-data storage: implemented state and proposed database

# R259 - dictionary identity and learning evidence foundations

Status: **source candidate; Rust compilation, generator regeneration, and browser validation pending.**

## Schema proposal assessment

| Proposal | R259 decision | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dictionary_versions` | Adopt snapshot fingerprint metadata | The fingerprint describes the generated lexical content, not a backward-compatibility migration version. |
| `vocabulary_identities` | Adopt **unresolved candidate** records only | Same surface form and reading do not establish same lexical sense across dictionary revisions. No verified stable keys are generated. |
| `characters` | Adopt Unicode scalar inventory | This records characters occurring in simplified word forms; readings and radical properties require a verified separate source. |
| `word_characters` | Adopt ordered character occurrences | Preserves repeats and position, even where words include non-Hanzi characters. |
| `example_sentences` / `sentence_vocabulary` | Defer | No approved licensed sentence dataset with sense-level provenance. AI-generated examples cannot silently become catalog evidence. |
| `word_relations` | Defer generic table | `sense_relations` already models explicit source annotations. Synonym/antonym edges need additional verified sources. |
| `character_components` | Defer | Requires a licensed structural dataset and accepted decomposition policy. |
| `classifiers` / `word_classifiers` | Defer | Current PoS membership identifies classifier words, not reliable noun-to-classifier links. |
| `word_frequency_sources` | Defer | Existing scalar frequency has no verified corpus-by-corpus provenance for a multi-source table. |

## Identity safety

The generator now populates `dictionary_versions` using a deterministic content digest and inserts a Unicode character index. The `vocabulary_identities` records have `identity_status = 'unresolved'`. Their candidate keys use a length-bearing spelling and numeric-reading representation, **not** a stable sense ID. They are not eligible to join personal mastery data across dictionary refreshes.

The pure learning domain supplies `LexicalIdentity` with explicit source-lexeme, reading, and sense keys; `reconcile()` classifies resolved, missing, and ambiguous references without falling back to word indexes. Only externally verified identities may be registered for assessment policies. A future generator change must trace stable source identifiers and sense reconciliation before emitting `verified` records.

## Learning evidence and mastery

The R258 checkpoint's in-memory attempt journal is retained and extended. Identical submission retries are no-ops; conflicting retries are rejected. Corrections are append-only and a single observation cannot be corrected twice without a new audited event design.

R259 adds an independent `mastery-v1` projection with **seven distinct successful local dates** plus at least one pair of consecutive successful review dates separated by **at least seven days**. Ordinary consecutive daily practice does not satisfy this delayed test. Qualified failure following the last success changes that **skill only** to `needs_review`; missed attendance is not a failed review. A conservative `scheduler-v1` suggests review intervals independently; its interval table is a configurable product heuristic, not calibrated learning science.

The four vocabulary competencies are separate. `receptively_learned` requires recognition and listening; `fully_learned` requires verified success across all applicable recognition, listening, pronunciation and typing. Inapplicability requires a versioned content policy, not an inferred pass. No spoken self-report or pinyin-only transcription establishes verified pronunciation or Hanzi typing.

The event journal, evidence gate and projections are still **pure Rust / in-memory**. R259 does not enable automatic production event capture, a writable personal DuckDB, mastery badges in the UI, or a new data authority.

## No migration or silent reset

This project permits replacing the **generated dictionary artifact** outright. No legacy-table compatibility reader or data migration is introduced. However the existing installed `hanzi-*.duckdb` files are retained until the user manually regenerates and installs a validated artifact. The browser-local Word Sets, preferences and practice session records are not deleted. Do not reset learner-owned storage as part of dictionary regeneration.

After local Rust checks, run `cargo make db-generate` and review the new artifact before `cargo make db-install`. Then run `cargo make serve`, exercise Browse and Practice, and verify the generated schema in the installed dictionary. The full user-owned DuckDB requires separate OPFS close/reopen, restart, cross-tab, export/import, quota and crash-recovery acceptance before becoming authoritative.

## Release gates

1. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
2. `cargo test -p zipeek-exercises --locked`
3. `cargo test -p zipeek-db-gen --locked`
4. `cargo test --workspace --locked`
5. `cargo check -p zipeek-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --locked`
6. `cargo make db-generate`, `cargo make db-install`, `cargo make serve`
7. Native/WASM generator equivalence, identity ambiguity fixtures, Chrome browsing, and personal-storage retention

No Rust compiler, native DuckDB generator, or managed Chrome was available in the packaging environment; these gates remain unverified.

## R270 input integrity follow-up (2026-11-08)

Invalid ISO local review dates are now rejected at the evidence qualification and journal append boundaries rather than counted as observations and discarded only when raw projections run. Verified lexical identities reject leading/trailing whitespace and NUL-bearing keys; the policy catalog rejects whitespace-only assessment version strings. This does not activate a persisted evidence journal or mastery publication from the UUID Practice runtime. The existing browser-local schema and model remain unchanged.
title: R259 - dictionary identity and learning evidence foundations

# Regeneration

**Current installation:** consult [the installed manifest](../../../../crates/zipeek-web/static/hanzi.manifest.json) for the actual 12,188-row bundle; the old A05 snapshots mentioned later are historical. Commands and tasks below should be checked against the current `Makefile.toml` before execution. Production dictionary generation and installation must not run as an unintended side effect of documentation or E2E work.

Generation is explicit and manual. Commands below run from the repository root.
No source acquisition or database generation runs during application builds.

## Live AI smoke and offline streaming regression coverage

`cargo make db-ai-smoke` sends one single-sense and one two-sense batch classification request through the
AiMux streaming client and taxonomy validator, using the same model, endpoint,
timeout and retry environment settings as `db-full`. It has no database/cache
writes and does not import the full HSK source. A missing final-text response
is reported as an actionable error; this does **not** establish whether the
model only produced reasoning, exceeded its token budget, or the streaming
provider dropped content. Inspect LM Studio's output when this occurs.

For an opt-in direct native invocation:

```powershell
cargo run -p zipeek-db-gen --locked -- ai-smoke --model "qwen3-14b-claude-4.5-opus-high-reasoning-distill" --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:1234
```

When classification work is pending, `db-full` runs the smoke request first
and refuses to generate/install on failure. Offline Rust mock HTTP tests
exercise AiMux aggregation of split SSE content and empty final text; Node
workflow tests verify the preflight gate. They do not replace a live model
or Windows end-to-end acceptance test.

## One-command AI-enriched regeneration

Run `cargo make db-full` from the repository root while the configured LM Studio
model and local inference server are available. This command performs a complete
resumable classification pass **before** creating a candidate, so it does not
create an intermediate unclassified artifact. It then runs the existing native
`zipeek-db-gen generate --classification-cache` export and the existing transactional
bundle installer. The generator verifies exact sense digests, prompt/taxonomy
versions and classification records; logical snapshots include AI-derived tables.

The command checks `zipeek-db-gen classify-plan` before and after inference and refuses
publication unless zero senses remain pending. AI failures preserve checkpoints
in `target/db-workflow/classification-cache/` and leave the installed bundle
untouched. A separate cache file is selected for each model. Environment
settings: `ZIPEEK_AI_MODEL` (default
`qwen3-14b-claude-4.5-opus-high-reasoning-distill`), `ZIPEEK_AI_ENDPOINT`
(default `http://127.0.0.1:1234`), `ZIPEEK_AI_TIMEOUT_MS` (default
`300000`), `ZIPEEK_AI_RETRIES` (default `1`). `cargo make db-full-dev`
performs this workflow before serving the web app.

`cargo make db-generate` and `cargo make dev` remain intentionally offline:
no AI inference and no classification cache is applied. This distinction keeps
routine development independent of the local model. Generated artifacts are
always source-and-cache specific; never hand-edit the DuckDB file.

### Incremental classification checkpoints (R57)

The cache path printed by `db-full` still identifies the model-specific
`<hash>.jsonl` snapshot. Existing classified senses in that JSONL remain
readable. Instead of rewriting the entire growing snapshot after each new sense,
R57 writes one synchronized and atomically renamed
`<hash>.jsonl.records/<word_id>-<sense_order>.json` checkpoint per newly
accepted sense. Native `classify-plan`, `classify`, and enriched export combine
both sources; neither path is a complete standalone export once new records
exist. **Do not delete, compact, or move either cache part while classification
is running.** Unexpected, truncated or duplicate checkpoints halt processing
rather than being silently skipped. Unresolved `.tmp` checkpoint files require
manual inspection before resuming. No installed database is modified unless
all senses pass validation.

Classification-level recovery is implemented separately in
`crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/llm/recovery.rs`: for an empty final response, invalid JSON,
or an invalid taxonomy payload, it attempts the same sense at most three times.
The source gloss, v3 classification prompt and model stay the same on retry.
This policy does not retry storage failures or override AiMux's existing
transport retry setting (`ZIPEEK_AI_RETRIES`). Failed batches never publish
an incomplete database; re-running `cargo make db-full` resumes valid cached
records. The current workflow defers an exhausted sense rather than inventing labels;
the final completeness gate still prohibits installing partial enrichment.

## Choose the command

For the complete local workflow, run from the repository root:

```powershell
cargo make dev
```

This generates a fresh candidate, verifies and installs the whole bundle with
a backup, then starts Trunk at http://localhost:1420. It runs once per invocation;
Trunk rebuilds do not regenerate data. Prerequisites are installed cargo-make,
Node, Rust/native generator prerequisites, Trunk and the locked web npm packages
(`cargo make setup` from the repository root after a clean unpack). Tasks do not install
or upgrade tools/packages. Tested cargo-make version: 0.37.24.

| Task from root | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| cargo make | List available tasks without changing the database |
| cargo make db-check | Verify/import in memory without writing a database |
| cargo make db-generate | Generate a base candidate under target/db-workflow/generated |
| cargo make db-classify | Validate offline CC-CEDICT labels and generate a NEW enriched candidate; no install |
| cargo make db-install | Install the latest successful candidate; never generate implicitly |
| cargo make db-ai-smoke | Diagnose single-sense and 100-sense LM Studio output; no data/cache writes |
| cargo make db-full | Import offline CC-CEDICT classifications, generate enriched bundle and install (LM Studio opt-in) |
| cargo make db-full-dev | Run db-full, then start Trunk |
| cargo make serve | Start Trunk using the installed bundle |
| cargo make dev | Generate, install and serve in that order; stop on failure |

For explicit review and installation stages, run `cargo make db-generate`,
`cargo make db-classify`, then `cargo make db-install` in that order. The
classification step imports and checks the bundled JSON, then builds a **new**
classified candidate and updates `target/db-workflow/latest.json`; it does not
edit the first candidate in place or replace the installed database. The
installer always uses the latest candidate, and can still install a base
candidate when classification has not been run. Do not mistake a successful
rule-based import for expert-reviewed classifications.

Each run prints absolute candidate/database/backup paths. The latest successful
candidate is recorded in target/db-workflow/latest.json. Installation validates
policy, every declared file's size/hash, required reports/notices and the pinned
INPUTS.toml before any replacement. It stages and rechecks the complete bundle,
backs up the previous crates/zipeek-web/static under target/db-workflow/backups and restores
that backup if publication fails. Candidate/backup directories are retained.
Unsafe paths, symlinks, missing notices and checksum mismatches are refused.
Copy the whole bundle, never just hanzi.duckdb. These operations are explicit
local tasks, not Trunk hooks or application startup behavior.

Direct generator commands remain available:

```powershell
# Show help and examples; no database is written
cargo run -p zipeek-db-gen --locked -- --help

# Verify sources, native engine/storage and import in memory; write no database
cargo run -p zipeek-db-gen --locked -- check

# Write a full bundle to a NEW directory
cargo run -p zipeek-db-gen --locked -- generate --output target/reviewed-dictionary
```

A bare cargo run -p zipeek-db-gen now displays Clap help, does no import/generation and
returns usage status 2. Previously it imported in memory without writing a file;
that behavior is now the explicit check command. Successful check ends with
"No database file was written" plus the generation command to use next.

Generate prints the absolute output directory before work and the absolute
hanzi.duckdb and hanzi.manifest.json paths after success, even if informational
logging is disabled. Relative --output paths resolve from the current working
directory. Paths with spaces can be quoted. --help and --version exit successfully.

## Default output and existing directories

```powershell
# Uses the repository crates/zipeek-web/static directory; only works if it does not exist
cargo run -p zipeek-db-gen --locked -- generate
```

The default is repository-relative crates/zipeek-web/static, independent of the shell's working
directory. Its normal checked-in existence means this command refuses to overwrite
it. Use an explicit fresh review directory for regeneration. Existing outputs are
always refused; there is no implicit overwrite or --force option.

## Review and replacement

1. Generate into a fresh review directory.
2. Compare hanzi.manifest.json, ordered logical rows, schema, indexes and
   hanzi.diagnostics.json against the current crates/zipeek-web/static bundle. Database file
   hashes can differ with identical logical content under D22.
3. Preserve a backup of the previous complete bundle. Never patch database bytes
   or replace only the database without its corresponding reports/notices.
4. After approval and verification, replace the complete crates/zipeek-web/static bundle:
   hanzi.duckdb, manifest, diagnostics, INPUTS.toml, ATTRIBUTION.md and notices.
5. Repeat the applicable native/read-only and pinned browser compatibility checks
   in [browser-db](../../../testing-quality/e2e/browser-db.md). Old compatibility evidence does
   not automatically validate a new artifact.

The approved sources/schema/dependencies do not change merely by regeneration.
Native generation requires v2.0.0 and v1.4.0 storage compatibility before output
creation. Artifact export checks complete logical equality and read-only reopening.

## Static serving and measured size

Trunk copies crates/zipeek-web/static contents to the distribution root. The Pages database
URL remains /zipeek/hanzi.duckdb; development uses /hanzi.duckdb. Reports and
notices accompany the database. The earlier A05 snapshot had 12,100 readings (historical, not the installed manifest),
514 diagnostics and a 3,158,016-byte database; file size is not a performance claim.

## References

- [Sources and notices](../../../dictionary-data/schema/sources.md)
- [Import rules](../../../dictionary-data/schema/import-rules.md)
- [Artifacts](../../../dictionary-data/schema/artifacts.md)
- [Logical reproducibility](../../../dictionary-data/schema/reproducibility.md)
- [Generator module](../../../architecture/modules/db-gen.md)

## R56 source-tag normalization and deferred inference

The primary HSK feed uses ICTPOS-style subtypes that the 42 canonical labels
cannot represent losslessly. `import/pos_mapping.rs` handles source-specific
normalization without weakening `PartOfSpeech::from_source_code`:

| Source code | Source meaning | Canonical label | Tradeoff |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `qv` | Verbal/event measure word | `classifier` | Subtype collapsed |
| `qt` | Temporal measure word | `classifier` | Subtype collapsed; not automatically a `time_word` |
| `mq` | Numeral-measure expression | `numeral` | Multi-PoS construction collapsed to single canonical label |
| `cc` | Coordinating conjunction | `conjunction` | Coordination subtype collapsed |

Unknown codes outside the reviewed set still produce diagnostics and do not
invalidate the whole entry. The mappings describe **source-level metadata**, not
AI-derived sense labels. Revisit `mq` and `cc` if the canonical taxonomy gains
additional subtypes. Reference: ICTPOS 3.0 tag descriptions in
https://github.com/memect/kg-beijing/wiki/%E4%B8%AD%E6%96%87%E8%AF%8D%E6%80%A7%E6%A0%87%E8%AE%B0%E9%9B%86 .

`zipeek-db-gen classify` now defers empty/invalid JSON/taxonomy outputs after the
existing three-attempt classifier policy, continues the normal pass, and tries
those deferred senses once more at the end (again at most three attempts).
Reports are JSONL next to the model cache at `<hash>.failures.jsonl`, with
sense ID, original gloss, model, v3 prompt identity, attempt count, error and
Unix timestamp. Successful classifications retain the same model-specific
cache; neither prompt version nor taxonomy version changes.

`zipeek-db-gen classify` may finish with nonzero `Remaining` and `Deferred` while
returning successfully for its batch. `db-full` independently calls
`classify-plan` and refuses generation **and installation** until `Remaining=0`.
Running the command again retries the still-pending senses; it does not accept
empty classifications or invent missing labels. Fatal transport, cache, and
storage failures still abort the batch immediately. The diagnostic report is
recreated for the current run and cleared when all attempted senses recover;
if interrupted, the last saved report survives until the next run begins.


### R111 - Offline AI classification V4 (2026-11-04)

**Developer-only db-gen workflow.** No learner-facing route, AI dashboard, or public model endpoint is added. `zipeek-db-gen classify` sends complete batches of *senses*, not words, to the configured local LM Studio model. The standalone `classify` CLI defaults to 20 senses/request; the `db-full` workflow defaults to a conservative 2 senses/request pending live verification; override with `--batch-size 10`, `20`, `40`, or another positive size up to 100. `ZIPEEK_AI_BATCH_SIZE` controls the `crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/ai_workflow.rs` orchestration; `ZIPEEK_AI_MODEL`, endpoint and timeout retain existing semantics. Context capacity (30k tokens) is not a promise that a 100-sense response fits the output-token budget.

The V4 system prompt distinguishes English sense glosses, grammatical functions and category evidence, prohibits cross-sense label leakage, and treats lexical relationships and source annotations as data rather than an excuse to infer additional semantics. `results` must contain **exactly one** record per requested `(word_id,sense_order)`, no unexpected/duplicated IDs, and only allowed labels. All records are validated before any records from a request are checkpointed. On malformed output or invalid classification, a multi-sense request is split into halves recursively (iteratively scheduled), while single-sense fallback uses the previous bounded recovery procedure. Non-recoverable model/transport errors abort with previous checkpoints intact; malformed single-sense output is deferred and reported.

The Rust workflow now uses a **V6-specific** `<model-hash>-v6.jsonl` cache and adjacent per-sense checkpoint directory. Do not point V6 generation at a V5 cache: old prompt labels are intentionally reclassified, not silently reused, and old checkpoint filenames collide with new records. Cache identity remains model + prompt version + taxonomy version + digest; individual accepted records remain usable after interruptions. `db-full` refuses to generate/install the database until classify-plan reports zero pending senses. The base DuckDB schema, deterministically extracted lexical relations and schema generator are unchanged.

**Benchmark before increasing batch sizes.** Compare 10, 20, 40, and optionally 100 on the same representative set including polysemous senses, function words, classifiers, proper names and explicit lexical relations. Capture wall time, accepted senses/minute, requests, retries and deferrals. The CLI logs `generated_senses_per_minute` and `requests`; record local model and generation settings with the benchmark. Observe response completeness and classification precision, not only throughput. No benchmark measurement against the user's LM Studio model is claimed in this checkpoint.
title: Regeneration

# Schema, index and search review

**Historical review brief, not current artifact specification.** This document evaluates the former 12,100-row HSK-only schema and DuckDB-WASM 1.32.0. The installed expanded dictionary reports 12,188 rows and browser dependency 1.33.1-dev114.0. For the implemented schema and release gates, read [schema](../../../dictionary-data/schema/schema.md), [runtime](../../../dictionary-data/schema/runtime.md), and [source reconciliation](../SOURCE_RECONCILIATION.md).

Requested 2026-10-29, tracked as A62. The original A62 benchmark/FTS work remains a review brief. The incremental
R01/R02 membership, sense and taxonomy DDL is user-approved source work, but
replacing the generated artifact, changing dependencies or breaking practice
replay is not covered by these checkpoints. The current contract remains in [schema](../../../dictionary-data/schema/schema.md),
[queries](../../../dictionary-data/schema/queries.md) and [runtime](../../../dictionary-data/schema/runtime.md).

## Current repository baseline

- 12,100 reading rows in one `words` table; reading identity differs from a
  headword or individual gloss/sense.
- Primary key `id` and unique `(simplified, pinyin)` constraints, with their
  implicit indexes, plus explicit `idx_words_hsk2` and `idx_words_hsk3` indexes.
- Glosses are pipe-separated and PoS values comma-separated. Practice queries
  currently split PoS and test complete tokens rather than search substrings.
- Browser runtime is pinned npm DuckDB-WASM 1.32.0, engine v1.4.3, opening
  v1.4.0-compatible generated storage read-only. Native generation uses the
  approved neo engine v2.0.0. These are distinct version constraints.
- No category/tag tables, FTS corpus/index or extension packaging exists in
  the current dictionary/search pipeline. Browse UI is still future A13 work.

## Tables to compare, not assume

| Candidate | Reason to evaluate | Open choice |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tag vocabulary plus word-to-tag relation | Multiple categories and stable tag identifiers without packing more delimiters into a column | Tag dimensions, reading versus sense ownership, unclassified entries, provenance |
| Word-to-PoS relation or typed list column | Cleaner complete-token filters than repeatedly splitting strings | Compare joins/lists with current scans; no speed claim yet |
| Separate gloss/sense records | Per-sense tags, explicit meanings and ambiguity handling | Introduce only if sense-level behavior is required; do not merge distinct readings |
| Generated search/read model | Keep a convenient row-shaped browser facade while improving storage/search internally | View versus materialized/generated data, row uniqueness and export cost |

A category dictionary and many-to-many assignment relation are a useful starting
proposal for A56/A62. Additional tables can improve data meaning and query
clarity; they are not automatically faster. Classification run metadata may
belong in a table or generation reports; do not choose extra tables merely
because AI enrichment is planned.

Practice candidates must remain one row per WordId after filtering. Joins must
not multiply candidates when a word has several tags or PoS values; compare
`EXISTS`/deduplicated membership strategies and retain deterministic ordering.
Respect D44 OR-within/AND-across semantics. Schema/query changes that affect
candidate identities/order also need the existing replay-impact review.

## Do we need more indexes?

Not established yet. DuckDB has automatic zonemaps and ART indexes associated
with constraints or explicit index creation. Its 1.4 guidance describes useful
ART scans for selective single-column equality/IN predicates; ordinary ART
indexes are not a blanket acceleration for joins, sorting or aggregation.
They also consume memory. See [DuckDB 1.4 indexing](https://duckdb.org/docs/1.4/guides/performance/indexing).

Retain the two approved HSK indexes for now. Measure whether they are used and
whether retaining, removing or adding indexes helps the actual browser workload.
Do not duplicate constraint indexes or infer that indexing a delimited PoS
string accelerates token membership. Any proposed composite membership key may
enforce uniqueness without providing the lookup performance one expects from
other databases. Review its purpose and plan explicitly.

## Is FTS supported in DuckDB-WASM?

Yes: the official DuckDB 1.4 WASM extension list includes `fts`. WASM extension
loading fetches and dynamically loads a matching WebAssembly extension; its
`INSTALL` behavior differs from native persistent installation. See
[WASM extensions](https://duckdb.org/docs/1.4/clients/wasm/extensions).

DuckDB's FTS extension creates an index schema and BM25 search macros. In 1.4,
defaults include Porter stemming, English stopwords, accent stripping and an
ignore pattern excluding characters outside lowercase ASCII letters. Those
defaults do not preserve our Chinese/pinyin/numeric-tone search semantics.
Evaluate FTS first for English gloss/sentence retrieval; suitable Chinese
segmentation and tone-preserving pinyin behavior require separate design/tests.
See [DuckDB 1.4 FTS](https://duckdb.org/docs/1.4/core_extensions/full_text_search).

BM25 word retrieval is also different from approved Browse substring/prefix and
exact-filter behavior. Do not silently replace that contract or ranking with
FTS. A ranked mode would require a product/URL review.

The documentation establishes platform availability, not tested support in
Zipeek's exact package/build. A62 must probe:

1. Matching extension version/build, asset loading and packaging/notices under
   the existing dependency and local-asset policy; no unapproved CDN/latest path.
2. Read-only queries over an index generated beforehand. Building FTS mutates
   storage, so never create it inside the shipped read-only dictionary at runtime.
3. Native v2.0.0 generator output versus v1.4.3 WASM extension compatibility;
   compatible base storage alone does not prove extension macros/data compatibility.
4. Root and `/zipeek/` browser serving, startup size/latency, missing extension
   behavior and how existing search works without an optional FTS path.
5. English stopwords/inflections, hanzi, pinyin tones/digits/case and rare/proper
   senses, with explicit expected behavior.

Any FTS schema is generated manually with an approved artifact change; no
generation or extension install is added to application builds by this brief.

## Required evidence and deliverable

Compare the current schema/query baseline against minimal candidate designs
using representative HSK-only, PoS-only, category-only and combined filters;
small and large result sets; counts; ordered pagination; exact word lookup;
and approved text-search strategies. Include unknown/multiple tags and PoS.

Record `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`, browser timings (cold/warm), database and extension
bytes, startup/memory cost and correct result/ordering parity. The small current
dictionary makes scans a legitimate baseline, not a proven performance problem.
Use isolated generated scratch artifacts for approved experiments; do not
replace `web/static` while conducting the review.

A62's deliverable is concrete DDL/query/index proposals, benchmark evidence,
FTS compatibility findings, schema/replay/dependency impacts and a recommended
scope for approval. A56 supplies taxonomy/ownership decisions and A61 supplies
the setup-filter workload; schema review itself need not wait for their UI.

## Candidate normalized search model (2026-11-04 review addition)

The current `words` table is a **reading-level projection**, not a normalized
sense dictionary. `part_of_speech` is comma-delimited, and `english` is
pipe-delimited; therefore a query cannot unambiguously associate an individual
sense with a part of speech or a category. A HSK-level filter can use the current
scalar column, but adding systems/editions and combinations complicates DDL.

A candidate layout for review (not approved DDL):

- `readings(reading_id PRIMARY KEY, simplified, traditional, pinyin,
  pinyin_numeric, frequency)`. Preserve existing `WordId` as `reading_id`,
  including the current `(simplified, pinyin)` identity contract.
- `senses(sense_id PRIMARY KEY, reading_id REFERENCES readings, gloss,
  source_order, source_id)`. Store a separate row for each actual source sense;
  **do not** assume splitting the legacy `english` display field reproduces
  independently attested senses or correctly attaches PoS.
- `parts_of_speech(pos_id PRIMARY KEY, code UNIQUE)` and
  `sense_pos(sense_id, pos_id, PRIMARY KEY(sense_id, pos_id))` for genuine
  sense-level labels. If existing input only supplies reading-level PoS,
  instead use `reading_pos(reading_id, pos_id)` until provenance supports the
  more granular model.
- `hsk_membership(reading_id, system, level, PRIMARY KEY(reading_id,
  system))` for system/level filtering. Current D07 semantics only permit one
  level per system per reading; preserving that constraint avoids duplicates.
- `tags(tag_id PRIMARY KEY, slug UNIQUE, label)` with explicit
  `reading_tags(reading_id, tag_id)` or `sense_tags(sense_id, tag_id)` only
  after A56 establishes category ownership and provenance.
- A **generated, stable `words` read projection** preserving the web `WordRow`
  shape during rollout. Build it once during native generation (not a browser
  runtime materialization); queries returning candidates must preserve one row
  per reading and order by `reading_id`.

Candidate index experiments should use selective access patterns, not blanket
indexing: compare `(system, level, reading_id)` on HSK membership, a PoS-to-
reading membership path, exact `(simplified, pinyin)` and `pinyin_numeric`
lookup, and ordered page scans. The PK/unique constraints already create ART
indexes and should not be duplicated. Text search should benchmark normalized
pinyin prefix/equality, Chinese substring queries and English gloss tokens
separately. DuckDB FTS is **not** a drop-in Chinese index; default English
stemming/tokenization is inappropriate for hanzi and tone-marked pinyin.

Acceptance evidence for a schema change: source-level attribution and sense
identity, before/after row parity, no join-induced duplicate candidates,
`EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on native and actual pinned browser-WASM runtime, size and
cold/warm query measurements, regenerated provenance manifests, and explicit
replay impact review. This section is a design proposal only: neither
`words.sql` nor generated DuckDB binaries are changed by the translation MVP.

## Checkpoint R01 - generated normalized memberships (2026-11-04)

The first approved schema implementation adds `word_hsk_membership` and
`word_pos_membership` as distinct, keyed many-to-many relations. Existing
`words` remains the reading identity and browser-facing compatibility table;
its IDs, SQL projection and matching/MCQ replay semantics are unchanged.

HSK rows use `(word_id, system)` as their unique key, with `hsk2` and `hsk3`
and levels 1-7 (7 denotes the consolidated advanced band). PoS membership is
**reading-level source metadata**, not sense-level AI classification; it is
populated from the existing canonical CSV values. No new taxonomy or inferred
per-sense metadata is claimed. Both relations are populated in the same import
transaction, with rollback on failure. The generator's logical snapshot now
includes sorted membership rows for output/reopen comparison.

This checkpoint intentionally does **not** change `words.sql`, browser reads,
indexes, source import formats, `hanzi.duckdb`, or dependency versions. The
compatibility table and its existing two HSK indexes remain because browser
queries depend on them. Adding indexes to membership predicates requires
`EXPLAIN ANALYZE` and WASM benchmarks before indexing decisions.

Next: preserve actual source sense boundaries before introducing `senses`,
controlled tag taxonomy, `sense_pos`/`sense_categories`, classification
provenance and reusable AiMux 0.6.0 enrichment. Then benchmark HSK+PoS+tag
filters and migrate read APIs without duplicating practice candidates.

Validation pending: this environment has no Cargo/Rust toolchain or native
DuckDB engine, so generated-schema tests and native/WASM round trips could not
be executed. R01 is a source checkpoint, not a verified release artifact.

## Checkpoint R02 - source-backed senses and controlled taxonomy (2026-11-04)

Generator source changes introduce `word_senses` keyed by `(word_id, sense_order)` and preserve the original nonempty HSK meanings as individual rows. `source_ref` identifies the one-based HSK source entry and `source_gloss_order` identifies the one-based meaning position; merged duplicate readings retain the first nonempty gloss source, matching the existing compatibility `words.english` selection policy. When primary meanings are missing, CC-CEDICT fallback senses retain the original source line and meaning index. A pipe within an original gloss is preserved as literal content, rather than being interpreted as a sense separator. No inference or silent reassignment of a meaning to another reading occurs.

A constrained `parts_of_speech` catalog uses all 42 canonical `zipeek-core` codes. A version-1 controlled category catalog initially contains travel, transport, food, shopping, family, education, work, health, nature, time, home, and communication. The new `sense_pos` and `sense_categories` relations are **empty by design**: reading-level source PoS cannot safely be assigned to every individual sense. `classification_runs` stores the model, prompt version, taxonomy version and input digest needed for subsequent AI-derived rows; classifier integration and caching are R03 scope. These are schema scaffolds, not claims of classified data.

Generation and staged/read-only verification now compare individual sense rows and category catalog contents. No index is added beyond existing HSK indexes and constraint-backed indexes: selective query benchmarks, shipped artifact growth, and GitHub Pages/WASM load time have not been measured. Current browser-facing `words` queries and deterministic practice URLs remain unchanged.

R02 is a source checkpoint only. The native DuckDB engine/Rust toolchain is not installed here; native schema syntax/constraint support, compilation, generation and browser tests still require validation before a generated artifact is approved.


## R03 - cache-backed sense classification (2026-11-04)

Classification output is strict JSON with allowed `pos` and `categories` codes. Each cached JSONL record references a `(word_id, sense_order)`, source digest, model, prompt version and taxonomy version. `db-gen generate --classification-cache PATH` validates every record before writing anything, applies validated assignments transactionally to both in-memory and staged databases, and verifies all classification rows in logical snapshots. Without the flag the existing offline generator writes no AI classifications. The native AiMux entry point is an async library function, not yet a batch CLI. Compilation, DB reopening and LM Studio integration are unverified; review history is retained in the 2026-11-04 completed outcomes.
title: Schema, index and search review

# R139 - Dictionary verification for AI sentence vocabulary

## Implemented

After structured AI translation, Zipeek attempts one read-only DuckDB query for the entire bounded vocabulary list (at most 24 candidates). The query uses parameter placeholders for exact simplified/traditional matches, with no fuzzy semantic matching. The result includes dictionary ID, Chinese forms, pinyin, source English glossary, HSK 2.0 and 3.0 levels, and frequency rank when available.

The reconciliation keeps the AI observation separate from the dictionary record. When several entries share a Chinese spelling, exact normalized pinyin is preferred, then known/lower frequency rank and stable word ID. Alternative-entry count is disclosed; selecting a likely row is not a disambiguated sense match. Original dictionary definitions and AI glosses are shown with separate provenance labels. A missing dictionary match is not presented as verified.

The source-only response remains functional when the dictionary is unavailable or lookup fails; the page reports the failed verification without discarding successful translation or AI analysis. Generation checks prevent an old database response from appearing after source or direction edits.

## Known limitations

- Dictionary verification establishes **word metadata**, not whole-sentence HSK difficulty; grammar and sentence level remain AI estimates.
- Dictionary glosses are word-level and may not describe the sense used in context. No word-sense alignment or Chinese segmentation correction is claimed.
- Frequency is a rank, not a probability; missing frequency is allowed.
- Pinyin matching strips whitespace and is case-insensitive, but does not transliterate numeric versus tone-mark forms. Ambiguous spellings require a future explicit sense selector.
- Dynamic queries rely on generated dictionary availability and browser DuckDB; Windows WASM build, live AI + database E2E, Traditional Chinese matching and HSK/frequency data correctness require verification.
- No new schema, dependency, AI configuration, or local learner data migration.

## Windows acceptance

1. `cargo fmt --all --check`
2. `cargo test --workspace --locked`
3. `cargo check -p zipeek --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --locked`
4. Run `cargo make serve`, configure LM Studio, translate Chinese → English and English → Chinese, and check verified HSK/frequency labels.
5. Test a phrase such as 一本 (missing exact entry), a homograph such as 行 (ambiguity) and a dictionary-unavailable scenario. Translation and AI analysis should remain readable.
title: R139 - Dictionary verification for AI sentence vocabulary
