# Coding standards

Conventions for application code. Process rules live in [AGENTS](../../../../AGENTS.md);
testing strategy in [testing/TESTING.md](../../../testing-quality/acceptance/testing.md); architecture in
[architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md](../../../architecture/architecture.md).

## General principles

- **Prefer clarity over cleverness.** A reader should understand the code without
  tracing types across files.
- **Fail loudly in development, gracefully in production.** `unwrap` / `expect` is
  acceptable in tests and unreachable branches; never in request handlers, DB
  queries, or user input parsing.
- **No silent fallbacks for correctness bugs.** If a query returns unexpected
  data, log it. If a computation can fail, return `Result`, don't `Option`-swallow
  it.
- **Preserve intent when editing.** Do not refactor adjacent code to "clean up"
  while fixing a bug; keep diffs focused.
- **Derive UI affordances from typed state.** Do not hide or enable actions by matching user-facing error-message text; pass explicit props from reducer-backed containers.
- **Keep pagination contracts shared.** Query limits, lookahead checks and displayed results must use the same page-size constant.

## Rust

### Formatting and lints

- `cargo fmt --all` - mandatory, no exceptions.
- Clippy checks deny warnings; use affected packages/targets during routine
  work and workspace/all-targets for full regression under AGENTS §6. Avoid `#[allow(...)]` without an approved technical reason. Do not add code comments. Prefer resolving the lint through code changes.
- Edition 2024, Rust 1.97.1 (see `rust-toolchain.toml`).

### Readability of expressions and match arms

- Keep match arms on separate lines when a match has multiple variants. Do not
  compress whole match expressions or control-flow branches onto a single line,
  even if Rustfmt accepts it.
- Format multi-step closures, error handling and long function calls as readable
  multi-line blocks. Short single-expression closures may stay inline when clear.
- Prefer `const fn` for genuinely compile-time-capable pure methods, such as
  enum-to-static-string mappings; do not mark functions `const` merely to save lines.
- Treat `cargo fmt` as the minimum formatting requirement, not permission to
  squeeze several logical operations onto a single line.

### Modules and platform API boundaries

- A stateful browser integration such as microphone capture must separate the
  public recorder API, owned state, event/capture wiring, waveform processing,
  and error conversion when those concerns become substantial. Keep the parent
  `mod.rs` limited to exports, shared constants, and module declarations.
- Keep JavaScript-API return types faithful to the pinned `web-sys` signatures.
  In particular, `BlobEvent::data()` is `Option<Blob>`; handle absent chunks
  without panicking, and pass `blob.as_ref()` to `js_sys::Array`.
- Keep tuple fields private by default. A sibling module requiring controlled
  construction should use a `pub(super)` constructor, not a public inner field.
- Keep source tests aligned with extracted module files; never weaken runtime
  assertions just to satisfy a source-layout assertion.
- Preserve single-field tuple structs for opaque ownership wrappers where
  they express the abstraction clearly, such as `MicrophoneRecorder(Rc<RefCell<State>>)`.
- When moving code to submodules, preserve public imports, existing behaviors,
  and test coverage. Source assertions must follow the actual module graph,
  rather than forcing code back into a large parent file.
- A source-level Node pass is not a substitute for a target-specific Rust build;
  WASM/browser APIs require `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`
  and browser acceptance before a release can be considered verified.

### Stateful Yew feature components

- Use `#[function_component]` and a typed `Properties` contract for standalone
  UI components; do not expose positional rendering helpers with many unrelated
  arguments (`view(board, feedback, hint, complete, ...)`).
- Keep feature-specific modules inside a named directory (`feature/mod.rs`,
  `feature/board.rs`, `feature/state.rs`) rather than accumulating sibling files
  such as `feature_board.rs` next to route files.
- Keep the route page responsible for URL decoding and data loading. A session
  owner manages interactive state; tiles, controls, progress and results are
  focused components. Use a scoped typed context and reducer when several
  nested components need the same state and actions; do not introduce global
  state for a single game.
- Model transitions as reducer actions with explicit guards. For advancing to
  another round, generate the next board before committing the counter and
  cumulative scores. Never mutate half a session on a failed transition.
- Retain stable `data-*` hooks, `aria-pressed`, keyboard-accessible buttons,
  and difficulty-dependent Hanzi font sizes through refactors.
- Preserve the domain engine in a pure Rust crate without `web-sys`, Yew or
  JavaScript dependencies. Split domain model, generation, gameplay and tests
  when they have separate reasons to change.

### Naming

- Types, traits, enums: `PascalCase`.
- Functions, variables, modules: `snake_case`.
- Constants and statics: `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`.
- Acronyms: `Url` not `URL`, `Api` not `API`, per Rust API guidelines.
- Domain types: `Word`, `CandidatePool`, `RoundFilter`, `HskSystem`, `Hsk2Level`,
  `Hsk3Level` - no `Data`, `Info`, `Item` suffixes.
- Error types: `BuildError`, `DbError`, `LoadError` - not `Error` or generic names.

### Errors

- Public functions returning fallible operations use `Result<T, E>` with a
  domain-specific error enum.
- Use `thiserror` for error enums (already a dependency). Do not use `anyhow`
  in library code; it's permitted only in `db-gen`'s `main.rs` if needed for
  user-facing errors.
- Errors must be actionable: include the offending input where possible.
  - Bad: `Err(BuildError::InsufficientPool)`
  - Good: `Err(BuildError::InsufficientPool { view: View::Strict, found: 5, needed: 8 })`

### `unwrap` / `expect` / `panic!`

- **Allowed:** in unit tests, in `const fn` when the failure is a compile-time
  error, and in demonstrably unreachable branches with self-explanatory types or control flow.
- **Not allowed:** on `Result`/`Option` from user input, DB queries, network
  calls, or parsing external data.
- Required provider contexts are component-tree invariants: `use_context::<RequiredContext>().unwrap()` is allowed when the parent route always mounts that provider. A missing provider is a programming defect, not a user-facing recoverable condition.
- Never panic on user input, database operations, localStorage, network failures, or other recoverable conditions in a Yew component or handler; render an error state or return a typed error instead.

### Modules and file organization

- One module per file. `web/src/components/foo.rs` not `web/src/components.rs`.
- Public API goes through `mod.rs` re-exports where it improves ergonomics
  (e.g., `pub use round::{build_round, CandidatePool, RoundFilter};`).
- Pure logic lives in `zipeek-core` when shared between `web` and `db-gen`;
  otherwise local to its crate.
- WASM-specific browser access (DOM, `js_sys`, `web_sys`) belongs in
  `zipeek-browser` or the `zipeek-db/wasm` adapter when it is not Yew-specific.
  Yew rendering stays in `zipeek-web`. `zipeek-core` must compile natively.

## Yew

### Tailwind styling (D31)

Tailwind CSS 4.3.4 remains the required component styling approach. A35 corrected
the shell/card stylesheet drift on 2026-10-28: mounted components use utilities,
main.css holds theme aliases and minimal foundation rules, and inline.css retains
critical bootstrap/loading styling. Rust source detection is explicit; the
unused v3 configuration and bespoke shell/card selectors are removed.

- Use Tailwind utilities in Yew markup for layout, spacing, sizing, typography,
  borders, responsive rules and interaction states. Keep conditional variants as
  complete class strings that Tailwind can detect; do not construct class names
  from fragments at runtime.
- Keep shared theme/design tokens in CSS where appropriate and consume them
  through utilities. Preserve the slate/blue theme and landscape composition.
- Allow focused custom CSS for critical pre-WASM bootstrap styling, shared
  tokens, keyframes or a concrete effect that benefits from it. A reason for one
  exception does not justify moving ordinary component styling into stylesheets.
- Do not hide the same bespoke component system behind blanket @apply rules.
  Factor repeated UI into Yew components and small explicit utility variants.
- Verify Tailwind 4 source detection for Rust/Yew files and remove obsolete
  conflicting rules as components migrate. Do not assume legacy v3 configuration
  is automatically active or upgrade packages during the correction.

The implemented styling boundary and visual checks are in
[UI_ARCHITECTURE](../../../architecture/ui-architecture.md#tailwind-styling-implementation-d31--a35).

### Components

- One component per file, function components only (no classes).
- Props are `#[derive(Properties, PartialEq)]` structs.
- Use `#[function_component]` with a clear component name matching the file
  (`WordCard` in `word_card.rs`).
- Avoid prop drilling past 2 levels; use contexts.
  The 2026-10-27 review's concrete provider/reducer proposal is in
  [UI_ARCHITECTURE](../../../architecture/ui-architecture.md). Shared services and
  feature state belong behind scoped hooks/providers; simple leaf inputs still
  use props. Do not expose raw state setters as another feature's public command
  interface.

### Yew presentation composition

- Import components explicitly at the module boundary (`use crate::components::{BrowseProvider, WordSetsProvider};`) rather than repeating qualified paths in `html!` markup. Wildcard imports are not required for component composition.
- Write nested providers and other multi-element Yew trees across multiple lines, with each element's closing tag aligned to its opener; do not compress provider nesting into one line.
- Keep page-specific callback conditions and view-building chains readable with normal Rust multiline blocks, even where the formatter would tolerate a dense expression.
- For nontrivial status-specific markup, compute `let status_component = match &state.status { ... };` before the parent `html!` and insert `{status_component}` in the shallow outer view.
- Extract meaningful loading/error/empty, result-card, and pagination views into focused components. Prefer keeping short related status components in one module over one file per line of markup.
- Container components access reducers/providers and wire callbacks; presentational components take focused `Properties` and do not reach into unrelated feature contexts.
- Keep stable `data-component` and existing `data-*` E2E hooks during refactors.

### Hooks

- `use_state` for temporary form input local to the owning component; use a pure `use_reducer` plus a scoped provider for shared feature state and interdependent transitions. Keep I/O in the provider/service, never inside `Reducible::reduce`.
- `use_effect_with` for side effects, with explicit dependency lists - do not
  use empty dependency lists unless the effect is genuinely once-only.
- `use_memo` for derived state that's expensive to compute; do not memoize
  cheap operations.
- `Callback` for event handlers passed to children; `use_callback` when the
  identity matters (prevents unnecessary re-renders).

### State ownership and refactor discipline (R161)

- A page with multiple interdependent request/output/error/loading fields should use
  a typed `Reducible` state machine. Independent controls such as a font preference
  may remain `use_state`; hook count is a review signal, not an automatic failure.
- Reducers must be pure. Network requests, browser storage and DOM operations stay
  in effects, callbacks or services; render state transitions are dispatched
  atomically, with stale asynchronous results rejected using request epochs.
- Place substantial reducer implementations in a feature-local `state.rs` module.
  Do not replace independently managed hooks with a large mutable "controller"
  that merely hides the same coupling.
- Split oversized presentation trees into focused feature components or view
  functions. Prefer short, named sections to nested 100-line `html!` expressions.
  Keep event types explicit (`FocusEvent` for focus, `MouseEvent` for clicks).
- A module declared as `mod foo;` may use either `foo.rs` or `foo/mod.rs`, never
  both. Parent modules named `foo.rs` may own child files `foo/bar.rs` without
  a second `foo/mod.rs`; do not use `#[path]` to paper over moves.
- A source-only Node suite does **not** validate Rust syntax or type checking.
  Before declaring a refactor compiled, run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`,
  `cargo check --workspace --locked`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, Clippy,
  and the WASM target. Report unexecuted checks explicitly.

### Events and handlers

- Never `unwrap` on `event.target_dyn_into::<HtmlInputElement>()` - the DOM can
  change. Use `if let Some(el) = ...`.
- Every interactive element has a keyboard equivalent (Enter/Space for buttons,
  arrow keys for navigation). See UX.md's accessibility section.

### Async

- Use `wasm_bindgen_futures::spawn_local` for fire-and-forget effects, or
  `use_async` patterns for stateful async work.
- Do not block the render loop. Long queries go through a state machine
  (Idle → Loading → Ready / Error), never a synchronous await in render.

## Shared crate (`zipeek-core`)

- Must compile on both `wasm32-unknown-unknown` and native.
- No `web_sys`, `js_sys`, `wasm_bindgen` imports.
- No I/O - it holds types and pure logic only. Queries take data as arguments,
  not a DB handle.
- Public API is versioned by the repo, not semver; breaking changes to
  `zipeek-core` are fine during development (AGENTS.md §2).

## Database generator (`crates/zipeek-db-gen`)

- Native binary; runs manually, never in an app build.
- Reads pinned inputs only - no network calls. Source fetching is a separate
  shell script (see DB.md).
- Verifies SHA-256 of every input file against `MANIFEST.toml` before parsing;
  aborts on mismatch.
- Logs every dropped word, unknown PoS code, level conflict, and gloss-pipe
  replacement.
- D22 requires deterministic logical output: identical verified inputs and
  pinned tooling produce the same ordered rows, IDs, schema/index definitions,
  and import/drop diagnostics. Record SHA-256 for each final `hanzi.duckdb`
  artifact as an integrity check; different runs need not have identical file
  bytes. Do not patch or mask database headers to force a matching checksum.
- Before generation, query `SELECT version()` against the native
  engine, log the returned version, and fail unless it is exactly `v2.0.0`
  (D23 supersedes D21's earlier v1.4.3 condition). Configure and verify
  `storage_compatibility_version = v1.4.0` before creating output; default neo
  files are not readable by the pinned WASM runtime. Future artifact creation
  must use this configured connection and explicitly compatible storage.
  This is a generator invocation check, not a Cargo build script or an
  automatic application-build generation step.

## Tests

- Unit tests in the same file as the code (`#[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }`)
  for pure logic.
- Integration tests in `tests/` for cross-module behaviour.
- Test names describe the scenario, not the function:
  - Bad: `test_build_round`
  - Good: `build_round_returns_insufficient_pool_when_strict_view_is_small`
- Fixtures live in `tests/fixtures/` as data, not inline structs, when larger
  than ~20 lines. See TESTING.md's fixture patterns.
- Golden tests (round builder, seed encoding) assert both the input string and
  the expected output hash - see ROUND_GENERATION.md for the contract.

## E2E component selectors

- Give significant mounted Yew page and feature roots a unique, stable
  `data-component="kebab-case-name"` value. Prefer identifying the component
  (for example, `browse-page`) rather than its current heading or CSS layout.
- Use `data-action` for controls where action identity improves testing, and
  `data-state` or an existing dedicated `data-*` attribute for observable state.
  Retain semantic roles, accessible labels, and native keyboard behaviour.
- E2E selectors must not infer a route from an incidental tag structure or
  placeholder once the route renders a real component. Placeholders may still
  be asserted for genuine unimplemented or not-found routes.
- Preserve existing test-specific attributes during gradual migration; no
  dependency or round-URL format changes are required.

## Documentation

Code carries no doc comments and no explanatory inline comments. The code
should be self-explanatory through naming and structure; if a reader needs a
comment to follow it, the fix is clearer names, smaller functions, or an entry
in the relevant `docs/` file.

- No `///` doc comments on functions, types, or modules.
- No `//` explanatory comments above or inside code.
- `// TODO:` and `// FIXME:` comments are also forbidden. If work is needed,
  add a task to `TASKS.md` and reference it in the commit message or PR body.
- Rationale and design decisions live in `docs/architecture/architecture.md`,
  `docs/games/round-generation.md`, `docs/dictionary-data/schema/db.md`, or the
  relevant decision record - not in the source tree.
- No comment exceptions apply to lint suppressions or unreachable branches. When a lint allowance is necessary, record rationale in maintained technical documentation and obtain approval for the change.

## Feature module organization (R148)

- Put feature-specific Yew components under `components/<feature>/`; Practice has
  `setup/`, `exercises/` and `session/` subdivisions. Generic primitives remain at
  the component root. Pages live under `pages/<feature>/`, keeping stable route
  module names through explicit Rust `#[path]` declarations where appropriate.
- Preserve existing public reexports while moving implementation files. Avoid
  adding icon abstractions: use `yew_icons::{Icon, IconData}` directly in views.
- Only use icon constants present in the pinned `yew_icons` inventory.
  `scripts/fixtures/yew-icons-lucide-r148.json` records the supplied generated
  Lucide collection, and `r148-feature-layout-icons.test.cjs` checks all Rust icon
  references. This source-level guard complements, but does not replace, Cargo.
- When moving files, update the owning `mod.rs`, import paths, source-contract
  tests and living documentation in the same change. Do not move files merely
  to shorten individual names or add wrappers without an actual dependency need.

## Additional implementation review contracts

- **Required contexts:** Trace the actual provider tree, routes, tests and callers before changing `Option<T>` hooks to required accessors. Required providers should have an explicit accessor contract and actionable absence diagnostics; intentionally optional providers remain optional. A provider's runtime loading/failure state is not its absence.
- **Workflow state:** Identify authoritative, derived, transient, request and persisted state before major refactors. Verify coordinated resets, invalid states, overlapping requests, stale callbacks and lifecycle cleanup; use a reducer only when it clarifies the invariant.
- **Markup and events:** Keep `html!` markup expanded and reviewable, name callbacks before markup rather than constructing them in attributes, and prefer typed callbacks over avoidable DOM parsing. If DOM `data-*` routing is justified, validate values, choose `current_target` when appropriate and test nested clicks and keyboard activation.
- **UX and accessibility:** Preserve shared shell, tokens, icons, semantic controls, focus, touch and keyboard behavior, and explicit loading/failure/recovery states. Inspect rendered UI when available; compilation alone does not verify usability.
- **Async performance:** Review browser work, cancellation, stale results and cleanup before adding timers or workers. Use measurable evidence before claiming performance improvements; deferring synchronous computation does not make it nonblocking.
- **Source audits:** For material findings cite file/line evidence, observed behavior, concrete impact, minimal remedy, priority and remaining uncertainty. Avoid judgments based only on line count, hook count or stylistic preference.
- **No legacy compatibility:** The development-phase policy in [AGENTS](../../../../AGENTS.md) applies to all historical formats. Deterministic current behavior, input validation and intentional handling of local data loss remain required.
title: Coding standards

> **R492 current source ownership:** Grammar teaching tables, guided-check data, region plan and published slugs now live under `crates/zipeek-pedagogy/src/grammar/`. Patterns 21-100 are generated there from `docs/learning-practice/GRAMMAR_CURRICULUM_SOURCE.tsv`. Step/reveal/answer logic lives under `zipeek-exercises::grammar_learning`, with only Yew interaction state in web. All 100 regions are draft-authored; editorial and HSK review remain outstanding. The historical R485 path/status note below is superseded.

# Courses authoring and structural validation

The five published grammar courses are teaching drafts, not verified HSK syllabus coverage or authoritative mastery assessments. This guide explains how to add a course without leaving its registry, teaching activities and assessment formats inconsistent.

## Source ownership

| Source | Authoring responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/zipeek-pedagogy/src/grammar/curriculum.rs` | Grammar explanations, examples, translations and original five guided three-choice banks |
| `courses/curriculum_registry.rs` | Stable course and grammar-point IDs, local sequence and prerequisites; official HSK status remains unverified |
| `courses/guided_bank.rs` | Guided sentence-builder and transformation banks, accepted tile sequences and feedback |
| `courses/assessment.rs` | Independent draft multiple-choice item for each registered point |
| `courses/construction_assessment.rs` | Independent unassisted sentence-construction draft for each authored course |
| `courses/authoring.rs` | Cross-format structural validation (`validate_published_courses`) and detailed failures |
| `courses/grammar_lesson.rs`, `courses/grammar_expansion_lesson.rs`, `courses/grammar_lesson_scaffold.rs` | Two teaching engines sharing navigation and progress shell; Yew-only course interaction |

## Adding or editing a grammar course

1. Author nonempty titles, explanations, examples and translations. Avoid claims of verified HSK syllabus coverage without an independently checked source.
2. Add a stable curriculum registry entry with the same course identifier and one point ID per authored grammar point; verify prerequisites refer to earlier published courses.
3. Author exactly one guided comprehension check and one independent draft MCQ per point. The independent question should not rely on a visible guided answer.
4. Provide guided tile activities with nonempty metadata, a distinct bank and a full display permutation. Every accepted order must use unique in-bounds tile indices and leave at least one distractor.
5. Add an unassisted construction assessment linked to a point in that same course. Do not repeat a tile or include a reference answer during the attempt.
6. Update `GuidedCourse` region mapping, mosaic region/link and course route. Update the E2E scenario and coverage inventory.
7. Run the structural validator's unit test and the existing Courses tests, then compile natively, compile WASM and run Chrome E2E on the pinned toolchain. A passing Node source-contract test alone is **not** Rust or browser acceptance.

The validator catches missing or duplicated authored identifiers, blank content, invalid question keys, duplicate choices, incomplete point coverage, malformed tile permutations, duplicate activity IDs, and cross-course construction-point mismatches. These are **structural safeguards only**: they do not prove pedagogical fairness, meaningful distractors, translation quality, accessible presentation or a qualified review of the Mandarin.

## Explicitly out of scope

No validation result is a mastery grant. Draft scores remain in memory; all 150 mosaic regions stay concealed. Award rules, verified evidence/provenance, DuckDB writes, completed grammar records, and artwork-reveal predicates require their separately approved implementation and browser acceptance.
title: Courses authoring and structural validation

# Docs Markdown renderer

The `zipeek-docs` crate uses `pulldown-cmark =0.13.0` with the `html` feature and no default CLI features. The existing Yew application calls it through Rust/WASM directly; there is no separate browser JS parser or WASM module.

## Syntax and security

CommonMark nested lists, fenced code, links and references, GFM tables, task lists, strikethrough and footnotes are supported. Rust emits deterministic unique heading IDs and exposes the same headings to the Docs TOC. Raw HTML becomes escaped text. Links are checked against a safe external-scheme and docs-root policy, including reference-style destinations. Invalid image targets render a placeholder.

All files in `docs/` remain published. `#/docs/` links and `/zipeek/` asset base behavior are preserved. Links to headings in another Markdown document use `#/docs/<encoded-path>?heading=<heading-id>` so the hash router receives one valid route. The Docs page scrolls to the heading after rendering, including direct links and reloads. Same-document `#heading-id` anchors remain local to the article.

## Acceptance

```powershell
cargo test --locked -p zipeek-docs
cargo check --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p zipeek-web
cargo run --locked -p zipeek-cli -- build docs
cargo make serve
```

In Chrome, verify nested Markdown, footnotes, checkboxes, tables, raw/source toggle, duplicate headings, CJK heading IDs, internal links, relative images and browser security under `/zipeek/`. These checks have not run here. TD-006 remains open until this R429 route/scroll behavior and prior renderer behavior pass locked WASM and real-browser acceptance.

## Static publication

Trunk copies `../../docs` directly into the published `docs/` directory via the
`copy-dir` entry in `crates/zipeek-web/index.html`. No duplicate Markdown tree
is maintained in `static/docs`. `cargo make docs` generates only
`crates/zipeek-web/static/docs/index.json`, which the Docs explorer uses for
navigation and search; run it after editing documentation or during first-time
setup. `cargo make setup-all` includes this preparation. `cargo make serve`
does not regenerate the index on every invocation. CI and deployment continue
to generate the index before building. GitHub Pages uses the same relative
`docs/` assets under `/zipeek/`.
title: Docs Markdown renderer

# Character Hunt - exercise contract (R215)

Character Hunt is a dictionary-backed Hanzi assembly exercise. It is available without AI in Quick Practice (and also Advanced Practice) under **Exercises → Choose** and configured under **Exercises → Configure**. Its difficulty is stored in the Rust `PracticeDraft`, not selected again during gameplay.

| Difficulty | Grid | Hanzi typography |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy | 2 × 2 | 5xl mobile, 7xl desktop |
| Medium (default) | 3 × 3 | 4xl mobile, 6xl desktop |
| Difficult | 4 × 4 | 3xl mobile, 5xl desktop |
| Hardcore | 5 × 5 | xl mobile, 3xl desktop |

## Rules and generation

The pure Rust domain engine (`zipeek-exercises::character_hunt`) takes an eligible vocabulary snapshot, a difficulty, and a seed. It accepts distinct Simplified-Hanzi entries containing exactly two or three characters. It allocates character tiles from dictionary entries, shuffles them deterministically, and retains the validated word-to-tile mapping privately. Word groups do not share characters or tiles, so removing completed words never makes another target unplayable. The generator deterministically retries 32 candidate orders to avoid rejecting a solvable board merely because a greedy word selection dead-ended. If a board cannot be filled from the supplied words, generation fails visibly; it never inserts fabricated answer words.

A single noninteractive decoy character from the eligible vocabulary may fill an odd-sized grid when the source lacks compatible three-character words. If there is no unused source character, generation fails rather than inventing a filler. The decoy does not count toward the word total. Completed words are presented as Hanzi with an optional word-level pinyin reading and the dictionary-sourced English gloss (not merely a list of Hanzi). A completion message also identifies the word and its meaning. Alternative dictionary glosses are deduplicated and displayed together, capped at three to keep the card readable; missing definitions are marked unavailable instead of fabricated. Pinyin is withheld if source readings cannot be aligned or do not agree. Each non-decoy tile displays a large Hanzi with smaller dictionary-sourced pinyin beneath when word-level syllables align with the characters. Multi-pronunciation entries with conflicting readings do not display an arbitrary reading. In Easy/Medium/Difficult, the large Hanzi typography is preserved; Hardcore uses compact typography. Learners select two or three active tiles in order; a matching known entry grays out those tiles and records the word. Incorrect combinations increment a local mistake counter and reset the selection without removing tiles. Three consecutive mistakes briefly highlight the first tile of a remaining solution; after five, the entire 2-3-character solution briefly highlights for approximately 950 ms. After seven consecutive mistakes the user may explicitly reveal one word; revealed words count as completed but are tracked separately as assisted. A correct match resets the consecutive-mistake escalation. Automatic visual hints appear only on the third and fifth consecutive mistakes, then clear after 950 ms or immediately on the next tile interaction. The tile highlight is static rather than continuously pulsing. Manual Hint works only when no tile selection is in progress, so it cannot obscure an active attempt. The hint button is disabled until the partial selection is cleared or finished. Completion requires finding every hidden target. No user-generated text or AI model is needed for verdicts.

## Session integration

The existing four-step setup (`Path → Exercises: Choose/Configure → Vocabulary → Summary`) launches `#/practice/character-hunt` with difficulty and vocabulary source. It uses Fixed 5 by default, with Fixed 10, Fixed 20, and Endless available. The UI keeps difficulty fixed across boards and shows round-level progress, completed words, mistakes, and an explicit Next round action. Learners can deselect individual tiles by tapping them again without counting an incorrect attempt. Fixed session completion shows cumulative rounds, words found and incorrect attempts; these totals are only recorded after a board is completed. A new round uses a new seed and the same eligible source. Exit practice is separate from puzzle controls and asks for confirmation before abandoning an unfinished session. The final summary distinguishes assisted reveals from independently found words. In Quick Practice, selecting Character Hunt replaces the core Matching/MCQ selection and vice versa, because the standalone engines are not yet mixed in one session.

Dictionary selection now supports one or more HSK bands, category-only sources, and any approved combination of HSK bands, categories and parts of speech. The setup route serializes these as the same validated dictionary-filter token used by Practice. The Character Hunt loader decodes that token and calls a parameterized database query with the shared OR-within-group/AND-across-group predicate. The query selects two- and three-character entries only, with a deterministic 1,024-row upper limit to bound browser memory. A saved Word Set is loaded by exact IDs instead and does not inherit dictionary filters. Legacy single-HSK game links remain readable. Extremely restrictive filters can legitimately yield too few playable words; this produces an explicit board-generation error instead of silently broadening the vocabulary. Mixed Character Hunt/Matching/MCQ plans are **not** supported yet; the existing scored mixed-session planner remains unchanged. The game has its own round progression and does not claim to publish scores to the central planned-session ledger.

## Verification

Unit tests cover grid sizes, default difficulty, reproducibility, word completion, three-character words, invalid combinations and insufficient vocabulary. A Chrome journey checks Quick Practice setup, choosing Easy, selecting an additional HSK band, preserving both filters in the URL, then solving five 2×2 boards using only visible tile controls and checking the cumulative Fixed 5 summary. Database SQL tests assert shared filtering semantics for multiple HSK bands, category and part-of-speech intersections, and category-only sources. The browser tests and Rust/WASM compilation require execution on a machine with Cargo and Chrome; Node source regression tests alone are not sufficient.

## R218 interaction and layout refinement

Gameplay has one bottom action bar: Hint/Reveal on the left and confirmed
Exit practice / Continue on the right. There is no Clear selection button:
re-tapping an already selected Hanzi deselects it, and invalid combinations
clear automatically. The practice round header shows the round and selected
difficulty without restating the grid dimensions.

The completed-word panel displays the exact dictionary-backed Hanzi, contextual
pinyin when available, English definitions and the shared Listen button for
audio playback. The completed-word list scrolls inside its panel on desktop,
without pushing the board or bottom actions offscreen. Progress is displayed
with a blue accessible determinate bar rather than native browser styling.
Both the game board and controls remain accessible by keyboard. Browser
viewport validation is pending.
title: Character Hunt - exercise contract (R215)

> **Current R489 state (2026-11-16):** All 100 Grammar-only regions contain draft lessons with 550 teaching entries. The historical R359/R366 registry below describes the first five courses only, not the complete curriculum. The separate teaching index (`GRAMMAR_TEACHING_INDEX.tsv`) now assigns stable IDs to all 550 entries. Official HSK 2025 grammar alignment is **not verified**; a reproducible external-source import and review process is documented in `HSK_GRAMMAR_ALIGNMENT.md`. The original five courses still have separately authored draft assessments; the other 95 have guided recognition only.

# Courses curriculum registry

R359 introduces a stable, local authoring registry for the four currently published grammar courses. It does **not** establish that the content is a verified mapping to the official HSK syllabus.

## Authoring registry

| Mosaic region | Stable course ID | Topic | Point IDs | Recommended prior course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `grammar-1` | Basic Sentence Structure | `g01-subject-predicate`, `g01-shi-identity`, `g01-bu-negation`, `g01-ma-question` | None |
| 2 | `grammar-2` | Time, Place & Everyday Actions | `g02-time-placement`, `g02-zai-location`, `g02-time-location`, `g02-qu-destination`, `g02-nali-question` | `grammar-1` |
| 3 | `grammar-3` | Possession, Existence & Quantities | `g03-you-possession`, `g03-meiyou-negation`, `g03-classifiers`, `g03-ji-count`, `g03-duoshao-quantity` | `grammar-1` |

| 4 | `grammar-4` | Descriptions & Comparisons | `g04-adjective-predicate`, `g04-hen-degree`, `g04-bu-adjective`, `g04-tai-le`, `g04-bi-comparison` | `grammar-1` |

The recommended prior-course relationship is teaching guidance, **not** an access restriction or assessed prerequisite. Existing authored lesson routes remain available directly.

The registry lives in `crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/learning/courses/curriculum_registry.rs` and enforces unique course regions, course IDs and grammar point IDs, matching authored lesson/check counts, and backward-only valid prerequisite references. Validation runs in Rust unit tests, not as a startup blocker. IDs are intended to remain stable once published and must not be treated as acquired grammar-point evidence.

## Syllabus provenance and limitations

All published registry entries currently use `PendingIndependentVerification`. Teaching stages are local editorial sequencing, not official HSK levels. No claim of 19 official HSK syllabus objectives, comprehensive HSK coverage, or independent assessment validity is made. Before publishing a verified syllabus mapping, obtain and independently review the authoritative grammar-standard edition and item identifiers, associate every item with authored content and an independent assessment, then add explicit verified references with validation tests. That is separate from implementing evidence-backed completion and irreversible mosaic reveals.

Future courses should receive new stable IDs only when their content exists, and should leave un-authored mosaic regions marked unavailable. The final grammar curriculum may exceed 100 regions to cover the approved syllabus.

## Independent grammar assessment draft (R360)

The first four published courses now expose `#/courses/grammar/assessment/grammar-1`, `grammar-2`, `grammar-3`, and `grammar-4`, with one separate three-choice item per registered grammar point (4 + 5 + 5 + 5). The items are authored in `assessment.rs` using stable point IDs and independent prompts, rather than reusing the guided lesson answer array. A distinct `AssessmentSession` records one answer per item, permits revisions *before* submission, disallows submission of incomplete attempts, locks answers afterwards and calculates a score only after full submission. The Yew page withholds rationales and correct answers until the review screen.

**No authoritative completion claim:** This remains an editorial and interaction draft. It does not implement HSK syllabus verification, qualified Mandarin-language assessment review, durable personal evidence, consent-backed recording, independently validated distractors, passing thresholds, retries/cooldowns, or artwork reveal. No score is stored or reported to the pedagogy engine. The mosaic stays concealed even if all draft items are correct. Assessment-time answer correctness is not the same as the acquisition engine's separate Hanzi 10×7 rule.

## R366 extension - Descriptions and Comparisons

Course 4 introduces adjective predicates, degree words 很, adjectival negation 不,
太…了, and comparisons with 比. It contains five explanatory teaching points,
five immediate-feedback guided questions, six authored word-bank activities,
five separately authored draft multiple-choice assessment items, and a separate
no-hints construction item. All item IDs use the new `g04-` registry namespace.
The ordinary lesson and draft assessment have different feedback rules.
All drafted answers need independent Mandarin linguistic review, particularly
nuances around 很, 太…了 and comparison interpretation. No achievements or mosaic
regions can be revealed based on these drafts.

# Mapping Zipeek Grammar to the 2025 HSK syllabus

## Evidence status

- Zipeek R488 has 100 draft Grammar courses and 550 teaching entries; this is not a certified inventory of independent grammatical rules.
- The 2025 HSK syllabus is a separate reference. A community transcription reports **593 items**, covering parts of speech, phrase structures, sentence patterns, pragmatic constructions and related categories. These items are not necessarily one independent rule each.
- **No HSK mappings have been verified in R490.** A matching Chinese example is only an editorial suggestion, never evidence of semantic equivalence.
- The third-party TSV was verified as publicly accessible through web search, but this runtime cannot download it into the source tree. The full HSK alignment has not been performed or fabricated.

## Sources and provenance

Official syllabus landing page: <https://www.chinesetest.cn/syllabus>.

Official PDF publisher: Center for Language Education and Cooperation, November 2025 (effective July 2026); grammar occupies pages 385-406. Reference download: <https://hsk.cn-bj.ufileos.com/3.0/%E6%96%B0%E7%89%88HSK%E8%80%83%E8%AF%95%E5%A4%A7%E7%BA%B21219.pdf>.

Community TSV transcription: <https://github.com/chelsea6502/hsk-2025-data/blob/master/grammar.tsv>. It contains `examLevelId`, `content`, `grammarType`, `categoryType`, `grammarDetail`, and `cases`; the repository advertises 593 source records. It is not itself an official certification. Keep its provenance and calculated SHA-256 with every imported mapping. Review malformed input rows rather than silently shifting field positions.

## Workflow

The former Python index/import/audit/report commands were removed in R493 at the user's request. The checked-in `GRAMMAR_TEACHING_INDEX.tsv` and the historical editorial mapping files remain for review. The full third-party HSK TSV still needs to be obtained and checked against the official PDF. Automated reimport, source-hash comparison, and mapping reports are **not currently available** until a Rust-native replacement is implemented. Do not assume the historical report can be refreshed or that a mapping has been verified.

`GRAMMAR_TEACHING_INDEX.tsv` was generated from the original 20 Rust courses and the 451-row editorial TSV for regions 21-100. Each entry receives an `gNNN-pNN` teaching ID, a region and a point ordinal, with `kind=unclassified` and `review_status=pending_linguistic_review` until an editor explicitly classifies it. The lesson runtime is not changed by this editorial index.

The HSK mapping queue has one row per source item. An exact shared Chinese example can suggest a teaching-entry ID. The status remains `unreviewed`; items with malformed source fields are marked `needs_source_review`. A reviewer must inspect the official syllabus and the lesson, decide whether a mapping is `candidate`, `verified`, or `unmapped`, and provide a rationale for `verified` and `unmapped` entries. Candidate and verified statuses require valid teaching IDs. Source metadata is checked on audit, and malformed source rows cannot advance beyond `needs_source_review` without correcting the reference. The former report command wrote a per-HSK-level count of unreviewed, candidate, verified, unmapped and source-review entries plus the number of unique verified teaching IDs. A summary of 593 items is not evidence of 593 verified mappings; the report sets `hsk_coverage_verified` only when all 593 are verified and no parse errors exist. Multiple HSK items may map to one teaching point; one HSK item may require multiple teaching points. A parent/variant relationship must be reviewed separately, not guessed from English labels.

## Acceptance gates

1. Confirm the source edition, legal use and all 593 source records (including levels 7-9). Resolve any malformed transcription rows against the official PDF.
2. Review each item's category, required competence, correct course placement and construction/variant relationships. No unreviewed item may count toward syllabus coverage.
3. Add explicit editorial review, natural Mandarin examples, tone-marked Pinyin and varied, independent point assessments; correct mistaken teaching entries without adding duplicate filler to reach an arbitrary total.
4. Only after independently scored evidence meets approved thresholds may a Grammar region be awarded mastery or reveal its artwork. Importing or mapping syllabus records never changes user progress.
5. Run locked Rust/WASM tests and Chrome journeys under both `/` and `/zipeek/` before accepting a release.

## Known limitation

The first Grammar region contains four points, while the intended curriculum structure is generally five to six points per course. This was preserved in R489 to avoid inventing an additional construction without expert review. Its four-point count should not be silently represented as full compliance with the updated authoring target.

## R490 verification status

The grammar reference is discoverable online, but downloading the 593-row TSV into the local project remains blocked by the environment network restriction. The tooling changes are tested with synthetic samples, not with a full 593-row import. The published level distribution for the 2025 transcription is HSK 1: 70, HSK 2: 78, HSK 3: 96, HSK 4: 95, HSK 5: 70, HSK 6: 50 and HSK 7-9: 134, totaling 593. Those figures are external-source metadata, not Zipeek verified teaching coverage.

# Learning evidence, proficiency, and history

**Status:** approved product requirements, refined 2026-11-09; **not yet implemented in the production learner database, Settings, or Stats route**. This is the normative future behavior, not a description of today's Practice scoring. See [personal-data architecture](../../../dictionary-data/schema/personal-data.md), [Practice setup](../../../learning-practice/practice/practice-session-builder.md), and [deterministic E2E plan](../../../testing-quality/e2e/learning-evidence-e2e.md).

## Purpose and authority

Collect **Practice records first**, then derive learning observations with traceable provenance. The personal DuckDB database is the planned durable authority, distinct from the read-only dictionary DuckDB and the temporary UUID Practice records in localStorage. Do not describe a probe database or a deleted temporary Practice record as saved pedagogical history. On completion, a durable session write must be acknowledged before clearing the last recoverable evidence and showing a saved confirmation. On write failure the learner must receive a truthful error and an explicit recovery path; silently losing results is unacceptable.

Record session ID, creation/start/end timestamps, configured vocabulary source, stable item IDs, exercise configuration, category and HSK membership where available, and a distinct attempt ID for each scored response. Derive per-Hanzi, per-word, per-grammar-point, and per-skill evidence from the scored attempts; preserve session and attempt references, item version, outcome, validity, and assessor. Distinguish a character within a word from a tested word identity; do not claim separate Hanzi recognition from an unrelated whole-sentence score without a defensible attribution rule. Duplicate delivery/replay of one attempt must be idempotent.

Raw microphone recordings and free-form learner text are more sensitive than score metadata. An assessed spoken result needs evidence of pronunciation/meaning correctness, **not merely permission to record or the presence of audio bytes**. Consent, audio retention, export, deletion, and local-only versus external AI processing remain to be specified before activation.

## Approved proficiency eligibility

All of the following apply to **the same stable Hanzi or word identity**:

1. **Seven distinct active local calendar days:** at least one qualifying, scored observation on each of seven different days. Seven encounters on one date, or a seven-day elapsed interval containing only two active dates, are insufficient. A missing day is not a failure. Dates must be evaluated consistently using a documented learner timezone policy; daylight-saving transitions must not change the day count arbitrarily.
2. **At least ten qualifying scored encounters**, distributed across **at least three different completed Practice sessions**. Repeated attempts in one session can contribute but **must be capped per item/session** so a learner cannot manufacture proficiency by endlessly repeating one item. The exact per-session cap and whether remediation retries count remain policy parameters to finalize, not numbers invented here. Record all attempts for diagnostics even when some do not contribute to eligibility.
3. **Successful evidence in four independently assessed competencies:** visual recognition, listening comprehension, assessed spoken production, and appropriate use in a sentence. Selecting Matching ten times can build recognition evidence, **not** certify speaking, listening, or sentence use. A competency with no qualifying successes remains unproven. The precise number and proportion of successful observations per skill are not yet approved. Ten encounters is an overall minimum, **not ten in each skill** unless a later decision changes the policy.
4. **Dynamic performance:** a later qualified failure can lower the affected skill rating or return the item to needs-review. A historical mastery award is not an immutable course-completion record. Repeated failures must not be masked by accumulated easy successes. The decay/recovery thresholds are still open.

The first three requirements are **necessary, not automatically sufficient**. Until per-skill acceptance criteria and validators are implemented, Stats may display the observed counts and pending competencies, but must **not** label the learner proficient simply on day seven or encounter ten.

### Classifying evidence by what an exercise actually tests

| Experience | Permissible evidence when scored and validated | Not automatically evidenced |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Matching / glyph-choice / image-to-Hanzi | Recognition of the tested identity | Listening, speech, productive sentence use |
| Listening comprehension (audio to meaning/selection) | Listening, where audio playback and answer are genuinely assessed | Speaking from merely hearing audio |
| Recorded spoken response | Speaking **only after a reliable assessor checks it** | Pronunciation competence from recording existence alone |
| Sentence creation, transformation, or context use | Sentence use if meaning and grammar are assessed and the target identity is attributable | All component words mastered, or free production from a fully revealed answer |
| Grammar-course guided examples and hints | Instructional activity; possibly separate assisted evidence | Unassisted mastery or passed grammar assessment |

Track `assistance_level` and `assessment_kind` so a word-bank Sentence Builder displaying the correct solution and playable audio remains a useful **teaching experience** without improperly awarding unassisted production credit. Learning activities and scored assessments are distinct events.

## Word Set eligibility in Practice setup

**New requirement, not currently enforced across the shipped setup:** a saved Word Set is selectable as a Practice vocabulary source only if it contains **at least ten distinct valid Hanzi-bearing vocabulary entries**. The intended user example is ten words, not ten total Unicode Hanzi code points. Deduplicate by stable vocabulary identity; ten duplicates or invalid/stale entries do not pass. If fewer than ten are playable for the chosen exercise, the option is **disabled/greyed out** with an accessible explanation and count (for example, `7 of 10 words available; add 3`). The same eligibility rule must be revalidated when launching, including after a set is edited or dictionary entries become unavailable; disabling only the visual button is insufficient.

This is a Practice **source eligibility requirement**, not a minimum size for creating or storing Word Sets, and not a claim that all ten words must appear in every question. A source with ten distinct entries allows the learner to practise; it does **not** guarantee ten qualifying observations for any one word. Other vocabulary sources and exercise-specific minimums remain separate unless explicitly revised.

## Future /stats experience

The proposed `/stats` route reports per-word/Hanzi evidence transparently: qualifying encounters, distinct sessions, distinct active days, per-skill measured/needs-evidence/needs-review status, category and HSK association, and relevant grammar points. Expose why an item is not proficient; do not show only an unexplained percentage. A character's observed skill state and a word's observed skill state must remain distinguishable. Current R282 does not implement this route or its durable backing ledger.

## Grammar learning and irreversible completion

The future [Courses mosaic](../../../learning-practice/courses/courses-mosaic.md) is built against the **HSK grammar syllabus**, with an explicit mapping from each authoritative grammar point to taught course, questions, assessments and stable IDs. Do not assert complete official coverage before item-by-item verification. Courses use authored explanations, worked examples, guided exercises (image-to-Hanzi, Hanzi writing, Character Builder, Sentence Builder and word-bank Sentence Transformation), and individually scored grammar-point assessments.

Instruction may intentionally reveal an answer, e.g. a Sentence Builder's correct-sentence label with playable audio below the builder. Such scaffolding is **not equivalent to a correct independent assessment**. Per-point assessment requires at least five scored questions and 80% in one attempt by default, as specified in the Courses contract. Passing every required point makes **course completion permanent** and reveals that course's large mosaic region. Vocabulary proficiency remains dynamic and separately determines small vocabulary-region opacity; grammar-point completion never implicitly marks associated words known.

## Storage/privacy gates

Use the personal DuckDB for authoritative session and derived evidence records once durability is verified; implement a clear Settings recording/retention control before collection. A final decision on opt-in default, raw audio/text retention, local/export/erase behavior, and handling of model-provider transfer is still required. The existing temporary Practice record must not be silently treated as a history database. Plan versioned schema and migrations, dictionary-identity continuity, idempotent commits, cross-tab coordination, quota/corruption recovery, export/import and user deletion.

## Verification, including time travel

Use an injected clock interface for both domain computation and timestamp generation. Production uses real time; tests use a deterministic fake clock with **explicit date/time and timezone**, advanced between sessions. Never change the operating-system clock, monkey-patch browser `Date` globally, or trust mutable DOM timestamps for proficiency. The Rust domain clock and browser persistence boundary must receive the **same simulated time**. Record timestamps immutably when attempts are scored; altering the test clock cannot rewrite history. See [E2E scenarios](../../../testing-quality/e2e/learning-evidence-e2e.md).

Tests must cover seven distinct dates, ten capped scored encounters over at least three sessions, all four skill categories, session replay, duplicates, failure-driven regression, disabled recording, successful durable saves, failed writes, cross-session reload, and Stats reading the same persisted facts. Test both the boundary just before eligibility and the first genuinely eligible state. When per-skill success thresholds remain undecided, test *eligibility evidence* and a clearly pending overall status, not a fabricated proficiency pass.

## Open decisions (only these remain policy-dependent)

- The maximum qualifying encounters for one identity in one session; counting of immediate retries and partial answers.
- Per-skill success sample sizes/thresholds, remediation, and reliable listening, speaking and sentence-use assessment rules. Selecting only Matching must never satisfy all four modalities.
- Learner timezone policy when travelling, recording opt-in default, and retention/export/deletion of raw responses and microphone audio.
- Stable vocabulary/character identity across dictionary updates and the distinction between a word's compositional evidence and its constituent characters.

Do not convert these unresolved details into undocumented hard-coded defaults.

## R333 clarification: Hanzi recognition award versus vocabulary proficiency

The separate [Hanzi recognition acquisition contract](../../../dictionary-data/schema/pedagogy.md) is approved for future Dragon Progression: ten valid correct recognitions in at least three completed sessions per qualifying day, at most four credits per session, over seven consecutive dates separated by at least 24 elapsed hours; a per-day 0/1/2 mistake allowance defaults to zero. A failed day resets that acquisition streak, and a successful day locks when it qualifies. Earlier specification passages above describe the pre-existing R259 vocabulary and full multi-skill proficiency design; they must not be used as the Hanzi Dragon awarding algorithm. Recognition acquisition is a distinct historical milestone, not proof of listening, speech, writing or sentence-use proficiency. The R333 engine is in-memory only and is not integrated into production event capture or `/stats`.

## Approved 2026-11-17 grammar observation window

For grammar visualization, the selected target rule is seven qualifying local days within a rolling fourteen-day window, per canonical grammar-pattern ID. On each qualifying day, ten independent correct and verified attempts must use that pattern in Translate Sentence, Sentence Builder or Sentence Transformation. Merely generating an AI sentence, revealing a solution or matching a transcript without a validated assessment is insufficient. This is not implemented or verified and does not revise the D52 Hanzi recognition streak or the existing per-point course assessment contract without separate reconciliation.
title: Learning evidence, proficiency, and history

# Settings workspace: implemented behavior

The Settings route is [`#/settings`](../../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/route.rs). The active panel is managed by [`pages/system/settings/mod.rs`](../../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/system/settings/mod.rs) and its seven-tab [`navigation.rs`](../../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/system/settings/navigation.rs). This is the current layout, not the earlier five-section R134 proposal.

| Tab | Current ownership |
| --- | --- |
| Appearance | Preset, light/dark and layout density via the shared preferences/theme state |
| Chinese Characters | Hanzi font preference and Character Builder sizes (Standard, Large, Extra large) |
| AI Translation | OpenAI-compatible endpoint, model ID, memory-only optional API key |
| Image Generation | Local image server configuration and test controls |
| Practice | Practice/matching audio preference |
| Personal Data | JSON export/import/preview, category deletion and experimental OPFS/probe operations |
| Pedagogy | Explicit read-only Rust/WASM worker availability check, no consent/recording activation |

## Preferences and credentials

[`preferences.rs`](../../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/preferences.rs) stores a JSON document at `zipeek.preferences.v1` with ten fields: `preset`, `density`, `dark`, `font`, `character_size`, `matching_autoplay`, `image_server_url`, `ai_url`, `ai_model`, `learning_history_enabled`. The source supplies defaults for omitted fields. The saved model and endpoint are shared with both the public translator and Practice generated translation; neither question should expose another editable model/URL form. [`services/ai/config.js`](../../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/services/ai/config.js) keeps an optional API key only in JS module memory, not in the JSON preferences. It may be lost on reload.

Selecting a palette does not itself change dark/light mode. Font preference does not install a missing host font. Character Builder tiles share the selected font and size; pinyin labels are separate.

## Practice learning-history recording (R283 checkpoint, unverified)

The Personal Data tab now exposes an explicit opt-in for saving completed Practice outcomes to a dedicated OPFS-backed personal DuckDB file (`zipeek-personal-learning-v1.duckdb`). The preference is off by default and stored as `learning_history_enabled` in the existing `zipeek.preferences.v1` JSON document. The former standalone consent key is no longer read or migrated; existing users who opted in using only that key must opt in again. The record includes session/step IDs, exercise IDs and outcomes only, not typed answers, AI-generated sentences, microphone audio or handwriting strokes. Completed temporary sessions are retained until a successful checkpoint, close and readback verification, with a retry control on failure. With recording off, the existing temporary cleanup remains the default.

The tab also offers a separately confirmed erase-history action. The existing portable JSON backup does **not** export or restore the personal DuckDB history. The database writer, Settings control, deletion flow and associated Rust code have not yet been browser/WASM tested; do not represent the checkpoint as a verified storage service. Authoritative progress aggregation remains unimplemented; the `/stats` page is currently a non-authoritative empty-state dashboard.

## R345 worker availability diagnostics

The Pedagogy tab offers an explicit, one-shot health probe through the read-only R339 monitor. The JavaScript bridge resolves `pedagogy-worker/` from `document.baseURI`, preserving `/` and `/zipeek/` deployment paths. The monitor starts an isolated worker for the probe and terminates it in `finally`. A missing generated worker WASM bundle is displayed as an error rather than a healthy or running engine. This diagnostic cannot enable tracking, read DuckDB history, enqueue analysis, or write mastery records. A successful probe confirms worker availability only. Live browser verification is pending.

## Test evidence and limitations

Rust browser suites for Settings, font persistence, Debug and panel navigation exist under [`crates/zipeek-e2e/tests/`](../../../../crates/zipeek-e2e/tests). Tests authored in source are not the same as test runs: current Windows confirmation is listed in [CURRENT](../../../project-management/current.md). Browser/screen-reader keyboard behavior and OPFS durability require their own acceptance evidence.

## Future storage work

Add verified portable history export/import, retention policy, schema migrations, user-data deletion integration, concurrency and quota recovery coverage before the personal database is considered fully production-ready. See [learning evidence](../../../learning-practice/practice/learning-evidence.md).
title: Settings workspace: implemented behavior

# Translate & Analyse - R136

## Approved product boundary

The standalone `#/translate-sentence` page uses the endpoint, model and optional browser-memory key configured **only** under Settings → AI Translation. There is no model selector or credential entry on the page. The user chooses Chinese→English or English→Simplified Chinese, types a sentence, then requests **Translate & Analyse**. A two-column editor/result layout is followed by four sections: estimated difficulty, language structures, vocabulary observations and learning notes. Clear, Swap and Copy are available. The global route title remains in the centered app header.

## Typed response contract

`zipeek-ai/src/sentence_analysis.rs` owns the typed response, the prompt, size limits and structural validation. The model must return JSON with `translation`, `difficulty`, `estimated_hsk`, `rationale`, `vocabulary`, `grammar` and `notes`. Allowed difficulty values: beginner, elementary, intermediate and advanced. HSK estimate may be null or 1-9. Vocabulary Hanzi and grammar example excerpts must occur literally in the original Chinese sentence (Chinese→English) or the translated Chinese sentence (English→Chinese). Unrelated lexical or grammatical evidence is rejected. Arrays and text fields have size limits; unknown fields are rejected. Prompts instruct the model to treat the source sentence as data rather than as instructions.

**Classification is AI-estimated, not dictionary verified**. R136 does **not** assert official HSK levels or word-frequency values for individual tokens. Dictionary-backed lexical lookups, validated tokenization, grammar taxonomy, calibrated difficulty, alternate translations and persisted history are future work. Avoid presenting AI output as a certified educational assessment.

## Requests and failure modes

`crates/zipeek-web/src/services/ai/mod.rs` uses the existing OpenAI-compatible transport. A first call asks for translation plus structured analysis. If it returns text but cannot be validated as structured data, the client makes **a second request** for translation-only. The page shows that translation and a brief notice that language analysis was unavailable. Both requests may use model tokens or incur provider charges. If the transport itself fails, the existing HTTP/timeout/CORS errors are shown. Changing the source sentence, direction, swapping or clearing increments a generation ID to ignore outdated responses.

No local translation history, database migration, model discovery or new server is introduced. Existing AI key handling is unchanged: it is held in browser-page memory only; endpoint/model preferences are stored in localStorage.

## Acceptance and limitations

- Focused Node checks verify page contracts and existing AI settings/transport behaviour.
- Pure Rust unit tests cover typical JSON, unrelated Chinese vocabulary, unsupported grammar evidence, out-of-range HSK, English→Chinese and unexpected fields.
- Windows `cargo fmt --all --check`, native Rust unit tests, WASM `cargo check` and actual browser/provider verification remain **pending**, because Cargo is unavailable in the packaging environment.
- Verify status, error, Copy, Clear, Swap, no model selection and keyboard navigation on desktop/mobile. Try a JSON-capable LM Studio model and a model that returns malformed output to verify fallback and usage.
- Results should be considered model suggestions. A later milestone must join segmented vocabulary to the local dictionary for authoritative HSK/frequency annotations.

## R137 - Workspace interactions and accessibility

The translation editor and result use stacked cards on small and medium displays, with side-by-side cards from the large breakpoint. Cards and translation output have `min-width: 0`/word wrapping to prevent long provider text from overflowing the viewport. The source field exposes a keyboard hint: **Ctrl+Enter**, or **Command+Enter** on macOS, submits using the same guarded request callback as the primary button; normal Enter remains available for line breaks, and IME composition does not trigger translation.

Copy now reports clipboard success, unavailable clipboard or denied permission in a polite status region. The feedback is guarded by the same generation token as result requests, so a delayed clipboard response cannot claim success for a subsequently edited result. Editing the source, changing direction, swapping and clearing invalidate in-flight translation results and clear obsolete errors and clipboard feedback. Output declares busy state, the request button has a loading indicator, and provider errors remain role=alert.

The compact AI indicator says whether a model is selected; **it does not claim that the endpoint is reachable**. Connection tests and all model/credential settings remain exclusively in Settings. Translation and analysis are still sent directly to the configured provider and may incur charges, including an extra fallback call. Automated Node tests inspect these contracts. **Real keyboard, clipboard, responsive layout, screen-reader, Cargo/WASM and provider tests are still required on Windows.**

## Interpretation of sentence evidence

`crates/zipeek-ai/src/sentence_insights.rs` owns the pure `GrammarFamily`, `GrammarEvidence` and `LexicalCoverage` interpretation types. Grammar families are heuristic labels for AI-proposed example fragments anchored in the observed Chinese sentence, not independent syntactic verification. Dictionary evidence summarizes which model-suggested words had exact or ambiguous matches and HSK membership. It is **not** complete sentence segmentation, certification of HSK difficulty, or proof that unmatched words are absent. If enrichment fails, do not imply all vocabulary was verified.
title: Translate & Analyse - R136

# Sentence translation: utility and Practice exercise

Zipeek has **two different translation experiences**. They share Settings-owned AI endpoint and model configuration but do not share scoring semantics.

## Translate a supplied sentence

`#/translate-sentence` accepts text authored by the learner and provides a model-generated translation, including optional analysis where supported. It is a utility, not a scored Practice question. Source input limits, direction controls and cancellation/error handling are owned by the translator page and AI client. Do not count its requests as Practice results.

## Sentence Translation in Practice

Under Practice -> Advanced, select **Sentence Translation** as the only exercise, select a vocabulary source, translation direction (Chinese to English, English to Chinese, or Mixed) and five, ten or Endless questions. The launch creates a UUID-backed record at `#/practice/session/<id>`; it does not require AI model or endpoint fields inside the exercise.

Generated questions use a seeded sample of at most ten distinct eligible source words. The generation prompt requests only a Chinese sentence and an English translation. Zipeek validates the response, constructs the ordered answer and shuffled word bank, persists the generated instance, and exposes stable canonical tile-order attributes for tests. Repeated words are assigned occurrence-aware positions. These attributes are an E2E interaction seam, not proof the sentence is linguistically valid.

The learner assembles the translation, submits it for AI evaluation and sees feedback before advancing. Fixed runs stop at five or ten questions; Endless continues until explicitly finished. Reload and navigation can restore saved unfinished questions. Completion removes the temporary record and explains that results are not durably retained.

## AI and privacy

Settings -> AI stores the endpoint (`ai_url`) and model (`ai_model`) in the consolidated preferences document (`zipeek.preferences.v1`). The optional API key is held in tab memory, not persisted. Requests go from the learner's browser to the chosen provider and require compatible CORS and transport security. Do not place an administrator API secret in a public browser deployment.

The R283 checkpoint introduces an unverified opt-in Practice-outcome writer and recording preference; browser acceptance and portable export are pending. The personal OPFS/DuckDB facilities are not an exercise-outcome store. See [personal data](../../../dictionary-data/personal/personal-data-storage.md) and [technical boundary](../../../architecture/modules/sentence-exercises.md).

## Implementation and tests

- Translation utility: `crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/translation/sentence_translator/`.
- Standalone generated exercise: `crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/translation/sentence_practice/` (still independently routable).
- Persisted Practice: `crates/zipeek-web/src/services/practice_launch.rs`, `practice_generated.rs`, `practice_session_store.rs`, and `pages/practice/local_session.rs`.
- AI config and request client: `crates/zipeek-web/src/services/ai/`, `crates/zipeek-ai/` and `crates/zipeek-ai-client/`.
- Deterministic and optional live Chrome tests: `crates/zipeek-e2e/tests/translation_fixture.rs` and `ai_learner.rs`.

See [current validation](../../../project-management/current.md) before claiming the latest Practice integration is browser-verified.
title: Sentence translation: utility and Practice exercise

# Word Discovery: AI examples and app notifications (R138)

The Random Word and Word of the Day cards share `WordSpotlight`. Copying Hanzi uses browser Clipboard, with visible success and error toasts provided by `ToastProvider` at app root. The toast automatically dismisses after 3.8 seconds, can be dismissed manually, and exposes accessible `status`/`alert` roles. This is an ephemeral notification; it is not persisted or exported.

**Example sentence** calls the configured OpenAI-compatible model only after the user presses the button. The request includes the displayed Hanzi, pinyin and dictionary display meaning, asks for one Chinese sentence and one English translation, and checks that the output contains the exact chosen Hanzi. It enforces a 1,200-character response cap. Successful output is explicitly **AI-generated and unverified**-not CC-CEDICT data or an authoritative pedagogical example. A missing model, endpoint failure, malformed response or absent target shows an error. Toggling the panel does not reissue the same request; choosing another random word clears the old example and invalidates an in-flight result. This functionality may incur provider fees.

The new Settings AI connection diagnostics show an inspectable bounded transcript of the test, including the exact fixed system/user prompts and returned text, without storing or rendering authentication credentials. A successful endpoint test is not a quality guarantee. The diagnostics are not exported with learning data.

The standalone About page retains licence and attribution information; Settings no longer duplicates that page. A legacy Themes deep link redirects to Settings. Debug is only rendered when `cfg!(debug_assertions)` is true and contains only non-secret runtime metadata. Release-build users see NotFound for the Debug route.

The next milestone still needs real Rust/Yew compilation and browser/LM Studio acceptance. The `scripts/` directory and root images are R200-deferred.

## Ordered meanings and metadata

Word Discovery and the daily spotlight now display one ordered dictionary sense at a time. The left and right controls are bounded and the selection resets on word changes. Topics and explicit qualifiers belong to each sense, not the entire word; the HSK and part-of-speech metadata remain at word level. AI examples use the currently selected sense and invalidate stale examples when that sense changes.

Generated databases must be rebuilt with the updated `sense_qualifiers` table. The importer preserves the source gloss in `word_senses`, removes only recognized leading annotations from `sense_display`, and stores explicit region, usage, and register labels with source provenance. The first supported tags are Taiwan, Loanword, Figurative, and Colloquial. Unknown annotations remain verbatim; the application does not infer regional or usage tags from arbitrary text. No database migration is supplied.

## Ordered meanings and source labels (R329)

Word Discovery and expanded Browse results use ordered `sense_display` records rather than reconstructing meanings from a combined English string. `sense_categories` provides the categories for an individual sense and `sense_qualifiers` stores strictly parsed leading source annotations. Only recognized markers are converted into structured labels; unrecognized tags remain visible as source gloss text. Example generation uses the currently selected sense and its response is invalidated when the sense changes. The generator requires a full database rebuild; there is no migration.
title: Word Discovery: AI examples and app notifications (R138)

# Landing Page (R127)

## Purpose and scope

Only new visitors to the root Home route receive a short first-visit landing experience. The current application Home, Word of the Day, navigation drawer and all functional routes are unchanged after entry. This is not a mandatory account sign-in or a wizard.

## Entry and persistence

- On root `#/`, show the landing if `zipeek.preferences.v1` is absent and the browser has no existing personal Word Sets, Pinyin course progress, or excluded-vocabulary record.
- Clicking **Enter Zipeek** initializes `zipeek.preferences.v1` with default settings only if it does not already exist. No independent welcome marker is stored.
- Existing users with preferences or learning records bypass the landing.
- Direct links such as `#/browse`, `#/write-hanzi`, and `#/games/cloud-match` bypass the welcome screen.
- App startup does not write default appearance preferences merely to render the initial theme; user actions persist preferences explicitly.
- localStorage is a required application environment dependency. If browser policy denies access, startup reports an explicit initialization failure instead of silently treating the visitor as new.

## UI contract

- Full-height introductory hero with a concise proposition, a single prominent Enter action using the Yew Lucide play icon, and a theme-aware, static product preview. The preview includes a 16:9 media slot and feature labels for Practice, Browse, and Word Sets; it must not imply that a video is playable until a trailer exists.
- No drawer, application header, promotional tagline badge or footer on the first-visit landing. Normal shell appears immediately after entry.
- Keyboard-operable button and reduced-motion behavior. The layout stacks on narrow displays.
- Do not initialize the dictionary for the landing itself. The preview is static and does not require data or network requests. A future trailer may replace its media slot without changing the first-visit entry contract.

## Verification

Source contract tests are not equivalent to a compiled/browser pass. Run Windows Rust/WASM checks, then verify first root visit, entry and reload, existing-user bypass, direct deep links, theme colors, touch/keyboard navigation and the explicit startup failure when localStorage is blocked. Do not reset actual learning data to test onboarding; use a clean browser profile or an isolated origin.
title: Landing Page (R127)
