# Ux Browse

## Browse

### Search and filters (UX-BROWSE01)

Browse uses the **R79 compact-list amendment to D45**: a prominent
search bar and compact filter controls above five-row dictionary lists, with a
separate personal Word Set management panel. On wide screens, results and Word
Set management sit side by side; on narrow screens, the management panel stacks
below or opens from a clearly labelled disclosure. This replaces the previously
required smart-combobox and desktop-table presentation, **not** the A37 URL,
query, token, or pagination semantics documented below.

The R79 implemented behaviour and the approved exercise-first setup are described in
[Dictionary Browse](../../../dictionary-data/dictionary-browse.md) and
[Practice setup history](../../completed/PRACTICE_SETUP_HISTORY.md). Older URL/chip and numbered-page
requirements in this section are still future work, not implemented features.

The main search input accepts free text. Filter controls can expose dropdowns
or an add-filter affordance; choosing a supported filter creates a removable,
visible chip. Typed text is a text query unless the user explicitly chooses to
create a filter. Recognized tokens may be suggested to accelerate entry, but
an autocomplete combobox is no longer a mandatory interaction. Each chip shows
its canonical filter token and a keyboard-operable remove action. Removing a
chip commits the changed filter set and immediately refreshes results.

Word Set management is visually distinct from search results and exposes saved
set creation, rename, deletion, and backup actions. Selecting a predefined or
saved Word Set for browsing is a filter, not permission to broaden a failed or
invalid saved-set query into unrestricted results. The right-hand panel may
include quick selection and bulk-add actions when their behaviour and
accessibility are implemented and tested.

| Token | Filter |
| --- | --- |
| Any of the 42 canonical PoS tokens, e.g. `noun`, `verb` | Complete-token PoS match |
| `hsk2`, `hsk3` | HSK system membership |
| `hsk2:1` … `hsk2:6` | HSK 2.0 level |
| `hsk3:1` … `hsk3:7`, `hsk3:7-9` | HSK 3.0 level; 7 and 7-9 mean the advanced band |
| `hsk2:1-4`, `hsk3:2-7` | Inclusive level range within the chosen system |
| `freq:100`, `freq:100-500` | Exact frequency rank or inclusive range; no artificial cap |
| `id:42` | One WordId per chip; comma-separated IDs do not parse |
| `simp:吃`, `trad:吃` | Exact simplified/traditional hanzi |
| `pinyin:chi` | Exact pinyin match |

Filter chips always use exact matching independently of the global strategy.
Combine multiple chips with AND. Each chip displays its token and a visible,
keyboard-operable ×; removal reruns the query immediately.

HSK range bounds are clamped to 1-6 or 1-7 for their respective systems.
Invalid single levels such as `hsk2:0` and `hsk3:8` create no chip and show a
small inline valid-range message. Reversed ranges, missing endpoints,
non-integers and negative values create no chip and show an inline error. Do not
swap reversed bounds. Keep numeric HSK range clamping; frequency ranks must be
positive integers, without an artificial product cap.

The settings icon opens a modal with global free-text match strategy radio
buttons: Exact, Prefix, Substring (default). Selection closes the modal and
updates the URL immediately; there is no Save button or per-field override.

Free text returns the union of matches across:

- Pinyin: global strategy against a tone-stripped, whitespace-free, case-folded
  comparison value. Support source display and numbered forms without rewriting
  stored pinyin; this search key is distinct from D18's tone-preserving replay key.
- English: case-insensitive substring, regardless of global strategy.
- Simplified hanzi: prefix, including exact full-sequence matches, regardless
  of global strategy.

Order by pinyin ascending, with simplified-hanzi bytes as the tie-break.
Page sizes are 5, 10, 15, 20, default 5. Show numbered page links with previous/
next arrows and ellipses for gaps, e.g. `← 1 2 [3] 4 5 … 100 →`.

### Browse URL state

All Browse state belongs in the URL. The approved A37 contract is:

| Parameter | Meaning / default |
| --- | --- |
| `q` | Free text; empty when omitted |
| `strategy` | `exact`, `prefix`, `substring`; default `substring` |
| `f` | Ordered comma-separated encoded filter tokens; empty when omitted |
| `page` | One-based page number; default `1` |
| `page_size` | `5`, `10`, `15`, `20`; default `5` |

Canonical filter tokens are `pos:<canonical-pos>`, `hsk2`, `hsk3`,
`hsk2:<level-or-range>`, `hsk3:<level-or-range>`, `freq:<rank-or-range>`,
`id:<id>`, `simp:<hanzi>`, `trad:<hanzi>` and `pinyin:<text>`. A bare PoS token selected through an optional suggestion or filter control
emits `pos:<token>` on the wire. HSK 3.0 advanced `7-9` single-tier
alias canonicalizes to `7`; ordinary inclusive ranges use their normalized bounds.

Encode each complete filter token individually, join tokens with literal commas
in insertion order, then serialize that entire `f` value once in the outer URL
query. Decode the outer query once, split its `f` value at literal commas, then
decode each token once. This intentional two-layer codec keeps commas/percent
signs inside token values distinct from filter separators; it is specific to
Browse and changes no practice URL encoding rule. Example semantic filters:
`pos:verb`, `hsk3:2`, `freq:100-500`.

Query, chip/filter and page-size changes reset page to 1. A requested page beyond
the available result pages uses the last available page; zero results use the
initial page 1 with the approved empty view. Malformed loaded values use safe
defaults/validated filters and never trigger an implicit URL rewrite. Explicit
new state generation uses the canonical grammar. Full codec tests must cover
Unicode, commas, percent signs, malformed escapes and reload roundtrips.
Debounce live search by 300 ms. Enter forces an immediate query and commits the
URL. Typing alone does not update it. Chip changes, strategy changes and page
navigation query and update immediately. All Browse state updates use
`replaceState`, never `pushState`; Back returns to the page before Browse.

Tab focuses the input, filter controls and chips in document order. Enter in
the search input commits free text immediately. If optional suggestions are
shown, Up/Down moves among them and Escape closes them. Chip removal supports
Enter/Space and has an accessible name.

### Browse fields (UX-BROWSE01, resolved A37 and amended by D45)

Use the same five fields on vocabulary cards, in this order:
simplified hanzi, pinyin, English, HSK and PoS. English uses the first stored
gloss. HSK shows every available system and its level/band; do not collapse
HSK 2.0 and 3.0 into one inferred level. Missing metadata is not invented.
Do not add traditional-hanzi or frequency columns. Their exact filter tokens
remain supported independently of the displayed field set.

### Browse states (UX-BROWSE02)

With no query/chips, show all words on page 1 and "Type to search or add a filter".
Zero results shows "No words matched" and Clear search, which clears query,
chips and page number and returns to the initial view.

Show no spinner for normal queries; after a query takes more than 200 ms,
show a subtle results-area spinner. This is a performance guard, not a measured
latency promise. Query failure shows "Couldn't load results" and Retry inline;
retry reruns the last query without changing the URL.
title: Ux Browse

# AI dictionary classification - operational guide

## Safety

`cargo make db-full` is a potentially long, cache-writing classification and bundle-publication operation. It is **not** a smoke test. Publication is gated on zero pending classifications; a failed run must leave the installed database unchanged. The workflow checkpoints successful classifications, but confirm this against local output.

## Why the 2026-11-05 run stalled

The single-sense smoke succeeded, but the subsequent 20-sense requests repeatedly failed strict JSON decoding (`expected value at line 1 column 1`). The batch scheduler split failures into smaller batches, then individual requests; several individual responses also failed. This is a **response-format / response-extraction compatibility problem**, not evidence of bad source data. The exact response prefix was not present in the supplied logs, so we cannot yet conclude whether it is Markdown, a `<think>` block, empty final text, or some other prefix.

## Changes in R173

- Live smoke tests **one single sense and one two-sense batch**, without cache/database writes. A model that only handles singles now fails before the full job.
- Known response envelopes (`<think>…</think>` and Markdown JSON fences) can be stripped before strict parsing. Validation of allowed labels, IDs, completeness and field names remains strict.
- Rejected batch/single responses log an escaped, bounded 120-character prefix for diagnosis. Do not log or share private inputs; classification source data is dictionary content.

## Run order (PowerShell)

```powershell
cargo test -p db-gen --locked
cargo make db-ai-smoke
```

If smoke fails, stop. Check the `response_prefix` field and LM Studio logs; adjust output formatting or token limits based on actual evidence, not repeated prompt guesswork. For bounded classification after smoke, use `cargo run -p db-gen --locked -- classify --help` to obtain the actual argument names. Start with `--limit 20 --batch-size 2` and the same model, cache and endpoint. Back up the cache before changing model/prompt versions. Do not run `cargo make db-full` until the bounded job produces valid, reproducible results at useful throughput.

## Verification

A successful local 2-sense smoke is **necessary, not sufficient** for 20-sense batches. Evaluate 5-, 10- and 20-sense batches progressively using bounded classify runs before raising the default from 2. The 2026-11-05 full-run output provides no proof that larger batches can be decoded correctly.

## R174: expanded semantic taxonomy and rejected response evidence

The v6 prompt has a controlled taxonomy with more than 50 defined subjects, shared between the prompt and the database schema. The taxonomy version is 2, so old classification caches cannot be reused. This is intentional: rebuild from pinned dictionary sources.

Malformed model completions are now saved in full, by default, to `target/db-workflow/classification-rejections.jsonl` (one JSON object per line, including model, sense IDs, rejection reason, raw response and timestamp). This diagnostic file is not the classification cache and is not included in the generated dictionary. Override the path with `ZIPEEK_CLASSIFICATION_REJECTION_LOG`; set it to `off` to disable logging. Treat raw outputs as untrusted data and review them locally before sharing.

For example, PowerShell: `Get-Content .\target\db-workflow\classification-rejections.jsonl -Tail 1 | ConvertFrom-Json | Select-Object -ExpandProperty response`.

**Current model issue:** responses beginning with `Assistant` or `system` are reasoning-like prose, not strict JSON. More detailed prompts alone cannot force this model to obey structured output. Smoke must pass first. If it continues to fail, use an LM Studio model or inference setting that supports JSON schema/constrained generation, or implement a provider-specific structured-output mode with tests before running all senses. Do not extract plausible classification labels from unstructured reasoning.

## R175: use Aimux's structured output contract

The R174 smoke logs prove that the Qwen model sometimes returned role-labelled reasoning in the **final text** (`system\n...` or `Assistant\n...`). These strings are not dictionary classifications. They must never be salvaged as labels from prose.

R175 sends `GenerateTextOptions.output = Some(Output::Object { schema, ... })` specifically for classifier requests. The schema is constructed directly from the shared `POS` and `CATEGORIES` allowlists, with exact top-level keys, nonempty PoS, unique labels, and required ID fields in batches. The existing domain validator still checks sense identity, duplicate IDs, taxonomy, and other invariants after Aimux's parsed `output()`. Classifier requests use temperature 0 and a bounded final-output token budget. The generic LLM client retains its prior behavior for other features.

Structured classification remains **streamed** because Aimux's `StreamTextResult::consume` preserves a `GenerateTextResult` when the output parser rejects the model text, so full rejected text and metadata can be saved. Non-streamed `generate_text` can return a parse error without exposing that result. A provider that does not support JSON-schema output may reject the call outright; do not silently switch to an unrestricted request.

When a model response is rejected, `classification-rejections.jsonl` includes the raw final text and a `diagnostics` field with the final step's reported reasoning, unified/raw finish reasons, usage, and provider warnings. This helps distinguish reasoning-only text, truncation, and unsupported provider options. The diagnostics file is local and must never be published as part of a generated bundle. Avoid sharing prompts or API credentials from local logs.

Run `cargo test -p db-gen --locked`, then `cargo make db-ai-smoke`. Confirm that single-sense and two-sense responses both pass. If it fails, inspect the entire last diagnostic entry:

```powershell
Get-Content .\target\db-workflow\classification-rejections.jsonl -Tail 1 |
  ConvertFrom-Json | Format-List *
```

Do not start `db-full` based on passing Node source tests. The structured-output request's actual behavior against the installed Aimux provider and LM Studio model remains a live acceptance test.

## R177: 100-sense smoke and observed JSON suffix

The 2026-11-05 `db-full` log contains a nearly valid two-sense JSON response ending in `..`, which Aimux rejects as trailing characters. It also contains individual responses beginning `system` followed by reasoning prose; those remain invalid and must not be mined for labels. R177 narrowly normalizes **one or two trailing periods after an otherwise complete JSON object** when Aimux parsing fails, then applies the existing domain validator for IDs, PoS and categories. Prose is rejected as before.

`cargo make db-ai-smoke` now runs a single sense plus one **100-sense** request, chosen evenly from the real imported dictionary; it may be much slower than the earlier two-sense smoke. No classification cache/database/published bundle is changed. The batch output allowance scales to 16,384 tokens for 100 senses. If the model does not handle that size, inspect `target/db-workflow/classification-rejections.jsonl` and retry at an intermediate size via `cargo run -p db-gen --locked -- ai-smoke --model <MODEL> --batch-size 20`. The `db-full` workflow deliberately retains a small preflight matching its production batch setting; a failure of the optional 100-sense stress test does not imply that 2-sense classification must fail. Do not increase `ZIPEEK_AI_BATCH_SIZE` to 100 until its live response has passed strict validation and throughput is acceptable.

## R178: deterministic CC-CEDICT classification export

`node scripts/cedict-classify.cjs` reproduces the full CC-CEDICT gloss-level JSON export under `crates/zipeek-db-gen/data/classifications/`. This is a **heuristic annotation aid** for reviewing the taxonomy, **not** a replacement for model/lexicographer review and **not** automatically ingested by `db-full`. Raw dictionary line/gloss locations differ from the 32,500 HSK source-sense IDs. Use `needs_review` and `evidence` to audit the suggested assignments; records with insufficient evidence retain `pos: ["unclassified"]` and empty categories. The source is CC BY-SA 4.0; retain attribution and license with any redistribution.

## R179: offline CC-CEDICT classification import is the default for `db-full`

`cargo make db-full` no longer contacts LM Studio by default. It converts the bundled R178 rule-generated gloss classifications to the exact `CachedClassification` records required by the current imported HSK senses, then uses the existing verified publisher and atomic installer. Source-line plus gloss-index are used for CC-CEDICT fallback senses. HSK-primary senses match only when simplified form, normalized pinyin, and exact English gloss agree uniquely. Conflicting or missing matches become `pos:["unclassified"]`, `categories:[]`; **they are not guessed or assigned invented IDs**. The command prints exact matches, review flags, ambiguous matches, and unmatched counts. The full 199,699-gloss export remains alongside the pinned source and CC BY-SA attribution.

The import verifies the source checksum, taxonomy version, export record count, duplicate locators, and all allowed labels. It refuses to overwrite an existing generated classification cache and validates all newly generated records against their database-sense digests before publication. The default cache is `target/db-workflow/cedict-gloss-rules-v1.jsonl`. If source inputs change and the cache becomes stale, remove that generated cache and retry; the installed database remains unchanged on failure.

**Quality warning:** This is a deterministic heuristic export, not AI-reviewed data. A large proportion of imported senses may remain unclassified, and some exact matches are flagged for review. `db-full` now makes this data available to Browse without claiming expert linguistic validation. Review the summary and inspect a sample of classified senses before relying on the labels for pedagogy.

`cargo make db-ai-smoke` remains an explicit LM Studio diagnostic task; it is **not necessary for the offline default**. If needed, opt into the previous full LM Studio pipeline for `db-full` with PowerShell `$env:ZIPEEK_DB_CLASSIFIER='lmstudio'`, then remove the variable after use. To regenerate the rule-classification export, run `node scripts/cedict-classify.cjs` and delete the generated cache before the next `db-full` run.

## R181 - independent offline classification stage

Use `cargo make db-generate` to create the base candidate, then
`cargo make db-classify` to validate/import the shipped CC-CEDICT rule labels
and generate a **second, enriched candidate**. Finally run
`cargo make db-install` to install the latest verified candidate with the
existing backup/rollback publisher. Classification never directly modifies
an installed database. It may reuse the validated JSONL cache at
`target/db-workflow/cedict-gloss-rules-v1.jsonl`; remove that cache if the
bundled export has been regenerated and the cache is stale.

`cargo make db-full` retains the one-command convenience workflow.
`ZIPEEK_DB_CLASSIFIER=lmstudio` remains an optional path when the local model
has passed its independent smoke tests. `db-install` intentionally accepts
unenriched candidates for fast development; ensure `db-classify` completed
before installing when enrichment is required.
title: AI dictionary classification - operational guide

| 9 | Translate sentence | **New** route smoke; `tests/translation_fixture.rs` + AI fixture | **R204:** `translator_diagnostics::{structured_rejection_returns_plain_translation, structured_success_shows_analysis}` now submits real page input to deterministic server fixture; Chrome execution still pending |
| 10 | Games | **New** route smoke; `recent_routes::crossword_click_to_place_and_reset` | Add Cloud Match end-to-end play/finish path |
| 11 | Random | **New** Home tile transition | Follow word details, reload behavior and audio |
| 12 | Settings | **New** route smoke; `recent_routes::settings_font_and_theme_are_independent` | Persist all key preference panels and test failure messaging |
| 13 | About | **New** route smoke | Verify attribution links and keyboard navigation |

## New progression contract

`learner_journeys::practice_progress_and_configuration_journey` proves that: future step circles are disabled; selecting Advanced opens Exercises; the six exercise tiles are available; tile selection reflects `aria-pressed` and `data-selected`; Continue first opens **Configure** (where the selection grid is absent), then Vocabulary; previous progress circles navigate back without losing selected exercises. This is the acceptance contract for the R202 navigation redesign.

## Injecting a loader failure

**Do not introduce `/#/?fail`** merely to make production fail. The current harness can reproduce real failures with Chrome DevTools Protocol `Network.setBlockedURLs`, as implemented in `tests/suites/database.rs`. This works in both debug and release builds without adding user-facing failure switches or an injection branch to application code. For deterministic error types unreachable through network blocking, use fixture server responses or a test-only CDP request interception. If a future Rust-only fault seam becomes necessary, gate it under `debug_assertions`, require a precise fault name, and verify that release builds ignore it. Never interpret a production-facing URL parameter as authorization to break startup.

## Determinism and isolation

No sleep-based synchronization: wait on `data-*` hooks or page state. Use fixture responses instead of live AI/audio/image service availability. Check a real outcome, not only that a page opened. Keep each scenario in a separate function under `tests/suites/`, and register it once in `suites/mod.rs`; the harness isolates storage and captures browser diagnostics. Run the root suite with:

```powershell
cargo make setup
cargo test -p zipeek-e2e --test smoke --locked -- --test-threads=1
```

The older MCQ/Matching/Mixed E2E selectors may still predate the R202 stepper and must be migrated before the entire root suite can be considered passing. The new paths extend coverage; they do not claim to complete all 13 journeys.

## R204 diagnostics and setup migration

The managed AI fixture now supports `translator-rejected-analysis` (HTTP 400
with a model context-limit reason, followed by a successful plain translation)
and `translator-valid-analysis` (valid structured JSON). The dedicated Chrome
cases verify the real `/translate-sentence` route, result rendering and
presence/absence of analysis. `tests/suites/setup.rs` now tests the actual
interactive progress rail, Choose/Configure substeps, selection guards,
Fixed 5 default, change of session length, and responsive screenshots.
Old removed `data-activity-picker` / `data-exclusions-reset` form selectors
were deleted from that suite. The other legacy practice suites have not all
been migrated or executed; source-contract tests alone are insufficient.

## R219 HSK selection load and Summary navigation

`learner_journeys::rapid_hsk_selection_remains_responsive` clicks several HSK levels in a short burst, checks that the reducer retains the correct final selections, proceeds directly to Summary, and verifies that Back and Start remain together while the page-owned debounced vocabulary preflight resolves. This scenario is registered in the managed Chrome suite but has not been executed in this packaging environment.

## R518 Word Sets UI acceptance

The Word Sets management sidebar shows all existing sets directly (no dropdown). Switching between sets updates the vocabulary list and clears any search query. Search matches simplified Hanzi, pinyin or English gloss case-insensitively. Rename is behind an explicit, keyboard-operable Rename disclosure; deleting a set requires a second, clearly labelled action. The document owns vertical scrolling on desktop and mobile, including long word lists; no nested word-list scrollbar. Export/import remains available under Data tools. R518 remembers the selected set as the default destination for Dictionary Add/Remove. Practice remains independently configured.

# Testing and validation

> **Current approved target behavior:** [Approved behavior acceptance](../../../testing-quality/acceptance/approved-behavior-acceptance.md). Older implementation descriptions below record prior contracts and may not match the latest approved behavior or verified source.


Rust unit/integration tests and real Chrome runs answer different questions. JavaScript source-contract tests under `scripts/` were retired by decision in R392. A test appearing in the repository is not proof that it has run successfully. Current acceptance state is maintained in [CURRENT](../../../project-management/current.md); open gates are in [TASKS](../../../project-management/tasks.md). Historical evidence belongs in [release history](../../RELEASE_HISTORY.md).

## Commands from the workspace root

```powershell
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo check --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p zipeek-web
cargo check --locked -p zipeek-e2e --tests
```

Run affected Rust tests first for routine work. For comprehensive release acceptance use:

```powershell
cargo make e2e-full
cargo make pack-e2e
```

`e2e-full` first checks WASM, compiles all release E2E targets, then runs the managed Rust/Chrome suites serially. The pack task prepares evidence for review. Browser suites use a managed server, an isolated Chrome profile and scenario-specific artifacts; see [E2E](../e2e.md) and [E2E architecture](../../../testing-quality/e2e/e2e-architecture.md).

## Current browser coverage

- Shared catalog: 34 concrete route cases under root and the `/zipeek/` deployment base, plus separate accessibility and 320/390/768px responsive checks.
- Behavioral suites: Browse/Word Sets, Settings/Debug, Practice setup and persistence, courses, games, speaking, translation, writing, shell navigation and errors. See test targets under `crates/zipeek-e2e/tests/`.
- Sentence Translation: deterministic Rust AI fixture and optional live provider journey through Settings, Practice setup and the UUID-backed generated exercise. Fixture tests cover canonical tiles, finite completion, restore and Endless behavior.
- AI fixture: `crates/zipeek-e2e/src/harness/ai_fixture.rs`; the old Node `ai-server.cjs` is removed.

**Acceptance limitation:** The user reported successful Windows accessibility, Browse and an earlier live translation test. The newest UUID translation implementation and full suite still need their own execution. An ignored test is not a pass; route presence is not equivalent to complete interaction or WCAG compliance.

## Live AI test

Provide a running OpenAI-compatible endpoint and exact model ID, then run:

```powershell
$env:ZIPEEK_E2E_AI_ENDPOINT = 'http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1/'
$env:ZIPEEK_E2E_AI_MODEL = 'your-loaded-model-id'
cargo test --release --locked -p zipeek-e2e --test ai_learner -- --ignored --nocapture
```

The live test is intentionally excluded from deterministic CI. It sends actual requests to the locally configured provider; it is not a general assertion of model correctness.

## Related focused guides

[Browser database](../../../testing-quality/e2e/browser-db.md), [matching](../../../testing-quality/e2e/matching.md), [MCQ](../../../testing-quality/e2e/mcq.md), [startup](../../../testing-quality/e2e/startup.md), [shell](../../../testing-quality/e2e/shell.md), [E2E recording](../../../testing-quality/e2e/e2e-recording.md), [evidence](../../../testing-quality/e2e/evidence.md), [UI acceptance](../../../testing-quality/acceptance/ui-acceptance.md).

# UI feature acceptance - Cloud Match, CSS, Write Hanzi

This document consolidates the current non-crossword UI checks. Previous release-specific checklists are superseded; versioned evidence remains in [Release history](../../RELEASE_HISTORY.md).

## Cloud Match

1. Setup has a shared Back/Cloud Match title row and a compact **Start** action with a play icon. Verify both HSK and Word Set sources, three matching formats and all difficulty settings.
2. During a wave, clouds have varied silhouettes and individual movement speeds, remain visible/selectable throughout their bounded motion, and do not shift lanes when a match is removed.
3. Selection highlights the cloud silhouette, not a detached oval. Correct/incorrect feedback updates the score/lives HUD, not a bottom notification. Announcements remain accessible.
4. Match, miss, time out, pause, resume and stop: assert the pure engine score/lives/wave transitions still agree with the HUD and no pair can score twice.
5. Hide the browser tab during a wave; return to a **paused** round with its score, wave and remaining time intact. Resume explicitly. Test keyboard and touch, small screens, zoom, and `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Styles and shared shell

1. `crates/zipeek-web/styles/main.css` stays a Tailwind entry point, not a feature-style dumping ground. Tokens, base, accessibility, shared layout and feature-specific CSS retain their separate ownership.
2. Run asset preparation and the normal Trunk build to confirm Tailwind expands all local imports and scans Rust `@source` declarations.
3. Check light/dark and preset themes, button/action classes, focus/contrast, scrollbar styling and Chinese fonts. Verify shell fullscreen routes do not inherit an unwanted sidebar grid.
4. Visually compare Crossword, Cloud Match, Write Hanzi and landing layouts at desktop, mobile and high zoom. Source checks cannot establish pixel equivalence.

## Write Hanzi

1. Change between My Word Sets and English search; changing source or set resets selection and pagination as intended.
2. Search with fast successive edits and verify the latest submitted query wins. Page through more than five results and select a different word.
3. Navigate via a deep-linked word ID, including missing/unsupported entries; confirm explicit statuses and no stale selection.
4. Change characters inside a chosen word; prevent out-of-range indices. Verify the drawing workspace, stroke interactions and responsive sizing are unchanged.
5. Shared `Dictionary` and `WordSetsContext` remain providers. Route-local query/source/loading/selection/character state belongs in one typed workflow reducer; presentation children receive typed props and callbacks.

## Verification

Run `cargo make release-check` and the focused Rust/web tests appropriate to the change. Check behavior in Chrome with real browser data. Node source-contract successes are not build proof. Historical test counts and known missing gates are documented in [Release history](../../RELEASE_HISTORY.md).

## Practice setup (R266 acceptance)

1. At `/practice`, traverse Path → Exercises → Vocabulary → Summary and back. Verify the single top action bar does not jump below the panels, including on narrow screens and with a large font; Start is followed by the play icon.
2. Toggle ten then zero then all fifteen exercise cards. The selected-count badge must always match the draft, including when moving to Configure and back; test keyboard and screen reader announcements.
3. In Categories & filters, confirm suggestions load before typing, filter immediately, prevent stale response overwrite, and allow selection/removal. With dictionary unavailable, no fabricated category options should appear.
4. Review the Summary icons, HSK and category chips, Word Set alternative, chosen session mode, and truthful practice-only limitations. Test zero and multiple selected filters.
5. Verify initial and per-session loading statuses, screen-reader announcements, light/dark contrast and `prefers-reduced-motion`; confirm no Animato transition is being claimed for this release.
title: UI feature acceptance - Cloud Match, CSS, Write Hanzi

# Browser dictionary verification

## Current test targets

The dictionary is served from [`zipeek-web/static`](../../../../crates/zipeek-web/static) and loaded through [`zipeek-db` WASM](../../../../crates/zipeek-db/src/wasm). The installed manifest currently declares **12,188** words, normalized relations and browser package `1.33.1-dev114.0`. The original 12,100-row tests and 1.32.0 browser engine described in old A06 notes were evidence for a **different, earlier artifact** and are not release criteria for the current one.

From the workspace root on a configured Windows development machine:

```powershell
cargo check --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p zipeek-web
cargo test --release --locked -p zipeek-e2e --test browse_interactions -- --nocapture
cargo test --release --locked -p zipeek-e2e --test settings_diagnostics -- --nocapture
cargo test --release --locked -p zipeek-e2e --test route_matrix -- --nocapture
```

The user reported all six Browse scenarios passing (Word Sets, pronunciation accessibility, empty search, live search/clear, pagination) and the accessibility matrix passing on an earlier R282 source. The latest UUID translation changes have not undergone the full browser matrix. The tests must check actual runtime readiness and query behavior rather than accepting the presence of a manifest or an element as a pass.

## Invariants to verify

- Manifest checksums and source metadata refer to the installed compressed database; the browser resolves local worker/Arrow assets for both root and `/zipeek/` base.
- The connection opens dictionary data **read-only**; no Practice/personal-data mutation occurs there.
- A typed read must succeed before the app reports Ready; failure and Retry remain navigable.
- The current manifest metadata, browser engine and runtime disk statistics are separate sources of facts, displayed separately in Debug.
- Browse filtered search must not duplicate IDs; pages must be ordered and next/previous transitions reproducible for the same source snapshot.
- Confirm generator `character_readings` presence against the actual installed database before claiming character-reading query coverage: the installed manifest table list omits it although the generator SQL defines it.

See [current validation](../../../project-management/current.md), [browser DB architecture](../../../architecture/modules/browser-db.md) and [source reconciliation](../SOURCE_RECONCILIATION.md). Historical output-specific hashes and old Chrome runs remain in [release history](../../RELEASE_HISTORY.md).

## A15 modular Chrome harness - 2026-10-28

All five required gates pass: formatting, workspace Clippy with warnings denied,
locked workspace tests, wasm check and the /zipeek/ Trunk build. Workspace tests
pass 94 Rust tests: 88 existing domain/generator/query tests, four new lifecycle

adapter scenarios; Pages runs one. Two additional expected browser faults (error
and panic) prove same-session recovery and are not product failures/test counts.

target/e2e/pages-30952-1793180767003955600. Each summary records successful browser
quit and reaped owned servers. Scenario screenshots and console/resource JSON,

retained. A process inventory after validation found no live Node/Trunk PID from
the recorded harness runs.

listener, early-exit status/output, guard Drop during assertion unwinding and
termination of a descendant TCP listener. The first sandbox run denied Windows

actual link and preserves the same text assertion; application markup/branding
was not changed. All 46 original explicit assertions remain across the modular
suites, including 12,100 rows, ten columns, bound ID lookup, read-only rejection,
loading/retry, URL replay boundary, themes, keyboard, responsive and Pages prefix.

records otherwise match the pre-task graph. The AGENTS version/dependency policy
table, source scratchpad, dictionary and background hashes remain unchanged.

Clippy with warnings denied, locked workspace tests (94 Rust tests), wasm check
and /zipeek/ Trunk build. Both Chrome entry points pass: nine root scenarios and
two Pages scenarios, plus the existing expected-fault/recovery probes. Log:
target/a35/workspace-tests.log; gate summary: target/a35/gates.json.

Before screenshots/metrics: target/e2e/root-30556-1793181623041320200/
shell_and_card_styling. Final root/Pages runs:
target/e2e/root-20944-1793198301539203200 and
target/e2e/pages-42024-1793198288786632300. Dark/light captures cover 400/640/768/
1024/1280/1920px in each build. The final root run also captures mounted Loading
and Failed at 400/1280px in both themes, and the existing bootstrap checks remain.
The scrolled 400px footer, desktop/ultrawide cards and mobile failure view were
visually inspected. Twelve before/after metric comparisons preserve card/tile

boundaries, full-width panel/content and approved navigation/footer cleanup.
Report: target/a35/comparison-report.json.

Acceptance verifies no horizontal overflow at supported widths, md rail and lg
three-tile layout, no max-width cap, label-only navigation with unchanged visual
appearance for active/inactive links and retained aria-current, footer repository
attributes/24px target, single row with attribution wrapping inside its item,

All five gates pass: formatting, workspace/all-targets Clippy with warnings denied,
locked workspace tests (100 Rust tests), wasm32 zipeek check and standalone

# Planned pedagogical-history and proficiency E2E contract

**Status: specification for future Rust tests, not existing passing coverage.** The current R282 code has no `/stats` implementation, durable Practice history writer, or production clock injection. This plan deliberately does not assert they exist.

## Testable architecture

- Introduce a `Clock` / `TimeProvider` boundary in the core learning-evidence domain. Reads of *now*, session start/finish, attempt timestamps, calendar-day classification and Stats computation use the same injected service. Production uses a real clock; E2E harness uses a fixed, advancing clock. Prevent direct scattered calls to `SystemTime::now`, `Date.now`, or `new Date()` for evidence timestamps. An explicit learner timezone or deterministic calendar-day rule must be shared by both app and tests.
- Expose the fake clock only in an E2E-authorized build or fixture boundary, never via a publicly writable production endpoint or page attribute. Time travel changes future timestamps, **not previously stored timestamps**. Keep the read-only vocabulary dictionary separate from the personal DuckDB.
- Provide a Rust fixture that can reset an isolated personal database, set the clock, read persisted sessions and derived observations, and assert event counts. Verify the browser's actual OPFS/personal-DB connection; a mocked in-memory ledger cannot substitute for durability tests.
- Use deterministic exercise/assessor fixtures to simulate four genuinely assessed competencies, including a controlled recorded-speech evaluation result. Separately run device-level recording tests; a browser fixture cannot verify microphone or model accuracy.

## Full user journey: seven active days

1. Start with a fresh user profile, enable pedagogical recording when the setting is implemented, and populate a Word Set with ten **distinct, playable Hanzi-bearing entries**. Verify the selected set becomes enabled in Practice setup. Before adding the tenth entry, assert it is disabled and explains how many more are needed.
2. Start Practice from this Word Set. Complete a scored session containing real target-word opportunities and multiple exercise modalities. Verify the session record is committed to the personal DuckDB and the temporary UUID record is cleared only after the durable-write contract has completed.
3. Advance the injected clock to the **next local calendar day**, open another Practice session, and score further independent evidence. Repeat across seven **distinct active dates**, including at least three unique session IDs and a total of at least ten qualifying encounters for one target identity, subject to the configured session cap.
4. Include separately assessed successes for recognition, listening comprehension, spoken production, and correct sentence use. Visit `/stats`; verify the per-skill evidence and totals are sourced from stored events. Only assert an overall *proficient* label once approved per-skill success thresholds exist and all conditions are met. Before that policy is approved, assert **eligibility satisfied / overall proficiency pending**.
5. Reload the browser, navigate away and back to `/stats`, and confirm the same durable outcomes without seeding the totals directly. Verify HSK/category labels and grammar-point references can be traced back to the original scored attempts.

## Negative and boundary scenarios

| Scenario | Required assertion |
| --- | --- |
| Seven encounters on one day, or elapsed seven days with only two active dates | Not eligible: fewer than seven distinct active dates |
| Nine qualifying encounters over seven active days | Not eligible: fewer than ten encounters |
| Ten encounters in one session, even when repeated correctly | Not eligible: fewer than three sessions, with per-session qualification cap enforced |
| Ten correct Matching answers and no other modalities | Recognition evidence only; speaking, listening and sentence use remain unproven |
| Recorded audio without assessed speech result | No speaking success credited |
| Guided Sentence Builder shows correct answer and plays audio | Instructional/assisted event; no unassisted sentence-production credit |
| Incorrect attempt after previous proficiency | Affected dynamic skill moves toward review under the approved failure policy; permanent grammar course completion does not revert |
| Duplicate event, refresh, browser retry, or replayed submission | Idempotent event storage and no extra qualifying encounter |
| Disabled recording or missing consent | No durable pedagogical record is written |
| DuckDB write fails or is blocked | No false saved confirmation; recoverable error state and no silent loss |
| Edited Word Set drops below ten valid entries | Practice source disabled again; launch path rechecks eligibility |
| One word seen ten times, other nine only once | No blanket proficiency award to the other nine |
| Two identical word labels with different stable identities | No accidental aggregation across identities |
| DST transition or timezone change | Distinct-day classification follows the single documented timezone rule |
| Import/export and database reload | Totals reproduce from authoritative session/attempt evidence, not a mutable cached score |

## Separate grammar-course acceptance

Use the approved [Courses spec](../../../learning-practice/courses/courses-mosaic.md) and [learning evidence policy](../../../learning-practice/practice/learning-evidence.md). For each HSK grammar point, verify explanation, examples, guided practice, independently scored assessment, and retained per-point pass state. Include guided image-to-Hanzi, Hanzi writing, Character Builder, Sentence Builder with a visible/playable correct sentence, and word-bank Sentence Transformation. Confirm visible teaching hints never automatically award independent proficiency. After all required points pass, the grammar region permanently reveals; incorrect later vocabulary answers affect dynamic proficiency only, not historic course completion.

## Integration boundaries

Tests should live in the Rust E2E harness (not a new Node server), reuse the shared page objects, and isolate fixtures per scenario. Do not advance the real machine clock, bypass the actual Practice/storage flow by directly writing mastered flags, or call a simulation-only Stats URL in production. A passing test must verify results *from the personal DuckDB and public UI* and must report whether real microphone/acoustic scoring was exercised or simulated.

## R352 full-run harness checkpoint (2026-11-12)

Two explicit Rust/Thirtyfour suites now exist: `full_run_standard` and `full_run_pedagogical`. Both use a seed from `ZIPEEK_E2E_SEED` (default `20261112`), a hard execution budget from `ZIPEEK_E2E_MAX_MINUTES` (default 60, valid 1-120), a clean landing/onboarding choice, and mandatory PNG screenshots with a JSONL screenshot manifest. The standard run captures the complete route itinerary and five seeded exercise *entry* views; the pedagogical run captures the course/practice/writing/game/Stats itinerary. Both verify persisted opt-in selection. A route visit is never reported as an answered exercise, completed session, or acquired Hanzi.

These suites have `#[ignore]` and are deliberately **non-passing** when invoked explicitly: the standard variant records the missing five scored rounds, word-set editing and AI practice finish gates; the pedagogical variant records the missing independently validated recognition producer, consent-gated personal DuckDB journal, worker verified readback, browser clock injection, and 90%-HSK Golden Dragon award. They emit `full-run-prerequisites.txt` and existing harness failure artifacts. Until these gates are implemented, do not remove `#[ignore]` or assert these journeys passed.

Run on a machine with the pinned Rust toolchain and Chrome E2E prerequisites:

```powershell
$env:ZIPEEK_E2E_SEED = '20261112'
$env:ZIPEEK_E2E_MAX_MINUTES = '60'
cargo make e2e-full-standard
cargo make e2e-full-pedagogical
```

`zipeek-pedagogy::RecognitionClock` abstracts the projection's as-of timestamp; the E2E-only `SimulatedClock` advances monotonically by 86,400,000 ms/day and has unit tests for seven-day spacing. This does **not** yet inject virtual timestamps into the browser's practice and persistence pipeline. Production exposes no simulated-time control or unlock endpoint. Simulated time will be meaningful to the full run only after the same clock is used to timestamp real scored evidence through the approved pipeline.
title: Planned pedagogical-history and proficiency E2E contract

# Practice exercise browser coverage inventory - R286 WIP

The authoritative registry is `crates/zipeek-exercises/src/definition.rs` (`DEFINITIONS`).
These entries describe **observed test scope**, not a claim that every behavior is passing in Chrome.
An exercise appearing in a setup selector or route test does not establish a completed answer,
recovery, score, persistence, or accessibility contract.

| Exercise | Browser evidence located | Missing depth |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Matching | Dedicated matching scenarios, round navigation | UUID history persistence and cross-tab duplicate launch |
| Multiple Choice | Setup and learner journey references | Dedicated answer, correction, resume and completion journey |
| Type Pinyin | Wrong-answer retry, settings, resume | Completed answer and history journey |
| Character Builder | Tile interaction, preferences, refresh, resume | Completion and history journey |
| Word Mosaics | Setup selection | Tile answer, finish, restore |
| Sentence Translation | Deterministic translation fixture | All directions, UUID history error/retry |
| Listening Choice | Route/interactions, prerequisites | Answer, recover, completion |
| Image Vocabulary | Selection interaction | Full scored result and recovery |
| Speaking | Dedicated standalone interactions | Audio lifecycle under UUID host and unscored evidence |
| Character Hunt | Hint/interactions and learner journey | Complete rounds, restore, history |
| Fill Blank | Setup selection | Answer, feedback, resume and finish |
| Audio Dictation | No exercise-specific browser scenario located | Full journey |
| Sentence Builder | Setup selection | Tile correctness, recovery, completion |
| Sentence Transformation | No exercise-specific browser scenario located | Grammar alternatives, feedback, recovery |
| Spot Mistake | Setup selection | Detection + correction journey |
| Handwriting Recall | Setup selection | Draw/reveal, restore, unscored completion |

`practice_answer_options.rs` now additionally tests that an existing UUID Practice session
blocks setup and remains resumable. This does not establish a cross-tab atomicity guarantee:
`localStorage` provides synchronous individual operations, not a compare-and-swap transaction.

## Required release coverage

For each type, test a representative launch, incorrect/correct or unscored action,
completion, and any applicable refresh/recovery. Test browser recording opt-in/out and
failure retry separately. Generated AI types need deterministic fixture cases; a live
model remains an optional integration run. Keep route smoke checks as a separate layer.

## R289 Practice options acceptance (pending Chrome)

The new Type Pinyin preference exposes the expected Pinyin as a placeholder when guided hints are enabled. The hint is not evidence of independent recall. Character Builder offers optional automatic validation when the bank fills, including red incorrect-feedback and reset when retries are enabled. The browser suite now exercises configuration independence, the configured hint on launch and refresh, automatic answer submission, and same-tab restoration of `/practice` after the reminder discards a session. These additions are unverified until the Windows Chrome run completes.

The persistent `PracticeExerciseOptions` model contains configurable options for Character Builder and Type Pinyin only. It is not a statement that every option of all sixteen exercise types is snapshotted there. Other configuration fields (for example Matching variants, translation direction, and Character Hunt difficulty) are stored in the session's step metadata or vocabulary map where implemented. The remaining per-type option completeness audit is open.

# Startup loading checks

**Historical acceptance scenarios:** old 12,100-row readiness numbers refer to an earlier artifact, not the installed 12,188-row manifest. Current startup implementation and current acceptance are in [browser-db](../../../architecture/modules/browser-db.md) and [CURRENT](../../../project-management/current.md).

Static loading shell, handoff, and database readiness coverage. Part of the
[testing index](../../../testing-quality/acceptance/testing.md). Approved requirement in
[D26](../../../project-management/decisions/web-and-ui.md#d26-persistent-landscape-and-loading-presentation);
product contract in [PRODUCT](../../../product-ux/product.md#startup-loading-experience).

## Required coverage

- Delay app bootstrap to verify the static HTML loading shell is visible before
  Yew mounts. Check its theme/background/loading indicator without depending on
  the database or Yew having initialized.
- Delay database loading independently of bootstrap. Verify Yew's first render
  is Loading and that the loading view remains visible after mount while the
  database is fetching/opening; no blank or premature ready content.
- Verify Ready appears only once the read-only database is queryable, including
  when its valid word pool is empty (D05's neutral card, not a stuck spinner).
- Simulate a failed download/open, verify loading ends in the centered dictionary
  error card with a readable alert and Try again action, and verify retry
  transitions through Loading to success or another handled failure. Confirm
  technical exception details remain in the console rather than the error card.

Use controlled delays/failures when implementing this coverage; fixed sleeps do
not establish the loading-state lifecycle.

## Related runtime requirements

The startup lifecycle is defined in
[ARCHITECTURE §Startup](../../../architecture/modules/web-shell.md#startup-static-loading-shell-and-yew-loading-state)
and implemented by A06, with A31 pure readiness reducer/provider and
DatabaseBoundary separation. The visual
presentation (landscape outside `#root`, centered spinner, reduced-motion) is
[D26](../../../project-management/decisions/web-and-ui.md#d26-persistent-landscape-and-loading-presentation)
and implemented by A30. This file covers the *state transitions* during startup;
the *visual presentation* is covered in [shell.md](../../../testing-quality/e2e/shell.md).

## Current status

A06 implements Loading/Ready/Failed+Retry; A31 separates provider ownership
above the router from DatabaseBoundary presentation inside the shell. A30
implements the static loading shell and Yew Loader composition. Chrome tests
exercise mounted Loading while a controlled fetch is held, download failure and
Retry, and the real 12,100-row Ready state (see
[browser-db.md](../../../testing-quality/e2e/browser-db.md)). The checks above are the target coverage once
feature tasks wire their remaining query surfaces; the loading-state tests described in the first
four bullets are already implemented by A06.

## A21 route/query coverage

After dictionary Ready, controlled worker-message delays prove practice Loading
persists until queries settle. A delayed old query failure released after a new
variant is Ready cannot replace it. A one-shot query failure reaches Retry, which
prepares the same URL/offset successfully. Run these at root and /zipeek/. An
unknown route displays its 404 even with dictionary fetch blocked, then Home
recovery can use the ordinary dictionary Retry. Ready practice placeholders replace
the previous permanent spinner; gameplay is still unimplemented.

## Rust startup preferences (R196)

`crates/zipeek-web/src/setup.rs` applies dark/light mode, Hanzi font, preset
and layout density through the existing typed settings before calling Yew
`Renderer::render()`. `index.html` contains no duplicate localStorage policy.
The static HTML loader and hidden fatal panel remain available independently
of Yew, but a WASM download failure cannot be caught by Rust code that did not
start. Check dark and light saved preferences, invalid and blocked localStorage,
root absence, and the browser console manually. The initial HTML defaults to
dark, so a saved light theme may flash dark before WASM initialization.

# Practice route and replay validation

There are **two different state models**. Classic Matching/MCQ rounds use typed URL queries with a deterministic round seed; translation-only Advanced Practice uses a browser-local UUID record and should not embed per-question configuration into the URL. Tests must not conflate them or treat previous release encodings as permanent compatibility requirements.

## Classic URL rounds

`zipeek-core/src/practice/` owns query parsing and normalization. Tests cover HSK system/level, Fixed/Endless selection, exclusions, seed, offset, saved Word Set snapshots and safe failure for invalid inputs. Reproducing a shared round requires the same dictionary snapshot and effective inputs. Reloading a Fixed round does not imply restoring its prior page-local score or progress. See [round generation](../../games/round-generation.md), [matching](../../testing-quality/e2e/matching.md) and [MCQ](../../testing-quality/e2e/mcq.md).

## UUID-backed generated Practice

`#/practice/session/<id>` resolves a record created by Practice setup. The persisted record contains selected vocabulary, translation direction, schedule seed, generated question and outcomes. Missing/corrupt IDs must show a recovery error rather than silently launching an unrelated question. Navigation/reload of unfinished work restores that record; completion deletes the temporary record. See [sentence exercises](../../architecture/modules/sentence-exercises.md) and [Practice setup](../../learning-practice/practice/practice-session-builder.md).

## Actual acceptance

`crates/zipeek-e2e/tests/translation_fixture.rs` covers the UUID translation journey with the Rust fixture. Other integration test targets cover classic URL replay and browser interactions. The latest UUID translation implementation still requires execution on Windows. Do not preserve obsolete URL encodings merely to satisfy old snapshots: the active Rust types and explicit user decisions govern the contract.
title: Practice route and replay validation
