# Archived source snapshot: product-ux/product.md

This source snapshot preserves historical descriptions, not current requirements. Use the maintained document at its original location for approved behavior.

> **Courses routes (R482 WIP):** The three independent learning tracks have dedicated URLs `/courses/vocabulary`, `/courses/grammar`, and `/courses/pinyin`; `/courses` redirects to Vocabulary. The compact tab navigation shows track names only. See [Courses](../../../learning-practice/courses/courses-mosaic.md).

> **Current approved target behavior:** [Practice outcomes](../../../learning-practice/practice/practice-outcomes.md), [vocabulary selection and exclusions](../../../dictionary-data/vocabulary/vocabulary-selection.md), [profile portability](../../../learning-practice/practice/practice-profile-portability.md), [AI Hanzi recognition](../../../learning-practice/hanzi/ai-hanzi-recognition.md), and [platform policy](../../../product-ux/foundation/interface-and-platform-policy.md). Older implementation descriptions below record prior contracts and may not match the latest approved behavior or verified source.


> **Vocabulary curriculum update (2026-11-15, R471 WIP):** The Vocabulary track now has 100 separate domain/theme/word-class regions covering all 11,494 pinned HSK source records, with 132 independently acquirable Word Sets of up to 200 words. Source-entry coverage is audited; semantic classification is glossary-assisted and still needs human review. Acquiring a set is not mastery. See [Courses](../../../learning-practice/courses/courses-mosaic.md) and [coverage report](../../../learning-practice/VOCABULARY_COVERAGE.json).
> **Vocabulary mosaic sizing (R472 WIP):** All 100 Vocabulary-only tiles use deterministic area-proportional geometry based on the count of distinct acquirable HSK readings in each region. Small themed sets occupy small map areas, not equal-sized grid squares. This is unrelated to mastery progress; Grammar and Pinyin geometry do not change. Compiled and visual acceptance are pending.

> **Vocabulary mosaic refinement (R473 WIP):** Reading counts still determine relative region size, but a square-root scale and minimum area replace strict proportionality. The 100 regions are spatially scattered; the panel omits internal region numbering and algorithm descriptions. Verification pending.

> **Courses update (2026-11-15):** The current requirement is **three independent tracks**. Grammar mosaic contains 100 Grammar regions **only**; Vocabulary has its own 100-region mosaic, not pockets within Grammar; Pinyin has a separate six-region mosaic. The R355/R356 descriptions below are historical and their 100+50 combined topology is superseded. Grammar now has a single Start course route and staged lesson workspace without the global application shell. See [current Courses specification](../../../learning-practice/courses/courses-mosaic.md) for verified scope and pending completion evidence.

## R358 Courses third guided grammar lesson

The Courses mosaic now links three authored guided grammar regions. Course 3, **Possession, Existence & Quantities**, teaches 有, 没有, counting with classifiers (本 and 个), 几 and 多少. Five comprehension checks and six guided sentence-building/transformation activities have reference answers and explanations. They do not independently assess mastery or unlock mosaic artwork. The remaining 97 grammar regions and all 50 vocabulary pockets await authored syllabuses and verified proficiency. The existing first two courses and three Pinyin lessons remain available.

## R357 Courses second guided grammar lesson

The Courses mosaic now links two authored guided grammar regions. Course 2, **Time, Place & Everyday Actions**, teaches when and where actions happen: 今天 / 明天 before a verb, 在 + location before an action, combinations of time and place, 去 + destination, and 在哪里 questions. Five knowledge checks and six guided sentence-bank activities provide teaching feedback with answers visible; they are not independent assessments. Course 1 remains available with its four checks and six guided bank activities. The remaining 98 grammar regions have not been authored, and all 150 grammar/vocabulary regions remain covered pending separately verified durable completion and word proficiency.

# Product specification

This document records product intent and earlier approved D-number contracts; **current source and the [source reconciliation](../SOURCE_RECONCILIATION.md) take precedence for implemented behavior when older contracts have been superseded.** For implemented behavior and known gaps consult [CURRENT](../../../project-management/current.md), and for actual route definitions consult `crates/zipeek-web/src/route.rs`.
See [ARCHITECTURE](../../../architecture/architecture.md) for the current implementation
and [DECISIONS](../../../project-management/decisions/index.md) for choices still requiring approval.

## R356 Courses guided grammar practice (no assessed completion)

The Basic Sentence Structure introductory lesson now contains six authored word-bank teaching tasks in addition to its four existing explanation/comprehension checks: three Sentence Builder prompts and three Sentence Transformations. Learners can construct a sentence by choosing individual Hanzi/word tiles, remove individual tiles, undo and reset, see a *visible* reference answer throughout the guided stage, receive pattern-specific feedback and repeat all tasks. This is an instructional flow, not evidence of unassisted grammar mastery. It does not save completion, write pedagogical records or reveal any mosaic artwork. The remaining 99 grammar regions and all 50 vocabulary groups still require authored syllabus mappings and independent assessment evidence.

## Courses and proficiency roadmap (R355 mosaic foundation, assessments pending)

R355 changes Courses from a catalogue to an interactive 100-grammar/50-vocabulary mosaic with an original illustration and a genuine first guided grammar lesson. Existing three Pinyin lessons remain available, with local completion separate from mosaic progression. **This is not yet the assessed grammar-mastery platform**: the other grammar courses are unauthored, all vocabulary group memberships are pending, every region remains concealed, and no completion evidence is inferred from selecting/reading a course. The [approved Courses mosaic specification](../../../learning-practice/courses/courses-mosaic.md) defines 100 large grammar regions and 50 tiny vocabulary regions in one contiguous image, course-specific assessed grammar-point progression, and irreversible completed-course reveals. Vocabulary-region opacity depends on real distinct-word mastery and remains independent of grammar completion; never substitute the current marked-complete stub.

The future [pedagogical history policy](../../../learning-practice/practice/learning-evidence.md) records Practice sessions first and derives per-Hanzi, per-exercise, category, HSK and grammar evidence. Proficiency requires seven distinct active local dates, at least ten qualifying scored encounters across three or more sessions (subject to a per-session cap), and independent successes in recognition, listening, assessed speaking and sentence use. Matching-only repetition cannot establish proficiency. Exact per-skill thresholds, cap and retention policy still require specification; nothing in the existing local completion store provides this automatically.

## Purpose

Query Chinese words by hanzi, pinyin, English, and part of speech, and practise
them through matching and multiple-choice exercises. The app runs client-side
on GitHub Pages under `/zipeek/` and reads a pregenerated DuckDB database.

The original D07 design limited the pool to the union of HSK 2.0 and HSK 3.0. The **current generator** additionally imports valid CC-CEDICT-only readings, and the checked-in manifest reports **12,188 rows**. HSK-filtered exercise pools still use HSK membership, while an unfiltered dictionary pool can include additional entries. See [installed database](../../../dictionary-data/schema/db.md) and [source rules](../../../dictionary-data/schema/sources.md).

## Startup loading experience

Database-owned Loading/Ready/Failed+Retry is implemented. Ready requires a queryable read-only database; Browse, Random, daily-word content and exercises are implemented separately and must still handle their own data/error states.

Show the static loading shell from `crates/zipeek-web/index.html` while the app boots. When
Yew first mounts, its first render must also be the loading state, with a continuous
handoff from the HTML loader. Keep loading visible until DuckDB-WASM is initialized
and the fetched database is open and ready for queries; mounting Yew is not the
end of startup loading. Avoid a blank screen or a flash of empty/ready content.

On a database load failure, show the retry state described for Word of the Day
instead of leaving a permanent spinner. See [ARCHITECTURE](../../../architecture/modules/web-shell.md)
for the startup stages. The shared centered loading presentation and persistent
landscape are implemented in A30; the actual database readiness/retry pipeline
is implemented by A06/A31; A21 adds practice-query loading after database Ready.

## Routes

Paths below are app-relative; deployment retains the `/zipeek/` prefix.

| Route | Intended view |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | Shared collapsible drawer/top-panel theme switch, Word of the Day, Practice/Browse/Random tiles |
| `/practice` | Setup: HSK system/level, practice mode, Fixed count, exclusions reset; PoS picker is future work |
| `/practice/type-pinyin` | Type the pinyin reading of a dictionary word and check it against its tone-marked or numbered reading |
| `/practice/character-builder` | Assemble dictionary-backed Hanzi from selectable character tiles |
| `/practice/word-mosaics` | Clear eight Chinese-to-English vocabulary pairs by selecting matching tiles |
| `/practice/eng-pinyin` | English to pinyin matching |
| `/practice/pinyin-hanzi` | Pinyin to hanzi matching |
| `/practice/hanzi-eng` | Hanzi to English matching |
| `/practice/mcq/hanzi-to-meaning` | MCQ: simplified hanzi prompt, English answers |
| `/practice/mcq/meaning-to-hanzi` | MCQ: English prompt, simplified hanzi answers |
| `/practice/mcq/meaning-to-pinyin` | MCQ: English prompt, display-pinyin answers |
| `/browse` | Paginated word list with a smart search box, filter chips and settings modal |
| `/stats` | Five-section learning dashboard shell; displays no mastery claims until approved consent-gated evidence and personal DuckDB readback are authoritative |
| `/games` | Playable game gallery, including three first-pass curated mini-games |
| `/games/cloud-match` | Source-backed pre-game selection followed by drifting-cloud vocabulary matching; see [CLOUD_MATCH](../../../games/cloud-match.md) |
| `/games/classifier-market` | First-pass curated Mandarin measure-word selection game; currently uses six reviewed-by-code examples, not a dictionary source |
| `/games/listening-navigator` | First-pass browser-spoken Mandarin direction game on a small grid; speech depends on browser voice availability |
| `/games/sentence-relay` | First-pass curated sentence tile-ordering game; authored prompts require linguistic acceptance |

All three matching variants and the D20 MCQ variants are in scope for v1. The overall query requirement
also includes English; the answered Browse controls are specified in [UX](../UX.md#browse).
A37 selects simplified/pinyin/first-English-gloss/HSK/PoS result fields and
the complete q/strategy/f/page/page_size URL contract in UX.
Pinyin browse queries support both display-tone and original numbered forms (D07).
Preserve D16's source transcriptions, including their spacing and conventions.
Both English-bearing variants show the first gloss: left in eng-pinyin, right in
hanzi-eng. Exclude rows without English from those variants; pinyin-hanzi can
still use them. Duplicate detection normalizes labels, not display casing.

## Practice

Practice product contracts and historical constraints now have a dedicated reference. See [Product Practice](../PRODUCT_PRACTICE.md) for the full maintained section.

### HSK filters

Moved to [Product Practice](../PRODUCT_PRACTICE.md).

### Round generation (D02: approved)

Moved to [Product Practice](../PRODUCT_PRACTICE.md).

### Practice modes (D03: approved)

Moved to [Product Practice](../PRODUCT_PRACTICE.md).

### Random shortcut (D04: approved)

Moved to [Product Practice](../PRODUCT_PRACTICE.md).

### Practice URLs and replay (D13: approved)

Moved to [Product Practice](../PRODUCT_PRACTICE.md).

## A22 scope boundary - 2026-10-27

The answered UX requirements in [UX](../UX.md) guide later feature work. Mid-round
exclusion affordance deferred, not part of v1; retain D13/D15 URL/exclusion
lifecycle and setup Reset. A37 now adds secondary traditional text to hanzi-labeled exercise surfaces,
while primary simplified labels and replay comparison keys remain unchanged.

UX-SUM01 was deferred from A22 by explicit user instruction. A10 now applies its
summary/restart/timer requirements under D35; A09 applies matching's first-attempt
pair accounting, clarified under D39. Chart.js 4.6.1 is approved for the ring only,
with esbuild 0.28.2 for the local tree-shaken build and retained licenses.
A22 itself added no dependency or policy row. A37 records the initial route/
drawer motion profile; that separate A32 work does not block practice.

## A37 product reconciliation - 2026-10-28

Traditional display is secondary presentation on hanzi exercise labels; D12
comparison keys and replay bytes stay unchanged. Browse uses the five approved
fields and complete URL/range rules in UX. Home must retain the daily fallback/
Retry and navigation tiles during dictionary failure, implemented with A12.

The earlier product-gap list does not reopen these existing decisions:

- D04 Random selects among the three match variants and always starts Endless;
  adding MCQ to Random is not approved by this pass.
- D13/D15 keep loaded URL exclusions authoritative, saved/pending IDs for generated
  URLs, and explicit setup Reset. Counts reflect the deduplicated valid saved set;
  there is no per-card exclusion/reset control in v1 exercises.
- D15 keeps Fixed progress independent of pool wrapping and resets it on reload.
- D20 meaning-to-pinyin answers use display pinyin; no prompt-variety expansion.
- UX-MATCH02/MCQ01 already define practice progress/streak presentation.
- Theme stays dark by default with saved-choice precedence; automatic OS-theme
  selection is not part of the approved policy.
- Wrong attempts/answers follow the recorded UX. The user's later first-attempt
  metric was deferred from A37 and is now applied to MCQ by A10/D35; matching's
  implementation is now provided by A09, including both-pair disqualification
  on a wrong A/B attempt (D39).

The 150 ms fade-only motion profile is selected; A32 implementation remains
separate. No schema, URL replay format, scoring implementation or dependency
change is made by this documentation pass.

## Site sharing metadata (D34)

Before v1, A40 implements static Open Graph and Twitter/X large-image cards with
one 1200×630 image for every current hash route. Use the existing landscape with
a dark slate overlay, Zipeek wordmark and blue accent; no particular word, round
or score. Approved title: "Zipeek - Chinese hanzi practice". Approved description:
"Look up Chinese words and practise hanzi, pinyin, and meanings." Keep absolute
canonical/image URLs under /zipeek/. This design is approved, not an implemented
asset or a promise that social platforms have fetched it.

## A11 setup delivery

The A48 extension permits a nonempty selection of any of the six types. Start
chooses randomly; each Next chooses a random selected type excluding the previous
one when possible. Mixed matching/MCQ sessions share Fixed round/question counts,
stats and timing. Summary requirements accumulate four pairs per matching round
and one answer per MCQ. D39 disqualifies both pairs on a wrong A/B match attempt.
The optional types URL parameter carries canonical selected tokens, encoded once;
the current route still controls current-round replay. Unknown/duplicate types
are ignored; if the route type is absent from the valid set, use that type alone
without rewriting the loaded link. Single-type URLs remain unchanged. D40 records
the approved session metadata/selection/accounting contract, with no v1 RNG break.

Setup now selects all six variants and starts a new unseeded URL using the
approved HSK/mode/count and validated saved exclusions. Start uses offset zero;
Endless omits rounds, empty exclusions are omitted, and no seed/PoS is invented.
Reset clears storage/local exclusions and updates the next Start URL while
remaining on setup. This does not alter a loaded round. Setup defaults to the
first MCQ activity for the quiz-first priority. The Endless MCQ question loop
is now playable under A10; A11 delivered setup controls/navigation.


## Practice presentation refinement (A49 / D41)

Matching and MCQ use a centered, opaque practice board capped at 56rem inside
the full-width shell. Matching keeps two aligned columns on phones and desktop,
with audio contained in each card and readable settled matched states. Hanzi-to-
English matching and Hanzi-to-meaning MCQ add display pinyin beneath hanzi.
A52 makes matching rows compact with right-edge Listen; MCQ keeps Listen below
the pinyin. Representative desktop matching views fit without vertical scroll. This is presentation only; matching/replay keys are unchanged.

Requested follow-ups A50/A51 are documented in [UX](../UX.md#requested-navigation-and-exercise-help-follow-ups):
narrower icon-labelled drawer navigation and per-exercise info dialogs explaining
the activity. A49 records these requests without implementing those features.


## Recorded future directions (A53)

[Future practice, settings and AI enrichment](../FUTURE.md) owns the 2026-10-29
requests: remove matching success checkmarks; address visually ambiguous
readings such as jing/Jing; local generator-side AI category tags and filtering;
a Settings route with theme and click-to-speak audio preference; two independently toggleable experimental audio exercises (microphone
pronunciation and three-option listening) and AI-assisted sentence translation
using a useful subset of 20 sampled words. These are planned
features with explicit open questions, not implemented routes/schema/exercises
or a change to the existing v1 round contract. A54-A60 track implementation
review and prerequisites in TASKS.

A53 follow-up: sentence translation is experimental too. It is enabled in
Settings with a configured AI base URL, model and API token when the server
requires authentication. Local LM Studio is the first intended connection
target; Pages-to-local browser support is subject to CORS/permission validation.
See [connection requirements](../FUTURE.md#ai-connection-in-settings).

Practice setup also needs richer category and part-of-speech selection (D44 /
A61). Apply OR within each selected group and AND across category, PoS and the
existing HSK filter. Category data depends on A56; existing practice PoS query
support does not mean the setup picker already exists. See
[future filter requirements](../FUTURE.md#practice-setup-category-and-part-of-speech-filters).

## Proposed learning review workflow (R61 discovery; not yet approved as product policy)

A learner can save five HSK 6 verbs from Browse into a personal Word Set. The existing Word Set is a collection, not a mastery claim. A future My Vocabulary view should show collected words and their independent recognition, listening, recall, writing and usage evidence; saved words should remain visible even before any practice. A unified review queue may draw from multiple sets without duplicating learning history for the same word.

Each successful or failed exercise could generate one or more *attributed observations*, with the exercise definition declaring which skill it actually tests. Recognition via MCQ must not be treated as writing; translation from visible tiles must not be treated as unassisted recall. The exercise instance and session retain gameplay authority, while the evidence ledger records learner performance across sessions.

A proposed mastery policy would require repeat successful retrieval across different calendar days over a span of at least one to two weeks, rather than permitting mastery in a day. Exact day count, minimum interval, timezone semantics, treatment of assisted attempts, spaced-review scheduling and downgrade rules remain **open decisions**. R61 introduces only the unscored evidence domain type, without changing the browser's behaviour or persistence.

### R263 authored Practice exercise: Handwriting Recall

Handwriting Recall is selectable from Practice, uses an eight-character example corpus, and runs inside the resumable browser-local UUID session model. The learner sees meaning and pinyin but not Hanzi, draws strokes on the existing canvas, then reveals the target for self-comparison. Undo and Clear are available before reveal. No handwriting recognition, automatic grade or mastery credit is awarded. Ink is not persisted on refresh; the UUID session step is restored for another attempt. Selected vocabulary filters do not yet determine recall prompts.


## Proposed game roadmap - chronology and science (2026-11-12)

These are **future concepts**, not registered routes, authored lesson decks, or acquisition-grade evaluations. They require separate feature approval and implementation planning before becoming playable.

**Time Weaver (时光拼图)**: Playable randomized date, weekday and clock-time slice at `/games/time-weaver`. Configurable 10, 15 or 20 randomized rounds, balanced across five modes, cover assembling a Hanzi date from year/date tiles, choosing a Chinese date, identifying a weekday (星期), assembling a clock time from Hanzi tiles and choosing one of three plausible clock-time readings. Example dates include 21 April 2015 → 二零一五年四月二十一日; example times include 3:20 PM → 下午三点二十分. The pure Rust engine rejects invalid Gregorian dates and clock values, handles leap years/month boundaries, and generates unique valid dates and times from a session seed; browser-started sessions use fresh random seeds, and the same seed reproduces the same questions. It practices conventional Mandarin clock expressions including 一刻, 半, 三刻, 两点 and leading-zero minutes. The standalone setup provides accessible switch cards for Pinyin and speak-on-tap, a three-size segmented tile selector, a 10/15/20 prompt selector and a live tile preview. Choices persist as browser-local `zipeek.time_weaver.options.v1`; invalid records return to safe defaults (15 prompts, large tiles, Pinyin on, audio off). This local preference is not included in personal Word Sets backups. All rounds are game-only scoring, not acquisition evidence. Alternative synonymous expressions, actual microphone speech, free-form text typing, seasons, relative dates, scheduling, lunar-calendar questions, or spoken audio remain unimplemented pending explicit validation policy. No personal schedule data is used.

**Cosmic Lab** (working title): advanced Chinese-language scientific reasoning covering the Solar System, stars, cosmology, and related physics such as neutron stars and nuclear fission. Each authored question and **all three** choices are in Chinese; exactly one answer is scientifically valid under the stated assumptions, while two distractors are plausible but subtly incorrect. Explanations identify the misconception after submission; pre-answer hints must not leak the correct option. Content needs independently reviewed scientific sources, date/version provenance, difficulty and Chinese-language quality review, stable question IDs, deterministic option shuffling, explicit valid-answer validation, and separate science-knowledge vs. language-evidence attribution. AI may assist drafting but cannot publish or score unverified facts. Nuclear fission is nuclear physics, not a planetary topic, so the game is deliberately broader than astronomy.

**Gallery layout amendment:** On page one Province Quest spans a 2×2 four-slot featured card; on page two Sentence Relay now uses that same four-slot treatment. Gallery pagination remains capacity-nine, six game links on page one and five on page two after Time Weaver is introduced. This is presentation only; neither the Sentence Relay question engine nor the game roster has changed.

### R349 first-run setup and developer diagnostics (WIP)

On a first visit with no existing user preferences or work, the landing **Enter Zipeek** action opens a short setup form with one of the six existing themes and a separate, default-off choice to save completed Practice outcomes locally. Both the theme and `learning_history_enabled` consent are stored in `zipeek.preferences.v1`, the single preferences document also read at Practice completion and controlled under Settings → Learning Data → Practice learning history. The retired standalone recording-consent key is not read or migrated; previously opted-in users must opt in again. Saving the choice updates the shell recording indicator immediately and survives reloads. The setting permits local Practice outcome recording only; it does not enable mastery assessment, course unlocking, AI transmission, or the unfinished pedagogical evidence pipeline. Disabling it prevents subsequent outcome recording but does not erase previously saved records. Returning learners retain any consent already stored in `zipeek.preferences.v1`.

In development builds only, the Debug page has Overview, DuckDB and SQL tabs; the SQL tab includes a bounded SELECT terminal for the **read-only packaged dictionary**, an accessible table preview of up to 100 rows and a CSV export of exactly those displayed rows. No personal OPFS database is connected. A future personal-storage admin terminal would require an explicit ownership, permission, export, delete/backup and privacy design; the dictionary-only terminal must not be presented as such a tool.

## R483 Courses mosaic presentation

Grammar and Vocabulary have separate 100-region curricula and region IDs. Their rendering may share clipping and softly curved boundary utilities, but must not mix Grammar and Vocabulary cells. Grammar uses balanced independent regions; Vocabulary retains size cues from HSK word counts. The incomplete-region dim overlay may show the illustration for orientation, but is not completion or mastery evidence. No icons appear inside mosaic pieces. Visual and interaction acceptance is pending Chrome review.

## R485 Grammar curriculum development

As of R488, the 100 Grammar-only mosaic regions all have available teaching courses with **550 authored teaching entries**: the original five courses (24), fifteen courses from R485 (75), and eighty newly populated courses (451). The new lesson data has original pattern labels, short explanations, Chinese examples and English translations and has passed structural/duplicate audits. **This is draft teaching content pending independent Mandarin and HSK review**; a count of entries does not prove 550 distinct linguistic constructions or verified syllabus coverage. Expanded courses use single-question staged guided reviews and browser-local checkpoints, not scored independent mastery assessments. Neither viewing nor practising unlocks mosaic artwork; AI examples remain optional unverified supplementary material.

## November 17 approved next-stage behavior (pending implementation)

AI-requiring practice exercises are disabled when the required service is unavailable, with an actionable explanation. Pedagogical course tiles without proven progress remain visibly locked, with lesson details concealed in the tile. Per-pattern grammar visualization uses ten verified eligible sentence-exercise successes on each of seven qualifying days in a rolling fourteen-day window. New speech-to-text practice must support browser recognition and a configured local recognizer with separate capability/consent and scoring rules. These four decisions are recorded as D53-D56; current source is not evidence of implementation.

# Practice session builder - approved four-step navigation

Approved by the user on 2026-11-04 after discussion of the original Practice mockups.
This document supersedes the single long Practice setup layout in `PRACTICE_SETUP_HISTORY.md` where they disagree. It is the UX target, not evidence that every feature has shipped.

## Navigation model

One persistent top-level tab strip, in this order:

1. **Exercise Types** - select any number of available exercise definitions using a responsive grid. The library must scale beyond five: Drawing Hanzi, image-to-Hanzi, and future listening/writing exercises must not need a redesign. Use compact cards, a discoverable expanded library when needed, and disabled states for nonfunctional exercises. Exercise selection never changes the active tab, top-level or nested.
2. **Vocabulary** - exclusive Dictionary/HSK or personal Word Set source shared across the session. For Dictionary, choose **HSK 2.0 / HSK 3.0 / Mixed** first, then show only the corresponding levels. Preserve explicit multiple level selection in Mixed mode; do not conflate HSK 2.0 and 3.0. Show category autocomplete/removable chips, optional PoS and accurate source/exclusion/variant-aware vocabulary preflight. Switching sources must never silently combine filters with a Word Set.
3. **Configure** - second-level tabs: **General** and tabs for selected exercises with configuration. Dynamic and horizontal-scrollable on narrow viewports, never wrap the page into a long set of forms. General covers session-wide options; per-exercise tabs own that exercise's options. Selecting/deselecting an exercise must not automatically switch nested tabs. If the selected nested tab disappears, return to General. Preserve the unsaved draft settings for a deselected exercise until the user explicitly saves/discards the profile.
4. **Summary** - authoritative review of chosen exercises, vocabulary source, exact selected HSK levels and categories, eligibility for each selected exercise, length, and any unsupported/unscored exercises. Show actual verified counts, not invented estimates. Start Session is enabled only after compatible planning, validation, publish/acknowledge/advance, and navigation are all integrated. Save Profile persists the validated complete draft only once its format/recovery policy exists. No fake action buttons.

Navigation is available by clicking top-level tabs and by Back/Continue controls; all steps share one draft and preserve values across visits. Hide unrelated configuration surfaces so ordinary sessions do not require excessive vertical scrolling. Use keyboard-accessible tab controls and visible focus states. Small screens stack or scroll content appropriately without clipping actions.

## Phased implementation

- **R100 first slice:** render the four top-level tabs, isolate existing exercise selection and source picker, put existing conditional settings under Configure and truthful separate launch actions in Summary. Remove implicit settings-tab changes when clicking exercise cards. Add HSK 2.0/3.0/Mixed version-first level grouping; selecting one standard drops the other standard's selected levels and defaults to its level 1 when empty. Retain existing launch/replay contracts. No schema or dependencies changed.
- **R101:** Configure now renders General plus selected Matching, Multiple Choice, Translation and Speaking tabs in a horizontally scrollable row. Matching and MCQ display only their respective selectable question variants; General retains the existing mode, round-count and exclusion settings. Translation retains its existing sentence-count setting and separate launch; Speaking remains an unscored preview. Deselection of the active exercise falls back to General without clearing other draft settings. Shared session scheduling, per-exercise independent format persistence, and full browser accessibility validation remain open.
- **Next:** complete the per-exercise configuration models and summary eligibility messaging. Improve keyboard focus management and verify responsive height/scroll behaviour.
- **Following:** connect R99 planner to authoritative result ledger, safe acknowledgement and cross-route navigation, then activate a single Start Session; implement saved profiles only with explicit recovery policy. Do not claim these are shipped before tests.

## Exercise expansion

Drawing Hanzi requires stroke datasets and handwriting assessment; image recognition requires source/licensing and sense-level image mappings. Neither is enabled merely by adding an exercise card. Do not introduce unverified scoring or image provenance claims.

### R102 implementation note - selected family readiness

Enabling Matching or Multiple Choice must initialize that family's question-format selection if empty, without replacing the other family's choices. Deselecting and reselecting an exercise retains its configuration. Summary must expose each selected family's actual formats and warn if a selected family has none. The combined legacy Matching/MCQ launch requires every selected family to have at least one configured format; another family's format is not a substitute. This is not yet a single unified multi-exercise session.

### R103 implementation note - authoritative exercise options

The typed `PracticeDraft` now owns Matching and Multiple Choice format selections separately, plus the Sentence Translation count (5, 10, or 0 for Endless). The selected formats used by Summary, playable-pool preflight, and the legacy Matching/MCQ launch are derived from the draft, not a second configuration reducer. Selections persist through deselection and re-selection of an exercise; a selected family with no formats fails validation, while an unselected family's retained formats do not launch. Translation count is read from the draft for both Summary and Translation route parameters. The setup reducer no longer stores exercise-format selections.

**Not yet consolidated:** shared Fixed/Endless Matching/MCQ session mode and round count, which remain in the setup reducer; the draft's existing `length` field is not yet the launch authority. Translation direction and word-bank options are typed in the draft but not exposed as functional controls in the current Translate route. Keep these differences visible until they are reconciled and validated in Windows. Saved profiles and the unified Start Session remain gated on a complete authoritative model and planner/ledger integration.

## R103 - Practice exercise settings owned by draft (Windows verification pending)

- `PracticeDraft` now owns Matching and MCQ question-format selections independently and the Translation count (5/10/Endless). Its validation rejects selected families without formats, cross-family format contamination and unsupported Translation counts.
- Configure, Summary, pool preflight, Matching/MCQ launch query, and Translation route parameters read these settings from the same draft. The setup reducer no longer stores exercise formats; legacy session mode/round count and HSK level still live there pending a subsequent consolidation. Existing legacy URL/replay encoding and round builders are unchanged.

# Practice setup - historical design

**Update (2026-11-04):** The newly approved top-level four-step session builder and nested Configure tabs are documented in [PRACTICE_SESSION_BUILDER.md](../../learning-practice/practice/practice-session-builder.md). Follow that document if this historical one-page layout conflicts.

Approved direction: 2026-11-04. The reference is the user's two dark-theme
Practice/Dictionary mockups; the mocks illustrate hierarchy, not a promise that
all depicted options already work. This document is the product contract for
the next stages of implementation. R79 implements the Browse-facing first slice and chosen-Word-Set handoff.
R80 implements a pure, typed draft and validation model in `zipeek-exercises`.
R81 introduces the first exercise-first selector and definition-derived settings tabs using that draft.
R82 uses a single, shared source selector on the Practice page: Dictionary/HSK
(single selected band) or a saved personal Word Set. Both the Matching/MCQ and
Translation launch paths consume it; there are no independent vocabulary inputs
in their settings panels. R85 adds multi-HSK and database-suggested category chips to the shared selector and routes custom filters to Translation through a validated URL source; Matching/MCQ still deliberately requires a single HSK band and no other dictionary filters. The unified mixed-session planner, complete combobox keyboard support, and pool-size validation are not yet connected.

## Product mental model

1. **Browse** searches and curates dictionary words. A row can be listened to
   using Chinese speech synthesis and saved into a personal Word Set. It does
   not launch a one-word quiz.
2. **Practice setup** chooses one or more exercise definitions, a vocabulary
   source, relevant exercise-specific options, and session length. The
   configuration is validated before starting.
3. **Session** owns the selected configuration and one shared result ledger;
   exercise UIs own only their interaction state. Abandoned questions are
   terminal without scoring.
4. **Profiles** save configuration for later reuse, not current results,
   microphone recordings, or generated AI answers.

## Screen: Practice setup

The first interaction is **Choose exercise types**. Use accessible multi-select
exercise cards (keyboard toggle, visible selection, and descriptive support
text) for Matching, Multiple Choice, Sentence Translation, Speaking, and
Listening. Speaking is a selectable exercise, **not** a separate top-level
practice route. Recording without validated assessment is permitted only as an
explicitly labelled preview and contributes no proficiency evidence.

Additional configuration surfaces unlock from selected exercise definitions,
not a fixed catch-all set of page tabs:

- **Vocabulary source** appears for any vocabulary-dependent exercise.
- **Session options** (Fixed/Endless, number of finalized questions) appear
  for every quiz type that supports them.
- **Translation options** appear only when Sentence Translation is selected:
  direction, word-bank assistance, and permitted generation backend.
- **Speaking options** appear only when Speaking is selected: reading prompt,
  waveform preference, and a local-only recording disclosure.
- **Listening options** appear only once an actual listening exercise is
  implemented and selected; don't advertise nonfunctional scoring.
- **Profiles** offer Load, Save as, Rename, Delete and explicit overwrite.

The tab strip is conditional: General is always available; specialized tabs
appear only for selected exercise types. Removing a type removes its tab but
must not silently delete saved profile data until explicitly saved. If the
active tab becomes unavailable, focus/selection returns to General. A top
stepper communicates Exercise types → Vocabulary → Options → Review/Start;
only currently available stages are actionable. On mobile the stepper is a
compact progress label, not a horizontal overflow rail.

## Vocabulary source is an exclusive choice

**Personal Word Set:** choose one named, nonempty saved set; use an exact
snapshot of its Word IDs. HSK, category and PoS filters are hidden/disabled
and **never** intersected with that set. Show name, word count and an explicit
empty-set error. A chosen set from Browse can prepopulate this selector.

**Dictionary vocabulary:** use HSK **systems and levels** (multiple selection),
category autocomplete with removable chips, and optional advanced PoS chips.
Never conflate HSK 2.0 and HSK 3.0 levels. Within each filter group selections
are OR; across groups HSK/categories/PoS are AND, consistent with D44. A user
can select multiple categories from suggestions searched as they type. Every
chip has a labelled Remove action, Backspace works when the input is empty,
keyboard arrows navigate suggestions, Enter accepts, Escape closes, and
screen readers receive an announcement of selected count. The control must
support search even with no available categories and never fabricate tags.
Display the estimated eligible word count and reject empty pools before Start.

The initial HSK/category query must be backed by installed database values,
not generated by the model. An AI model may generate a sentence *using* the
selected vocabulary, but cannot choose an unrelated hidden vocabulary pool.
Sense-specific readings and translations must be preserved during sampling.

## Profiles and persistence

Profiles are optional, device-local **versioned configuration snapshots**.
They contain selected exercise definition IDs and versions, vocabulary-source
selector/filters or saved Word Set reference, per-exercise options, session
mode/length, and a human-readable profile name. No scores, hidden answers,
recorded audio, model credentials or generated content. Do not change the
existing Word Set persistence key. Profile storage requires a separate
approved and tested schema; R79 does not introduce it.

Loading a profile atomically replaces the draft setup after validation.
Deleted/missing Word Set, unsupported exercise version, or no supported
exercises blocks Start with a specific recovery message; **never** silently
switch to unrestricted HSK vocabulary. Saving a profile does not start a
session. Start always begins a fresh session with a frozen configuration.

## Launch and acceptance rules

- No session-wide score UI before a meaningful exercise result exists.
- One Start action from setup; AI endpoint/model requirements must be clear
  before an AI-dependent session starts. A missing model never starts an empty
  session that then fails on its first question.
- Fixed count measures **finalized exercises**; an abandoned question does
  not consume a slot or contribute proficiency evidence. Completion shows
  authoritative totals; a sixth question cannot appear in Fixed/5.
- Source/exercise changes during setup don't mutate an existing active
  session. A new Start creates a new session generation.
- Visible exercise payloads and AI learner observations never include hidden
  reference answers. Session scoring remains authoritative in the domain.

## Implementation order

1. R79: compact Browse, row pronunciation, explicit selected-set handoff,
   five-row pagination, remove ambiguous dictionary quiz actions.
2. R80: extract pure typed `PracticeDraft` and source filters; domain tests for
   OR/AND semantics, empty selectors and unsupported assessments. This is
   a validation contract, not a claim that the browser queries support all
   these filters or that dictionary pool sizes are checked yet.
3. R81: Exercise-first multi-select cards with accessible pressed states,
   conditional configuration tabs, and retained existing launch routes.
   The category multi-combobox and shared source/launch controller remain
   follow-up work, not features attributed to R81.
4. Session-aware Start and per-exercise configuration; then versioned local
   profiles with explicit import/export policy.
5. Thirtyfour cross-route acceptance including profile reload and Fixed/5
   HSK6 translation, and responsive accessibility/visual review.

Keep all phases within existing crates. Do not add dependencies, change the
DB schema or change AI classification prompts/cache keys to support this UI.

## R80 typed draft boundary

`zipeek-exercises::practice_draft` now owns a `PracticeDraft` with a set of
registered exercise definition IDs, an exclusive `VocabularySource`, a
`SessionLength`, and translation-specific options. The selected IDs refer to
existing `definition::DEFINITIONS`, not to a parallel central exercise-kind enum.
`configuration_tabs()` derives the optional tab IDs from selected definitions.
`validate_for_scored_session()` distinguishes the current unscored Speaking
preview and not-yet-implemented Listening from scored practice.

`DictionaryFilters::matches()` defines OR within HSK/category/PoS groups
and AND across populated groups, with HSK 2.0 and 3.0 treated as distinct
keys. Category chip insertion removes surrounding whitespace, normalizes to
lowercase, deduplicates and supports removal. The model does not itself
perform a DuckDB query, validate a saved set's contents, resolve category
suggestions, or start a browser session. Those integrations require separate
source adapters, database-backed validation, and explicit UI tests.

Until the exercise-first UI is migrated, existing Practice tabs and route
query semantics remain unchanged. Do not treat the new draft as already
being used by the current Start buttons.

## R81 selector boundary and rollout

`PracticeBuilder` is a Yew presentation component that receives an actual
`PracticeDraft`, invokes domain-validated exercise toggles, and renders
`configuration_tabs()` directly. General is always available, while the
Translation and Speaking settings appear only when those definitions are
selected. Listening is displayed disabled because no playable listening-choice
exercise is implemented. Speaking remains explicitly unscored.

The existing Matching/MCQ variant picker is still responsible for question
formats and the existing routing, and the Translation panel still supports
the established one-HSK-level, saved-set or sample-topic source contract.
Selecting multiple exercise definitions **does not** yet launch a mixed
cross-route session. The UI says this explicitly, and the two launch controls
are labelled for the exercise they actually start. Do not build profiles on
these intermediate route-specific source controls; finish the shared source
and launch controller first.

The Dictionary → Practice handoff uses `saved:<index>` in the URL; the
Matching/MCQ adapter converts this to its established numeric selector,
while Translation keeps its `saved:<index>` source encoding. Empty or deleted
sets are rejected, not silently replaced with unrestricted vocabulary.

## R82 implementation boundary and next work

The source switch is one-of-two, not an intersection. In Word Set mode the
selected set is handed to Matching/MCQ as the exact ID snapshot and to
Translation as `saved:<index>`. In HSK mode one band is passed using the
existing canonical route/query representations. The shared selector is the
only source control; the per-exercise panels retain their own session-length
options until the shared session planner is completed.

The `PracticeDraft` domain already models OR within HSK/category/PoS groups
and AND between groups. To expose those selections safely, extend the
database-backed candidate-pool contract for **both** Matching/MCQ and
Translation first; then add a category autocomplete sourcing valid slugs
from the installed database. Until then, the UI intentionally offers one HSK
band, not decorative chips that are silently ignored on launch.

## R83 parameterized filter adapter

`web/services/database/practice_filter_queries.rs` now provides a bounded,
parameterized read-only dictionary query for the approved filter semantics:
HSK bands match by (system, level) with OR across selections; category and
part-of-speech membership use OR within their own groups; groups intersect.
The category autocomplete data source queries distinct `sense_categories`
slugs, returning at most 24 ordered suggestions for a typed prefix.

This is a **query foundation, not the live practice source picker**. The
current UI still chooses one HSK band. Before displaying additional selected
bands or category chips, both the Matching/MCQ and Translation launch adapters
must consume this same filter contract, handle an insufficient pool explicitly,
and verify that no selected filter is silently ignored. The bounded query's
ordered first rows are not an unbiased sample; subsequent adapter work must
choose a suitable seeded sampling strategy without changing v1 replay
semantics. No profile storage is added here.

## R195 exercise activation amendment

The earlier disabled-listening wording in this document describes pre-R195
behavior. Listening and Picture vocabulary are now selectable from Advanced
Practice, but each opens a standalone exercise page. Their source selection
is currently performed on the destination page using saved Word Sets. The
regular scored-session planner still rejects these IDs until mixed-session
scheduling, feedback, and persistence are explicitly implemented.

## R268 generated exercise Start gate

AI-dependent fixed UUID sessions now require a configured AI model before Start is enabled, as required by the launch contract above. The generated question and image URL are saved as bounded, validated browser-local session content. Sentence translation and picture recognition currently use practice-only feedback, not authoritative mastery scores. Live AI and image-server availability remain runtime dependencies; errors are surfaced with bounded Retry or Skip. Full browser acceptance remains outstanding.

# R184 - Source archival, web database distribution and Settings

## Included in this release

- `crates/zipeek-cli`: native Rust ZIP pack/unpack using the existing `zip 9.4.0` lockfile dependency. Tracks repository source, omits compiled/generated artifacts and symlinks, rejects traversal entries on extraction, stages extraction, backs up replaced source trees and overlays the remainder. Managed directories (including `crates/*/src`, `docs`, `scripts`, `crates/web/static`) are replaced so deleted source files do not linger.
- `cargo make pack` / `cargo make unpack`: default artifact `target/zipeek-source.zip`. Explicit paths supported through the CLI directly. Archives are **not signed**, so only unpack files from trusted sources.
- `cargo make db-compress`: Gzip-compresses the latest verified candidate to `hanzi-*.duckdb.gz`, records size/SHA-256, revalidates the complete bundle; never installs. `db-full` includes compression before installation. The installer renames raw and compressed artifacts in sync when timestamping.
- Compressed installed database shipped alongside raw DuckDB for development. With `23,080,960` uncompressed bytes the Gzip asset is `5,350,281` bytes (76.82% smaller), checked for exact decompression and SHA-256.
- Browser bridge prefers Gzip, checks the compressed hash and size, decompresses through native `DecompressionStream`, verifies original size and hash, then registers the raw bytes with DuckDB-WASM. An early manifest-aware `<link rel="preload" as="fetch" crossorigin>` hints the exact asset; measure browser network results because cache behavior varies.
- Complete version-policy update to `@duckdb/duckdb-wasm@1.33.1-dev114.0` in web JS preparation, database generator policy, bundle publisher, tests and installed bundle metadata.
- Independent Settings Image Generation panel with persistent API URL, reset and health probe. Native image-server CORS permits the two Trunk development origins, not arbitrary internet origins.
- Five focused web feature refactors: Settings image-server panel, Practice Setup route preselection, Cloud Match vocabulary-pool loader, Word Spotlight data loader, Practice Session round diagnostics.

## Manual commands

```powershell
cargo check -p zipeek-cli --locked
cargo run -p zipeek-cli --locked -- pack
cargo run -p zipeek-cli --locked -- unpack
cargo make db-generate
cargo make db-classify
cargo make db-compress
cargo make db-install
cargo check -p zipeek --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --locked
cargo check -p zipeek-image-server --locked
cargo make serve
```

**Unpack warning:** the unpack command intentionally replaces source-owned directories and overlays repository files. Keep a clean commit or external backup before using it; a timestamped backup is created under `.unpack-backups/`.

## Validation gates

- Node regression suite and new gzip tests must pass.
- Native Rust compile, WASM compile, Trunk browser startup and image-server CORS must be verified on Windows. Do not treat static Node contracts as substitutes for Cargo checks.
- Check that DuckDB-WASM `1.33.1-dev114.0` actually opens the installed native-v2.0.0 database, and inspect Network for duplicate preload transfers.
- Physical DuckDB rebuilding/compaction (`COPY FROM DATABASE`) is a separate optional follow-up, requiring comparisons of schemas, indices and query results. `VACUUM` alone does not guarantee file shrinkage.
- Image exercises, their scheduling and image approval workflow are not included in R184.
title: R184 - Source archival, web database distribution and Settings

# Generated asset integrity and deployment preflight

## Source checkout versus deployable build

A complete source checkout does not necessarily include the generated dictionary binary, compressed dictionary, Province Quest geography, or pedagogy Worker bindings. A source ZIP passing integrity checks is not evidence that these assets are present or that the website is deployable.

Use `cargo make asset-integrity-source` to check the files actually present in a source checkout. It reads `static/hanzi.manifest.json`, validates included manifest-declared files using their recorded sizes and SHA-256 hashes, validates the dictionary preload path in `index.html`, and checks representative Courses and Practice artwork. Missing generated dictionary, Worker, and geography artifacts are reported as **notices** in source mode. Missing manifest-declared source metadata, such as attribution or licensing files, is an error.

Use `cargo make asset-integrity-deploy` before publishing. Deploy mode treats missing generated dictionary, Worker, and Province Quest geography artifacts as **errors**. A manifest-declared artifact that is present but has changed size or hash is an error in both modes. A partial Worker output is always an error. The audit never generates, installs, deletes, or repairs assets and never changes dependency versions.

`cargo make preflight-source` and `cargo make preflight-deploy` also invoke the corresponding Node checks before the existing Rust preflight. The Rust source preflight permits an entirely absent generated Worker, but deploy preflight requires a complete Worker with a compatible bootstrap.

Run offline regression tests with `cargo make asset-integrity-tests`. For direct execution without Rust: `node scripts/asset-integrity-audit.cjs --source` and `node --test scripts/tests/asset-integrity-audit.test.cjs`.

## Limits and acceptance

The audit validates recorded file hashes and basic headers, not DuckDB table contents, complete WebP/PNG decoding, grammar correctness, or actual browser asset loading. The existing Rust preflight verifies Docs index consistency and additional media properties. A successful deploy preflight does not replace a locked WASM build, the `/zipeek/` navigation check, or real Chrome acceptance. Never mark technical-debt acceptance closed based solely on either preflight.

The current source archive omits generated dictionary binaries, Worker output, and geography files. Source-mode notices reflect that known distinction; deploy mode is expected to fail until the approved generation and installation steps are completed.

The uncompressed `.duckdb` file in the generator manifest is a build input and may be absent from the deployed static directory when the compressed `.duckdb.gz` artifact is present and validated. The deploy gate requires the compressed artifact, not an unnecessary duplicate uncompressed database.
title: Generated asset integrity and deployment preflight

# CI and deployment

Local commands and prerequisites live in [testing/TESTING.md](../testing-quality/acceptance/testing.md).
A16 implements the workflow migration on 2026-10-28. Configuration and local
validation are recorded here; GitHub-hosted execution is not claimed by a local run.

A10 adds exact chart.js 4.6.1 and dev-only esbuild 0.28.2 under D35.
CI runs locked npm installation, then `cargo run -p zipeek-cli --locked -- web prepare`
to prepare DuckDB/Arrow and the tree-shaken summary bundle with licenses.
Trunk never regenerates these files on each Yew rebuild. Both root/Pages
Chrome builds and the standalone Pages gate consume prepared vendor files.

## Entry points and validation

.github/workflows/ci.yml handles pushes to master, pull requests and manual runs.
Its Windows validate job selects Rust 1.97.1 with rustfmt, Clippy and the wasm32
target, Node 22 and the existing Trunk installation action. It verifies installed
Chrome, prints tool versions and installs web assets from crates/zipeek-web/ using
npm ci --ignore-scripts, then runs explicit Rust CLI vendor preparation before any Trunk build or browser test.

The current `.github/workflows/ci.yml` does **not** run the retired Node source-contract suites. Its Windows validation job installs locked npm browser assets, prepares vendor assets through the Rust CLI, runs Rust formatting, Clippy and locked workspace tests, checks the AI client and web WASM targets, builds documentation and builds the `/zipeek/` Trunk bundle. Rust/Chrome E2E coverage is exercised by configured Rust test targets; successful source inspection is not a substitute for execution. D36 permits focused local validation for routine work; it does not change the current workflow:

```powershell
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p zipeek-web --locked
```

```powershell
# From crates/zipeek-web/
trunk build --public-url /zipeek/
```

Workspace tests include the owned root and Pages Chrome suites. Each harness
build uses its own directory and dynamic server ports. Trunk must serve HTTP
200 before Chrome starts; a regression fixture covers initial 404 responses.
No external server or
separate ChromeDriver setup is used. Thirtyfour manages its matching driver.
The GitHub Windows image supplies installed Chrome; the prerequisite check fails
explicitly if it is absent. See the official
[runner image inventory](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/blob/main/images/windows/Windows2025-Readme.md).
Network/cache access is needed for managed driver and pinned native neo prebuilt
library downloads, in addition to Rust/npm/Trunk tool setup. The neo revision's
own .duckdb-release selects native v2.0.0; do not substitute a runner DuckDB.
Existing native tests enforce that engine and v2.0.0 storage compatibility.

## Validation-gated Pages

Only a non-PR master run with successful validate calls the local reusable
.github/workflows/deploy.yml. Other-branch manual runs validate without deploying.
Manual deployment starts from the CI workflow on master. deploy.yml has only a
workflow_call trigger, preventing an independent push/manual path from bypassing
validation or testing a different commit. Local reusable calls use the caller's
checkout context; see [GitHub reusable workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/reuse-automations/reuse-workflows).

The reusable Ubuntu build installs Rust 1.97.1/wasm32, matching wasm-bindgen-cli
0.2.130, the existing Trunk selection and Node 22. It installs locked npm assets
from crates/zipeek-web/, then runs:

```sh
trunk build --release --public-url /zipeek/
```

That command runs from crates/zipeek-web/. Trunk handles the pinned Tailwind tool and copies already prepared
DuckDB and summary assets; no vendor preparation hook or DB generation runs. actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3 uploads crates/zipeek-crates/zipeek-web/dist/.
The dependent deploy job uses actions/deploy-pages@v4 and the github-pages
environment, publishing its page_url output. Existing repository Pages publishing
must be configured for GitHub Actions; this change does not modify remote settings.
A separate configure-pages step is unnecessary for the explicitly configured
Trunk public URL and existing Pages site. Deployment permissions, environment and
build dependency follow [GitHub's custom workflow requirements](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/using-custom-workflows-with-github-pages).

PR validation has contents: read only. The caller Pages job grants contents: read,
pages: write and id-token: write to the reusable call; its deployment job requests
only Pages/OIDC writes. A PR cannot enter that job. Validate has a 45-minute bound,
release build 30 minutes and deploy 10 minutes. Superseded PR validation can cancel;
master validation and an active Pages deployment are not cancelled by a newer run.
The Pages concurrency group serializes active deployments using GitHub's normal
pending-run handling.

## Caches and tool selections

Cargo caches registry/Git sources and target/, keyed by OS, Rust 1.97.1, the
root Cargo.lock, workspace manifests, rust-toolchain.toml, crates/zipeek-web/Trunk.toml and web
package lock. Pages release uses a separate key. Cargo executables are not cached:
restoring old binaries must not replace selected tools. setup-node caches npm's
package cache using crates/zipeek-web/package-lock.json; node_modules and vendor outputs are installed/prepared explicitly before Trunk;
dist output is rebuilt by Trunk.

Existing action versions are retained: checkout v6, CI cache v5, Pages cache v4,
setup-node v4, trunk-action v0.5.0, upload-pages-artifact v3 and deploy-pages v4.
No new package, Cargo feature or action version is introduced. Rust is corrected
to the already-approved 1.97.1. Trunk remains latest as in the previous deployment
workflow: no exact version is approved by A16, and this remains an explicit
reproducibility limitation. Local evidence uses installed Trunk 0.22.0.

## Tooling advisory review

The preserved lockfile contains picomatch 2.3.1 through micromatch. The original
A06 audit and the A16 locked npm install report one high-severity dependency.
The reviewed upstream advisories cover
[extglob ReDoS](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c2c7-rcm5-vvqj) and
[POSIX character-class method injection](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3v7f-55p6-f55p),
with 2.3.2 as the patched 2.x release. These concern processing attacker-controlled
glob patterns; here the dependency belongs to build tooling, not browser search
input. PR source is already executable build input. Under [D33](../project-management/decisions/process-and-infra.md#d33-accept-build-tool-picomatch-advisories),
the user accepts both advisories under that build-tool-only input condition.
Do not add an override, run npm audit fix or refresh the lockfile for them.
Reassess if untrusted application patterns reach this dependency. Acceptance is
not remediation; audit output may persist. An independently approved future
Trunk/Tailwind upgrade may bring a fixed version naturally. A39 is retired.

## Validation limits

Local checks cover YAML structure, triggers/permissions/needs, cache/input paths,
gate commands, all five actual code gates and the release artifact contents.
Root/Pages Chrome run locally. The Actions service, fresh hosted Windows/Ubuntu
images, remote permissions/environment approval and actual Pages publication
cannot be exercised by this workspace. No push, dispatch, remote setting change
or deployment was performed. Confirm the first hosted run after these changes
are committed/pushed; do not describe local success as a hosted deployment.

## Release ZIP installation

For numbered hand-off ZIPs accepted by the legacy PowerShell `unpack.ps1`,
use `zipeek-R<number>-<description>-YYYYMMDD.zip`. The native Rust CLI
uses `target/zipeek-source-<version>-<UTC-timestamp>.zip` for pack snapshots. See
[RELEASE_NAMING.md](release-naming.md) for the distinction and checks.


The supported `unpack.ps1` mirrors `crates/*/src`, `docs`, and `scripts` as **managed directories**. Each old directory is moved into `.unpack-backups` before the new release copy is installed; this removes retired source, release-note, and script files. It preserves `.git`, target caches, and local configuration outside these managed directories. Installing this release using an older unpacker that only mirrors `src` will **leave old docs/scripts behind**. Replace your local unpacker with the version included in the historical source once. The installer itself is excluded from installation to avoid overwriting the running script.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/build-deployment-ci.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.

```text
zipeek-R<number>-WIP-<description>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.zip
```

A WIP checkpoint is not an accepted major release. Use a real UTC packaging timestamp, a positive decimal release number and a lowercase hyphen-separated description. Check the latest established release before incrementing the number.

The filename patterns above are illustrative; obtain the actual sequence and timestamp from the release process.

`cargo make unpack` searches Downloads for the highest numbered native release or checkpoint. When both a completed release and a WIP checkpoint have the same number, the completed release has priority. An explicit archive path avoids relying on Downloads selection:

```powershell
cargo run -p zipeek-cli --locked -- unpack C:\path\to\archive.zip
```

Before delivering an archive, validate that its filename is recognized by the actual parser in `crates/zipeek-cli/src/command.rs`. Check the ZIP structure for `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `AGENTS.md`, the `crates/`, `docs/` and `scripts/` trees at the ZIP root, with no wrapper directory. The CLI also validates required source files before modifying the checkout. Preserve local edits and backups before unpacking.

The legacy `unpack.ps1` expects an older date-only naming format. The current time-stamped handoff contract is authoritative for `cargo make unpack`; do not assume legacy PowerShell acceptance. Do not silently rename an old archive to a higher release number.

## Native source snapshots

`cargo make pack` produces a different archive under `target/`:

```text
zipeek-source-<workspace-version>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.zip
```

A source snapshot does not use the numbered handoff naming convention. To restore it, supply the path explicitly to the CLI. Review excluded generated assets and source completeness before using any archive as a release handoff.

## Numbered major-release acceptance

The following **major-release-only** gate does not apply to routine tasks, WIP checkpoints, documentation-only changes or native `cargo make pack` snapshots. A numbered major release requires purposeful improvements to at least **20 distinct `.rs` paths**, compared against the agreed baseline. Count each qualifying path once from the final diff; generated code, placeholders, wrappers without meaningful behavior, renames, formatting-only edits, comments and non-Rust files do not qualify.

Do not inflate the count by splitting modules, adding hypothetical features or modifying unrelated code without approval. If the planned work reaches fewer than 20 qualified files, report the shortfall and propose additional valuable changes with risks, validation and expected affected paths **before** expanding scope. If not approved, retain an incomplete or unverified candidate rather than calling the major release accepted.

Before delivering an accepted numbered major release, provide a file-by-file qualifying Rust inventory, separate non-Rust/filtered counts, the actual final diff baseline, applicable test commands and results, unresolved verification, known failures, data-loss implications and archive layout validation. With unavailable build/browser tooling label the output **unverified release candidate**, not a tested release.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/build-deployment-release-naming.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.
title: Release archive naming and installation

# Image service scaffold

The standalone native crate `crates/zipeek-image-server` is **not used by the Yew frontend yet**. It runs an Axum server bound to `127.0.0.1:1431` and uses a deterministic **SVG placeholder** backend, not Candle or a diffusion model. A trait in `src/inference` is the future inference integration point. Generated placeholders are **not valid image questions** and must not be used as learner-facing assessment content.

## Build and launch

On first install, run `cargo check -p zipeek-image-server` **without** `--locked` to update Cargo.lock for the new dependencies. Commit the generated lockfile, then use `--locked` in CI. This release could not regenerate Cargo.lock because no Rust toolchain is available in its packaging environment. Do not run `cargo generate-lockfile` blindly if preserving existing pinned dependency resolutions matters.

```powershell
cargo check -p zipeek-image-server
cargo test -p zipeek-image-server
cargo make image-server
```

### API

- `GET http://127.0.0.1:1431/health` returns the backend identifier.
- `POST /v1/images` with `{ "prompt": "red apple on a table", "width": 512, "height": 512 }` returns HTTP 202 and an in-memory job ID.
- `GET /v1/jobs/{uuid}` returns `queued`, `running`, `completed` or `failed`, and `image_url` on completion.
- `GET /v1/images/{uuid}` serves the persisted SVG.

Job statuses are process-local; image bytes and their metadata survive restart in `target/zipeek-images`. A restart does not restore old job statuses. Queue admission is capped at four pending/running tasks, with one active generator. IDs are parsed as UUIDs; request bodies, dimensions and prompt length are bounded. There is no public-bind or authentication support, and no configured cross-origin access.

This is an architecture scaffold. Production work must add a real inference implementation, GPU feature-gating, output image validation, review/approval, durable queue state, retention/cleanup, authentication if remote exposure is needed, and image-exercise planning and scoring in `zipeek-exercises`.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/build-deployment-services-image-server.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.
title: Image service scaffold

# Local SDXL Base inference

The `zipeek-image-server` is a native, loopback-only Axum service.
The default backend remains the deterministic SVG placeholder. Select `sdxl`
explicitly to generate actual PNG images using Candle 0.11.1 and CUDA.

## Local model assets

The SDXL backend reads files **only** from disk, with no automatic downloads.
Default root: `<Cargo workspace>/models/sdxl` (resolved from the image-server crate manifest, independent of the launch directory). Set `ZIPEEK_IMAGE_MODEL_DIR` to override.

```text
sdxl/
  base/
    unet/diffusion_pytorch_model.fp16.safetensors
    text_encoder/model.fp16.safetensors
    text_encoder_2/model.fp16.safetensors
  vae/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors
  clip/tokenizer.json
  clip2/tokenizer.json
```

The VAE file is from `madebyollin/sdxl-vae-fp16-fix`; the tokenizers are
from `openai/clip-vit-large-patch14` and
`laion/CLIP-ViT-bigG-14-laion2B-39B-b160k`. These match Candle's SDXL
Stable Diffusion example. Download and review model licences separately.

Direct file sources (download only any files you do not have):
- SDXL FP16 base weights: https://huggingface.co/stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0/tree/main
  (`unet/diffusion_pytorch_model.fp16.safetensors`, `text_encoder/model.fp16.safetensors`,
  `text_encoder_2/model.fp16.safetensors`). The unqualified UNet file without `.fp16.`
  is **not** the expected FP16 file and is much larger.
- VAE: https://huggingface.co/madebyollin/sdxl-vae-fp16-fix/blob/main/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors
- CLIP 1 tokenizer: https://huggingface.co/openai/clip-vit-large-patch14/blob/main/tokenizer.json
- CLIP 2 tokenizer: https://huggingface.co/laion/CLIP-ViT-bigG-14-laion2B-39B-b160k/blob/main/tokenizer.json

The first two encoder weights already on disk can be reused; only download missing
files. The image server validates its six required files at startup and reports a
structured `SdxlSetupError` when any is missing, empty, or not a regular file.

**Prompt length:** The Rust backend accepts up to 300 content tokens
per tokenizer. Each CLIP encoder processes repeated windows of up to 75 content
tokens plus its two special tokens, preserving the model's 77-position context.
All encoded windows are concatenated along the sequence dimension and passed to
the U-Net, with the two SDXL encoders and unconditional guidance aligned to the
same window count. This avoids the old silent 77-token truncation and needs no
new weights. A prompt beyond 300 content tokens fails explicitly.

Long prompts are a conditioning technique rather than equivalent to a model
trained with a longer attention context. Semantics may weaken across chunks and
VRAM/latency increase with prompt length. The live CUDA smoke test remains
opt-in; no runtime inference or image-quality acceptance has been completed in
this packaging environment.

```powershell
cargo test --locked -p zipeek-image-server clip_chunks_preserve_all_250_content_tokens
cargo test --locked -p zipeek-image-server sdxl_generates_png_from_250_token_prompt -- --ignored --nocapture
```

## Run on Windows PowerShell

The PNG encoder uses `flate2` and `crc32fast`, both already present in
the uploaded workspace lockfile. updates the image-server lockfile entry
to include them and `tokenizers`. Validate the pinned dependency graph:

```powershell
cargo check -p zipeek-image-server
cargo test -p zipeek-image-server
cargo make image-server-sdxl
```

For a custom model directory or step count:

```powershell
$env:ZIPEEK_IMAGE_MODEL_DIR = "C:\zipeek-models\sdxl"
$env:ZIPEEK_IMAGE_STEPS = "20"
cargo make image-server-sdxl
```

Send a request from another terminal:

```powershell
$job = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post `
  -Uri http://127.0.0.1:1431/v1/images `
  -ContentType application/json `
  -Body '{"prompt":"A red apple on a plain wooden table, product photograph, no text","width":512,"height":512}'
$job
do {
  Start-Sleep -Seconds 3
  $status = Invoke-RestMethod "http://127.0.0.1:1431/v1/jobs/$($job.id)"
  $status
} while ($status.status -in @("queued", "running"))
if ($status.status -eq "completed") {
  Invoke-WebRequest "http://127.0.0.1:1431$($status.image_url)" -OutFile "$PWD\sdxl-test.png"
}
```

`GET /health` reports `backend: sdxl` when selected.

## Limits and known caveats

- **Not CUDA verified in the release-build environment**: compile and generate
  on the Windows RTX 5080 laptop before considering inference operational.
- One concurrent generator; four total queued/running jobs. Inference is run on
  a Tokio blocking worker; it does not block the web executor.
- The initial implementation reconstructs Candle weights for each request,
  keeping the architecture simple at the cost of warm-up time. Model lifetime
  caching can be added after an actual CUDA memory profile.
- It uses the official Candle SDXL dual-CLIP, DDIM, UNet and VAE path,
  with FP16 UNet/VAE, CLIP inference in F32 and guidance 7.5.
- CUDA generation can exhaust VRAM, especially at 768px. Start with 512px,
  batch 1, and unload large language models first.
- Jobs are in memory across server restarts; completed images and metadata
  persist in `ZIPEEK_IMAGE_DATA_DIR` as `.png` or `.svg` plus `.json`.
- Prompts and images are local. No remote model/API calls occur.
- Image exercise answer correctness and visual validation are separate work.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/build-deployment-services-sdxl-image-server.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.
title: Local SDXL Base inference
