# Dictionary Browse - design and implementation status

Approved 2026-11-04. The design reference is the dark-theme Dictionary mockup.

## Responsibilities

Browse is for **finding, hearing, inspecting and collecting words**, not for
choosing quiz types or launching an ambiguous one-word quiz. Any selected Word
Set can be handed off to Practice with its identity preserved. Practice then
chooses exercise types, mode and any relevant specialized configuration.

## Results presentation

- Five visible rows per page; issue the database query with one lookahead row
  so Next is enabled only if another page exists. Keep Previous/Next inside
  the result panel and show the current page number. No synthetic total count.
- Each list row places simplified hanzi and pinyin **on the same line** when
  horizontal space allows; traditional characters remain supplemental.
  Meanings wrap. Long definitions do not force horizontal page overflow.
- Each row has an accessible **Listen** icon using the existing `ListenButton`
  and Web Speech synthesis `zh-CN`, plus Add/Remove from the chosen Word Set.
  Do not imply TTS provides authoritative tone/reading validation for
  heteronyms; speech synthesis uses simplified word text and device voices.
- No generic per-word Practice action, and no bottom-of-Browse “Translate
  selected vocabulary” button that might mean either word translation or
  exercise generation. The selected Word Set panel offers a named, disabled-
  when-empty “Use <name> in Practice” action instead.
- Search is automatic with a short debounce for text; filters change
  immediately. Refresh uses a Lucide icon with an accessible name. Clear
  resets filters. The underlying reducer/query contract is retained.

## Later (not yet implemented)

- Row details disclosure with sense/reading provenance, usage examples,
  full meanings and an explicit pronunciation target if disambiguated.
- Optional bulk selection and Save selected rows, with clear scope semantics
  (current page versus complete filtered result set). No implicit “all”
  operation across undisplayed pages.
- A full URL-authoritative Browse state codec and history handling remain
  separate work. Current route-local reducer does not implement that design.
- Additional numbered page navigation only after a trustworthy total-count
  query exists; do not invent “Page N of M”.

## Dictionary Word Set destination

The current Word Set selection is the default destination for Dictionary Add/Remove actions, as clarified by the user. Selecting a set in Word Sets or Dictionary updates a separate browser-local preference. On reload the selection is validated against existing Word Set IDs; if the set no longer exists, the first available set is selected. The preference does not change the Word Set backup format and does not override Practice vocabulary selection.

## E2E acceptance

Verify 5 rows per page, independent next/previous, query lookahead,
state-cancelled searches, keyboard search/refresh, row Listen accessibility,
selected-set Add/Remove, empty saved-set start disabled, and route handoff with
saved-set preselection. Run at 320, 768 and 1440 px in both themes. Speech
synthesis calls may be mocked at the browser boundary for deterministic CI;
voice quality is a device test, not an automated correctness assertion.

## Structured filter suggestions

Browse separates free-text search from structured filter suggestions for HSK system and level, category and part of speech. Active chips can be removed independently, and Clear returns to the unfiltered query. The result list is capped at five visible rows with lookahead pagination. Do not resurrect the obsolete release-specific autocomplete contract or infer unverified AI categories from text.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/dictionary-data-dictionary-browse.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.
title: Dictionary Browse - design and implementation status

# Personal learner data and storage

## Existing browser storage

Zipeek uses a generated read-only DuckDB dictionary and separate learner-owned browser storage. The dictionary must not be described as the writable destination for learning results.

- `zipeek.preferences.v1`: consolidated appearance/character preferences, explicit default-off Practice-history recording consent (`learning_history_enabled`), and non-secret AI endpoint/model configuration. The optional AI API key is memory-only.
- `zipeek.user_word_sets.v1`: personal Word Sets. Sets acquired through Courses carry an optional typed `source` with one-based `region_id` and `set_index`. Only this source identity establishes acquisition; matching display names are not proof of acquisition. Renaming or editing words preserves the source, deletion removes acquisition. Pre-existing source-less sets remain personal but are not automatically attributed to courses.
- `zipeek.excluded_words`: vocabulary exclusions.
- `zipeek.crosswords.rotation.v1`: optional browser-local crossword variety history. Contains the 100 most recently used distinct Hanzi answers with usage sequence/count and the 10 most recent puzzle word lists and session IDs; assists seed selection but does not change restored crossword solutions or Practice learning evidence. Separate from `zipeek.crosswords.v5.<session-id>` puzzle snapshots. This key is not included in Word Set personal-data exports.
- `zipeek.practice.session.v1.<uuid-v7>`: temporary session JSON containing one configuration per exercise type, ordered step instances with ISO start/finish timestamps, and session lifecycle timestamps. Finished records are removed after successful optional learning-history handling. Existing records with an incompatible JSON shape are not migrated; they fail current-session validation and must be cleared explicitly if they block new sessions.

The Settings Data & Storage panel supports a versioned JSON personal-data backup/import for Word Sets and exclusions, plus selective deletion. This does **not** imply backups include temporary Practice records or an authoritative learning-history database. Existing importer validation and deletion confirmation remain application features.

Pinyin modules now persist passed **written recognition checks** in `zipeek.courses.progress.v1` after two correct answers. Opening a lesson or listening to an example never marks a module as passed. The same browser-local key saves Grammar step checkpoints and best draft assessment scores, but **never** awards full listening/speaking competence, independently verified grammar mastery or mosaic completion. This category is not included in the current Word Set/exclusions backup/export interface; clearing browser site data can remove it. Browser storage failures are surfaced in the lesson UI. No old manual-completion key is read or written.

## Personal OPFS/DuckDB status

The inspected but browser-unverified source includes an opt-in personal DuckDB Practice-outcome writer with commit/readback-before-cleanup behavior, separate from the diagnostics and snapshot/probe functionality. A browser-local OPFS snapshot is a point-in-time backup, not a live transactional learning store. Do not claim real-world persistence until a browser-verified commit and readback succeed. The completion view only reports success after that operation returns successfully.

The Practice completion screen now distinguishes recorded, disabled and retryable failure outcomes; recording defaults to off. The **approved future direction** is session-first pedagogical evidence with derivation of per-Hanzi/word, exercise, HSK/category and grammar observations. The eligibility floor is seven distinct active dates and ten qualifying scored encounters over at least three sessions with a per-session cap, plus separately assessed recognition, listening, speaking and sentence use; this does **not** constitute a running proficiency algorithm. See [learning evidence](../../learning-practice/practice/learning-evidence.md). The new default-off opt-in and minimal v1 outcome table are source-implemented but not browser-verified; retention, portable export/import, migrations and durability acceptance remain open.

## Development-only persistence simulator (R613 WIP)

The debug DuckDB diagnostics panel has explicit Start/Stop controls for a synthetic persistence run: at most ten cycles scheduled five seconds apart. Every cycle uses the existing personal DuckDB-WASM/OPFS file and exclusive Web Lock, atomically updates the isolated `persistence_simulator` table, checkpoints, closes/reopens, and verifies the revision and deterministic payload. The latest saved run can be checked again after a page reload with **Verify saved state after reload**. Background tab timer throttling and DuckDB startup time can extend the actual interval. Stop prevents later cycles; an in-flight transaction may still finish.

The simulator neither writes real Practice sessions nor changes R608 learner scores. Its synthetic table is dropped when personal learning history is erased. Browser acceptance and failure-injection checks have not been executed; the implementation does **not** establish durable Knowledge Points persistence.

## Data risks and planned acceptance

Browser-local storage can be deleted by site-data clearing and may fail due to quotas or browser restrictions. JSON export is the user-controlled portability path for the categories that it actually exports. OPFS and future personal DuckDB adoption require close/reopen, reload, cross-tab, quota, corrupt-record, export/import and deletion coverage.

See [schema design](../schema/personal-data.md), [current implementation](../../project-management/current.md) and [open tasks](../../project-management/tasks.md).

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/dictionary-data-personal-personal-data-storage.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.

## Confirmed app reset (2026-11-26)

Settings has a Reset app section with an explicit destructive confirmation. It permanently removes Zipeek-owned preferences, course progress, Word Sets, exclusions, saved sessions, personal snapshots and learning history, then reloads the current deployment base at `#/` to show fresh landing/onboarding. The packaged dictionary, model files, exported files outside application storage and unrelated same-origin data are retained. This reset scope was explicitly approved by the user; the browser confirmation is still required when using it.

Confirmation stores a one-use session authorization and fully reloads into the isolated `#/reset-app` bootstrap. Normal UI providers, microphone state, credentials in WASM memory and browser workers are discarded before cleanup. Opening that URL directly does not authorize deletion. Normal documents hold a shared `zipeek-app-storage-session` Web Lock; the reset runner requires an exclusive lock and refuses while another app tab/window is active. A newly opened app document waits for the reset lock before normal startup. Browsers without the required storage/locking APIs show a failure instead of claiming success.

Browser/WebView cleanup removes `zipeek.*` local/session keys and the app's `RUST_LOG` preference, and deletes only top-level personal OPFS entries beginning `zipeek-` or `zipeek.`. It does not clear the whole origin or WebView profile. Current DuckDB personal history, its WAL, snapshot and probe files use those owned names. Native `personal_data_reset` requires an explicit confirmed argument; its serialized database worker closes owned connections, removes only the expected `zipeek-personal.duckdb` and its WAL, and reinitializes empty personal storage on the next normal open. Unexpected paths, symlinks/directories and filesystem errors are rejected.

Cleanup across browser and native storage is not atomic. Errors remain visible in the isolated runner with an explicit partial-cleanup message and Retry. Success navigation occurs only after every required stage succeeds; retries are idempotent. Data reset cannot be undone. Exported backups can restore only the categories supported by the existing importer, not all removed history. Canceling the initial confirmation leaves data unchanged.
title: Personal learner data and storage

# Dictionary generation and published artifacts

This is the **current** generator pipeline, as implemented in [`crates/zipeek-db-gen`](../../../crates/zipeek-db-gen) and described by the installed [`hanzi.manifest.json`](../../../crates/zipeek-web/static/hanzi.manifest.json). Task-by-task historical snapshot sizes, temporary checksums and former pre-expansion counts belong in [release history](../../archive-history/RELEASE_HISTORY.md), not in current generator specifications.

## Inputs and preparation

`inputs/` validates the pinned HSK and CC-CEDICT source files, declared license notices, paths, lengths and SHA-256 hashes. [`generator.rs`](../../../crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/generator.rs) calls `prepare()` to verify sources and open the engine-guarded in-memory schema. Native `duckdb-neo` must report `v2.0.0`; the writer explicitly uses storage compatibility `v2.0.0`.

`import_primary()` parses HSK, applies CC-CEDICT gloss fallback where required, expands valid CC-CEDICT-only readings and preserves explicit character readings. This is no longer an HSK-only, fallback-on-missing-glosses-only pipeline. See [import rules](import-rules.md) and the actual [`import/`](../../../crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/import) modules.

## Schema, enrichment and output

[`schema.sql`](../../../crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/schema.sql) defines the `words` compatibility table, normalized senses/characters/identities, classification tables, memberships, constraints, indexes and controlled taxonomy. The generator may apply validated AI classification cache data if supplied; a table existing does not mean every sense is classified.

[`artifact/writer.rs`](../../../crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/artifact/writer.rs) writes a staging directory, attaches an explicitly compatible native DuckDB file, bulk-copies generated tables, compares logical snapshots, checkpoints/detaches, reopens read-only and validates again before publishing. Failed stages do not publish a partial output. [`artifact/report.rs`](../../../crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/artifact/report.rs) records manifest, diagnostics, source/artifact provenance and table metadata.

## Current installed bundle

| Property | Value from manifest |
| --- | --- |
| Dictionary `words` rows | **120,970** |
| Character occurrences | **312,649** |
| Identity candidates | **120,970** |
| Diagnostic events | **10,187** |
| Native engine | `v2.0.0` |
| Storage version | `v2.0.0` |
| Browser package | `@duckdb/duckdb-wasm@1.33.1-dev114.0` |
| Data artifact | `hanzi-20261115-215819.duckdb` (plus compressed `.gz`) |

These are manifest **declarations** read from the supplied source, not an independent native replay or validation of every row. The source ZIP does not bundle the generated database bytes; binary hash verification and Chrome loading remain outstanding. To inspect the actual asset filenames and hashes, read the installed manifest directly. Do not use the original 12,100-row, 514-diagnostic HSK-only export as the current count.

## Browser integration and boundaries

The [`zipeek-db` WASM adapter](../../../crates/zipeek-db/src/wasm) verifies and opens the installed read-only dictionary; the app supplies a local worker and asset bundle. The manifest's required generator/storage fields are distinct from the live browser engine version and Debug's runtime storage metrics. A new generated dictionary requires native output verification plus browser/Pages tests. It is **not** a writable user database.

See [regeneration](regeneration.md), [runtime](runtime.md), [reproducibility](reproducibility.md) and [provenance testing](../../testing-quality/e2e/provenance.md).

## English full-text indexing

Generation explicitly sets `BLOCK_SIZE 262144` on the new `artifact` database.
After copying dictionary data and validating its logical snapshot, the native
generator installs and loads DuckDB `fts` and creates an immutable BM25 index
on `words.id` / `words.english`. This requires the DuckDB 2.0 `fts` extension
to be available to the native generator. A missing extension fails generation
rather than publishing an artifact without the declared index. The generator
verifies the index schema and executes a BM25 query during generation and
read-only reopening. FTS-owned auxiliary tables are excluded from the canonical
logical dictionary snapshot, which still compares all dictionary relations.

The read-only `Database::english_full_text_search` provides a standalone ranked
query. Browse also exposes `English relevance (FTS / BM25)` as an explicit
field selection. It uses the persisted `fts_main_words` index, sorts by BM25
score, and retains HSK, part-of-speech, category, Word Set and pagination
filters. Ordinary English substring search and Hanzi/Pinyin search remain
separate modes.

On browser dictionary initialization, the DuckDB-WASM connection attempts
`INSTALL AND LOAD fts;`. The extension is fetched dynamically by the versioned
WASM runtime. If it cannot be loaded, the dictionary remains available but
ranked queries will report an error instead of quietly changing to substring
search. The browser compatibility and offline behavior require actual Chrome
verification with a regenerated DuckDB 2.0 bundle at both `/` and `/zipeek/`.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/dictionary-data-schema-artifacts.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.
title: Dictionary generation and published artifacts

# Dictionary database: current implementation

This index describes the **checked-in source and installed manifest**, not an original HSK-only proposal. The physical SQL definition in [`schema.sql`](../../../crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/schema.sql), the generator in [`generator.rs`](../../../crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/generator.rs), and [`hanzi.manifest.json`](../../../crates/zipeek-web/static/hanzi.manifest.json) are the evidence for the installed layout. The database is generated natively and opened read-only by the browser; it is not a writable learning-history store.

## Installed artifact

| Manifest fact | Installed value |
| --- | --- |
| Dictionary `words` rows | **120,970** |
| Identity candidates | 120,970 |
| Source entries | 11,494 |
| Diagnostic events | 10,187 |
| Native generator engine | `v2.0.0` |
| Storage compatibility | `v2.0.0` |
| DuckDB-WASM npm package | `@duckdb/duckdb-wasm@1.33.1-dev114.0` |
| Read-only database file | `hanzi-20261115-215819.duckdb` |
| Compressed browser asset | `hanzi-20261115-215819.duckdb.gz` |

The manifest includes checksums, source metadata, table names and generated-time properties. It declares 312,649 character occurrences and 11,846 explicit character readings. The 12,188 distinct HSK source reading keys described in the source audit are not the row count of this expanded dictionary. The original **12,100-row, 10-column HSK-only snapshot** is historical, not the installed database. The `words` compatibility projection remains ten columns, but normalized tables, senses, membership, classifications and identity candidates are part of the generated schema. The checked-in manifest lists the `character_readings` table, although its physical contents remain unverified until the database file is opened. See [schema](schema.md).

## Installer safety

`cargo make db-install` now publishes only verified dictionary artifacts (the database and gzip, manifest, diagnostics, pinned input metadata, attribution, and license notices). It leaves the existing `static/` directory and unrelated Practice, Courses, brand and Docs assets untouched. Obsolete timestamped dictionary files are moved to `target/db-workflow/backups/` for recovery. The preload in `index.html` is changed only after the dictionary files are published. The installer does not regenerate the database.

## Generator and browser responsibilities

- [`zipeek-db-gen`](../../../crates/zipeek-db-gen) verifies pinned inputs, imports HSK, applies source-backed CC-CEDICT enrichment/expansion, builds normalized relations, and publishes a staged, checked and reopened artifact. Database generation is explicit, not part of every Trunk build.
- [`zipeek-db`](../../../crates/zipeek-db/src/wasm) owns the DuckDB-WASM transport, worker/connection and manifest verification. [`zipeek-web` database services](../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/services/database) expose typed read-only queries to pages.
- The manifest's native engine and storage compatibility are required strings; the running DuckDB-WASM engine and `pragma_database_size()` results are queried independently by Debug.
- Local learner data uses browser storage and optional personal-data probes, **not the generated dictionary**. See [personal-data architecture](personal-data.md).

## Maintained references

| Question | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| Actual SQL tables, constraints and HSK compatibility columns | [schema](schema.md) |
| Original sources, parsing rules and reading identities | [sources](sources.md), [import rules](import-rules.md), [PoS mapping](pos-mapping.md) |
| Generator stages, output and validation | [artifacts](artifacts.md), [regeneration](regeneration.md) |
| Actual package pins and compatibility boundary | [runtime](runtime.md), [generator dependencies](generator-deps.md) |
| Browser queries and Browse/Practice behavior | [queries](queries.md), [browser DB architecture](../../architecture/modules/browser-db.md) |
| Logical reproducibility and testing | [reproducibility](reproducibility.md), [browser DB testing](../../testing-quality/e2e/browser-db.md) |
| Unapproved FTS/index redesign | [review proposal](review.md) |

Dependency governance: the installed npm package pin agrees with the generator policy and artifact manifest. Historical decisions about the storage compatibility version describe a prior artifact; do not treat them as source verification. Changes to dependencies or storage formats require explicit user approval.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/dictionary-data-schema-db.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.

## Generator bulk-import and lexical reference additions (R615 WIP)

The native generator now batches `sense_display`, `sense_qualifiers`, `sense_relations`, `characters`, `word_characters` and `vocabulary_identities` inserts. Performance changes require the same verified input set and fresh before/after timestamps; no measured speedup has been established in this authoring environment.

The bundled `crates/zipeek-db-gen/data/relationships.csv` is imported into `word_relations` during full artifact generation. The original spelling pairs and relationship type are preserved, with separate `source_resolution` and `target_resolution` statuses (`resolved`, `missing`, `ambiguous`). A canonical `word_id` is populated only when exactly one `words.simplified` row matches the spelling. Ambiguous forms are **not** expanded into all pronunciation combinations. These lexical relationships are separate from sense-level source-annotation relations.

`pinyin_syllable_candidates` groups numeric character-reading strings by attested characters. `character_gloss_candidates` associates each one-character dictionary entry's raw sense gloss with its character. Neither candidate table is an approved, curated R608 scoreable catalogue. Existing `vocabulary_identities.identity_status = 'unresolved'` also remains non-scoreable until explicit curation.

The CSV is resolved from the db-gen crate's compile-time source location. Running the generator from a source checkout requires the bundled CSV to remain present. It is now part of the dictionary snapshot fingerprint. Test the locked native generator and verify final artifact row counts, relation resolution totals and snapshot equality on the target machine.

## R616 WIP: relation import verification

The relationship importer verifies the row count against the bundled CSV before it reports completion. It records `total`, `fully_resolved`, `ambiguous_endpoint` and `missing_endpoint` in the native build log. An unresolved or ambiguous endpoint is retained in the table, never expanded into guessed word IDs. These last two status counts can overlap when a row has one ambiguous and one missing endpoint.

Focused generator tests cover unambiguous, ambiguous and missing endpoint resolution, plus an incomplete CSV import. The native test runner and full generator remain unverified in the R616 authoring environment.

## R617 WIP: artifact dependency ordering

The generated `character_gloss_candidates` table references `(word_id, sense_order)` in `word_senses`. The artifact writer now copies `word_senses` before this dependent table, preserving the schema's foreign key. A schema-driven unit test checks all foreign-key dependencies between tables in the artifact-copy sequence. The user's 2026-11-23 native generator run reached the artifact-copy stage after populating 267,447 word relationships but failed on the prior copy order; a completed artifact is not yet verified.

Relationship resolution counters are now a mutually exclusive partition: `fully_resolved`, `ambiguous_only`, `missing_only`, and `ambiguous_and_missing`. This avoids double-counting rows that have one ambiguous and one missing endpoint. The source spellings remain intact irrespective of resolution.

At audit time, the ignored root Cargo.lock resolved duckdb-neo 0.20000.0 and

# Import rules

How source rows become `words` rows: reading identity, level mapping, text
preservation, gloss rules, and key conflicts. Part of the
[database documentation](db.md). Approved rules in
[D16](../../project-management/decisions/database-and-artifacts.md#d16-primary-import-and-ids)
and [D18](../../project-management/decisions/database-and-artifacts.md#d18-source-comparison-and-serialization).

## Import identity, forms, and deterministic IDs (D16)

The logical import key is **`(simplified, numeric_pinyin)`**, where staging
`numeric_pinyin` maps to the persisted `pinyin_numeric` column. Expand distinct
readings from `forms[]`; do not add a separate word merely for a traditional
variant sharing the same reading key. Retain the first form's traditional value
in source-array order and log a warning when multiple forms share that key.

D07 still enforces `UNIQUE (simplified, pinyin)` on display pinyin. These are
different representations, not universally interchangeable keys. The audited
snapshot has no numeric-key group with conflicting display pinyin and no
display-key group with distinct numeric pinyin (case-sensitive checks). Assert
that relationship when generating; do not silently normalize or collapse readings
if a future input violates it.

After reading-key grouping, assign:

```sql
ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY simplified, numeric_pinyin)
```

Here numeric_pinyin is the staging name; ordering the final column would use
pinyin_numeric. Persist the assigned value as the INTEGER id, checking its
range. IDs are snapshot-local. Changing data between runs may shift IDs; saved
exclusions and shared seed=<word_id> URLs can break or identify another word.
Committing the DB with its consumer does not make old URLs portable across DB
regenerations. No cross-snapshot ID guarantee or migration is required.

Level mapping (D16)
Source token	Stored membership
old-1 through old-6	Corresponding hsk2_level, else NULL
new-1 through new-6	Corresponding hsk3_level, else NULL
new-7 or new-7+	hsk3_level = 7, the combined 7-9 band
The pinned JSON actually uses new-7+, while its README illustrates new-7.
Accept both exact spellings as known tag-format variance; do not accept arbitrary
suffixes, separate levels 8/9, or other unrecognized tokens. Log and skip unknown
level tokens. Deduplicate repeated identical tags. If different levels occur
within one system, choose the lowest and warn; retain the independent value in
the other system. No conflicting distinct levels were found in the audited input.

Exact text preservation and field coverage (D16)
Target	Source / import rule
simplified	Entry's simplified text, unchanged
traditional	Selected form's traditional text, unchanged
pinyin	Selected form's transcriptions.pinyin, unchanged; do not derive from numeric
pinyin_numeric	Selected form's transcriptions.numeric, unchanged
english	Nonempty trimmed meanings in source order, pipe-separated; preserve display casing
part_of_speech	Map source pos codes to canonical lowercase enum tokens; nullable if unavailable
frequency	Source integer ranking when provided; lower means more common; otherwise NULL
Preserve spacing, case, and hanzi codepoints exactly, without extra Unicode
normalization of stored hanzi/pinyin. Missing or blank pinyin makes a word unusable:
drop it and log it rather than synthesizing a reading. The audited input has none,
but the generator must handle bad future input.

Verified format differences: the pinned data is not uniformly CC-CEDICT's
u:/neutral-5 convention. It includes ban4 lü3, unnumbered neutral syllables
such as zhen1 de, spaced pinyin, and display text such as bàn lu:3.
Preserve those originals per D16. Lookup and round-comparison normalization is
separate from storage; do not claim raw numeric strings are interchangeable with
CC-CEDICT without the comparison-only D18 policy below.

Gloss selection and CC-CEDICT fallback (D18)
For each reading, trim meanings and remove blank strings. Use the first form's
nonempty meanings when available; inspect remaining same-reading forms if needed.
Keep source order and original case. Replace literal ASCII | inside each gloss
with fullwidth ｜ (U+FF5C) before joining glosses with ASCII |. Log both the
original and replaced string for each occurrence. This is deliberately lossy;
never substitute /, which already carries meaning in glosses such as he/she.
Do not reorder glosses merely to choose a different match label.

Consult CC-CEDICT if and only if the resulting primary gloss list is empty.
Match simplified hanzi and disambiguate by numeric reading as needed. Ignore
fallback entries whose gloss begins with variant of. If no usable fallback
exists, store english = NULL and warn; do not drop an otherwise usable reading.

The first serialized gloss is the English label in both English-bearing variants:
the right column in hanzi-eng, the left column in eng-pinyin. The right
column of eng-pinyin shows the source's diacritic/display pinyin. A row with
NULL English remains eligible for pinyin-hanzi, but is ineligible for either
English-bearing variant. Filter missing required labels before candidate indexing.

The exact trigger is an empty list, not a heuristic quality score or a preference
for another dictionary. Use D18's comparison-only reading keys for fallback lookup.

Numeric/display key conflicts and seed eligibility (D18)
Different exact numeric reading keys that produce the same (simplified, pinyin)
display key violate the approved UNIQUE constraint. Fail generation and log both
source rows verbatim; never silently select one. Conversely, forms with the same
(simplified, numeric_pinyin) and differing display renderings are one reading:
keep the first source form and warn, per D16. Do not fail for display drift alone.

A nonexcluded seed lacking English is ineligible for eng-pinyin and hanzi-eng.
Use D15's deterministic URL recovery: up to ten ChaCha draws from the ordered,
exclusion-clean pool, then the first eligible word by id. pinyin-hanzi does not
require English. The same eligibility condition applies to D20's English-bearing
MCQ variants; D20 separately approves their routes and scope.

What the importer rejects
Any entry with an unknown PoS code after lowercasing (whole entry, all forms;
warning logged, skip before grouping).

Any reading with missing required pinyin (dropped, warning logged).

Any reading with no HSK membership at all (rejected entry).

Any display-key collision between distinct numeric keys (fatal; fails
generation and logs both source rows).

What the importer preserves
First form's traditional text; all distinct readings stay separate.

Exact source spacing, case, and hanzi codepoints.

Both display and numeric pinyin, unchanged.

Source gloss order and casing after trim, with only the | → U+FF5C substitution.

Lowest within-system level with a warning if repeated tags disagree.

Related
Schema the importer writes into: schema.md.

PoS token mapping: pos-mapping.md.

Source bytes this reads: sources.md.

Implemented importer behavior: artifacts.md.

# Pedagogy: recognition acquisition foundation

## Status and authority

This design records the user's 2026-11-11 decisions for **historical Hanzi recognition acquisition**. The source-only checkpoint introduces `zipeek-pedagogy`, a pure Rust domain crate with deterministic, in-memory projections. It does **not** activate automatic assessment capture, a persistent personal-data authority, a worker, `/stats`, or dragon awards in the UI. Those remain separately gated.

It deliberately does not replace the historical source `zipeek-exercises::learning::MasteryPolicy`, which continues to represent its older multi-skill vocabulary projection until an approved migration of domain ownership and reconciliation of its separate definitions. Dragon acquisition and full multi-skill proficiency are not interchangeable.

## Recognition acquisition contract

- Each individual Hanzi independently earns a historical recognition award after **seven consecutive qualifying local dates**.
- Each qualifying day requires **ten correct, eligible, unassisted recognition observations**, across **at least three completed sessions**. At most **four** correct observations from any one session count toward the daily ten.
- The maximum mistakes before daily qualification is **0, 1, or 2**, default 0. The allowance is frozen in the submitted evidence for each item and local date. An inconsistent allowance within one day is an error, not a retroactive adjustment.
- An additional eligible incorrect observation that exceeds the allowance **fails that day immediately** and resets the active acquisition streak. Earlier attempts are not deleted.
- Once a day qualifies it **locks immediately**. Later mistakes that day do not alter that qualification; they remain available for subsequent retention analysis.
- Qualifying days must be **consecutive local calendar dates** with **at least 24 elapsed hours** between the moments each day qualifies. A missed date resets the active streak.
- Later recall failures can change a separate retention status. They do not revoke the timestamp of a historical acquisition award.
- The full HSK 1-9 learning pool is accessible regardless of acquisition progress. Dragon achievements count distinct acquired Hanzi in the selected dictionary-HSK target; words and readings have independent evidence identities and do not automatically award character recognition.

## Evidence boundary

All games may submit scored observations, but game scoring is not itself an acquisition decision. Recognition events have stable attempt/session identities, submission time, local date and zone context, assessment version and evaluator provenance. Invalid dates, inconsistent local dates/UTC offsets, duplicate IDs with conflicting content, and evidence from the future are rejected.

Independent recognition assessments qualify when unassisted and complete. Multiple-choice recognition requires a validated assessment proof from a separate gate: the the historical source `ValidatedChoice` type carries a non-empty validation identifier, but **this crate cannot verify its content**. This is a provisional domain API, not permission for production games to fabricate validation IDs. Hinted, incomplete, unvalidated-choice and general exposure events are recorded as supporting-only evidence. No production game is wired to this API yet.

**Outstanding correctness requirements before persistent mastery:** define the authoritative choice-validation gate (prompt/distractor diversity and independent recall), fixed-zone behaviour across travel, trustworthy item identity through dictionary refresh, recovery of clock anomalies, and atomic persistence with one active tab. the historical source's projection must not be the sole source of durable mastery until those gates pass.

## Crate boundaries

`zipeek-pedagogy` is independent of Yew, JS, DuckDB and all third-party crates. `zipeek-exercises` continues to own game outcomes and the existing the historical source learning contract. The future adapter validates outcomes and passes independent evidence to pedagogy. The existing database crate owns authoritative writes after persistence acceptance. A Rust/WASM browser worker is an execution host in existing browser infrastructure, not a reason to put learning rules in `zipeek-worker`.

The new crate includes its own pure calendar-date validation because no dependency direction between the existing learning calendar module and this new domain was approved for the historical source. Consolidating identical calendar functionality is a follow-up refactoring task before production integration.

## Scheduled stages

1. **Domain prototype:** pure evidence and recognition projection plus deterministic tests. WIP until compiled and reviewed.
2. **Later:** validated game-to-evidence adapter, historical policy readback, OPFS DuckDB durability/atomicity, and consent gating. Schema changes require separate approval.
3. **Later:** background WASM worker host, pending-work recovery, single-tab ownership and Settings diagnostics.
4. **Later:** `/stats`, separate skill and retention views, dragon colour progression, HSK-target denominator and accessible UI.
5. **Later:** optional advanced AI insights with external-transfer consent and independently validated generated exercises.

Do not imply the app is collecting pedagogical data, awarding character mastery, or using a running analysis worker until these integrations and tests are completed.

## verified evidence-journal boundary (WIP)

`zipeek-pedagogy::EvidenceJournal` is a synchronous pure-Rust port for reading
recorded recognition events and atomically appending a batch. `append_and_verify`
first validates candidate evidence against the existing journal, requests the
append, then rereads stored records and refuses to return a learning projection
unless the candidate events are present and unchanged. `project_committed`
computes only from journal readback. Replayed identical attempt identifiers are
idempotent; conflicting IDs are rejected before append.

The port contract requires an adapter to provide **atomic, durable** append,
consistent readback, and exclusive single-writer coordination. Those
requirements are **not** implemented by this port itself. Test doubles model
write failures, discarded writes, altered readbacks, and duplicate retries. The
existing Practice session JSON table is not automatically equivalent to a
character-level assessment event journal, and cannot be used without approved
schema and provenance work.

No worker, browser persistence adapter, production capture, award writes, or
`/stats` view was described in the historical source. The independent choice-validation gate,
learner timezone authority, consent controls, and authoritative OPFS durability
remain prerequisites to production integration.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/dictionary-data-schema-pedagogy.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.

# Personal-data storage: implemented state and proposed database

## Current authority

The application uses `localStorage` for settings, personal Word Sets, Pinyin-course progress, exclusions and temporary UUID Practice records. The keys and backup boundary are documented in [Personal Data](../personal/personal-data-storage.md). `PracticeSessionStore` saves unfinished work under `zipeek.practice.session.v1.<uuid-v7>`; completion removes that temporary record. The the historical source unverified checkpoint introduces a dedicated OPFS DuckDB outcome ledger, gated by a default-off recording preference. This requires browser validation before durability claims.

The Settings Personal Data page implements category-based JSON backup/preview/import/delete. It also exposes isolated OPFS/snapshot diagnostics and a writable DuckDB-WASM persistence **probe**. The probe uses its own database and does not migrate or replace user Word Sets, exclusions, course progress or Practice records. See [`zipeek-db/src/wasm/probe.rs`](../../../crates/zipeek-db/src/wasm/probe.rs) and [`zipeek-web/src/services/personal_data/`](../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/services/personal_data).

## Not yet production-accepted

The inspected source describes an initial `zipeek-personal-learning-v1.duckdb` outcome table, a default-off opt-in and an exclusive Web Lock. There is still no production-accepted pedagogical-history writer, completed migration model, verified cross-tab locking and durable exercise-evidence schema beyond completed Practice outcome records. A successful OPFS probe does not imply any of those capabilities. Attempts/events in [`zipeek-exercises`](../../../crates/zipeek-exercises/src) are domain/test structures, not automatically persisted browser records.

## recognition evidence table (approved WIP, not activated)

The user explicitly approved a dedicated recognition-evidence table and Rust/WASM
adapter on 2026-11-12. The WIP adapter is implemented in
`zipeek-db/src/wasm/recognition_history.rs` and uses the existing personal OPFS
DuckDB file, the same exclusive Web Lock, and the existing DuckDB-WASM bridge.
The table is created lazily on the first explicit append:

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS recognition_evidence (
    attempt_id VARCHAR PRIMARY KEY,
    evidence_json VARCHAR NOT NULL
);
```

The versioned JSON payload includes `schema_version: 1`, `attempt_id`, a single
`character`, session `session_id` and `completed`, `occurred_at_utc_ms`,
`timezone_iana`, `timezone_offset_minutes`, `local_date`, `mistake_allowance`
(0, 1 or 2), `evaluator_id`, `assessment_version`, `correct`, `assisted`, and
`format` (tagged object: `independent_recall`, `validated_choice` with
`validation_id`, or `supporting_only`). The adapter rejects inconsistent
identities, invalid fields, oversized records/batches and conflicting duplicate
IDs. It inserts an entire batch in a transaction, checkpoints, reopens the
database and verifies the exact stored JSON by attempt ID. Exact-match retries
are idempotent. `PersonalLearningHistory::erase` now drops both learning
history tables in one transaction.

The API provides `PersonalRecognitionHistory::append_verified` and `read_all`.
The latter is bounded to two million records and is intended for replay and
verification, not repeated per-render dashboard queries. Aggregate SQL and
pagination will be needed before high-volume dashboard adoption.

**Not activated:** This adds neither opt-in collection wiring nor a production
`RecognitionEvent` serializer, browser worker, `/stats` UI or authoritative
acquisition projection. The personal DuckDB migration is additive and lazy;
existing `practice_sessions` records remain untouched until the user explicitly
requests deletion. Browser transaction/OPFS/restore/consent acceptance is
pending; do not treat source-level tests as durability proof.

## Design gates before adoption

1. Implement the approved session-first scored observations in a personal DuckDB with explicit recording consent; finalize opt-in defaults and raw audio/text retention before production collection.
2. Select versioned vocabulary identity keys that remain valid when the read-only dictionary changes; generated integer WordIds alone are not portable.
3. Define append-only attempt semantics, stable exercise/step IDs, schema versions, deletions, backup/import/rollback and a quota/retention policy.
4. Prove write, checkpoint, restart, cross-tab lock, failure recovery, export/import and corruption handling in real browsers for the approved DuckDB-WASM package.
5. Only after durable-write verification, show a success confirmation; when disabled show a privacy notice, and on real write errors show an explicit failure.

Historical exploratory steps and proposed tables are recorded in [completed history](../../archive-history/completed/) and [release history](../../archive-history/RELEASE_HISTORY.md). They must not be read as a deployed learner database specification.

## Approved pedagogical evidence direction (not implemented)

Persist Practice sessions as the evidence authority; derive attempt and skill observations linked to their original session/step, normalized word/Hanzi IDs, exercise kind, HSK/category labels and assessed grammar point. The approved eligibility floor is **seven distinct active local calendar days**, **at least ten qualifying scored encounters over three or more distinct Practice sessions**, a per-session counting cap, and separately successful evidence for recognition, listening, assessed speaking and sentence use. The per-session cap, exact modality thresholds, learner timezone policy and audio privacy/retention remain undecided; never grant mastery automatically on the tenth encounter. Inject a test clock so E2E can advance dates without altering the OS clock. Preserve a distinct irreversible grammar course-completion record once all required grammar-point assessments pass. See [learning evidence](../../learning-practice/practice/learning-evidence.md) and [future Courses spec](../../learning-practice/courses/courses-mosaic.md).

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/dictionary-data-schema-personal-data.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.

# PoS mapping

The 42-code canonical part-of-speech mapping and audit counts. Part of the
[database documentation](db.md). Approved mapping in
[D18](../../project-management/decisions/database-and-artifacts.md#d18-source-comparison-and-serialization).

## Canonical part-of-speech mapping (D18: approved)

The shared `PartOfSpeech` mapping and fixture tests are implemented in A02. The
A03 importer logs and rejects entries on mapping failure. Pinyin and hanzi remain
stored exactly as supplied under D16; the derived PoS column intentionally stores
mapped canonical values.

Lowercase every source code **before lookup**. The source codes are
case-insensitive: `Mg` -> `mg` -> `numeric_morpheme`; `Rg` -> `rg` ->
`pronoun_morpheme`. Implement locale-independent lowercasing for these ASCII
codes, preserving source provenance rather than rewriting input data.

| Source code after lowercasing | Canonical enum string |
| --- | --- |
| `a` | `adjective` |
| `ad` | `adjective_adverbial` |
| `ag` | `adjective_morpheme` |
| `an` | `adjective_nominal` |
| `b` | `non_predicate_adjective` |
| `c` | `conjunction` |
| `d` | `adverb` |
| `dg` | `adverb_morpheme` |
| `e` | `interjection` |
| `f` | `directional_locality` |
| `g` | `morpheme` |
| `h` | `prefix` |
| `i` | `idiom` |
| `j` | `abbreviation` |
| `k` | `suffix` |
| `l` | `fixed_expression` |
| `m` | `numeral` |
| `mg` | `numeric_morpheme` |
| `n` | `noun` |
| `ng` | `noun_morpheme` |
| `nr` | `personal_name` |
| `ns` | `place_name` |
| `nt` | `organization_name` |
| `nx` | `nominal_string` |
| `nz` | `other_proper_noun` |
| `o` | `onomatopoeia` |
| `p` | `preposition` |
| `q` | `classifier` |
| `r` | `pronoun` |
| `rg` | `pronoun_morpheme` |
| `s` | `space_word` |
| `t` | `time_word` |
| `tg` | `time_word_morpheme` |
| `u` | `auxiliary` |
| `v` | `verb` |
| `vd` | `verb_adverbial` |
| `vg` | `verb_morpheme` |
| `vn` | `verb_nominal` |
| `w` | `symbol_punctuation` |
| `x` | `unclassified` |
| `y` | `modal_particle` |
| `z` | `descriptive` |

## Rejection policy

If **any** code in a source entry is unrecognized after lowercasing, skip the
**entire word entry and all its forms**, and log a warning identifying the word
and unknown code(s). Do not guess a mapping, silently drop only the bad tag, or
keep the entry with NULL PoS. Apply the skip before reading-key merging and
row-number ID assignment, so counts and IDs reflect the accepted input.

A missing/empty PoS list is different from a present unknown code: retain the
word with `part_of_speech = NULL` under D07. Recognized multi-PoS values use the
existing comma-separated canonical-string column; ensure deterministic output
and no duplicate canonical tokens. Query by complete tokens, never substrings.

## Naming notes

This full table supersedes the earlier illustrative vocabulary:
- `q` maps to `classifier`, not `measure_word`.
- `y` maps to `modal_particle`, not generic `particle`.

The canonical enum, DB values, query filters, and RNG seed tokens must agree.
URL `pos` still follows D13's different input policy: ignore unknown query tokens
while keeping recognized tokens; empty/omitted or all-unknown means no filter.
Source import's whole-word rejection does not apply to malformed URL filters.

## Audit against the pinned source

Audit against pinned `a66fd30b9580da2c2af7eb19e4b9d8099a29c061`, using the
case-insensitive table above:

| Observation | Count / consequence |
| --- | --- |
| Mapping entries | 42 |
| Source entries containing mixed-case codes | 6; case alone does not reject them |
| Unknown lowercase codes | `cc`, `mq`, `qt`, `qv`; do not invent extensions |
| Source entries rejected by the unknown-code rule | 64 out of 11,494 |
| Forms belonging to those rejected entries | 105 out of 12,655 |

Counts describe source entries/forms before other import rules and reading-key
grouping, not final generated DB rows. Some entries have more than one unknown
code. Log/report these exclusions during generation and warn on newly observed
codes rather than silently changing the approved table.

## Related

- Import rules that apply this mapping: [import-rules.md](import-rules.md).
- Schema column storing these tokens: [schema.md](schema.md).
- URL filter policy: [queries.md](queries.md).
- Fixture test requirements: [../../testing/provenance.md](../../testing-quality/e2e/provenance.md).

# Queries

Word of the Day query contract, practice pool queries, right-label
normalization, and round builder tuning. Part of the
[database documentation](db.md). Approved contracts in
[D05](../../project-management/decisions/foundations.md#d05-word-of-the-day),
[D12](../../project-management/decisions/rounds-and-replay.md#d12-deterministic-round-builder),
and [D13](../../project-management/decisions/rounds-and-replay.md#d13-counts-urls-exclusions-offsets).

## Word of the Day query contract (D05: approved)

Use the full word pool, not practice filters. Count using `COUNT(*)`; when zero,
return an empty result for the neutral placeholder without modulo or offset work.
Otherwise use D14's 64-bit FNV-1a local-date hash modulo that count as the offset
in an ordered query. Use `u64` for the hash/modulo arithmetic. Count and selection
must refer to the same pool; never substitute `DefaultHasher`.

With D07's synthetic IDs, use `ORDER BY simplified, pinyin` for Word of the Day;
the unique natural key makes that a total order. This maps D05's generic `hanzi`
ordering to the selected physical column. `ORDER BY id ASC` is also deterministic
for a fixed snapshot, but must not be confused with cross-snapshot ID stability.
`LIMIT 1 OFFSET n` without an explicit deterministic `ORDER BY` is forbidden.
Regeneration can change the selected word; preserving a prior generated pool's
Word of the Day is not a backward-compatibility requirement.

Surface load failure separately from a successfully loaded empty pool so the UI
can add Retry only to the load-failure placeholder. See
[PRODUCT](../../product-ux/product.md).

## Practice pool queries (D13: approved)

Practice meaning-based rounds select the first `sense_display` definition classified `lexical` for the exact `word_id`/reading, ordered by `sense_order`. All strict, widened, filtered and Word Set pools exclude readings without such a definition. The saved `words.english` projection is not used as an exercise-sense selector; Browse continues to show legitimate usage references. The same selected definition is used to build and display a round. The generator classifies source glosses during regeneration, currently excluding standalone `used in ...` references and relation-only cross-references; it does not discard or reorder dictionary data. This is a conservative vocabulary eligibility classification, not a universal guarantee that every lexical sense makes an unambiguous question.

Apply the active HSK system/level and PoS context, remove excluded `WordId`s before
selection, and reapply exclusions during D02 widening. Unseeded rounds start with
ordered slices of four at the URL offset, then apply D12's bounded duplicate-label
slide; seeded rounds use the seed plus its HSK context and do not use offset.
Under D12 the caller issues three queries for the strict, widened-HSK, and
widened-HSK/any-PoS views. Every query applies exclusions in SQL and includes
`ORDER BY id ASC`. Views are nested supersets, using clamped levels from the same
HSK system. The pure builder makes no further DB calls.

The URL's parsed exclusions are authoritative for a loaded round; saved browser
exclusions must not alter its queries. URL generation unions saved and current
round sets first. Unknown integer IDs naturally match no rows and are ignored;
noninteger entries are dropped before query construction, with a debug warning.

Use the same eligible ordered pool for its count, offset bounds, and selection.
If offset plus four exceeds pool size, wrap to zero. Exclusions leaving fewer
than eight candidates after widening require the reset-exclusions state. Neither
old generated pools nor old ID-based bookmarks are guaranteed unchanged after DB
regeneration; replay assumes the same database snapshot.

## Right-column label normalization (D12)

Use only the actual right-column label, never the left label, to form duplicate
keys.

| Variant | Right label | Comparison key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `eng-pinyin` | Pinyin | Canonical numeric tone form, no whitespace, lowercase; e.g. `chīfàn` becomes `chi1fan4` |
| `pinyin-hanzi` | Simplified hanzi | Exact bytes; no case folding or whitespace stripping |
| `hanzi-eng` | Displayed English gloss | Trim, lowercase, collapse internal whitespace |

Compare normalized keys byte-for-byte. Homophones collide in `eng-pinyin`; 行 with
different readings collides in `pinyin-hanzi`; equal normalized English labels
collide in `hanzi-eng`. English `to eat` and `eat` remain different. Earlier
examples checking the left column were corrected and are not part of the rule.

English `to eat` and `eat` are distinct keys. Do not silently remove words or
punctuation as a synonym heuristic. The comparison key is derived from the exact
label the UI displays, not another gloss or the entire pipe-separated storage
field. D16 selects the first gloss for both English-bearing variants; rendering
and comparison must use that same gloss. D18 specifies pinyin comparison details;
no new normalization dependency is approved.

## Round builder tuning

Initial `const MAX_SLIDE: usize = 16`; each view tries at most
`min(pool.len(), MAX_SLIDE)` four-word windows before falling through. This is a
tunable performance guard, not a fixed user-facing round count. Most pools are
expected to have near-unique right labels, so sixteen windows provide headroom;
verify that assumption with real pool data. Seeded rounds do not slide.

Always pick the first clean window and give each view its own cap. Changing the
cap leaves windows found before both limits unchanged, but can change a successful
widened fallback into a successful strict result (or the reverse), changing that
URL's round. Do not claim all successful replay is unaffected by cap tuning.
D19 requires explicit approval, a new prefix and URL selector, and a documented
compatibility path for replay-changing tuning. Test first-clean-window/fallthrough
behaviour rather than asserting the constant equals 16.

See [ROUND_GENERATION](../../games/round-generation.md) for the complete
algorithm and the distinction between URL offset, internal slide start, and
zero-based widened views.

## Related

- Builder algorithm: [ROUND_GENERATION](../../games/round-generation.md).
- Browser query implementation: [../modules/browser-db.md](../../architecture/modules/browser-db.md).
- Schema read by these queries: [schema.md](schema.md).

## Future schema/query review (A62)

Compare the existing candidate/search workload with normalized tag/PoS and
optional English FTS proposals. Ensure membership joins do not duplicate WordIds
or change deterministic order; preserve approved Browse search semantics.
Measure plans/browser latency/size before selecting more indexes. See
[review brief](review.md) for official support and the pinned-WASM/read-only probe.

## Implemented normalized Browse search

`crates/zipeek-web/src/services/database/browse_queries.rs` introduces a typed, parameterized
read-only search endpoint over the regenerated schema. Search uses the original
`words` projection only for rendering and stable `ORDER BY w.id ASC`; individual
English glosses are matched through `word_senses`. HSK, source PoS and AI-assigned
category filters are applied with correlated `EXISTS` subqueries so multiple senses
and labels cannot duplicate the same result. Filters are OR within a code list and
AND across dimensions; paging is limited to 100 results per request.

The query is now connected to Browse through `BrowseSearchForm` and `BrowseResults`. The installed manifest declares normalized membership, sense and category tables, and the user reported a successful Windows run of Browse interactions. This is not a claim that all filter combinations or the latest UUID Practice changes have been browser-tested.

Text matching currently uses `contains(...)` (case-folded for pinyin/English),
which is a substring scan rather than an indexed full-text search. It deliberately
does not pretend that an index on an HSK column will speed up arbitrary substrings.
Benchmark real generated data with `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` for exact hanzi, pinyin,
English substring, HSK-only, category-only and combined filters using both sparse
and common categories. Compare latency, plans and file size before approving
new secondary indexes or FTS features in DuckDB-WASM.

PoS filters use `word_pos_membership` (source reading-level PoS), while category
filters use `sense_categories` (AI-derived sense-level labels). An entry with no
AI classification does not match a category filter; an unfiltered search still
returns it. Future sense-level PoS filtering can be added explicitly once the
product rules for source vs AI classification are decided.

# Regeneration

**Current installation:** consult [the installed manifest](../../../crates/zipeek-web/static/hanzi.manifest.json) for the actual 120,970-row manifest declaration; the old A05 snapshots mentioned later are historical. Commands and tasks below should be checked against the current `Makefile.toml` before execution. Production dictionary generation and installation must not run as an unintended side effect of documentation or E2E work.

Generation is explicit and manual. Commands below run from the repository root.
No source acquisition or database generation runs during application builds.

## Live AI smoke and offline streaming regression coverage

`cargo make db-ai-smoke` sends one single-sense and one two-sense batch classification request through the
AiMux streaming client and taxonomy validator, using the same model, endpoint,
timeout and retry environment settings as `db-full`. It has no database/cache
writes and does not import the full HSK source. A missing final-text response
is reported as an actionable error; this does **not** establish whether the
model only produced reasoning, exceeded its token budget, or the streaming
provider dropped content. Inspect LM Studio's output when this occurs.

For an opt-in direct native invocation:

```powershell
cargo run -p zipeek-db-gen --locked -- ai-smoke --model "qwen3-14b-claude-4.5-opus-high-reasoning-distill" --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:1234
```

When classification work is pending, `db-full` runs the smoke request first
and refuses to generate/install on failure. Offline Rust mock HTTP tests
exercise AiMux aggregation of split SSE content and empty final text; Node
workflow tests verify the preflight gate. They do not replace a live model
or Windows end-to-end acceptance test.

## One-command AI-enriched regeneration

Run `cargo make db-full` from the repository root while the configured LM Studio
model and local inference server are available. This command performs a complete
resumable classification pass **before** creating a candidate, so it does not
create an intermediate unclassified artifact. It then runs the existing native
`zipeek-db-gen generate --classification-cache` export and the existing transactional
bundle installer. The generator verifies exact sense digests, prompt/taxonomy
versions and classification records; logical snapshots include AI-derived tables.

The command checks `zipeek-db-gen classify-plan` before and after inference and refuses
publication unless zero senses remain pending. AI failures preserve checkpoints
in `target/db-workflow/classification-cache/` and leave the installed bundle
untouched. A separate cache file is selected for each model. Environment
settings: `ZIPEEK_AI_MODEL` (default
`qwen3-14b-claude-4.5-opus-high-reasoning-distill`), `ZIPEEK_AI_ENDPOINT`
(default `http://127.0.0.1:1234`), `ZIPEEK_AI_TIMEOUT_MS` (default
`300000`), `ZIPEEK_AI_RETRIES` (default `1`). `cargo make db-full-dev`
performs this workflow before serving the web app.

`cargo make db-generate` and `cargo make dev` remain intentionally offline:
no AI inference and no classification cache is applied. This distinction keeps
routine development independent of the local model. Generated artifacts are
always source-and-cache specific; never hand-edit the DuckDB file.

### Incremental classification checkpoints

The cache path printed by `db-full` still identifies the model-specific
`<hash>.jsonl` snapshot. Existing classified senses in that JSONL remain
readable. Instead of rewriting the entire growing snapshot after each new sense,
The described generator writes one synchronized and atomically renamed
`<hash>.jsonl.records/<word_id>-<sense_order>.json` checkpoint per newly
accepted sense. Native `classify-plan`, `classify`, and enriched export combine
both sources; neither path is a complete standalone export once new records
exist. **Do not delete, compact, or move either cache part while classification
is running.** Unexpected, truncated or duplicate checkpoints halt processing
rather than being silently skipped. Unresolved `.tmp` checkpoint files require
manual inspection before resuming. No installed database is modified unless
all senses pass validation.

Classification-level recovery is implemented separately in
`crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/llm/recovery.rs`: for an empty final response, invalid JSON,
or an invalid taxonomy payload, it attempts the same sense at most three times.
The source gloss, v3 classification prompt and model stay the same on retry.
This policy does not retry storage failures or override AiMux's existing
transport retry setting (`ZIPEEK_AI_RETRIES`). Failed batches never publish
an incomplete database; re-running `cargo make db-full` resumes valid cached
records. The current workflow defers an exhausted sense rather than inventing labels;
the final completeness gate still prohibits installing partial enrichment.

## Choose the command

For the complete local workflow, run from the repository root:

```powershell
cargo make dev
```

This generates a fresh candidate, verifies and installs the whole bundle with
a backup, then starts Trunk at http://localhost:1420. It runs once per invocation;
Trunk rebuilds do not regenerate data. Prerequisites are installed cargo-make,
Node, Rust/native generator prerequisites, Trunk and the locked web npm packages
(`cargo make setup` from the repository root after a clean unpack). Tasks do not install
or upgrade tools/packages. Tested cargo-make version: 0.37.24.

| Task from root | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| cargo make | List available tasks without changing the database |
| cargo make db-check | Verify/import in memory without writing a database |
| cargo make db-generate | Generate a base candidate under target/db-workflow/generated |
| cargo make db-classify | Validate offline CC-CEDICT labels and generate a NEW enriched candidate; no install |
| cargo make db-install | Install the latest successful candidate; never generate implicitly |
| cargo make db-ai-smoke | Diagnose single-sense and 100-sense LM Studio output; no data/cache writes |
| cargo make db-full | Import offline CC-CEDICT classifications, generate enriched bundle and install (LM Studio opt-in) |
| cargo make db-full-dev | Run db-full, then start Trunk |
| cargo make serve | Start Trunk using the installed bundle |
| cargo make dev | Generate, install and serve in that order; stop on failure |

For explicit review and installation stages, run `cargo make db-generate`,
`cargo make db-classify`, then `cargo make db-install` in that order. The
classification step imports and checks the bundled JSON, then builds a **new**
classified candidate and updates `target/db-workflow/latest.json`; it does not
edit the first candidate in place or replace the installed database. The
installer always uses the latest candidate, and can still install a base
candidate when classification has not been run. Do not mistake a successful
rule-based import for expert-reviewed classifications.

Each run prints absolute candidate/database/backup paths. The latest successful
candidate is recorded in target/db-workflow/latest.json. Installation validates
policy, every declared file's size/hash, required reports/notices and the pinned
INPUTS.toml before any replacement. It stages and rechecks the complete bundle,
backs up the previous crates/zipeek-web/static under target/db-workflow/backups and restores
that backup if publication fails. Candidate/backup directories are retained.
Unsafe paths, symlinks, missing notices and checksum mismatches are refused.
Copy the whole bundle, never just hanzi.duckdb. These operations are explicit
local tasks, not Trunk hooks or application startup behavior.

Direct generator commands remain available:

```powershell
# Show help and examples; no database is written
cargo run -p zipeek-db-gen --locked -- --help

# Verify sources, native engine/storage and import in memory; write no database
cargo run -p zipeek-db-gen --locked -- check

# Write a full bundle to a NEW directory
cargo run -p zipeek-db-gen --locked -- generate --output target/reviewed-dictionary
```

A bare cargo run -p zipeek-db-gen now displays Clap help, does no import/generation and
returns usage status 2. Previously it imported in memory without writing a file;
that behavior is now the explicit check command. Successful check ends with
"No database file was written" plus the generation command to use next.

Generate prints the absolute output directory before work and the absolute
hanzi.duckdb and hanzi.manifest.json paths after success, even if informational
logging is disabled. Relative --output paths resolve from the current working
directory. Paths with spaces can be quoted. --help and --version exit successfully.

## Default output and existing directories

```powershell
# Uses the repository crates/zipeek-web/static directory; only works if it does not exist
cargo run -p zipeek-db-gen --locked -- generate
```

The default is repository-relative crates/zipeek-web/static, independent of the shell's working
directory. Its normal checked-in existence means this command refuses to overwrite
it. Use an explicit fresh review directory for regeneration. Existing outputs are
always refused; there is no implicit overwrite or --force option.

## Review and replacement

1. Generate into a fresh review directory.
2. Compare hanzi.manifest.json, ordered logical rows, schema, indexes and
   hanzi.diagnostics.json against the current crates/zipeek-web/static bundle. Database file
   hashes can differ with identical logical content under D22.
3. Preserve a backup of the previous complete bundle. Never patch database bytes
   or replace only the database without its corresponding reports/notices.
4. After approval and verification, replace the complete crates/zipeek-web/static bundle:
   hanzi.duckdb, manifest, diagnostics, INPUTS.toml, ATTRIBUTION.md and notices.
5. Repeat the applicable native/read-only and pinned browser compatibility checks
   in [browser-db](../../testing-quality/e2e/browser-db.md). Old compatibility evidence does
   not automatically validate a new artifact.

The approved sources/schema/dependencies do not change merely by regeneration.
Native generation requires v2.0.0 and v2.0.0 storage compatibility before output
creation. Artifact export checks complete logical equality and read-only reopening.

## Static serving and measured size

Trunk copies crates/zipeek-web/static contents to the distribution root. The Pages database
URL remains /zipeek/hanzi.duckdb; development uses /hanzi.duckdb. Reports and
notices accompany the database. The earlier A05 snapshot had 12,100 readings (historical, not the installed manifest),
514 diagnostics and a 3,158,016-byte database; file size is not a performance claim.

## References

- [Sources and notices](sources.md)
- [Import rules](import-rules.md)
- [Artifacts](artifacts.md)
- [Logical reproducibility](reproducibility.md)
- [Generator module](../../architecture/modules/db-gen.md)

## source-tag normalization and deferred inference

The primary HSK feed uses ICTPOS-style subtypes that the 42 canonical labels
cannot represent losslessly. `import/pos_mapping.rs` handles source-specific
normalization without weakening `PartOfSpeech::from_source_code`:

| Source code | Source meaning | Canonical label | Tradeoff |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `qv` | Verbal/event measure word | `classifier` | Subtype collapsed |
| `qt` | Temporal measure word | `classifier` | Subtype collapsed; not automatically a `time_word` |
| `mq` | Numeral-measure expression | `numeral` | Multi-PoS construction collapsed to single canonical label |
| `cc` | Coordinating conjunction | `conjunction` | Coordination subtype collapsed |

Unknown codes outside the reviewed set still produce diagnostics and do not
invalidate the whole entry. The mappings describe **source-level metadata**, not
AI-derived sense labels. Revisit `mq` and `cc` if the canonical taxonomy gains
additional subtypes. Reference: ICTPOS 3.0 tag descriptions in
https://github.com/memect/kg-beijing/wiki/%E4%B8%AD%E6%96%87%E8%AF%8D%E6%80%A7%E6%A0%87%E8%AE%B0%E9%9B%86 .

`zipeek-db-gen classify` now defers empty/invalid JSON/taxonomy outputs after the
existing three-attempt classifier policy, continues the normal pass, and tries
those deferred senses once more at the end (again at most three attempts).
Reports are JSONL next to the model cache at `<hash>.failures.jsonl`, with
sense ID, original gloss, model, v3 prompt identity, attempt count, error and
Unix timestamp. Successful classifications retain the same model-specific
cache; neither prompt version nor taxonomy version changes.

`zipeek-db-gen classify` may finish with nonzero `Remaining` and `Deferred` while
returning successfully for its batch. `db-full` independently calls
`classify-plan` and refuses generation **and installation** until `Remaining=0`.
Running the command again retries the still-pending senses; it does not accept
empty classifications or invent missing labels. Fatal transport, cache, and
storage failures still abort the batch immediately. The diagnostic report is
recreated for the current run and cleared when all attempted senses recover;
if interrupted, the last saved report survives until the next run begins.


### Offline AI classification V4 (2026-11-04)

**Developer-only db-gen workflow.** No learner-facing route, AI dashboard, or public model endpoint is added. `zipeek-db-gen classify` sends complete batches of *senses*, not words, to the configured local LM Studio model. The standalone `classify` CLI defaults to 20 senses/request; the `db-full` workflow defaults to a conservative 2 senses/request pending live verification; override with `--batch-size 10`, `20`, `40`, or another positive size up to 100. `ZIPEEK_AI_BATCH_SIZE` controls the `crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/ai_workflow.rs` orchestration; `ZIPEEK_AI_MODEL`, endpoint and timeout retain existing semantics. Context capacity (30k tokens) is not a promise that a 100-sense response fits the output-token budget.

The V4 system prompt distinguishes English sense glosses, grammatical functions and category evidence, prohibits cross-sense label leakage, and treats lexical relationships and source annotations as data rather than an excuse to infer additional semantics. `results` must contain **exactly one** record per requested `(word_id,sense_order)`, no unexpected/duplicated IDs, and only allowed labels. All records are validated before any records from a request are checkpointed. On malformed output or invalid classification, a multi-sense request is split into halves recursively (iteratively scheduled), while single-sense fallback uses the previous bounded recovery procedure. Non-recoverable model/transport errors abort with previous checkpoints intact; malformed single-sense output is deferred and reported.

The Rust workflow now uses a **V6-specific** `<model-hash>-v6.jsonl` cache and adjacent per-sense checkpoint directory. Do not point V6 generation at a V5 cache: old prompt labels are intentionally reclassified, not silently reused, and old checkpoint filenames collide with new records. Cache identity remains model + prompt version + taxonomy version + digest; individual accepted records remain usable after interruptions. `db-full` refuses to generate/install the database until classify-plan reports zero pending senses. The base DuckDB schema, deterministically extracted lexical relations and schema generator are unchanged.

**Benchmark before increasing batch sizes.** Compare 10, 20, 40, and optionally 100 on the same representative set including polysemous senses, function words, classifiers, proper names and explicit lexical relations. Capture wall time, accepted senses/minute, requests, retries and deferrals. The CLI logs `generated_senses_per_minute` and `requests`; record local model and generation settings with the benchmark. Observe response completeness and classification precision, not only throughput. No benchmark measurement against the user's LM Studio model is claimed in this checkpoint.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/dictionary-data-schema-regeneration.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.

# Reproducibility

The logical database reproducibility rule. Part of the
[database documentation](db.md). Approved in
[D22](../../project-management/decisions/database-and-artifacts.md#d22-logical-database-reproducibility).

## Logical reproducibility (D22: approved 2026-10-26)

D22 replaces the former byte-identical-output requirement. The inspected
[DuckDB 1.4.3 file writer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/duckdb/duckdb/v1.4.3/src/storage/single_file_block_manager.cpp)
contains `GenerateDBIdentifier` using `RandomEngine`; `CreateNewDatabase` calls it
when encryption is enabled or the selected file storage version is at least 67.
The identifier is serialized into the main header. This is conditional: it does
not prove every unencrypted older-format file is nondeterministic. Exact storage
settings have not been selected or exercised, and byte identity is not established.

**Approved D22 rule:** require identical ordered logical rows, IDs, schema/index
definitions, and import/drop diagnostics for identical verified inputs and pinned
tooling. Record SHA-256 of each final artifact for integrity without requiring
different builds to have the same file hash.

CODING_STANDARDS and TESTING now use that logical-content rule. Do not patch, mask,
or hand-edit database headers to force checksums to match. A05 must compare
independent runs at the logical level and record each artifact checksum; physical
checksum equality is not the reproducibility acceptance criterion.

## What "logical" means

The reproducibility contract compares:

- Every column of every row, in `ORDER BY id ASC` order.
- Assigned IDs 1..N, in that order.
- Table, column, constraint, and index definitions.
- The ordered `ImportDiagnostic` list (applied/ignored/unresolved warnings,
  rejections, conflicts, pipe transformations).

It does **not** require:

- Identical `.duckdb` file SHA-256 across runs.
- Identical checkpoint metadata, page ordering, or header bytes.
- Identical file sizes.

## Why files may differ

DuckDB's file writer can generate a random database identifier and serialize it
into the main header when encryption is enabled or storage version ≥ 67. This is
why D22 is logical-only. Any future requirement for byte identity would need a
different storage configuration, which is not approved.

Do not:

- Patch or mask header bytes to make checksums match.
- Hand-edit a database to make logical comparisons pass.
- Declare reproducibility satisfied because one run's SHA-256 happens to match
  another's.

## Where it is verified

- A05 artifact tests: independent exports compared row-by-row, schema-by-schema.
- A05 evidence: `target/a05-repeat` vs `web/static/`, with matching logical hash
  and differing physical hash.
- D22 policy is enforced in the generator at every full-source export.

See [artifacts.md](artifacts.md) for the concrete hashes from the A05 run and
[../../testing/provenance.md](../../testing-quality/e2e/provenance.md) for the required
reproducibility checks in any future regeneration.

## Related

- Artifact export and evidence: [artifacts.md](artifacts.md).
- Coding standards reference: [../../process/CODING_STANDARDS.md](../../engineering/coding-standards.md).
- Testing plan: [../../testing/provenance.md](../../testing-quality/e2e/provenance.md).
title: Reproducibility

The installed [`hanzi.manifest.json`](../../../crates/zipeek-web/static/hanzi.manifest.json) and [`db-gen policy.rs`](../../../crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/policy.rs) agree.
- Native generator engine: **`v2.0.0`**; explicitly written disk storage: **`v2.0.0`**. Neither is the browser's running engine version; Debug obtains the latter from the runtime connection.

The source ZIP contains the manifest and diagnostics but not the generated `.duckdb` or `.duckdb.gz` files.
