- The browser-facing dictionary service in [`services/database/runtime.rs`](../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/services/database/runtime.rs) owns typed SQL metadata queries, including `pragma_database_size()`. UI code does not receive a public generic SQL runner.

# Generated dictionary schema

**Implementation contract:** [`crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/schema.sql`](../../../crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/schema.sql) is the exact DDL. The installed manifest's `tables`, `columns`, `constraints`, `indexes` and `rows` report the generated artifact. This document summarizes the implementation; it does not replace the SQL.

## Compatibility projection: `words`

The ten original display/query columns still exist: `id`, `simplified`, `traditional`, `pinyin`, `pinyin_numeric`, `english`, `part_of_speech`, `hsk2_level`, `hsk3_level`, and `frequency`. `id` is a generated integer PK, `(simplified, pinyin)` is unique, and HSK level indexes are `idx_words_hsk2` and `idx_words_hsk3`. `english` and `part_of_speech` are compatibility/display fields; do not assume they fully model sense provenance or taxonomy.

HSK 2.0 permits levels 1-6; HSK 3.0 stores combined 7-9 as 7. A nullable HSK level is valid for the **extra CC-CEDICT readings**: the old rule that every word must belong to an HSK set is obsolete.

## Normalized source and enrichment relations

The generator DDL defines `dictionary_versions`, `vocabulary_identities`, `characters`, `character_readings`, `word_characters`, `word_hsk_membership`, `word_pos_membership`, `word_senses`, `sense_display`, `sense_relations`, `classification_runs`, `sense_pos`, `sense_categories`, `parts_of_speech` and `categories`. The last two are controlled seed/taxonomy tables. **Installed-manifest evidence:** `character_readings` is present in the top-level table list. This verifies the manifest declaration, not the physical contents of a database binary that is absent from the source archive. Enrichment is not inferred to be complete merely because the tables exist.

- `character_readings` stores source-explicit readings separately from vocabulary-word characters and supports polyphonic characters.
- `vocabulary_identities` records candidate keys/status; it does **not** establish portable learner WordIds across regeneration.
- `word_senses` and relation/category tables distinguish provenance and sense-level metadata from the legacy pipe-separated English projection.
- `sense_display.sense_kind` is the generator-owned, non-null classification (`lexical`, `usage_reference`, `cross_reference`). The source `word_senses.gloss` remains unchanged. A usage-only pronunciation such as 上 shǎng is retained for lookup but is not an ordinary meaning-recognition exercise candidate. This column requires a completely regenerated dictionary; there is no migration.
- `word_hsk_membership` preserves HSK associations independently of the compatibility level columns.

See [`schema.sql`](../../../crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/schema.sql) for each key, foreign key and check constraint. The prior single-table/HSK-only and “no CHECK constraints” declarations are historical plans and must not be applied to the installed database.

## Scope and verification

[`generator.rs`](../../../crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/generator.rs) imports HSK and expands with verified CC-CEDICT. [`artifact/writer.rs`](../../../crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/artifact/writer.rs) copies normalized tables and verifies a reopened snapshot before publication. The installed manifest currently reports **120,970 `words` rows**; see [database index](db.md) for exact installed metadata. Generated artifacts are replaceable read-only data. Personal Word Sets, temporary Practice progress and any future evidence ledger are separate browser-owned data.

Proposals for further FTS, index or learning schema redesign belong in [schema review](review.md) and [personal data](personal-data.md), not here as already-implemented columns.
title: Generated dictionary schema

# Sources

Pinned primary HSK vocabulary and CC-CEDICT fallback **and supplemental reading expansion**, licensing and provenance. Part of the [database documentation](db.md). Approved source selection
in [D16](../../project-management/decisions/database-and-artifacts.md#d16-primary-import-and-ids);
licensing policy in [D06](../../project-management/decisions/database-and-artifacts.md#d06-sources-and-licensing).

## Primary: pinned HSK vocabulary snapshot

Use [jelleverheyen/hsk-vocabulary](https://github.com/jelleverheyen/hsk-vocabulary)
`complete.json` as the HSK source for forms, levels, PoS, frequency, pinyin and English. The current generator also parses CC-CEDICT for gloss fallback, valid extra readings and explicit character pronunciations; it does not import every raw CC-CEDICT entry indiscriminately. Do not import superseded leonsilicon packages.

Pinned commit: **`a66fd30b9580da2c2af7eb19e4b9d8099a29c061`** (2025-02-28).
Use the [immutable JSON URL](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jelleverheyen/hsk-vocabulary/a66fd30b9580da2c2af7eb19e4b9d8099a29c061/complete.json),
not a moving branch URL. Audit on 2026-10-26 found 11,494 entries and 12,655 forms,
with no missing display/numeric pinyin at the form level. These are source counts,
not an already-generated database. Case-sensitive reading-key grouping yields
12,188 distinct `(simplified, numeric_pinyin)` keys; 394 keys have repeated forms.

The pinned [LICENSE](https://github.com/jelleverheyen/hsk-vocabulary/blob/a66fd30b9580da2c2af7eb19e4b9d8099a29c061/LICENSE)
declares MIT with a 2023 Yanis Zafirópulos notice; its README carries a 2025 notice.
Retain the supplied copyright and permission notices when distributing data.
The [source README](https://github.com/jelleverheyen/hsk-vocabulary/blob/a66fd30b9580da2c2af7eb19e4b9d8099a29c061/README.md)
also attributes dictionary definitions to CC-CEDICT, so the repository's MIT
declaration does not erase upstream data provenance. Preserve CC-CEDICT attribution
and applicable upstream notices alongside the dataset's MIT notice. Record actual input checksums and transformations in the generator provenance.

The earlier missing-license audit of leonsilicon HSK packages remains in COMPLETED
history. Those packages are no longer selected, so that package-specific blocker
does not apply to this import plan. Do not fetch or redistribute them as substitutes.

## CC-CEDICT licensing and attribution

The [CC-CEDICT download page](https://cc-cedict.org/editor/editor.php?handler=Download)
declares [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/) and
recommends verified releases from
[MDBG](https://www.mdbg.net/chinese/dictionary?page=cc-cedict). D21 approved the
A24 snapshot and its notices; A25 preserves those input bytes and provenance in
`crates/zipeek-db-gen/data`. The verified files are part of the generator source workflow and are imported into the checked-in expanded dictionary. Preserve exact licenses and source bytes.

The user reported an older homepage/download discrepancy of 3.0 versus 4.0; on
2026-10-26 the [homepage](https://cc-cedict.org/wiki/) also declared 4.0. Preserve
the historical note and do not relabel an older snapshot whose terms differ.

Required attribution in README and the visible site footer remains:

> Chinese dictionary data from CC-CEDICT ([cc-cedict.org](https://cc-cedict.org/)), licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

Retain the primary dataset's MIT notice as well as applicable CC-CEDICT notices.
The approved derived-data distribution policy remains CC BY-SA 4.0 for the
generated database containing CC-CEDICT-derived content, with transformations
documented. Application code retains its own licence. Source selection does not
replace checking the actual notices and upstream provenance of acquired inputs.
README credits are documented; the visible footer is implemented in `AppFooter`.

## Accepted fallback snapshot (D21)

Downloaded from the official
[MDBG release link](https://www.mdbg.net/chinese/export/cedict/cedict_1_0_ts_utf-8_mdbg.txt.gz)
on 2026-10-26 at 14:47:06 UTC, into temporary audit storage only. The release
page and file header agree on 125,320 entries and publication timestamp
`2026-10-26T02:33:39Z` (header epoch 1792982019), format version 1/subversion 0,
traditional/simplified UTF-8. The header identifies MDBG, CC BY-SA 4.0, and the
original CEDICT copyright of Paul Andrew Denisowski (1997, 1998). The
[official release page](https://www.mdbg.net/chinese/dictionary?page=cc-cedict)
and [CC-CEDICT download page](https://cc-cedict.org/editor/editor.php?handler=Download)
support that provenance; the actual downloaded header was also inspected.

| Input bytes | Size | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Official gzip archive | 3,982,067 | `bf50c9b8944fb6dce62c1dc3923d189ce11957c97e7ccda8dcb8435bb079b060` |
| Decompressed CC-CEDICT text | 9,868,269 | `3d8967fe566bc23a74f8ba008d38ac83269a8c7550bd7dc48218fc9bdf284885` |
| Existing D16 primary complete.json commit a66fd30 | 9,668,204 | `fc474be223d2196b13bfc7c13e10054f1793c2f840eb1287dfc9620fa0d507d2` |

Python hashlib and PowerShell Get-FileHash independently agreed on all three
hashes. Gzip decompression and strict UTF-8 decoding passed. Counting nonempty,
noncomment dictionary rows gives 125,320, matching the header; this is not a
count of imported fallback rows or generated words. The fallback text has CRLF
line endings and no UTF-8 BOM; preserve those bytes if pinning its checksum.

The official download URL is moving, not immutable. D21/A25 preserve the exact
uncompressed text as `crates/zipeek-db-gen/data/cc-cedict-2026-10-26.u8` and the pinned
primary JSON as `crates/zipeek-db-gen/data/hsk-complete-a66fd30.json`, with
path/URL/date/size/SHA-256, notices and transformations recorded in
`crates/zipeek-db-gen/data/MANIFEST.toml`. Path-specific `.gitattributes` entries with
`-text` prevent Git changing input bytes. The complete fallback header, primary
MIT notice/source README and full CC BY-SA 4.0 licence are preserved beside the
inputs, with `ATTRIBUTION.md` and manifest checksums. These are working-tree
inputs for review, not web assets or a committed/generated DuckDB database. The
Rust preparation pipeline now loads this manifest, validates its policy, and
verifies every source and notice before exposing their bytes for parsing.

The accepted source-preservation choice matters: a checksum identifies bytes
but cannot make a moving URL reproduce them later. Subsequent acquisition must
reject differing bytes; reuse the approved preserved snapshot rather than
silently updating to the newest export. Manual source acquisition/decompression
is separate from the offline generator, which now verifies every declared input
and notice before any source parser can receive the retained bytes. No dataset
is added to app assets automatically; generation stays manual.

## Excluded sources

Do not use Wiktionary, the noncommercial Anki deck, or the superseded leonsilicon
packages. No additional data source or runtime dependency is installed by D16.

## Related

- Import rules applied to these sources: [import-rules.md](import-rules.md).
- PoS mapping applied during import: [pos-mapping.md](pos-mapping.md).
- Dependency pins used with these sources: [generator-deps.md](generator-deps.md).

# Nonblocking vocabulary eligibility calculation

## Requirement

Eligible vocabulary counts may require substantial HSK, category, part-of-speech, source and global-exclusion filtering. **No eligibility count, pool preparation or validation may freeze the browser main thread.** An asynchronous Rust future that performs a long synchronous calculation without yielding does not meet this requirement.

## Data semantics

Compute the count from the currently selected vocabulary source and filter combination, including exact-entry global exclusions, not an unfiltered dictionary total. Preserve OR semantics among selections within a filter group and AND semantics between applicable groups according to the actual configured source. Count dictionary identities without accidentally double-counting aliases or joined HSK memberships. Exclusion applies to the complete vocabulary entry, never arbitrary substrings.

## Request lifecycle

- Run costly work outside the UI event loop, preferably in a worker supported by the existing database runtime, or in explicitly bounded yielding batches where a worker is not possible.
- Give each filter revision a generation/request identity. Cancel prior work when possible; otherwise ignore stale results after cancellation, unmount or newer filter changes.
- Show a visible progress component while computing. Use measured phases/batches for determinate progress and an indeterminate state when meaningful progress cannot be measured. Never invent a completion percentage.
- Permit continued editing, navigation, keyboard interaction and screen reader use during calculation.
- Cache equivalent results when beneficial, invalidating when dictionary source, personal Word Sets, exclusions or relevant filter definitions change. Cache keys must not conflate sources or leak user data.
- Distinguish `calculating`, `counted zero`, `counted positive`, `cancelled`, `failed` and `stale` states. A failed count must never be rendered as zero.
- Offer Retry for failures and an accurate diagnostic without exposing private data. Do not silently broaden HSK or Word Set scopes to manufacture available entries.

## Session-launch boundary

The optional displayed count must not block wizard navigation. Starting a session still requires successful eligibility validation; if necessary, show an explicitly cancellable preparation state while validation completes. A confirmed empty pool yields a clear error, while an exhausted but nonempty pool follows the globally configured reuse-or-finish policy. User-visible responsiveness is required in both cases.

## Acceptance

Test rapid filter changes, active cancellation, late/stale response arrival, exclusions updated from another view, cache invalidation, database failure, zero eligible entries, large-dataset performance, and navigating away mid-calculation. Capture the progress widget in the E2E evidence suite and separately verify main-thread responsiveness under load; no numerical timing guarantee is implied without measured performance targets.

See [vocabulary selection](vocabulary-selection.md), [setup](../../learning-practice/practice/practice-session-builder.md) and [E2E coverage](../../testing-quality/e2e/e2e-requirements-matrix.md).
title: Nonblocking vocabulary eligibility calculation

# Vocabulary selection and exclusions

## Selection principles

This document defines approved target behavior, separate from current source verification. Vocabulary selection, exposure history and learning evidence are three distinct concerns.

With pedagogical mode enabled, prioritize **rarely encountered words with recent meaningful mistakes**, then **unseen words**, then words with unresolved partial correctness. Repeated successful assessments lower their priority, while mastered words remain eligible for occasional review. A historical mistake must not permanently outrank newer successful evidence. Use only actual assessment verdicts to affect learning evidence.

With pedagogical mode disabled, favor less recently visited eligible words using persisted visitation history. Exposure records do not imply proficiency. Share the underlying visitation store across vocabulary-driven activities where feasible, while allowing activity-specific ranking and bounded history policies. Do not reuse a game's 100-entry cap as a global Practice cap without capacity analysis.

If multiple multiple-choice formats are enabled, distribute those formats approximately evenly over the session. Honor the enabled set, the configured length, accessibility and vocabulary prioritization. Exact equal counts are not required when the length is not divisible by the number of formats.

## Global exclusions

An exclusion applies to one **exact vocabulary entry**, preferably identified by a stable dictionary key. Excluding `好` does not exclude `你好` or `好吃`. Exclusion is a deliberate user preference, not proof of mastery. Excluded entries remain discoverable in Dictionary and Word Sets.

Manage, search, add and restore exclusions in **Word Sets > Excluded vocabulary**. In **Practice Setup > Vocabulary**, display the number of selected-source entries excluded and a link to the manager, but no bypass toggle. Apply the exclusion list always, regardless of selected HSK bands, saved Word Sets or active profile. During an active session, apply changes to subsequently generated exercises. Excluding the current exercise's word is compatible with Skip and Replace; for multiword exercises, ask which vocabulary entry is meant.

## Global pool exhaustion policy

The preference lives in **Settings > Learning > Vocabulary selection**, not Practice Setup. Default: **Reuse eligible words**, preferring least recently visited eligible entries and varying contexts when possible. Alternative: **Finish early** when all unique eligible entries have been used. Persist the preference globally and snapshot it when starting a session so changing Settings does not unexpectedly alter an active session.

When eligible words exist but none is unused, follow the configured policy. When exclusions and source constraints leave **zero eligible words**, explain that no content can be generated, regardless of policy. Never silently override exclusions or expand beyond the selected HSK or Word Set source. A skip cannot endlessly recreate the identical prompt; use bounded retries and explain an exhausted selection pool.

## Storage and privacy

Store global exclusions and visitation locally through the established application storage abstraction. Validate loaded identifiers and data structures. Keep exposure, submitted outcomes, and course acquisition evidence separate. No automatic server transfer of personal histories. See [visitation architecture](vocabulary-visitation.md) and [acceptance](../../testing-quality/acceptance/approved-behavior-acceptance.md).
title: Vocabulary selection and exclusions

search_text:
# Vocabulary visitation and selection boundaries

## Responsibilities

A shared browser-local vocabulary visitation service records exposure without interpreting it as mastery. Each entry should identify a canonical vocabulary item and preserve most recent visit order and bounded visit frequency. The storage schema and capacity must be validated; different games may use different rotation windows, but the underlying API must not let one game's eviction policy silently discard all Practice history.

The selector consumes eligible vocabulary, global exact-entry exclusions, current session constraints, exposure history and, when enabled, separately stored pedagogical outcome evidence. Do not let game-specific randomness or local-storage handling leak into core assessment logic. The selector must be testable with deterministic inputs, and tie breaking must be stable for a fixed session seed.

Model exposure, assessment attempts and mastery as independent typed records. A visited word is not a scored word. An exercise skipped without submission does not award mastery. A previously scored mistake stays in evidence even if the learner skips a subsequent attempt. Recent successes can lower review priority without deleting prior evidence.

Apply the global Settings pool-exhaustion policy captured at session start. Do not expand outside the vocabulary source, ignore exclusions or spin indefinitely on an exhausted pool. Maintain a bounded replacement search with a clear no-eligible-content state. Browser-storage failures must degrade safely and transparently, without fabricating persisted history.

This document is the target architecture, not a claim that a shared manager already exists. See [vocabulary requirements](vocabulary-selection.md) and [learning evidence](../../learning-practice/practice/learning-evidence.md).
title: Vocabulary visitation and selection boundaries

# R591 complete-source content inventory and technical-debt triage

## Scope and level of assurance

**Input:** `zipeek-R590-WIP-statistics-chart-state-audit-20261119-152512.zip`.

**Coverage:** Every one of the 11,010 input archive file bodies was read. The file ledger includes path, byte size, SHA-256, detected kind, structural findings and content-derived indicators. All Rust and JavaScript source files were read and scanned for relevant code patterns. JSON files were parsed, image files structurally verified, and the bundled Hanzi Writer data was cross-checked at record level. The refreshed scan of the updated checkout is generated separately with `node scripts/source-content-audit.cjs`.

**Assurance boundary:** This is exhaustive **file-content coverage**, not a complete proof of semantic correctness for 152,454 lines of Rust. Automated scans do not establish the correctness of every function or UI interaction. The source archive has no accompanying compiled-build or browser evidence, and the environment has no `cargo`, `rustc`, `rustfmt`, Clippy or browser runner. No file is labeled semantically verified without executable tests and review. A high number of pattern matches is not evidence that each match is a defect.

## Complete-file inventory

| Content group | Input count | Verification |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Rust source (`.rs`) | 973 | UTF-8 read, content-pattern scan, function/state/panic/unsafe indicators, per-file digest |
| JSON documents (`.json`) | 9,608 | Complete JSON parse and per-file digest |
| Other text/configuration/source | 376 | UTF-8 read, type-sensitive syntax/shape checks, per-file digest |
| Images (`.png`, `.webp`, `.ico`) | 50 | Image decode/structure check and per-file digest |
| UTF-8 dictionary source (`.u8`) | 2 | UTF-8 decode and per-file digest |
| WASM binary | 1 | WASM magic and per-file digest |
| Total | 11,010 | Every input member examined |

The VS Code `.vscode/settings.json` uses JSONC with trailing commas, which is supported by VS Code but rejected by strict JSON parsers. This is a format exception, not corrupt application JSON. All 9,608 other JSON documents parsed successfully. All 50 images passed a Pillow structural integrity check in the audit environment. The 9,574 per-glyph Hanzi Writer JSON records match the 9,574 records inside `all.json`; all stroke and median counts agree. `radStrokes` is absent in 556 records and is not required for the stroke/median contract.

The separate file ledger records content evidence for each path. Keep it as audit evidence, not as a Rust test result. The reproducible scanner lives at `scripts/source-content-audit.cjs`, and a dedicated data consistency check lives at `scripts/hanzi-dataset-audit.cjs`.

## Executed checks

| Check | Result | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full input-file read, hash and classification | 11,010/11,010 processed | Every input file body was inspected programmatically |
| Strict JSON parse | 9,608/9,608 passed | JSON syntax only, not domain semantics |
| Image structural verification | 50/50 passed | Image decoder accepted input images |
| Hanzi combined vs individual records | 9,574/9,574 equal | Source duplication is internally consistent |
| Hanzi stroke/median lengths | 9,574/9,574 valid | Shape contract holds |
| Node offline suites | 16 passed, 0 failed | Only the three offline audit suites |
| Node JavaScript syntax checks | 33/33 passed with module-aware check for worker ES module | Syntax only, not runtime behavior |
| Source asset integrity | Passed with two generated database artifact notices | Source mode, not deploy readiness |
| Docs validator before fixes | 4 active errors | Included broken maintained link, historical links and stale index |
| Docs validator after fixes | 0 active errors, 3 frozen-history warnings | Validates current docs and generated index |
| Rustfmt, Clippy, native/WASM compile, Rust tests, browser E2E | Not run | Required release blockers |

## Concrete corrections in R591

1. `docs/learning-practice/practice/settings-workspace.md`: replace obsolete `services/ai/config.js` reference with the actual `zipeek-browser/src/ai_configuration.rs` module. The API key lives in Rust thread-local browser memory, not a deleted JS config module.
2. `scripts/docs-validate.cjs`: classify paths under the frozen `docs/archive-history/` tree as historical warnings, rather than incorrectly treating some historical source snapshots as maintained-document blockers. Current document links remain strict errors.
3. `crates/zipeek-web/static/docs/index.json`: regenerate the bundled docs index to match maintained source files.
4. `scripts/source-content-audit.cjs`: add reproducible full-source per-file content and digest reporting, with no third-party dependencies.
5. `scripts/hanzi-dataset-audit.cjs`: add reproducible per-glyph and combined dataset consistency checking.

No Rust implementation logic, dependencies, databases, stored user data or public routes were changed. The correctness and architecture debt below remains open.

## Risk-ranked outstanding code findings

These are source-identified review targets, not proven bugs unless explicitly described as such.

| ID | Priority | Scope and evidence | Unresolved action | Confidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A01 | Blocker | No Rust/WASM compile or browser evidence for successive Statistics architecture checkpoints | Run locked workspace tests, formatting, Clippy, WASM and root/Pages E2E on exact candidate | Verified evidence gap |
| A02 | High | `crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/system/stats/grammar/page.rs` and `stats/explorer/page.rs` duplicate generation/query/cancellation state for bulk selection | Extract and test shared typed request lifecycle; prove query changes and unmount cannot commit stale selections | Source-confirmed architecture debt |
| A03 | High | `stats/state/mod.rs` holds coupled reducer fields including selected preview string IDs | Audit each reducer action invariant; introduce canonical typed identities before Practice and Word Set integration | Source-confirmed architecture debt |
| A04 | High | `crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/practice/local_session.rs` combines setup, generation, scoring and session UI lifecycle | Function-by-function ownership review with reducer-transition and failure tests | Review required |
| A05 | High | `crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/system/settings/mod.rs` owns a large Settings workspace | Review component and preference ownership and split only independent responsibilities | Review required |
| A06 | High | `crates/zipeek-web/src/services/personal_data/{backup,storage,opfs}.rs` and Practice session store parse and persist browser-local learner data | Fault-inject invalid/truncated backups, quota failures, repeated writes and cancellation; verify readback and deletion | Risk boundary, not confirmed flaw |
| A07 | High | AI endpoints, response parsing, streaming, and model payloads in `zipeek-ai-client`, `zipeek-ai-protocol`, `zipeek-web/src/services/ai` | Validate external-input budgets, redirect and URL behavior on native/WASM and malformed responses | Risk boundary, not confirmed flaw |
| A08 | High | CLI archive unpacker at `crates/zipeek-cli/src/archive/unpack.rs` now has entry/size/path/symlink controls | Execute the Rust archive-limit and restore/rollback tests; test file collisions and partial failure on Windows | Existing mitigations source-confirmed, not tested here |
| A09 | Medium | Chart hook at `stats/overview/lifecycle.rs` derives chart accent at initialization but its effect key follows weekly buckets | Verify theme changes do not leave stale chart color; select explicit theme dependency if required | Potential UI defect |
| A10 | Medium | Dialog focus helper supplies Tab wrapping but background inertness and nested dialog behavior are not browser-verified | Run keyboard, screen-reader and mobile browser acceptance, both base paths | Verification gap |
| A11 | Medium | `crates/zipeek-exercises/src/cloud_match.rs`, `crossword.rs` and `time_weaver.rs` are large domain gameplay modules | Check deterministic state transitions, failed generation and replay handling with seeded tests | Maintainability and correctness review |
| A12 | Medium | `crates/zipeek-db/src/lib.rs` declares crate-level `allow(dead_code)`, `allow(unused)`, `allow(private_interfaces)` | Check which lint suppressions are actually needed, narrow them once compiling | Source-confirmed lint debt |
| A13 | Medium | `crates/zipeek-pedagogy/src/curriculum/vocabulary.rs` is a 5,658-line curriculum source | Verify editorial data constraints and split source data only when useful, not for arbitrary line counts | Editorial maintainability review |
| A14 | Medium | Browser `unsafe` extern import wrappers at `zipeek-browser/src/charts.rs` and `zipeek-db/src/lib.rs` | Confirm JS/WASM signatures and import error paths with actual WASM build | Reviewed wrapper pattern; not assumed vulnerability |
| A15 | Medium | Historical docs contain three broken source links, preserved as frozen history | Keep warnings discoverable; no retrospective rewriting of source evidence | Historical warnings acknowledged |

## Cross-crate review register

This table records which areas were inventoried, which contained concrete risk indicators, and where semantic verification remains necessary. **Content scanned** means every file body was read by the audit; it does not mean every function passed a human or compiler review.

| zipeek-core | 26 | 3,591 | Practice domain invariants |
| zipeek-db | 19 | 2,992 | Native/WASM facade and lint suppressions |
| zipeek-db-gen | 62 | 8,976 | Data ingestion, generators and deterministic outputs |
| zipeek-docs | 3 | 445 | Sanitization of Markdown/HTML |
| zipeek-e2e | 135 | 24,777 | Coverage and reproducibility |
| zipeek-exercises | 71 | 14,744 | Seeded engines and transitions |
| zipeek-geo-assets | 9 | 1,530 | External geometry validation |
| zipeek-hanzi-writing | 9 | 1,507 | Stroke/recognition correctness |
| zipeek-image-server | 11 | 1,296 | Inference resource management |
| zipeek-pedagogy | 20 | 12,772 | Curriculum contracts and generated worker data |

| zipeek-tts-stt | 4 | 704 | Microphone/TTS external boundaries |
| zipeek-ui | 1 | 3 | Placeholder crate necessity |

## Reproducibility and interpretation

```powershell
node scripts/source-content-audit.cjs target/source-content-audit.jsonl
node scripts/hanzi-dataset-audit.cjs
node --test scripts/tests/*.test.cjs
node scripts/asset-integrity-audit.cjs
node scripts/docs-validate.cjs
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p zipeek-web --locked
```

The first command emits a path-by-path evidence ledger, including source patterns, hash and verification exceptions. Node source checks can detect broken files and flag risky constructs, but cannot certify Rust ownership, lifetime, concurrency, sanitization, UX or runtime behavior. No clean Rust build or application-wide debt-free claim is supported by the present evidence. Future fixes require compiler and behavior gates before acceptance.

# Coding standards

Conventions for application code. Process rules live in [AGENTS](../../AGENTS.md);
testing strategy in [testing/TESTING.md](../testing-quality/acceptance/testing.md); architecture in
[architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md](../architecture/architecture.md).

## General principles

- **Prefer clarity over cleverness.** A reader should understand the code without
  tracing types across files.
- **Fail loudly in development, gracefully in production.** `unwrap` / `expect` is
  acceptable in tests and unreachable branches; never in request handlers, DB
  queries, or user input parsing.
- **No silent fallbacks for correctness bugs.** If a query returns unexpected
  data, log it. If a computation can fail, return `Result`, don't `Option`-swallow
  it.
- **Preserve intent when editing.** Do not refactor adjacent code to "clean up"
  while fixing a bug; keep diffs focused.
- **Derive UI affordances from typed state.** Do not hide or enable actions by matching user-facing error-message text; pass explicit props from reducer-backed containers.
- **Keep pagination contracts shared.** Query limits, lookahead checks and displayed results must use the same page-size constant.

## Rust

### Formatting and lints

- `cargo fmt --all` - mandatory, no exceptions.
- Clippy checks deny warnings; use affected packages/targets during routine
  work and workspace/all-targets for full regression under AGENTS §6. Avoid `#[allow(...)]` without an approved technical reason. Do not add code comments. Prefer resolving the lint through code changes.
- Edition 2024, Rust 1.97.1 (see `rust-toolchain.toml`).

### Readability of expressions and match arms

- Keep match arms on separate lines when a match has multiple variants. Do not
  compress whole match expressions or control-flow branches onto a single line,
  even if Rustfmt accepts it.
- Format multi-step closures, error handling and long function calls as readable
  multi-line blocks. Short single-expression closures may stay inline when clear.
- Prefer `const fn` for genuinely compile-time-capable pure methods, such as
  enum-to-static-string mappings; do not mark functions `const` merely to save lines.
- Treat `cargo fmt` as the minimum formatting requirement, not permission to
  squeeze several logical operations onto a single line.

### Imports and qualification

- Prefer explicit `use` declarations at module scope for externally defined types,
  traits, functions and constants used in implementation logic. Group related
  imports clearly and keep application code focused on behavior rather than
  repeated module paths.
- Use a qualified path when it resolves ambiguity or materially improves clarity,
  including naming conflicts and one-off references. Do not use wildcard imports
  except for established preludes or intentionally scoped test imports.
- Keep imports needed by a module at its boundary rather than inside event
  callbacks, effects or render expressions. Preserve a local import only when
  its limited scope serves a concrete purpose.

### Modules and platform API boundaries

- A stateful browser integration such as microphone capture must separate the
  public recorder API, owned state, event/capture wiring, waveform processing,
  and error conversion when those concerns become substantial. Keep the parent
  `mod.rs` limited to exports, shared constants, and module declarations.
- Keep JavaScript-API return types faithful to the pinned `web-sys` signatures.
  In particular, `BlobEvent::data()` is `Option<Blob>`; handle absent chunks
  without panicking, and pass `blob.as_ref()` to `js_sys::Array`.
- Keep tuple fields private by default. A sibling module requiring controlled
  construction should use a `pub(super)` constructor, not a public inner field.
- Keep source tests aligned with extracted module files; never weaken runtime
  assertions just to satisfy a source-layout assertion.
- Preserve single-field tuple structs for opaque ownership wrappers where
  they express the abstraction clearly, such as `MicrophoneRecorder(Rc<RefCell<State>>)`.
- When moving code to submodules, preserve public imports, existing behaviors,
  and test coverage. Source assertions must follow the actual module graph,
  rather than forcing code back into a large parent file.
- A source-level Node pass is not a substitute for a target-specific Rust build;
  WASM/browser APIs require `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`
  and browser acceptance before a release can be considered verified.

### Stateful Yew feature components

- Use `#[function_component]` and a typed `Properties` contract for standalone
  UI components; do not expose positional rendering helpers with many unrelated
  arguments (`view(board, feedback, hint, complete, ...)`).
- Keep feature-specific modules inside a named directory (`feature/mod.rs`,
  `feature/board.rs`, `feature/state.rs`) rather than accumulating sibling files
  such as `feature_board.rs` next to route files.
- Keep the route page responsible for URL decoding and data loading. A session
  owner manages interactive state; tiles, controls, progress and results are
  focused components. Use a scoped typed context and reducer when several
  nested components need the same state and actions; do not introduce global
  state for a single game.
- Model transitions as reducer actions with explicit guards. For advancing to
  another round, generate the next board before committing the counter and
  cumulative scores. Never mutate half a session on a failed transition.
- Retain stable `data-*` hooks, `aria-pressed`, keyboard-accessible buttons,
  and difficulty-dependent Hanzi font sizes through refactors.
- Preserve the domain engine in a pure Rust crate without `web-sys`, Yew or
  JavaScript dependencies. Split domain model, generation, gameplay and tests
  when they have separate reasons to change.

### Naming

- Types, traits, enums: `PascalCase`.
- Functions, variables, modules: `snake_case`.
- Constants and statics: `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`.
- Acronyms: `Url` not `URL`, `Api` not `API`, per Rust API guidelines.
- Domain types: `Word`, `CandidatePool`, `RoundFilter`, `HskSystem`, `Hsk2Level`,
  `Hsk3Level` - no `Data`, `Info`, `Item` suffixes.
- Error types: `BuildError`, `DbError`, `LoadError` - not `Error` or generic names.

### Errors

- Public functions returning fallible operations use `Result<T, E>` with a
  domain-specific error enum.
- Use `thiserror` for error enums (already a dependency). Do not use `anyhow`
  in library code; it's permitted only in `db-gen`'s `main.rs` if needed for
  user-facing errors.
- Errors must be actionable: include the offending input where possible.
  - Bad: `Err(BuildError::InsufficientPool)`
  - Good: `Err(BuildError::InsufficientPool { view: View::Strict, found: 5, needed: 8 })`

### `unwrap` / `expect` / `panic!`

- **Allowed:** in unit tests, in `const fn` when the failure is a compile-time
  error, and in demonstrably unreachable branches with self-explanatory types or control flow.
- **Not allowed:** on `Result`/`Option` from user input, DB queries, network
  calls, or parsing external data.
- Required provider contexts are component-tree invariants: `use_context::<RequiredContext>().unwrap()` is allowed when the parent route always mounts that provider. A missing provider is a programming defect, not a user-facing recoverable condition.
- Never panic on user input, database operations, localStorage, network failures, or other recoverable conditions in a Yew component or handler; render an error state or return a typed error instead.

### Modules and file organization

- One module per file. `web/src/components/foo.rs` not `web/src/components.rs`.
- Public API goes through `mod.rs` re-exports where it improves ergonomics
  (e.g., `pub use round::{build_round, CandidatePool, RoundFilter};`).
- Pure logic lives in `zipeek-core` when shared between `web` and `db-gen`;
  otherwise local to its crate.
- WASM-specific browser access (DOM, `js_sys`, `web_sys`) belongs in
  `zipeek-browser` or the `zipeek-db/wasm` adapter when it is not Yew-specific.
  Yew rendering stays in `zipeek-web`. `zipeek-core` must compile natively.
- **Rust/WASM-first browser implementation:** Implement Zipeek-owned application behavior,
  state, validation, async orchestration, resource lifetime and cleanup in Rust.
  Prefer typed `web-sys`/`js-sys` APIs. If a browser feature or third-party
  library needs JavaScript, use the smallest `wasm-bindgen` interop boundary,
  normally `inline_js`, with typed Rust-facing functions and opaque newtypes
  for external objects. Do not add handwritten `.js` service layers merely to
  call another JavaScript module or to hold application state.
- **Exceptions are intentional:** Pinned third-party JavaScript/WASM assets
  (including D35 Chart.js and DuckDB-WASM), build scripts, test probes, and
  minimal pre-WASM bootstrap remain supported. Preserve their packaging and
  licenses. Distinguish a permitted vendor module from application logic.
  See [Rust/WASM browser interoperability](../architecture/modules/rust-wasm-interop.md)
  for ownership, newtype, dynamic-import, lifecycle and verification rules.

## Yew

### Tailwind styling (D31)

Tailwind CSS 4.3.4 remains the required component styling approach. A35 corrected
the shell/card stylesheet drift on 2026-10-28: mounted components use utilities,
main.css holds theme aliases and minimal foundation rules, and inline.css retains
critical bootstrap/loading styling. Rust source detection is explicit; the
unused v3 configuration and bespoke shell/card selectors are removed.

- Use Tailwind utilities in Yew markup for layout, spacing, sizing, typography,
  borders, responsive rules and interaction states. Keep conditional variants as
  complete class strings that Tailwind can detect; do not construct class names
  from fragments at runtime.
- Keep shared theme/design tokens in CSS where appropriate and consume them
  through utilities. Preserve the slate/blue theme and landscape composition.
- Allow focused custom CSS for critical pre-WASM bootstrap styling, shared
  tokens, keyframes or a concrete effect that benefits from it. A reason for one
  exception does not justify moving ordinary component styling into stylesheets.
- Do not hide the same bespoke component system behind blanket @apply rules.
  Factor repeated UI into Yew components and small explicit utility variants.
- Verify Tailwind 4 source detection for Rust/Yew files and remove obsolete
  conflicting rules as components migrate. Do not assume legacy v3 configuration
  is automatically active or upgrade packages during the correction.

The implemented styling boundary and visual checks are in
[UI_ARCHITECTURE](../architecture/ui-architecture.md#tailwind-styling-implementation-d31--a35).

### Components

- One component per file, function components only (no classes).
- Props are `#[derive(Properties, PartialEq)]` structs.
- Use `#[function_component]` with a clear component name matching the file
  (`WordCard` in `word_card.rs`).
- Avoid prop drilling past 2 levels; use contexts.
  The 2026-10-27 review's concrete provider/reducer proposal is in
  [UI_ARCHITECTURE](../architecture/ui-architecture.md). Shared services and
  feature state belong behind scoped hooks/providers; simple leaf inputs still
  use props. Do not expose raw state setters as another feature's public command
  interface.

### Yew presentation composition

- Import components explicitly at the module boundary (`use crate::components::{BrowseProvider, WordSetsProvider};`) rather than repeating qualified paths in `html!` markup. Wildcard imports are not required for component composition.
- Write nested providers and other multi-element Yew trees across multiple lines, with each element's closing tag aligned to its opener; do not compress provider nesting into one line.
- Keep page-specific callback conditions and view-building chains readable with normal Rust multiline blocks, even where the formatter would tolerate a dense expression.
- For nontrivial status-specific markup, compute `let status_component = match &state.status { ... };` before the parent `html!` and insert `{status_component}` in the shallow outer view.
- Extract meaningful loading/error/empty, result-card, and pagination views into focused components. Prefer keeping short related status components in one module over one file per line of markup.
- Container components access reducers/providers and wire callbacks; presentational components take focused `Properties` and do not reach into unrelated feature contexts.
- Keep stable `data-component` and existing `data-*` E2E hooks during refactors.

### Hooks

- `use_state` for temporary form input local to the owning component; use a pure `use_reducer` plus a scoped provider for shared feature state and interdependent transitions. Keep I/O in the provider/service, never inside `Reducible::reduce`.
- `use_effect_with` for side effects, with explicit dependency lists - do not
  use empty dependency lists unless the effect is genuinely once-only.
- `use_memo` for derived state that's expensive to compute; do not memoize
  cheap operations.
- `Callback` for event handlers passed to children; `use_callback` when the
  identity matters (prevents unnecessary re-renders).

### State ownership and refactor discipline

- A page with multiple interdependent request/output/error/loading fields should use
  a typed `Reducible` state machine. Independent controls such as a font preference
  may remain `use_state`; hook count is a review signal, not an automatic failure.
- Reducers must be pure. Network requests, browser storage and DOM operations stay
  in effects, callbacks or services; render state transitions are dispatched
  atomically, with stale asynchronous results rejected using request epochs.
- Place substantial reducer implementations in a feature-local `state.rs` module.
  Do not replace independently managed hooks with a large mutable "controller"
  that merely hides the same coupling.
- Split oversized presentation trees into focused feature components or view
  functions. Prefer short, named sections to nested 100-line `html!` expressions.
  Keep event types explicit (`FocusEvent` for focus, `MouseEvent` for clicks).
- A module declared as `mod foo;` may use either `foo.rs` or `foo/mod.rs`, never
  both. Parent modules named `foo.rs` may own child files `foo/bar.rs` without
  a second `foo/mod.rs`; do not use `#[path]` to paper over moves.
- A source-only Node suite does **not** validate Rust syntax or type checking.
  Before declaring a refactor compiled, run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`,
  `cargo check --workspace --locked`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, Clippy,
  and the WASM target. Report unexecuted checks explicitly.

### Events and handlers

- Never `unwrap` on `event.target_dyn_into::<HtmlInputElement>()` - the DOM can
  change. Use `if let Some(el) = ...`.
- Every interactive element has a keyboard equivalent (Enter/Space for buttons,
  arrow keys for navigation). See UX.md's accessibility section.

### Async

- Use `wasm_bindgen_futures::spawn_local` for fire-and-forget effects, or
  `use_async` patterns for stateful async work.
- Do not block the render loop. Long queries go through a state machine
  (Idle → Loading → Ready / Error), never a synchronous await in render.

## Shared crate (`zipeek-core`)

- Must compile on both `wasm32-unknown-unknown` and native.
- No `web_sys`, `js_sys`, `wasm_bindgen` imports.
- No I/O - it holds types and pure logic only. Queries take data as arguments,
  not a DB handle.
- Public API is versioned by the repo, not semver; breaking changes to
  `zipeek-core` are fine during development (AGENTS.md §2).

## Database generator (`crates/zipeek-db-gen`)

- Native binary; runs manually, never in an app build.
- Reads pinned inputs only - no network calls. Source fetching is a separate
  shell script (see DB.md).
- Verifies SHA-256 of every input file against `MANIFEST.toml` before parsing;
  aborts on mismatch.
- Logs every dropped word, unknown PoS code, level conflict, and gloss-pipe
  replacement.
- D22 requires deterministic logical output: identical verified inputs and
  pinned tooling produce the same ordered rows, IDs, schema/index definitions,
  and import/drop diagnostics. Record SHA-256 for each final `hanzi.duckdb`
  artifact as an integrity check; different runs need not have identical file
  bytes. Do not patch or mask database headers to force a matching checksum.
- Before generation, query `SELECT version()` against the native
  engine, log the returned version, and fail unless it is exactly `v2.0.0`
  (D23 supersedes D21's earlier v1.4.3 condition). Configure and verify
  `storage_compatibility_version = v2.0.0` before creating output; check the actual installed runtime and artifact format rather than relying on an older compatibility claim. Future artifact creation
  must use this configured connection and explicitly compatible storage.
  This is a generator invocation check, not a Cargo build script or an
  automatic application-build generation step.

## Tests

- Unit tests in the same file as the code (`#[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }`)
  for pure logic.
- Integration tests in `tests/` for cross-module behaviour.
- Test names describe the scenario, not the function:
  - Bad: `test_build_round`
  - Good: `build_round_returns_insufficient_pool_when_strict_view_is_small`
- Fixtures live in `tests/fixtures/` as data, not inline structs, when larger
  than ~20 lines. See TESTING.md's fixture patterns.
- Golden tests (round builder, seed encoding) assert both the input string and
  the expected output hash - see ROUND_GENERATION.md for the contract.

## E2E component selectors

- Give significant mounted Yew page and feature roots a unique, stable
  `data-component="kebab-case-name"` value. Prefer identifying the component
  (for example, `browse-page`) rather than its current heading or CSS layout.
- Use `data-action` for controls where action identity improves testing, and
  `data-state` or an existing dedicated `data-*` attribute for observable state.
  Retain semantic roles, accessible labels, and native keyboard behaviour.
- E2E selectors must not infer a route from an incidental tag structure or
  placeholder once the route renders a real component. Placeholders may still
  be asserted for genuine unimplemented or not-found routes.
- Preserve existing test-specific attributes during gradual migration; no
  dependency or round-URL format changes are required.

## Documentation

Code carries no doc comments and no explanatory inline comments. The code
should be self-explanatory through naming and structure; if a reader needs a
comment to follow it, the fix is clearer names, smaller functions, or an entry
in the relevant `docs/` file.

- No `///` doc comments on functions, types, or modules.
- No `//` explanatory comments above or inside code.
- `// TODO:` and `// FIXME:` comments are also forbidden. If work is needed,
  add a task to `TASKS.md` and reference it in the commit message or PR body.
- Rationale and design decisions live in `docs/architecture/architecture.md`,
  `docs/games/round-generation.md`, `docs/dictionary-data/schema/db.md`, or the
  relevant decision record - not in the source tree.
- No comment exceptions apply to lint suppressions or unreachable branches. When a lint allowance is necessary, record rationale in maintained technical documentation and obtain approval for the change.

## Feature module organization

- Put feature-specific Yew components under `components/<feature>/`; Practice has
  `setup/`, `exercises/` and `session/` subdivisions. Generic primitives remain at
  the component root. Pages live under `pages/<feature>/`, keeping stable route
  module names through explicit Rust `#[path]` declarations where appropriate.
- Preserve existing public reexports while moving implementation files. Avoid
  adding icon abstractions: use `yew_icons::{Icon, IconData}` directly in views.
- Only use icon constants present in the pinned `yew_icons` inventory.
  Verify icon identifiers against the currently pinned `yew_icons` crate and compile affected Rust views. Historical icon fixture details are preserved in the linked source snapshot.
- When moving files, update the owning `mod.rs`, import paths, source-contract
  tests and living documentation in the same change. Do not move files merely
  to shorten individual names or add wrappers without an actual dependency need.

## Additional implementation review contracts

- **Required contexts:** Trace the actual provider tree, routes, tests and callers before changing `Option<T>` hooks to required accessors. Required providers should have an explicit accessor contract and actionable absence diagnostics; intentionally optional providers remain optional. A provider's runtime loading/failure state is not its absence.
- **Workflow state:** Identify authoritative, derived, transient, request and persisted state before major refactors. Verify coordinated resets, invalid states, overlapping requests, stale callbacks and lifecycle cleanup; use a reducer only when it clarifies the invariant.
- **Markup and events:** Keep `html!` markup expanded and reviewable, name callbacks before markup rather than constructing them in attributes, and prefer typed callbacks over avoidable DOM parsing. If DOM `data-*` routing is justified, validate values, choose `current_target` when appropriate and test nested clicks and keyboard activation.
- **UX and accessibility:** Preserve shared shell, tokens, icons, semantic controls, focus, touch and keyboard behavior, and explicit loading/failure/recovery states. Inspect rendered UI when available; compilation alone does not verify usability.
- **Async performance:** Review browser work, cancellation, stale results and cleanup before adding timers or workers. Use measurable evidence before claiming performance improvements; deferring synchronous computation does not make it nonblocking.
- **Source audits:** For material findings cite file/line evidence, observed behavior, concrete impact, minimal remedy, priority and remaining uncertainty. Avoid judgments based only on line count, hook count or stylistic preference.
- **No legacy compatibility:** The development-phase policy in [AGENTS](../../AGENTS.md) applies to all historical formats. Deterministic current behavior, input validation and intentional handling of local data loss remain required.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/engineering-coding-standards.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.

> **Source ownership described in this guide:** Grammar teaching tables, guided-check data, region plan and published slugs now live under `crates/zipeek-pedagogy/src/grammar/`. Patterns 21-100 are generated there from `docs/learning-practice/GRAMMAR_CURRICULUM_SOURCE.tsv`. # Courses authoring and structural validation

The five published grammar courses are teaching drafts, not verified HSK syllabus coverage or authoritative mastery assessments. This guide explains how to add a course without leaving its registry, teaching activities and assessment formats inconsistent.

## Source ownership

| Source | Authoring responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/zipeek-pedagogy/src/grammar/curriculum.rs` | Grammar explanations, examples, translations and original five guided three-choice banks |
| `courses/curriculum_registry.rs` | Stable course and grammar-point IDs, local sequence and prerequisites; official HSK status remains unverified |
| `courses/guided_bank.rs` | Guided sentence-builder and transformation banks, accepted tile sequences and feedback |
| `courses/assessment.rs` | Independent draft multiple-choice item for each registered point |
| `courses/construction_assessment.rs` | Independent unassisted sentence-construction draft for each authored course |
| `courses/authoring.rs` | Cross-format structural validation (`validate_published_courses`) and detailed failures |
| `courses/grammar_lesson.rs`, `courses/grammar_expansion_lesson.rs`, `courses/grammar_lesson_scaffold.rs` | Two teaching engines sharing navigation and progress shell; Yew-only course interaction |

## Adding or editing a grammar course

1. Author nonempty titles, explanations, examples and translations. Avoid claims of verified HSK syllabus coverage without an independently checked source.
2. Add a stable curriculum registry entry with the same course identifier and one point ID per authored grammar point; verify prerequisites refer to earlier published courses.
3. Author exactly one guided comprehension check and one independent draft MCQ per point. The independent question should not rely on a visible guided answer.
4. Provide guided tile activities with nonempty metadata, a distinct bank and a full display permutation. Every accepted order must use unique in-bounds tile indices and leave at least one distractor.
5. Add an unassisted construction assessment linked to a point in that same course. Do not repeat a tile or include a reference answer during the attempt.
6. Update `GuidedCourse` region mapping, mosaic region/link and course route. Update the E2E scenario and coverage inventory.
7. Run the structural validator's unit test and the existing Courses tests, then compile natively, compile WASM and run Chrome E2E on the pinned toolchain. A passing Node source-contract test alone is **not** Rust or browser acceptance.

The validator catches missing or duplicated authored identifiers, blank content, invalid question keys, duplicate choices, incomplete point coverage, malformed tile permutations, duplicate activity IDs, and cross-course construction-point mismatches. These are **structural safeguards only**: they do not prove pedagogical fairness, meaningful distractors, translation quality, accessible presentation or a qualified review of the Mandarin.

## Explicitly out of scope

No validation result is a mastery grant. Draft scores remain in memory; all 150 mosaic regions stay concealed. Award rules, verified evidence/provenance, DuckDB writes, completed grammar records, and artwork-reveal predicates require their separately approved implementation and browser acceptance.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/engineering-courses-authoring.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.

# Docs Markdown renderer

The `zipeek-docs` crate uses `pulldown-cmark =0.13.0` with the `html` feature and no default CLI features. The existing Yew application calls it through Rust/WASM directly; there is no separate browser JS parser or WASM module.

## Syntax and security

CommonMark nested lists, fenced code, links and references, GFM tables, task lists, strikethrough and footnotes are supported. Rust emits deterministic unique heading IDs and exposes the same headings to the Docs TOC. Raw HTML becomes escaped text. Links are checked against a safe external-scheme and docs-root policy, including reference-style destinations. Invalid image targets render a placeholder.

All files in `docs/` remain published. `#/docs/` links and `/zipeek/` asset base behavior are preserved. Links to headings in another Markdown document use `#/docs/<encoded-path>?heading=<heading-id>` so the hash router receives one valid route. The Docs page scrolls to the heading after rendering, including direct links and reloads. Same-document `#heading-id` anchors remain local to the article.

## Acceptance

```powershell
cargo test --locked -p zipeek-docs
cargo check --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p zipeek-web
cargo run --locked -p zipeek-cli -- build docs
cargo make serve
```

In Chrome, verify nested Markdown, footnotes, checkboxes, tables, raw/source toggle, duplicate headings, CJK heading IDs, internal links, relative images and browser security under `/zipeek/`. These checks have not run here. TD-006 remains open until this the historical source route/scroll behavior and prior renderer behavior pass locked WASM and real-browser acceptance.

## Static publication

Trunk copies `../../docs` directly into the published `docs/` directory via the
`copy-dir` entry in `crates/zipeek-web/index.html`. No duplicate Markdown tree
is maintained in `static/docs`. `cargo make docs` generates only
`crates/zipeek-web/static/docs/index.json`, which the Docs explorer uses for
navigation and search; run it after editing documentation or during first-time
setup. `cargo make setup-all` includes this preparation. `cargo make serve`
does not regenerate the index on every invocation. CI and deployment continue
to generate the index before building. GitHub Pages uses the same relative
`docs/` assets under `/zipeek/`.

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/engineering-docs-markdown-renderer.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.

# Statistics state ownership audit, R590 WIP

## Evidence and scope

Inspected the R589 source tree, particularly `stats/overview/chart.rs`, `overview/activity.rs`, `overview/breakdown.rs`, `stats/context.rs`, `stats/state/mod.rs`, `stats/query_hook.rs`, and Grammar/Vocabulary explorer page owners. This is a targeted state-management and correctness review, not a complete proof of correctness across the workspace. No Rust toolchain or Chrome session was available. Source observations below are not compiler or browser evidence.

## Ownership findings

| Area | Observed R589 source | Audit outcome | R590 treatment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Overview chart | One component owns two booleans (`ready`, `error`), a Chart.js handle, a stale-task guard, the async effect, fallback markup, and dialog visibility | Two booleans permit invalid/ambiguous status combinations, and concerns are unnecessarily coupled | Introduced `ChartStatus::{Loading, Ready, Unavailable}` and `overview/lifecycle.rs`; fallback moved to `overview/fallback.rs`; breakdown visibility stays local |
| Chart cancellation | A per-effect `Rc<Cell<bool>>` guard checks whether an async completion belongs to a still-mounted effect | This guard is appropriate in single-threaded WASM; not inherently unnecessary state | Retained guard and destroy-on-cleanup ownership pattern in the lifecycle hook |
| Fallback accuracy | A minimum 8% bar height was applied to zero-count weeks | Visually implies activity where there was none | Zero yields 0%; focused pure helper test authored |
| Chart instance | `use_mut_ref` retains `ChartInstance` without rerendering | Legitimate imperative-resource state | Kept in effect hook; explicitly drops previous retained chart before re-initialization |
| Breakdown visibility | Local `use_state<bool>` toggles one dialog | Appropriate ephemeral UI state | Kept local; no reducer action added |
| Async query pages | `use_query_page` stores `(query, QueryLoad)` and an effect-generation plus active flag | Stale query result protection exists; query/result association guards render | Preserve; evaluate redundant fields only after functional tests |
| Grammar/Vocabulary bulk selection | Each page duplicates active flag, query snapshot, generation counter, loading and error hooks | Maintenance and concurrency risk; query changes/cancellation need identical invariants | OPEN: extract typed reusable hook, with per-query tests and compiler validation; not mechanically edited in this checkpoint |
| DashboardState | Shared reducer owns selection, filters, pagination and overlay navigation; typed collections are separate in data layer | Some coupled transitions are appropriate; string identifiers and broad action interface remain debt | OPEN: action-by-action invariant audit, typed verified IDs at integration boundary; no parallel reducers invented |
| Chart theme | Effect dependency follows weekly buckets only, not accent CSS changes | Potential stale theme colors after switching theme; requires browser validation | OPEN: use explicit theme signal or observe theme changes after approved behavior contract |

## What must not be claimed

- Merely adding a `use_reducer` or extracting files does not establish good state management.
- `Rc<Cell<bool>>` does not make a component wrong by itself; it provides cleanup cancellation for futures whose underlying operation cannot be aborted.
- Static module checks and a successful ZIP CRC do not show that a Yew component compiles.
- No source-level change here proves correct chart behavior during theme changes, fast section switches or failed script imports.

## Validation requirements

```powershell
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --locked -p zipeek-web
cargo check --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p zipeek-web
cargo make release-check
```

Test `/` and `/zipeek/` bases where applicable. Open issues remain open until this evidence exists.

# Repository technical debt audit, 2026-11-19 (R588 WIP)

## Basis and confidence

Baseline is `zipeek-R587-WIP-shared-record-collections-20261119-144442.zip`. This audit inspected the root engineering, testing and release rules, workspace structure and selected high-risk implementation boundaries. A static inventory counted **970 Rust files** and approximately **152,175 Rust source lines** across 21 crates. This is not a line-by-line semantic or security assessment of every function. No Rust toolchain, WASM target or running Chrome session was available in the audit environment.

The three checked offline Node test suites returned **16 passes, 0 failures**. That result validates only those suites, not Rust code, browser interactions or the changes authored in this checkpoint. ZIP CRC and manifest checks are packaging integrity checks only.

## Fixes in this checkpoint

| Scope | Finding | Resolution | Acceptance evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `zipeek-cli` source unpack | ZIP extraction had path traversal and symlink guards but no bounded extracted size or entry count. A compressed archive could consume unexpectedly large disk space before stage validation. | Enforce at most 40,000 entries, 256 MiB per file and 2 GiB declared expanded data, with bounded copying and tests for count, file size and total size. | Source review; Rust tests authored, not executed. Baseline source ZIP totals ~225 MiB extracted with a largest entry ~52 MiB, inside limits. |
| Statistics Overview chart | Changing the weekly bucket data did not reset `ready` and `error` at the start of a new chart load; missing canvas could leave an unexplained placeholder. | Reset chart load flags on bucket changes and surface the existing failure fallback when the canvas cannot be resolved. | Source review; browser test outstanding. |
| Statistics Overview activity | The breakdown treated every category other than Practice as Games. This could mislabel unknown categories from future sources. | Count Games explicitly and leave unknown categories unclassified, with a focused regression test. | Test authored, not executed. |
| Release workflow | `cargo make release-check` exists, but a standard `cargo make pack` does not require it; previous source handoffs repeatedly bypassed compiler verification. | Added the explicit `cargo make pack-verified` workflow, combining the existing release-check gate with source packaging, without altering the lightweight native pack command. | Task configuration reviewed; cannot execute Cargo here. |
| README | Build instructions referenced `scripts/*.test.cjs` though tests are under `scripts/tests/`. | Corrected the executable Node test command. | Three offline test suites actually run successfully. |

## Open technical debt, prioritized

### Blockers: verification and contracts

- **Rust/WASM release gate:** R587 still has no successful compilation evidence. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, locked workspace tests, locked WASM check, lint and Chrome acceptance must run in a Rust-equipped environment. Source-level verification cannot substitute for them. This also applies to new R588 Rust edits.
- **Statistics learning transfer:** Selection uses preview string identifiers. Canonical Word Set and Practice transfers remain unimplemented. Do not silently map demo IDs to real records.
- **Statistics dialogs:** Selection review, Grammar details and Overview breakdown still lack a demonstrably shared focus containment and background interaction contract. Test Tab/Shift+Tab, Escape, restoration, and narrow-screen overflow before acceptance.

### Priority architectural debt

- **Large workflow owners:** `crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/practice/local_session.rs` (~799 lines), `crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/system/settings/mod.rs` (~645), `crates/zipeek-exercises/src/cloud_match.rs` (~1,103), `crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/system/stats/query.rs` (~612), `stats/grammar/page.rs` (~401), and `stats/state/mod.rs` (~484) need responsibility/invariant reviews. Their length alone is not a defect; do not mechanically create files to lower the counts.
- **Statistics reducer:** Shared filters, selection, overlay and section navigation state use one reducer. Retain atomic transitions. Prefer typed domain identities at integration boundaries and small pure helpers; do not introduce independent contexts without an actual shared-ownership need.
- **Query and demo scalability:** The current simulator caches shared immutable snapshots, but per-query sorting and lowercase string creation iterate the matching catalogue. Profile with 5,000/10,000 record scenarios before introducing caches or workers.
- **Native and browser trust boundaries:** Archive unpack has additional bounds in this candidate; browser storage and external API conversions still require targeted threat and invalid-input tests. This audit did not prove all such boundaries safe.
- **Safety/HTML policy:** Two Rust source files contain `unsafe {` blocks (`zipeek-db/src/lib.rs`, `zipeek-browser/src/charts.rs`). `zipeek-docs` sanitizes Markdown raw HTML and unsafe URLs before the web component constructs HTML; these remain future focused audit targets, not confirmed vulnerabilities.
- **Lint hygiene:** `zipeek-docs/src/lib.rs` contains crate-wide allow attributes. Review them under a functioning Clippy toolchain before narrowing/removing; do not blindly remove flags in an uncompiled checkpoint.

## Verification performed

- Read release naming and source unpack contracts, root development instructions, CI configuration and selected affected source.
- Reproduced the baseline source ZIP footprint statically and confirmed the new extraction limits exceed the native source archive's advertised size.
- Executed `node --test scripts/tests/e2e-evidence-audit.test.cjs scripts/tests/asset-integrity-audit.test.cjs scripts/tests/installation-workflow.test.cjs`: 16 passed, 0 failed.
- Tool availability: Node installed; Rust/Cargo/rustfmt absent. External Rust downloads were unavailable due to DNS resolution.

## Remaining acceptance commands (Windows, repository root)

```powershell
cargo make release-check
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo check --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p zipeek-web
cargo make e2e-full
cargo make pack-verified
```

The final packaging command is intentionally separate from compiling a numbered accepted release. A passed build still does not establish browser usability or production readiness. Do not mark this checkpoint accepted until the toolchain and browser gates complete.

## R589 continuation: overlay accessibility

Statistics Selection Review, Grammar detail and Overview breakdown now share a source-level initial-focus, Tab wrap and restoration helper. Forward/reverse boundary tests have been added but not executed. This is not an accessibility certification: Chrome keyboard focus, background inertness, screen readers and mobile behavior still require evaluation. The Rust/WASM gate remains unresolved. The two existing `unsafe` blocks were inspected and are WASM JavaScript import wrappers; they were not modified or classified as confirmed vulnerabilities.

# Character Hunt - exercise contract

Character Hunt is a dictionary-backed Hanzi assembly exercise. It is available without AI in Quick Practice (and also Advanced Practice) under **Exercises → Choose** and configured under **Exercises → Configure**. Its difficulty is stored in the Rust `PracticeDraft`, not selected again during gameplay.

| Difficulty | Grid | Hanzi typography |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy | 2 × 2 | 5xl mobile, 7xl desktop |
| Medium (default) | 3 × 3 | 4xl mobile, 6xl desktop |
| Difficult | 4 × 4 | 3xl mobile, 5xl desktop |
| Hardcore | 5 × 5 | xl mobile, 3xl desktop |

## Rules and generation

The pure Rust domain engine (`zipeek-exercises::character_hunt`) takes an eligible vocabulary snapshot, a difficulty, and a seed. It accepts distinct Simplified-Hanzi entries containing exactly two or three characters. It allocates character tiles from dictionary entries, shuffles them deterministically, and retains the validated word-to-tile mapping privately. Word groups do not share characters or tiles, so removing completed words never makes another target unplayable. The generator deterministically retries 32 candidate orders to avoid rejecting a solvable board merely because a greedy word selection dead-ended. If a board cannot be filled from the supplied words, generation fails visibly; it never inserts fabricated answer words.

A single noninteractive decoy character from the eligible vocabulary may fill an odd-sized grid when the source lacks compatible three-character words. If there is no unused source character, generation fails rather than inventing a filler. The decoy does not count toward the word total. Completed words are presented as Hanzi with an optional word-level pinyin reading and the dictionary-sourced English gloss (not merely a list of Hanzi). A completion message also identifies the word and its meaning. Alternative dictionary glosses are deduplicated and displayed together, capped at three to keep the card readable; missing definitions are marked unavailable instead of fabricated. Pinyin is withheld if source readings cannot be aligned or do not agree. Each non-decoy tile displays a large Hanzi with smaller dictionary-sourced pinyin beneath when word-level syllables align with the characters. Multi-pronunciation entries with conflicting readings do not display an arbitrary reading. In Easy/Medium/Difficult, the large Hanzi typography is preserved; Hardcore uses compact typography. Learners select two or three active tiles in order; a matching known entry grays out those tiles and records the word. Incorrect combinations increment a local mistake counter and reset the selection without removing tiles. Three consecutive mistakes briefly highlight the first tile of a remaining solution; after five, the entire 2-3-character solution briefly highlights for approximately 950 ms. After seven consecutive mistakes the user may explicitly reveal one word; revealed words count as completed but are tracked separately as assisted. A correct match resets the consecutive-mistake escalation. Automatic visual hints appear only on the third and fifth consecutive mistakes, then clear after 950 ms or immediately on the next tile interaction. The tile highlight is static rather than continuously pulsing. Manual Hint works only when no tile selection is in progress, so it cannot obscure an active attempt. The hint button is disabled until the partial selection is cleared or finished. Completion requires finding every hidden target. No user-generated text or AI model is needed for verdicts.

## Session integration

The existing four-step setup (`Path → Exercises: Choose/Configure → Vocabulary → Summary`) launches `#/practice/character-hunt` with difficulty and vocabulary source. It uses Fixed 5 by default, with Fixed 10, Fixed 20, and Endless available. The UI keeps difficulty fixed across boards and shows round-level progress, completed words, mistakes, and an explicit Next round action. Learners can deselect individual tiles by tapping them again without counting an incorrect attempt. Fixed session completion shows cumulative rounds, words found and incorrect attempts; these totals are only recorded after a board is completed. A new round uses a new seed and the same eligible source. Exit practice is separate from puzzle controls and asks for confirmation before abandoning an unfinished session. The final summary distinguishes assisted reveals from independently found words. In Quick Practice, selecting Character Hunt replaces the core Matching/MCQ selection and vice versa, because the standalone engines are not yet mixed in one session.

Dictionary selection now supports one or more HSK bands, category-only sources, and any approved combination of HSK bands, categories and parts of speech. The setup route serializes these as the same validated dictionary-filter token used by Practice. The Character Hunt loader decodes that token and calls a parameterized database query with the shared OR-within-group/AND-across-group predicate. The query selects two- and three-character entries only, with a deterministic 1,024-row upper limit to bound browser memory. A saved Word Set is loaded by exact IDs instead and does not inherit dictionary filters. Legacy single-HSK game links remain readable. Extremely restrictive filters can legitimately yield too few playable words; this produces an explicit board-generation error instead of silently broadening the vocabulary. Mixed Character Hunt/Matching/MCQ plans are **not** supported yet; the existing scored mixed-session planner remains unchanged. The game has its own round progression and does not claim to publish scores to the central planned-session ledger.

## Verification

Unit tests cover grid sizes, default difficulty, reproducibility, word completion, three-character words, invalid combinations and insufficient vocabulary. A Chrome journey checks Quick Practice setup, choosing Easy, selecting an additional HSK band, preserving both filters in the URL, then solving five 2×2 boards using only visible tile controls and checking the cumulative Fixed 5 summary. Database SQL tests assert shared filtering semantics for multiple HSK bands, category and part-of-speech intersections, and category-only sources. The browser tests and Rust/WASM compilation require execution on a machine with Cargo and Chrome; Node source regression tests alone are not sufficient.

## interaction and layout refinement

Gameplay has one bottom action bar: Hint/Reveal on the left and confirmed
Exit practice / Continue on the right. There is no Clear selection button:
re-tapping an already selected Hanzi deselects it, and invalid combinations
clear automatically. The practice round header shows the round and selected
difficulty without restating the grid dimensions.

The completed-word panel displays the exact dictionary-backed Hanzi, contextual
pinyin when available, English definitions and the shared Listen button for
audio playback. The completed-word list scrolls inside its panel on desktop,
without pushing the board or bottom actions offscreen. Progress is displayed
with a blue accessible determinate bar rather than native browser styling.
Both the game board and controls remain accessible by keyboard. Browser
viewport validation is pending.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/games-character-hunt.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.
