# Cloud Match

## Purpose and interaction

Cloud Match is a Chinese vocabulary matching game. Its presentation uses legible moving cloud tiles and consistent controls in the established Zipeek visual language. The game starts through its own setup route and makes gameplay, feedback and results distinct; the learner should not have to infer whether a match was accepted solely from the disappearance of a tile.

## Behavior contract

- Present readable Hanzi, corresponding meanings or other explicitly selected variants. Keep labels legible over the background and during movement.
- Show selection, accepted and rejected match states with accessible textual equivalents, not color alone.
- Keep motion and crossing paths stable. Controls remain keyboard-operable, and reduced-motion users get an equivalent non-moving path to complete the game.
- On exit, distinguish leaving a running game from discarding progress. Do not attribute successful learning evidence simply to game completion.
- Do not use content-specific progress or scoring as a substitute for the shared pedagogical evidence policy.

## Implementation boundary

Actual movement algorithms, match semantics and selected game settings must be verified in the game source before refactoring. See [games source audit](games-source-audit.md), [learning evidence](../learning-practice/practice/learning-evidence.md), and [testing](../testing-quality/acceptance/testing.md).

Historical source observations and prior visual experiments are preserved in [Cloud Match implementation history](../archive-history/audits/superseded-maintained/games--cloud-match-source.md).

## Learning progression

- Easy: locate provincial-level divisions from their Mandarin names. Show optional Pinyin and English reference during review.
- Medium: identify provincial-level divisions, their administrative seats, and region outlines. No invented provincial flags: the majority of mainland provinces do not have distinct official flags. Official symbols may be shown only with verified provenance and licensing.
- Hard: locate prefecture-level administrative divisions (prefecture-level cities, prefectures, autonomous prefectures, and leagues). Select the parent province first and then pick from a zoomed provincial map so touch targets remain usable.

The historic figure of 333 prefecture-level divisions is not a permanent dataset invariant. Display counts must be derived from the pinned geographic source. The source must state its census date, provenance, licensing, coordinate reference system, inclusion criteria, name translations and administrative codes.

## Data and acceptance requirements

- Version and bundle the map polygons locally instead of relying on a third-party server at play time.
- Use stable region codes for matching; display Chinese names and properly sourced Pinyin independently of polygon labels.
- Review legally reusable boundary geometry before committing it to the source archive. A GitHub repository license does not necessarily sublicense its upstream geographic data.
- Support polygons with multiple disconnected areas and maintain keyboard, pointer and touch selection.
- Separate geometry loading from pure game-state transitions. One game reducer owns the current prompt, selection, mistakes, review state and continuation; setup owns difficulty and learning-support options.
- Unit-test round generation and matching for every included code, including names that repeat at different administrative levels.
- Independently verify administrative seats/capitals; avoid using a single capital field for special administrative regions or municipalities without defining its meaning.
- No map route should be registered until a complete playable dataset and interactive hit-tested map are installed and validated.

## Gallery

The game gallery now shows six games per desktop page using previous/next controls, smaller cards and the same responsive grid. The gallery stays nine games until Province Quest is complete.

## Immersive gameplay presentation

Province Quest runs in the immersive game shell without the standard application header, drawer, or footer. The game provides its own accessible Exit and Settings controls. During play the map occupies available viewport space; map panning uses pointer dragging and wheel zoom, with accessible button alternatives. Results and choices remain keyboard-operable and review messages identify correct and incorrect selections in text, not color alone. Semantic map colors derive from the active theme. Geography provenance belongs in the maintained Credits page and distribution notices, not as a persistent label inside the map.

## R557 implementation boundaries

The `zipeek-exercises::province_quest::Session` domain remains the single scoring authority. A separate feature reducer coordinates setup selections, map asset loading and error states, active province selection, request invalidation, and session actions. The map owns only its typed viewport and pointer gesture state. Viewport math and drag thresholds are tested without browser APIs. Asynchronous load completion is accepted only for the active request generation. The UI retains keyboard map-region selection, immersive presentation and theme-driven semantic colors. Browser gesture acceptance remains necessary before considering the refactor complete.

## Hard-mode map navigation

The Hard-mode map renders a national overview immediately, rather than an empty map while waiting for parent selection. Selecting a province in the overview drills into its prefecture boundaries. The province selector lists only parent regions represented by usable prefecture geometry; an unpopulated administrative region must not produce a blank map. Returning the selector to its initial value shows the national overview again. Province navigation does not count as an answer.

The gameplay header uses accessible icon controls for leaving the game and opening settings, following the immersive game shell contract.

## R559 map gesture refinement

The SVG uses `preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"`. Wheel anchors and panning must therefore use the rendered map scale rather than the full rectangular SVG bounds, which may include letterboxing. Wheel deltas are normalized by delta mode and clamped per event. Dragging begins after a cumulative movement threshold; pointer capture starts on actual drag, preserving native region clicks and keyboard selection. Small incremental pointer moves must accumulate correctly. Zoom controls remain available as accessible alternatives.

## R560 region component contract

`RegionMap` owns viewport transforms, mouse-wheel/pointer gesture state and suppression of clicks after a drag. Its child `MapRegion` component owns one SVG path's theme-based visual state, accessible region label, pointer click, and Enter/Space activation. Child props reference the existing `Rc<GeoDataset>` and a stable region index rather than copy potentially large SVG path strings. Parent and child preserve the `data-region` hook and forward stable administrative IDs, not names or display indices. Event handlers bound directly to the SVG root may cast a present `current_target` from `EventTarget` to `Element` using `unchecked_into`; this assumption must not be reused for generic or delegated targets. Use named local `MapPoint` values for cursor and pointer geometry. Runtime browser verification remains outstanding.
title: Province Quest - approved feature contract

# Deterministic round generation (D12)

These approved requirements are implemented by A07 in `zipeek-core/round`. See
[PRODUCT](../product-ux/product.md) for the four-pair exercise and
[DECISIONS](../project-management/decisions/index.md) for approved source contracts (D18)
and the resolved v1 replay contract (D19). The pure builder and native/wasm golden
fixtures exist; A21 integrates database queries/normalization and calls the
builder. Playable UI remains A09/A10 work.

## Pure builder and candidate bundle

`build_round` is a pure function of `(CandidatePool, variant, filter, seed, offset)`.
It never queries DuckDB or reads the clock, localStorage, or ambient randomness.
It can be tested natively using plain Word fixtures.

The caller supplies three nested views:

```rust
struct CandidatePool {
    strict: Vec<Word>,
    hsk_widened: Vec<Word>,
    hsk_widened_any_pos: Vec<Word>,
}
```

strict: exact HSK system/level and requested PoS set.

hsk_widened: same system, original level plus valid adjacent levels, same PoS.

hsk_widened_any_pos: same widened HSK levels, with the PoS filter dropped.

strict is a subset of hsk_widened, which is a subset of
hsk_widened_any_pos. A wasm-side helper issues one DuckDB query per view.
Every query removes exclusions in SQL and includes ORDER BY id ASC. Do not
depend on implicit row order or substitute a Rust-side sort. Bind exclusion IDs;
an empty exclusion set needs no NOT IN predicate.

The caller also clamps HSK widening in SQL, never crossing systems:

Context	Widened levels, including original
HSK 2.0 level 1	1, 2
HSK 2.0 level 6	5, 6
HSK 3.0 level 1	1, 2
HSK 3.0 level 7 (combined 7-9)	6, 7
Intermediate levels include original +/-1 within the system's bounds. HSK 2.0
has no 7, and HSK 3.0 has no separate 8 or 9.

Try views in order: strict, widened HSK, then any PoS. Each matching attempt
must produce four correct pairs plus four distinct-label reserve distractors. Advance to the
next view if it cannot. All reserves remain internal; only four matching cards
on each side render.

Canonical seed input
Normalize raw URL inputs before calling the builder. For a seeded round, force
offset to zero at this boundary. For an unseeded round, retain the entered offset.
The formatter itself is a pure formatter with no offset policy.

text
zipeek-round-v1|{variant}|{hsk}|{level}|{pos}|{offset}|{seed}
All fields are hand-written ASCII tokens separated by |, with no extra whitespace:

Field	Encoding
Prefix	Literal zipeek-round-v1
Variant	Match: eng-pinyin, pinyin-hanzi, hanzi-eng; D20 MCQ: hanzi-to-meaning, meaning-to-hanzi, meaning-to-pinyin. Use an explicit seed_token() method, matching each variant route token.
HSK system	hsk2 or hsk3
Level	Unpadded unsigned decimal: 1-6 for hsk2, 1-7 for hsk3
PoS	Sort canonical lowercase token() strings, deduplicate, and join with commas; empty set is an empty field
Offset	Unpadded unsigned decimal; zero when unset or seeded
Seed	Decimal WordId, or literal lowercase none
Never derive fields from Debug, Display, iterator order, or HashSet ordering.
For PoS, explicitly collect tokens, sort_unstable, dedup, then join(",").
An absent seed encodes as literal none, never Debug's None or Some(...).
Empty PoS is no characters between separators, never {} or None. Equivalent
parsed filters must produce identical canonical bytes.

Apply D14's 64-bit FNV-1a to the canonical string's bytes; this string is the sole
hash input. Initialize rand::rngs::ChaCha12Rng::seed_from_u64(rng_seed) with
rand::SeedableRng in scope and rand's chacha feature enabled (D17).
StdRng is forbidden for round generation. Do not replace FNV-1a with DefaultHasher.

Documentation golden vector:

text
zipeek-round-v1|eng-pinyin|hsk3|3|noun,verb|10|none
fnv1a64 = 0xa0e531d76df62844
Under D19 (approved 2026-10-26), v1 is the only format version. There are no
v1 URLs outside development fixtures and no installed base to migrate. A future
replay break requires a v2 canonical prefix, a URL parameter selecting the format,
and a documented compatibility path, with explicit approval for the shared-URL
break. None of that v2 machinery exists today: do not add a v= parameter or
version parser speculatively. The earlier COMPLETED v2 forecast is superseded
by an append-only correction, not a commitment to implement v2 now.

Single-stream RNG and draw order (D19: approved)
AGENTS §5 is the authoritative contract if any
wording here conflicts. For each build_round, create exactly one
rand::rngs::ChaCha12Rng, seeded once with
ChaCha12Rng::seed_from_u64(fnv1a64(canonical_seed_input)). Recovery consumes
draws from this stream; generation continues from the resulting state. No reset,
no second RNG, no re-seed, including on candidate-view fallback. Never clone the
RNG to restart a phase. First-eligible-by-id recovery fallback consumes no RNG.

Before creating the RNG, apply D15's nonrandom URL validation: Fixed ignores a
seed; malformed, nonexistent, or URL-excluded seeds use unseeded canonical input
with seed=none and the entered offset. For a retained seed needing recovery,
canonical input uses the original URL seed and filter, with offset zero. Keep
that canonical input unchanged after recovery; the recovered ID and effective
context affect selection, not a second hash or initialization.

The caller parses inputs and supplies ordered data. The pure build_round
pipeline owns RNG initialization, recovery, selection, and shuffling; a recovery
helper borrows that same RNG as &mut ChaCha12Rng. The caller must not recover
with an independent RNG and then invoke a builder which seeds another one.
Ordered recovery data and original seed metadata are explicit pure inputs, not
hidden database queries. The implemented API is described below.

A08 implements the nonrandom boundary in zipeek-core/practice: decoded query
parsing, lookup-based normalization, Ready/Unseeded/RecoveryRequired disposition,
canonical v1 bytes and FNV-1a. RecoveryRequired preserves original seed/filter
with offset zero. These helpers never initialize or consume an RNG. A07's
build_round owns all recovery draws.

Implemented API (A07)
build_round(RoundCandidates, ExerciseVariant, &NormalizedPracticeQuery) returns
Result<Round, BuildError>. RoundCandidates borrows an initial CandidatePool,
the original seed row if retained, ordered/exclusion-clean recovery rows and
ContextPool entries for possible recovered contexts. For a Ready seed, initial
views must use its HSK/PoS context; unseeded views use the URL filter. Recovery
prefers HSK 3.0 membership and derives the seed's canonical PoS set, then selects
the supplied views for that context. It never performs a query or rehashes.
The original seed/filter remain canonical even when effective context changes.

The builder rejects unordered/duplicate IDs, inconsistent or nonnested rows,
excluded rows, wrong-system/level/PoS views and missing seed/context data with
actionable errors. It validates caller ordering rather than sorting the views.
SQL construction and exclusion binding remain A06 responsibilities.

RoundContent has Matching columns of four Cards, or an MCQ prompt and three
options with its correct ID. Card labels preserve display text; English uses
only the first stored pipe-separated gloss. Matching reserves never enter the
visible content. BuildTrace records recovery requests, view attempts, partner
and reserve requests, accepted IDs and rejection counts for diagnostics/replay
tests. It is not UI content or persisted state.

The 18 full-round fixtures in tests/fixtures/round-golden.txt lock canonical
bytes/hash, recovery, attempted/accepted IDs and final layouts. Their report
digest is a94efad5496532a0 on native and wasm32. Test-report Debug formatting is
not a URL or production serialization format. See
testing/round-builder.md for the executable wasm
check; it fails if pure fixture execution calls any host import.

Sampling primitive and recovery
Use rand 0.10.3's slice API, importing rand::seq::IndexedRandom:

rust
let candidate = ordered_candidates.as_slice().sample(&mut rng, 1).next();
Each candidate request uses exactly this sample call with amount 1. Do not
substitute iterator sampling, choose, deprecated choose_multiple, or combine
successive requests into a batch. An API request may consume multiple internal
RNG words; the locked order below is the order of API calls, not a promise of
one underlying RNG word per candidate. Check an empty pool before sampling.

Recovery makes at most ten such requests from the unchanged, id-ordered,
exclusion-clean recovery pool. Separate requests may select the same row again.
After each request, check membership and the selected variant's required labels;
stop immediately at the first eligible word. Do not consume the remaining
attempts after success. After ten ineligible candidates, take the first eligible
word by id without any RNG call. An empty pool or no eligible fallback fails
safely. Generation starts at exactly the stream position recovery leaves behind.
If recovery is unnecessary, it consumes no draws.

Generation and final shuffle
MCQ requires one prompt with its correct answer plus two distinct-answer
distractors, using the same view order; it does not require four correct pairs.

Try strict, widened-HSK, and widened-HSK-any-PoS views in that order. For each
view, all candidate slices preserve id ASC order. Eligibility/label checks,
unseeded window sliding, and offset wrapping consume no RNG. The sequence is:

Select correct content. Unseeded matching uses the first valid ordered
four-word window. Seeded matching puts the retained/recovered seed first,
then selects three partners using successive amount-1 sample calls. Start
with the view's ordered candidates excluding the seed; remove each sampled
row from that partner slice, preserving the order of the rest, even when its
right label collides. Accept distinct labels in sampling order; exhaust the
remaining slice safely if three partners cannot be found. MCQ selects its
one prompt at the ordered offset, or uses its retained/recovered seed;
prompt selection consumes no additional RNG.

Select distractors. After all correct content is selected, request four
reserve distractors for matching, or two distractor options for MCQ. Use
successive amount-1 sample calls on the unchanged active view, accepting
candidates in draw order. Reject correct IDs, the seed, and normalized answer
labels already used by correct content or accepted distractors. Count each
rejection against the existing per-view min(candidate_count, 50) retry
limit. Stop immediately at four accepted reserves or two accepted options;
do not make a fifth or third successful selection. Reserves never render.

Finish selection before shuffling. If the view fails, discard its partial
selection, continue to the next view from the current RNG position, and do
no shuffle for the failed view. Recover the seed only once, before view
attempts. Do not hash again or rewind for the new view.

Shuffle the successful result only. Import rand::seq::SliceRandom.
Matching constructs both four-card columns in correct-pair selection order,
calls left.as_mut_slice().shuffle(&mut rng) first, then
right.as_mut_slice().shuffle(&mut rng). Discard the four reserves without
shuffling them. MCQ constructs [correct, distractor_1, distractor_2] and
calls options.as_mut_slice().shuffle(&mut rng) once. Do not shuffle the
prompt, candidate views, or any intermediate list. Return without more draws.

This locks recovery, correct selection, four matching reserves or two MCQ
distractors, then final label layout on one stream. A07/A10 must record full
native/wasm golden rounds and recovery outcomes against these calls; A07 now
records them for all six variants. The hash vector above alone does not establish
full-round replay. Changing this sequence,
sampling API, recovery attempt count, shuffle order, or a tuning value that
changes selection is a replay break subject to the future-format approval path.

Correct pairs, windows, and offsets
For unseeded rounds, begin with the four-word window at the entered strict-pool
offset. Exclusions have already been removed before indexing. If offset + 4 is
beyond the view, wrap the window start to zero; never split a window across the
end of the array. Short views cannot produce a four-word window.

Validate right-label uniqueness in that window. If it fails, advance the start
by one and try again, wrapping to zero as needed. Select the first clean
window, not a best-scoring window. If the per-view cap is exhausted, try the next
view. Both widened views start their scan at zero, regardless of the entered
offset. If an otherwise clean window cannot yield the reserve distractors, advance
to the next view rather than choosing a different best window.

The URL retains the entered offset. Effective window start is internal and is
not persisted. The RNG seed includes the entered strict offset for unseeded
rounds, even if window wrapping/sliding/widening changes the effective start.
Seeded inputs hash offset zero, regardless of an offset in the raw URL.

Each view has its own min(pool.len(), MAX_SLIDE) attempt cap. Initial tuning:

rust
const MAX_SLIDE: usize = 16;
The cap is tunable; deterministic first-window selection and per-view fallthrough
are fixed rules. See DB for tuning and replay
caveats. Nominal Next round offsets still advance by four, but sliding/fallback
can overlap correct sets across rounds; unconditional session-wide non-repetition
is no longer guaranteed.

For seeded rounds, include the seed and sample three others from the active view,
excluding the seed and rejecting labels equal to the seed or another selected
correct word. Use the seeded ChaCha RNG; never slide past a fixed seed. Try the
same fallback views when needed. D15 resolves malformed/missing/excluded seeds
to unseeded inputs before building; Fixed always ignores a seed. Keep the original
entered offset in those unseeded fallbacks. Never reinsert an excluded word into
the bundle to force success.

Distractors and duplicate labels
Draw up to four reserve distractors from the active PoS/HSK candidate view using
the seeded RNG. Exclude all four correct WordIds, the seed, and any normalized
right-label key matching a correct word or an already-selected distractor.
Reject collisions with a bound of min(candidate_count, 50) retries per view.
If still short, widen in the prescribed order and reapply all exclusions/dedup.

Only the actual right-column label participates in uniqueness:

Variant	Right label	Comparison key
eng-pinyin	Pinyin	Canonical numeric tone form, no whitespace, lowercase; e.g. chīfàn becomes chi1fan4
pinyin-hanzi	Simplified hanzi	Exact bytes; no case folding or whitespace stripping
hanzi-eng	Displayed English gloss	Trim, lowercase, collapse internal whitespace
Compare normalized keys byte-for-byte. Homophones collide in eng-pinyin; 行 with
different readings collides in pinyin-hanzi; equal normalized English labels
collide in hanzi-eng. English to eat and eat remain different. Earlier examples
checking the left column were corrected and are not part of the rule. See
DB for the shared normalization contract.

Random entry and failure
Outside the pure builder, Random chooses its variant/seed inputs and captures
them in the URL. Select a seed row from the full HSK-union pool without setup
filters. The requested thread-local randomness is called rand::rng() in the
existing rand 0.10 API. No ambient RNG is allowed inside build_round.

There are two distinct caller paths:

Fresh Random click: ambient randomness is permitted for selecting the
variant/seed. Retry a word without either HSK membership up to ten times, then
choose the first ordered word with a membership. Prefer HSK 3.0 when both
exist. Capture the selected seed and its HSK/PoS context immediately in the URL.

Read an existing URL: no ambient RNG. Malformed/nonexistent/excluded seeds
become unseeded with the same filter and entered offset. A Fixed URL ignores
seed with a debug-only warning. An existing nonexcluded seed without membership
invokes deterministic recovery using a ChaCha RNG derived from canonical URL
inputs, with seeded offset zero. Draw candidate IDs one at a time from the
ordered, exclusion-clean pool, at most ten draws. Reject membership-less or
excluded candidates. If none works, take the first eligible word in id order.
Keep the original seed in the URL and the recovered seed only in effective
state; reloading repeats recovery rather than writing a new random seed.

The caller supplies original normalized URL state and ordered recovery data to
the pure build pipeline. Recovery helpers consume its sole RNG as specified in
the D19 section above; they do not run an independently seeded caller pipeline.
Tests can exercise normalization and the entire recovery/build flow on native
fixture vectors. The same URL, DB snapshot, exclusions, and algorithm reproduce
the recovered seed and round; preserve original URL state for canonical hashing.

An empty recovery pool or no eligible seed must fail safely. D07's generated-table
contract should exclude words without either membership; this is defensive
handling for malformed/legacy data, not permission to import non-HSK words.

D15's Next round on seeded Endless clears the seed and advances the normalized
offset from zero to four for the unseeded next round, keeping its filter. Raw
ignored offsets must not affect that transition.

If all three candidate views fail, return Err(BuildError::InsufficientPool { .. }).
Show "Not enough distinct words for this filter. Try a different HSK level or
reset exclusions." Preserve the Reset controls from D13. This replaces the older
D04 proposal to escape into a separate unfiltered round after pool failure.
Expected large pools never replace a tested, nonpanicking failure path.

Approved RNG provider and reproducibility checks (D17)
Use the already-declared rand 0.10.3 with its chacha feature. The intended
manifest configuration is:

toml
rand = { version = "0.10.3", features = ["chacha"] }
The user approved moving this dependency from web to zipeek-core for A07.
The core manifest now enables chacha; the pure builder and portable full-round
vectors are implemented. Web retains its existing getrandom wasm_js support.
Do not add rand_chacha: D17 supersedes that earlier D12 proposal. Reuse
rand::rngs::ChaCha12Rng and rand::SeedableRng instead of a separate provider.

The rand 0.10.3 RNG documentation
lists ChaCha8Rng/ChaCha12Rng/ChaCha20Rng behind chacha as named portable
generators. Rand's backend uses chacha20; no additional direct ChaCha crate is
needed for this design. Stable rounds additionally depend on exact
sampling/shuffling algorithms, seed expansion, feature settings, normalization,
input ordering, and tuning. The Rand reproducibility policy
permits value changes between minor library releases. Control dependency versions
and verify full-round vectors on native and wasm32; a named RNG alone is not proof.

The requested choose_multiple sampling is renamed to sample in rand 0.10;
the old alias is deprecated and would conflict with warnings-as-errors. The
rand API and
thread-local RNG docs
describe the current names: use sample for sampling and rand::rng() for the
allowed fresh-Random path. D19 above fixes sampling/shuffle/recovery call order
and the only current format, v1. Do not silently change versions
or substitute StdRng to make it compile.



## Future duplicate-hanzi matching requirement (D42)

The user approved avoiding different readings with identical simplified hanzi
in the four target pairs of a matching round after reporting jing/Jing. A55
tracks this future policy. Current v1 implementation still applies the
right-label-only rules above; no selection, draw-order or canonical encoding
was changed by A53. Before altering the builder, present the replay impact and
obtain explicit format/compatibility approval required by AGENTS. Do not merge
source reading identities. See [FUTURE](../archive-history/audits/FUTURE.md#matching-feedback-and-ambiguous-entries).
title: Deterministic round generation (D12)

# Sentence Relay

## Product contract

Sentence Relay is a Chinese word-order game. The player assembles a Chinese sentence matching an English prompt, receives contextual correction feedback, and progresses through the configured number of sentences. These are approved target requirements, not claims about the currently shipped implementation.

## Game stages

1. **Setup:** Select the vocabulary source and intended sentence count, review relevant game options and the availability of the configured AI sentence generator. Starting a game is an explicit action.
2. **Preparing:** After Start game, show preparation progress and a cancel action. Do not simultaneously present a disabled Start game button and a generation message without explaining the state. No AI generation or associated service usage should start implicitly when the user is still choosing settings.
3. **Play:** Present the English target, Chinese answer area, word bank, controls, completed-sentence progress and mistakes. Hide setup-only controls. A compact, labelled settings icon opens the setup transition; warn before abandoning meaningful progress.
4. **Results:** Present sentence-level outcomes and mistakes, with actions to play again or change setup. Keep gameplay-specific evidence separate from general Practice mastery claims.

The sentence-count setting belongs in setup and determines the generation request, progress denominator and finish condition. The exact preset values and default are pending confirmation; do not treat suggested values as a final product decision. If the service returns fewer valid sentences than requested, explain the shortage rather than silently displaying a different count.

## Word bank and interaction

- The word bank contains Chinese word or phrase tokens, not free-standing punctuation marks. Render Chinese punctuation in the appropriate position as part of sentence presentation and validation, including commas or question marks when relevant. Do not make a full stop a shuffled token.
- Support clicking or tapping to place a token; dragging to place it at a chosen answer position; and reordering tokens within the answer. Provide equivalent keyboard-accessible operations and explicit focus states.
- A placed token disappears from the available word bank rather than remaining as a faded duplicate. Undo or removing a token returns it to the bank.
- Provide a configurable pronunciation-on-selection option. When enabled, selecting a word should play its pronunciation; dragging should play once on drop, not continuously while moving. Reuse the shared pronunciation service and prevent overlapping audio. The option's initial default remains to be confirmed.
- The answer area clearly indicates how to build an answer when empty. Preserve answers during correction and allow editing without clearing the whole sentence.
- Count mistakes on incorrect submitted attempts, not on individual token actions. Progress measures completed sentences rather than placed words.

## Contextual correction feedback

A generic message such as "Not quite. Edit your sentence and try again." is insufficient when the system can identify a specific word-order error. The feedback must explain what kind of correction is needed and indicate the relevant tokens without reflexively revealing the entire answer.

For the prompt **He is eating now**, a submitted arrangement of **他 在 吃 饭 正** with the expected arrangement **他 正 在 吃 饭** illustrates a moved-token error. Highlight **正** and, when the validator has reliable evidence, indicate that it belongs before **在**. Keep the learner's answer visible and editable.

- If the right tokens are present in the wrong order, identify a misplaced token or phrase using sequence-aware comparison instead of flagging every later token by positional index.
- If a word is missing, indicate the missing position or needed grammatical component without immediately filling it in.
- If an extra token is present, identify that token.
- If multiple problems exist, prioritize a small, actionable subset; progressively increase hint specificity on subsequent incorrect submissions.
- If the submitted answer is correct, provide affirmative feedback and advance through an explicit or accessible transition, with optional spoken sentence playback according to audio settings.
- Valid alternate Chinese word orders must not be rejected solely because they differ from a single generated reference. Use suitable grammar-aware validation when available. When the validator cannot determine a specific grammatical fault reliably, give truthful, less specific feedback rather than fabricating an explanation.
- Retain highlighted errors until relevant tokens are edited. Make corrections perceivable with outlines, labels and accessible live announcements, not color alone. Feedback must not interrupt or overlap pronunciation inappropriately.

## Progress and chrome

Use a compact purple progress indicator with a visibly distinct track and accessible textual label. A thick uniform gray bar must not look like a disabled control. A settings icon replaces the prominent text label "Change setup" and carries an accessible name and tooltip. Keep the game's established dark violet cards, readable labels and compact spacing.

## Verification boundary

The screenshot review establishes shortcomings and target UX; it does not establish actual implementation mechanisms. Validate both pointer and keyboard input, mobile layouts, AI success/failure/loading states, alternative word orders, repeated mistakes, sound playback, progress, and results in a browser before marking acceptance complete.
title: Sentence Relay

# Getting started with Zipeek

Zipeek is a Rust/Yew WASM application for Chinese learning. The application uses a pregenerated DuckDB dictionary and has separate build, test, and E2E workflows.

## Before the first run

Read the [repository README](../../README.md) for current prerequisites and platform instructions. Consult [AGENTS](../../AGENTS.md) for code policy, approved-decision precedence and validation expectations. Do not run dependency upgrades without explicit approval.

## Find your way around

- [Product and UX](../product-ux/product.md) introduces the application.
- [Practice overview](../learning-practice/practice/practice-overview.md) explains the learner workflow and authoritative outcomes.
- [Architecture](../architecture/architecture.md) identifies the main runtime components.
- [Dictionary and regeneration](../dictionary-data/schema/db.md) describes data preparation and validation.
- [Build and deployment](../build-deployment/ci.md) documents build gates and CI tasks.
- [Testing](../testing-quality/acceptance/testing.md) explains the validation levels.
- [Project tasks](../project-management/tasks.md) distinguishes unfinished work from verified implementation.

## First verification

From the project root, use the commands appropriate to the change. For documentation edits, regenerate the Docs index with `cargo make docs`, then run `cargo make docs-validate`. For Rust and browser work, follow the [testing specification](../testing-quality/acceptance/testing.md).

A successful documentation validation is not evidence that Rust, WASM or Chrome builds pass.
title: Getting started with Zipeek

# Original R524 issue register - preserved snapshot

## Evidence and status

This register records the user's observed behavior and requested changes from the 2026-11-17 screenshots and message. Every issue is OPEN and unverified in source or live browser unless a later test result explicitly closes it. It is not an implementation or acceptance claim. The current project build was previously reported failing, with no authoritative first error supplied. All gameplay changes need separate scope and testing.

## P0 - Broken execution and user facing failures

- [ ] **Translate Sentence**: translation does not complete, with repeated localhost connection-refused requests and an unknown translator action warning in browser console. Capture the failing request, intended backend and first non-network exception. Distinguish service unavailable from application logic.
- [ ] **China Map Challenge**: map asset load reports `Map asset has an invalid schema: expected value at line 1 column 1`. Check the response status, MIME type, actual body and configured asset path under `/` and `/zipeek/`; confirm asset generator output before changing a schema.
- [ ] **Build health**: obtain exact current failing build command, first error and toolchain; do not assume current sources compile.
- [ ] **Onboarding / pedagogical mode**: enabling pedagogy shows an unexpected icon instead of dragon progress in the top bar. Clarify the intended compact progress dimensions and source of progress data.

## P1 - Practice flow and grammar exercises

- [ ] Practice Path: remove or repurpose empty panel; improve muted guidance text and saved-profile empty state; maintain concise actionable hierarchy.
- [ ] Practice Exercise availability: decide whether exercises requiring disconnected services should be disabled, omitted, or selectable with an explicit unavailable state. Require reliable service capability detection.
- [ ] Sentence Transformation setup: remove duplicate title; replace native grammar-pattern suggestion experience with a controlled autocomplete of up to five matches while typing; show human-friendly pattern names with link to Grammar Course; support multiple allowed patterns, but generate a question containing one selected pattern.
- [ ] Sentence Transformation answer method: replace stacked radios with a horizontal, accessible segmented group, responsive on narrow screens.
- [ ] Sentence Transformation session: remove redundant `Select Chinese tiles below` caption.
- [ ] Pronunciation Practice label: shorten to `Pronunciation`. Configure word-only versus sentence reading; sentence generation depends on a known, available AI provider.
- [ ] Speech-to-text verification: design a separate speaking exercise with microphone permission and transcript checking; distinguish recognition confidence, expected text and unscored mode. Decide on local versus service recognition.
- [ ] Audio Dictation: redesign to generate/play a Chinese sentence and reconstruct it from a word bank; define hints, audio replay, source disclosure and whether AI is mandatory.
- [ ] Spot the Mistake: AI-generated flawed sentence, configurable word-bank or typed correction; validate that an unambiguous correction exists.

## P1 - Vocabulary, discovery and navigation

- [ ] Write Hanzi > My Word Sets: list needs scroll containment or pagination with accessible item selection.
- [ ] Word Sets: fix vocabulary-pane overflow / missing vertical scroll; use otherwise-empty right-hand space responsibly; improve grouping and management controls.
- [ ] Word Sets: replace inline `Word Set created` feedback with accessible non-blocking toast / notification.
- [ ] Word Sets Data tools: clarify backup/restore as a separate drawer/dialog rather than multiple nested panels.
- [ ] Browse: deduplicate visible meanings and `Explore meanings` action; define when an expansion is useful.
- [ ] Browse: first page repeatedly displays same words; select five varied database words per refresh or navigation with an explicit repeat/seed policy.
- [ ] Random > Sentences: improve layout; request at least five generated sentences per action, larger Hanzi, per-character or per-word pinyin, playback control, and icon-based regenerate action. Move AI provenance note to an information affordance.

## P1 - Courses, evidence and progression

- [ ] Pedagogical mode: user expects course content gated until acquired; define whether completely hidden or visible as locked placeholders. Avoid claiming unknown abilities are mastered.
- [ ] Grammar Course: generated examples need playable Mandarin audio, compact regenerate icon, no redundant `Correct. You can continue.` label, configurable Hanzi font size.
- [ ] Grammar revelation hypothesis: only evidenced successful Translate Sentence, Sentence Builder and Sentence Transformation exercises may contribute to course tile opacity. Proposed rule: ten successful translations every day over seven days, matched to an identified grammar structure. Clarify consecutive days, scoring integrity, repetitions and partial opacity before implementing.

## P2 - Games and presentation

- [ ] Icon Pairs: configurable on-click audio, show-pinyin and Hanzi font size; remove unnecessary mastery disclaimer while preserving honest evidence semantics.
- [ ] Icon Pairs: HSK 6 reports too few distinct pairs. Measure catalog coverage and define fallback or disabled selection instead of an unexplained error.
- [ ] Classifier Market: redesign progress bar and game feedback, add optional pronunciation, and audit classifier coverage against source data. Avoid unsubstantiated `all classifiers` claims.
- [ ] Radical Forge: improve layout, optional pronunciation, audit covered component/radical inventory; distinguish Kangxi radicals from broader character components.

## Cross-cutting acceptance

- [ ] Screenshots and local observations are user-supplied evidence, not a passing browser test. Verify every fix at desktop/mobile sizes with keyboard focus, accessibility names and network unavailable states.
- [ ] Avoid empty surfaces, duplicated headings, inline low-contrast instructions, inaccessible custom controls and layout shifting when feedback appears.
- [ ] Use only the ordinary hyphen character for dash-style punctuation in maintained documentation and user-visible copy.
- [ ] Preserve separation between study hints, AI-authored examples, trustworthy mastery evidence and visually unlocked course content.

## R524 triage update

The product choices for AI availability, locked course visibility, rolling grammar evidence and dual speech recognition are approved as D53-D56. Their implementations and browser acceptance remain open. The translator click routing and service failure copy have a source-level correction candidate in R524. Province Quest now distinguishes HTML fallback, empty asset and malformed JSON, but the R523 source archive contains no generated Province Quest map JSON: map generation and installation remain required. Do not close the P0 incidents without a live build and browser check.


This is a preserved source snapshot. Track current issue statuses in the individual issue pages.

> **Current state (2026-11-16):** All 100 Grammar-only regions contain draft lessons with 550 teaching entries. The historical historical source snapshots registry below describes the first five courses only, not the complete curriculum. The separate teaching index (`GRAMMAR_TEACHING_INDEX.tsv`) now assigns stable IDs to all 550 entries. Official HSK 2025 grammar alignment is **not verified**; a reproducible external-source import and review process is documented in `HSK_GRAMMAR_ALIGNMENT.md`. The original five courses still have separately authored draft assessments; the other 95 have guided recognition only.

# Courses curriculum registry

introduces a stable, local authoring registry for the four currently published grammar courses. It does **not** establish that the content is a verified mapping to the official HSK syllabus.

## Authoring registry

| Mosaic region | Stable course ID | Topic | Point IDs | Recommended prior course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `grammar-1` | Basic Sentence Structure | `g01-subject-predicate`, `g01-shi-identity`, `g01-bu-negation`, `g01-ma-question` | None |
| 2 | `grammar-2` | Time, Place & Everyday Actions | `g02-time-placement`, `g02-zai-location`, `g02-time-location`, `g02-qu-destination`, `g02-nali-question` | `grammar-1` |
| 3 | `grammar-3` | Possession, Existence & Quantities | `g03-you-possession`, `g03-meiyou-negation`, `g03-classifiers`, `g03-ji-count`, `g03-duoshao-quantity` | `grammar-1` |

| 4 | `grammar-4` | Descriptions & Comparisons | `g04-adjective-predicate`, `g04-hen-degree`, `g04-bu-adjective`, `g04-tai-le`, `g04-bi-comparison` | `grammar-1` |

The recommended prior-course relationship is teaching guidance, **not** an access restriction or assessed prerequisite. Existing authored lesson routes remain available directly.

The registry lives in `crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/learning/courses/curriculum_registry.rs` and enforces unique course regions, course IDs and grammar point IDs, matching authored lesson/check counts, and backward-only valid prerequisite references. Validation runs in Rust unit tests, not as a startup blocker. IDs are intended to remain stable once published and must not be treated as acquired grammar-point evidence.

## Syllabus provenance and limitations

All published registry entries currently use `PendingIndependentVerification`. Teaching stages are local editorial sequencing, not official HSK levels. No claim of 19 official HSK syllabus objectives, comprehensive HSK coverage, or independent assessment validity is made. Before publishing a verified syllabus mapping, obtain and independently review the authoritative grammar-standard edition and item identifiers, associate every item with authored content and an independent assessment, then add explicit verified references with validation tests. That is separate from implementing evidence-backed completion and irreversible mosaic reveals.

Future courses should receive new stable IDs only when their content exists, and should leave un-authored mosaic regions marked unavailable. The final grammar curriculum may exceed 100 regions to cover the approved syllabus.

## Independent grammar assessment draft

The first four published courses now expose `#/courses/grammar/assessment/grammar-1`, `grammar-2`, `grammar-3`, and `grammar-4`, with one separate three-choice item per registered grammar point (4 + 5 + 5 + 5). The items are authored in `assessment.rs` using stable point IDs and independent prompts, rather than reusing the guided lesson answer array. A distinct `AssessmentSession` records one answer per item, permits revisions *before* submission, disallows submission of incomplete attempts, locks answers afterwards and calculates a score only after full submission. The Yew page withholds rationales and correct answers until the review screen.

**No authoritative completion claim:** This remains an editorial and interaction draft. It does not implement HSK syllabus verification, qualified Mandarin-language assessment review, durable personal evidence, consent-backed recording, independently validated distractors, passing thresholds, retries/cooldowns, or artwork reveal. No score is stored or reported to the pedagogy engine. The mosaic stays concealed even if all draft items are correct. Assessment-time answer correctness is not the same as the acquisition engine's separate Hanzi 10×7 rule.

## extension - Descriptions and Comparisons

Course 4 introduces adjective predicates, degree words 很, adjectival negation 不,
太…了, and comparisons with 比. It contains five explanatory teaching points,
five immediate-feedback guided questions, six authored word-bank activities,
five separately authored draft multiple-choice assessment items, and a separate
no-hints construction item. All item IDs use the new `g04-` registry namespace.
The ordinary lesson and draft assessment have different feedback rules.
All drafted answers need independent Mandarin linguistic review, particularly
nuances around 很, 太…了 and comparison interpretation. No achievements or mosaic
regions can be revealed based on these drafts.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/learning-practice-courses-courses-curriculum-registry.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.

# Courses and learning tracks

## Track ownership

Zipeek exposes separate learning tracks for Vocabulary, Grammar and Pinyin. Each track owns its curriculum content, learning activities, route-specific interaction state and progress semantics. Shared layout and mosaic utilities do not make the tracks share a single scoring engine.

## Mosaic presentation

Course mosaics use the application's Chinese-inspired visual style with readable regions and a clear selected/locked state. The selected region must have a visible label and accessible control. The previously retired static course mosaic reference is **not** an approved fidelity target; current working UI and the latest approved screenshot-driven requirements control new visual work.

Regions may remain visible but locked until the learner meets the qualifying evidence rules. A locked region is not an invitation to generate or record unearned proficiency. Locked state must explain how progress is earned and remain accessible to keyboard and screen-reader users.

## Grammar mosaic detail and example navigation

The selected grammar course detail panel displays the course title and available points without repeating generic course-category labels or development-status disclaimers. A compact example strip beneath the artwork presents one point at a time, with previous/next controls, a visible position counter, Hanzi first, its curated Pinyin directly underneath when available, then the English translation. Navigating examples does not alter the selected region or award progress. Course changes reset the example index. The mosaic selection remains keyboard accessible.

## Learning evidence

Grammar proficiency requires ten qualifying successes per pattern, distributed over at least seven distinct days within a rolling fourteen-day window, drawn from supported Translate Sentence, Sentence Builder and Sentence Transformation submissions. Mere lesson visits, draft examples or unscored interactions do not qualify. Vocabulary exposure and visitation must be distinguished from acquisition, and progress is derived from persisted evidence. See [learning evidence](../practice/learning-evidence.md).

## Curriculum and content boundaries

Teaching drafts, published course routes and assessed completion are different states. The presence of a curriculum record, route, generated lesson or practice sample is not sufficient evidence of an authored, validated, published assessment. Grammar examples generated by an optional AI service must be labelled as examples rather than scoring evidence. The application must show capability-aware service failures and keep personal credentials in their approved service boundary.

Course content design, registry updates and validation must follow [authoring](../../engineering/courses-authoring.md), [curriculum registry](courses-curriculum-registry.md), [HSK alignment](hsk-grammar-alignment.md), and [acceptance](../../testing-quality/acceptance/approved-behavior-acceptance.md).

## Source and verification

Inspect the source's course components and pedagogical crates for actually published slugs, lesson steps, region layouts and persistence before claiming implementation. Earlier route snapshots, historical asset directions and content inventory observations are preserved in [archived course source](../../archive-history/audits/superseded-maintained/learning-practice--courses--courses-mosaic-source.md).
title: Courses and learning tracks

# Mapping Zipeek Grammar to the 2025 HSK syllabus

## Evidence status

- Zipeek has 100 draft Grammar courses and 550 teaching entries; this is not a certified inventory of independent grammatical rules.
- The 2025 HSK syllabus is a separate reference. A community transcription reports **593 items**, covering parts of speech, phrase structures, sentence patterns, pragmatic constructions and related categories. These items are not necessarily one independent rule each.
- **Official HSK mappings remain unverified in the documented source audit.** A matching Chinese example is only an editorial suggestion, never evidence of semantic equivalence.
- The third-party TSV was verified as publicly accessible through web search, but this runtime cannot download it into the source tree. The full HSK alignment has not been performed or fabricated.

## Sources and provenance

Official syllabus landing page: <https://www.chinesetest.cn/syllabus>.

Official PDF publisher: Center for Language Education and Cooperation, November 2025 (effective July 2026); grammar occupies pages 385-406. Reference download: <https://hsk.cn-bj.ufileos.com/3.0/%E6%96%B0%E7%89%88HSK%E8%80%83%E8%AF%95%E5%A4%A7%E7%BA%B21219.pdf>.

Community TSV transcription: <https://github.com/chelsea6502/hsk-2025-data/blob/master/grammar.tsv>. It contains `examLevelId`, `content`, `grammarType`, `categoryType`, `grammarDetail`, and `cases`; the repository advertises 593 source records. It is not itself an official certification. Keep its provenance and calculated SHA-256 with every imported mapping. Review malformed input rows rather than silently shifting field positions.

## Workflow

The former Python index/import/audit/report commands were removed in the historical source at the user's request. The checked-in `GRAMMAR_TEACHING_INDEX.tsv` and the historical editorial mapping files remain for review. The full third-party HSK TSV still needs to be obtained and checked against the official PDF. Automated reimport, source-hash comparison, and mapping reports are **not currently available** until a Rust-native replacement is implemented. Do not assume the historical report can be refreshed or that a mapping has been verified.

`GRAMMAR_TEACHING_INDEX.tsv` was generated from the original 20 Rust courses and the 451-row editorial TSV for regions 21-100. Each entry receives an `gNNN-pNN` teaching ID, a region and a point ordinal, with `kind=unclassified` and `review_status=pending_linguistic_review` until an editor explicitly classifies it. The lesson runtime is not changed by this editorial index.

The HSK mapping queue has one row per source item. An exact shared Chinese example can suggest a teaching-entry ID. The status remains `unreviewed`; items with malformed source fields are marked `needs_source_review`. A reviewer must inspect the official syllabus and the lesson, decide whether a mapping is `candidate`, `verified`, or `unmapped`, and provide a rationale for `verified` and `unmapped` entries. Candidate and verified statuses require valid teaching IDs. Source metadata is checked on audit, and malformed source rows cannot advance beyond `needs_source_review` without correcting the reference. The former report command wrote a per-HSK-level count of unreviewed, candidate, verified, unmapped and source-review entries plus the number of unique verified teaching IDs. A summary of 593 items is not evidence of 593 verified mappings; the report sets `hsk_coverage_verified` only when all 593 are verified and no parse errors exist. Multiple HSK items may map to one teaching point; one HSK item may require multiple teaching points. A parent/variant relationship must be reviewed separately, not guessed from English labels.

## Acceptance gates

1. Confirm the source edition, legal use and all 593 source records (including levels 7-9). Resolve any malformed transcription rows against the official PDF.
2. Review each item's category, required competence, correct course placement and construction/variant relationships. No unreviewed item may count toward syllabus coverage.
3. Add explicit editorial review, natural Mandarin examples, tone-marked Pinyin and varied, independent point assessments; correct mistaken teaching entries without adding duplicate filler to reach an arbitrary total.
4. Only after independently scored evidence meets approved thresholds may a Grammar region be awarded mastery or reveal its artwork. Importing or mapping syllabus records never changes user progress.
5. Run locked Rust/WASM tests and Chrome journeys under both `/` and `/zipeek/` before accepting a release.

## Known limitation

The first Grammar region contains four points, while the intended curriculum structure is generally five to six points per course. This was preserved in the historical source to avoid inventing an additional construction without expert review. Its four-point count should not be silently represented as full compliance with the updated authoring target.

## verification status

The grammar reference is discoverable online, but downloading the 593-row TSV into the local project remains blocked by the environment network restriction. The tooling changes are tested with synthetic samples, not with a full 593-row import. The published level distribution for the 2025 transcription is HSK 1: 70, HSK 2: 78, HSK 3: 96, HSK 4: 95, HSK 5: 70, HSK 6: 50 and HSK 7-9: 134, totaling 593. Those figures are external-source metadata, not Zipeek verified teaching coverage.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/learning-practice-courses-hsk-grammar-alignment.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.
title: Mapping Zipeek Grammar to the 2025 HSK syllabus

## Scope and status

The user approved two independent navigation destinations, **Themes** and **Courses**, and a six-option appearance gallery plus a course-library design. The described implementation is an early source-level slice, not browser acceptance. Preserve the established light/dark toggle and Chinese font preference.

### Themes (`#/themes`)

- Six explicitly named presets: Lavender Classic, Jade Light, Sunset Warm, Midnight Blue, Ink Minimal, Autumn Maple.
- Each card previews its palette. Selecting a card applies semantic CSS tokens to the application immediately and persists `zipeek.appearance.preset` locally.
- Density control has Grid (baseline), Comfortable (readability-oriented spacing) and Compact (reduced spacing); its independent preference persists under `zipeek.appearance.density`.
- The existing top-bar light/dark toggle is independent. Selecting a preset initially chooses its default contrast mode; users may still toggle afterward. The Chinese font setting remains in Settings.
- The palette preset is distinct from the existing `zipeek-themes` crate's *vocabulary-topic background* `ThemeId`; do not mix the two concepts.
- No custom user-authored palettes, server synchronization or image/background replacement yet. Palette preview is a small CSS representation, not a snapshot of the actual rendered app.

### Courses (`#/courses`)

- Library categories: Pinyin & Pronunciation, Everyday Chinese, Topics & Vocabulary, Dialogues & Scenarios, Grammar Essentials, HSK Preparation.

- Pinyin lesson pages present instructional content and examples without a manual completion action. No Pinyin completion or mastery status is recorded by these pages.
- Lessons are authored and version-controlled in the web source in the historical source. Courses sequence explanations and learning activities; Practice supplies reusable exercises and assessments. The dictionary supplies classified vocabulary. # AI Hanzi recognition

## Purpose and route

Provide a dedicated **Recognize Hanzi** route for identifying unknown single Chinese characters or multi-character words from handwriting or images. Recognition supplies possible matches, not a guaranteed transcription. It is distinct from Write Hanzi stroke-order grading and must not award pedagogical evidence merely because a candidate was recognized.

## Unified canvas

Use **one canvas**, without separate Draw and Paste tabs. Support pointer, touch and stylus drawing; clipboard image paste; and image file selection from a compact toolbar action. Show clear empty, drawing, image-loaded, busy, error and result states. Support Undo and Clear for drawing. If annotation over a pasted image is enabled, keep original image pixels separate from editable stroke overlays so Undo does not destroy the input. Replacing an existing drawing or image requires an explicit user action.

Clipboard handling is capability-aware. A permission-enabling action may request image clipboard access when the browser and security context support it. A component lifecycle hook may register focus and paste listeners and clean them up, but **must not auto-prompt for permission on mount** or poll the clipboard continuously. Chromium's permission behavior does not apply universally to Firefox and Safari. Ordinary paste and file upload must remain usable without persistent clipboard permission. A detected image is offered as a contextual action, not pasted automatically over existing work.

The app must not transmit clipboard content just because a clipboard image is present. Upload to a configured vision-capable AI service requires the learner to explicitly press **Recognize**. Check service capabilities and availability before enabling recognition. Handle cancellation, stale responses, request size limits, unsupported image types, empty drawings, provider failure and malformed model output.

## Recognition and result validation

Normalize image dimensions and excess whitespace non-destructively. Keep enough visual context for multi-character text. Request a small ranked set of candidate Hanzi or vocabulary strings from the vision service. Verify dictionary hits through the existing dictionary lookup rather than trusting model-generated pinyin or meanings. Mark unsupported candidates as unverified. If characters are visually ambiguous, show alternatives with readable labels rather than claiming certainty from an uncalibrated score.

Provide Listen when the existing Mandarin audio service is available, Open in Dictionary, Add to the active Word Set, and Practise writing where valid. A failed dictionary match must not be silently promoted to a verified entry.

## Privacy and retention

Do **not** persist recognition history, source images or recognition results. Keep input and candidates only in the current interaction state; release them on Clear, navigation or unmount. Never upload automatically. No image data belongs in analytics, saved profiles or crash logs. Respect configured service privacy disclosures and browser permissions. See [AI service architecture](../../architecture/modules/ai-client.md) and [acceptance](../../testing-quality/acceptance/approved-behavior-acceptance.md).

## R532 implementation status

The initial route and single workspace are authored in `zipeek-web/src/pages/learning/recognize_hanzi.rs` and `recognition_workspace.js`. Drawing, Undo, Clear, focus-scoped image paste, PNG/JPEG/WebP upload, explicit submission, temporary results, a small strictly validated candidate list, local dictionary matching and existing Word Set/audio/writing actions are wired. The AI call sends an image URL data payload to the configured chat-completions endpoint only on button activation. Stale responses cannot update the page after another input event, Clear or unmount; the native browser request may continue because the WASM HTTP client has no explicit abort interface.

Unverified requirements: actual vision-capable model discovery, service-capability gating beyond requiring a configured model, cross-browser clipboard support, detailed candidate quality, cropped/whitespace optimized inputs, live source-image privacy audit and Chrome accessibility. No recognition history or source images are deliberately persisted. This is an unverified WIP implementation, not finished acceptance.

## R536 interface review

Recognition input now occupies a compact, centred canvas card with a single main
Recognize action. The Word Set picker is removed from the empty recognition workspace;
existing current-set context is used only after dictionary-verified results exist.
The provider response parser accepts strictly fenced JSON in addition to raw JSON,
but continues to reject invalid or non-Hanzi candidates. Browser recognition quality
and visual UX still require actual acceptance screenshots and tests.

## R537 theme and failure-diagnostic corrections

The drawing surface uses the active application surface and ink colors in light, dark and System modes, including when the appearance changes while a workspace is mounted. The canvas must remain compact enough for a standard desktop viewport while allowing the page to scroll normally when candidate results extend beyond the viewport. Error feedback must distinguish malformed JSON from invalid Hanzi, empty candidates and upstream request failures. Log only bounded structural response information such as response length, parsing location and classification; never log the submitted image, raw model text, credentials or character candidates.

## R539 interface redesign

The current source presents a responsive two-column writing-and-action workspace on wide viewports, a stacked layout on narrow screens, and candidate cards below. The canvas keeps the active theme surface and ink, and empty/input/error states are contextual. Undo is available only for editable strokes, Clear only for content, and recognition only after content is present and a model is configured. No history is saved. This update has not been visually accepted in Chrome or on mobile.

## R550 responsive results layout

On desktop the writing workspace and candidate results share a two-column layout, with the canvas occupying roughly three-fifths of the available width. The writing workspace remains visible during candidate inspection. Results have their own bounded vertical scroll region on large viewports; do not put scroll containers inside individual cards. On narrow screens the canvas comes first, followed by the candidate list, and successful recognition scrolls the results into view. The initial empty results panel stays quiet without repetitive instructions or fabricated candidate data. A visible busy indicator and accessible results announcement appear only when relevant. The page preserves normal mobile scrolling, theme support, and existing dictionary/Word Set actions. The implementation has not yet passed browser visual acceptance.

## Recognition request and result presentation

Use a single concise JSON-only recognition contract with a bounded output budget. A response with no recognized characters uses an empty `candidates` array, distinct from malformed JSON. The dictionary remains authoritative for pinyin and meaning. Preserve reasoning/output-length errors as actionable failures without logging submitted images or model content.

On desktop, align drawing and suggestions panels in one grid row and keep candidate suggestions concise. Each row includes the candidate, local dictionary pinyin/meaning when available, and accessible actions for listening, dictionary, writing and Word Sets. Keep an ordinary page flow on mobile. Do not repeat the same controls as large text-only action rows.
title: AI Hanzi recognition

# Write Hanzi activity

## Entry and selection

Write Hanzi is available as a standalone learning activity and as a Practice exercise. Its vocabulary finder supports configured Word Sets and dictionary search by Hanzi, English meaning and Pinyin forms, with visible source identity and keyboard-operable suggestions. An empty Word Set must never make broader dictionary suggestions appear to belong to that set. Relevant Dictionary and Word discovery actions may pass a selected word into the workspace.

## Writing workspace

The learner traces characters using pointer or touch input against canonical reference geometry. Show clear success, rejection and reference-loading errors, without accepting a missing or corrupt reference as completed handwriting. Preserve a stable drawing area during completion and responsive resize. Undo, guidance and Watch replay must not leave stale strokes or interfere with active input.

Practice options include guidance (`none`, `start_cue`, `full_guide`), optional stroke-order playback, independent Pinyin and meaning display, and manual word pronunciation when supported. Assistance after repeated failed attempts must be distinguishable from independently accepted strokes. A completed assisted stroke is not automatically mastery evidence.

## Playback and animation reliability

Canonical stroke animation, guidance preview and the learner's current stroke must share the correct reference-to-screen transform and have independent, cancellable lifecycles. Repeated Watch/replay, character changes, re-renders and viewport resizing must not produce displaced fragments, duplicated outlines, stale masks or clipped strokes. Interrupted playback must leave a coherent canvas. Honor reduced-motion settings, touch input and keyboard controls.

The screenshots provided by the developer show possible disconnected stroke fragments. Their cause is **unverified**; inspect reference geometry, SVG masking, transform order and competing timers before asserting a root cause. Record reproducible browser evidence across varied Hanzi.

## Practice integration and results

The Practice session host owns advancement, persistent session data and scored outcomes. Writing components return stroke and assistance evidence without independently updating global dragon progress. The active exercise uses the shared frame and has no redundant exercise-type title or exit button. See [Practice outcomes](../practice/practice-outcomes.md), [shared frame](../practice/shared-exercise-foundation.md) and [testing acceptance](../../testing-quality/acceptance/approved-behavior-acceptance.md).

Past implementation notes, matcher details and provisional thresholds remain in [archived Write Hanzi source](../../archive-history/audits/superseded-maintained/learning-practice--hanzi--write-hanzi-activity-source.md); do not mistake that snapshot for browser acceptance.

# Knowledge Points (R608 approved scoring model)

**Status:** Product rules approved on 2026-11-22; R612 extends the standalone pure-Rust scoring-core candidate, not connected to live Practice, AI, persistence or Statistics. Cargo compilation/tests are unverified in this environment.

## Canonical catalogue and access

The catalogue is fixed and final, with no catalogue evolution, unlock mechanism or HSK-based vocabulary filtering. All vocabulary is exposed from the beginning. Every unique active canonical entity contributes one point to the global maximum, even if unseen. Course and HSK views are descriptive projections of the same globally unique entities, not separate awards.

| Category | Canonical item | Scored targets | Weights |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pinyin | Valid syllable-tone combination | Reading, Listening, Speaking | 1/3 each |
| Hanzi | Canonical character, with curated simplified/traditional variants | Recognition, Pronunciation, Handwriting | 1/3 each |
| Vocabulary | Curated word sense, including curated expressions | Recognition, Listening, Speaking, Writing | 1/4 each |
| Grammar | Curated pattern | Whole grammar pattern, no subordinate skill dimensions | 1 |

`max_points = count(Pinyin) + count(Hanzi) + count(Vocabulary) + count(Grammar)`. No Contextual Use scoring dimension exists; context diversity is an evidence requirement. `score(target) = earned_chunks / required_days / number_of_dimensions`, with grammar using one target. Store chunks as integers and round only in presentation.

## Qualification, debt, relapse

- Default base success quota is 10 independently supported, meaningfully distinct context families per scoring target per local scoring day. Default required qualifying days: 7. Reusing a context family on a different day is permitted.
- Each target qualifies at most once per day; days need not be consecutive. A confidently attributable failure before qualification disqualifies that target for that day. Once qualified, its chunk cannot be revoked by a later same-day failure. Other targets are unaffected.
- Events process chronologically. Snapshot each target's effective success quota on its first event of the local day. Subsequent debt changes cannot retroactively alter that quota.
- Debt activates after 2 to 5 previously earned chunks, default 3; threshold must not exceed required days. At most one debt-generating failure per target per day. Debt is capped at 5. Add 2 successes per debt unit to the next day's quota; one successfully qualified day repays one debt unit.
- At full mastery, a confidently attributable failure starts one severe relapse episode, removes exactly one chunk, and sets debt to 5. Further failures cannot remove more chunks during that episode. Each subsequent qualified recovery day repays one unit; only the day reducing debt to zero restores the one missing chunk. No further relapse before recovery completes.

## Hidden Comeback recovery (approved)

After an ordinary pre-qualification disqualification, 100 consecutive independently valid correct observations for the same target on the same local day cancel that day's disqualification and trigger a one-time hidden **Comeback** notification. A further attributable mistake before 100 resets the streak. Invalid, duplicate or context-repeated observations do not advance it. The daily quota, meaningful context requirements and one-chunk/day ceiling remain in force; the 100 successes count toward the existing quota and the day may qualify immediately upon recovery. Previously generated debt remains until the normal qualification repayment, and Comeback does not override an active severe mastery relapse. The milestone must not be advertised as a progress counter or award bonus points.

## Evidence eligibility

One exercise can award multiple manifest-authorized entity/dimension observations, across categories, only when each is independently demonstrated; never automatically cascade credit to contained characters, syllables or senses. One attempt yields at most one observation per target. Distinct contexts must be genuine semantic-equivalence families certified upstream, not arbitrary generated IDs.

- Pinyin is assessed for the specific syllable and tone. Producing a whole vocabulary word does not automatically constitute Pinyin assessment.
- Hanzi Recognition may demonstrate character identity, meaning, function or contribution. Correctly producing a whole word may establish independently attributable Hanzi Pronunciation or Handwriting, but recognizing the word alone does not establish its characters. Polyphonic Hanzi Pronunciation requires all curated readings balanced over the daily success quota, without a predetermined extra-reading assignment. Correct structure recalled without visible guidance qualifies Handwriting; stroke order is feedback only. Pinyin IME candidate selection, tracing and copying do not earn Hanzi Handwriting.
- Vocabulary uses curated sense identities. Semantically equivalent translations qualify; independent contextual inference may qualify. Word banks only support dimensions they genuinely test. Curated expressions and component words earn evidence separately only if justified.
- Grammar must actually be assessed; incidental appearance of a pattern does not earn evidence.
- Ambiguous prompts, uncertain attribution, invalid observations and technical AI failures do not cause score gains, disqualification, debt or relapse. A sentence-wide error never automatically condemns every embedded target.

## Architecture and persistence boundary

The exercise manifest authorizes entity IDs, dimensions, context, modalities and cue visibility. The local or AI evaluator reports diagnostic outcomes, never point deltas. The Rust evidence validator checks authorization, independently delivered modality, attribution, context independence, per-attempt deduplication and policy epoch. The pure scoring engine accepts only validated observations. Observations and derived scoring state must persist durably with attempt IDs. R612 adds a pure manifest-aware evidence validator and an atomic in-memory batch transition ledger, but does **not** implement browser storage, durable cross-tab transactions, real catalogue ID authorization or upstream semantic context certification. The application must persist a complete ledger snapshot transactionally before publishing successful scoring results.

AI evaluation failures after bounded retries are technical failures. AI-only sessions end; mixed sessions skip remaining AI-dependent steps while locally assessed steps continue. Already validated daily evidence survives session interruption. Scoring policy changes require confirmation and a reset of pedagogical scoring observations/state, without deleting unrelated course content or history. No scoring policy migrations or catalogue migrations are required.

## Remaining integration work

Validate actual fixed catalogue IDs and polyphonic reading manifests; implement exercise authorization, semantic context certification, durable storage/transaction boundaries, AI/locally assessed report adapters and statistics projection. The pure Rust core is not an authoritative live learner score until connected and tested.
title: Knowledge Points (R608 approved scoring model)
