# Learning evidence, proficiency, and history

**Status:** approved product requirements, refined 2026-11-09; **not yet implemented in the production learner database, Settings, or Stats route**. This is the normative future behavior, not a description of today's Practice scoring. See [personal-data architecture](../../dictionary-data/schema/personal-data.md), [Practice setup](practice-session-builder.md), and [deterministic E2E plan](../../testing-quality/e2e/learning-evidence-e2e.md).

## Purpose and authority

Collect **Practice records first**, then derive learning observations with traceable provenance. The personal DuckDB database is the planned durable authority, distinct from the read-only dictionary DuckDB and the temporary UUID Practice records in localStorage. Do not describe a probe database or a deleted temporary Practice record as saved pedagogical history. On completion, a durable session write must be acknowledged before clearing the last recoverable evidence and showing a saved confirmation. On write failure the learner must receive a truthful error and an explicit recovery path; silently losing results is unacceptable.

Record session ID, creation/start/end timestamps, configured vocabulary source, stable item IDs, exercise configuration, category and HSK membership where available, and a distinct attempt ID for each scored response. Derive per-Hanzi, per-word, per-grammar-point, and per-skill evidence from the scored attempts; preserve session and attempt references, item version, outcome, validity, and assessor. Distinguish a character within a word from a tested word identity; do not claim separate Hanzi recognition from an unrelated whole-sentence score without a defensible attribution rule. Duplicate delivery/replay of one attempt must be idempotent.

Raw microphone recordings and free-form learner text are more sensitive than score metadata. An assessed spoken result needs evidence of pronunciation/meaning correctness, **not merely permission to record or the presence of audio bytes**. Consent, audio retention, export, deletion, and local-only versus external AI processing remain to be specified before activation.

## Approved proficiency eligibility

All of the following apply to **the same stable Hanzi or word identity**:

1. **Seven distinct active local calendar days:** at least one qualifying, scored observation on each of seven different days. Seven encounters on one date, or a seven-day elapsed interval containing only two active dates, are insufficient. A missing day is not a failure. Dates must be evaluated consistently using a documented learner timezone policy; daylight-saving transitions must not change the day count arbitrarily.
2. **At least ten qualifying scored encounters**, distributed across **at least three different completed Practice sessions**. Repeated attempts in one session can contribute but **must be capped per item/session** so a learner cannot manufacture proficiency by endlessly repeating one item. The exact per-session cap and whether remediation retries count remain policy parameters to finalize, not numbers invented here. Record all attempts for diagnostics even when some do not contribute to eligibility.
3. **Successful evidence in four independently assessed competencies:** visual recognition, listening comprehension, assessed spoken production, and appropriate use in a sentence. Selecting Matching ten times can build recognition evidence, **not** certify speaking, listening, or sentence use. A competency with no qualifying successes remains unproven. The precise number and proportion of successful observations per skill are not yet approved. Ten encounters is an overall minimum, **not ten in each skill** unless a later decision changes the policy.
4. **Dynamic performance:** a later qualified failure can lower the affected skill rating or return the item to needs-review. A historical mastery award is not an immutable course-completion record. Repeated failures must not be masked by accumulated easy successes. The decay/recovery thresholds are still open.

The first three requirements are **necessary, not automatically sufficient**. Until per-skill acceptance criteria and validators are implemented, Stats may display the observed counts and pending competencies, but must **not** label the learner proficient simply on day seven or encounter ten.

### Classifying evidence by what an exercise actually tests

| Experience | Permissible evidence when scored and validated | Not automatically evidenced |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Matching / glyph-choice / image-to-Hanzi | Recognition of the tested identity | Listening, speech, productive sentence use |
| Listening comprehension (audio to meaning/selection) | Listening, where audio playback and answer are genuinely assessed | Speaking from merely hearing audio |
| Recorded spoken response | Speaking **only after a reliable assessor checks it** | Pronunciation competence from recording existence alone |
| Sentence creation, transformation, or context use | Sentence use if meaning and grammar are assessed and the target identity is attributable | All component words mastered, or free production from a fully revealed answer |
| Grammar-course guided examples and hints | Instructional activity; possibly separate assisted evidence | Unassisted mastery or passed grammar assessment |

Track `assistance_level` and `assessment_kind` so a word-bank Sentence Builder displaying the correct solution and playable audio remains a useful **teaching experience** without improperly awarding unassisted production credit. Learning activities and scored assessments are distinct events.

## Word Set eligibility in Practice setup

**New requirement, not currently enforced across the shipped setup:** a saved Word Set is selectable as a Practice vocabulary source only if it contains **at least ten distinct valid Hanzi-bearing vocabulary entries**. The intended user example is ten words, not ten total Unicode Hanzi code points. Deduplicate by stable vocabulary identity; ten duplicates or invalid/stale entries do not pass. If fewer than ten are playable for the chosen exercise, the option is **disabled/greyed out** with an accessible explanation and count (for example, `7 of 10 words available; add 3`). The same eligibility rule must be revalidated when launching, including after a set is edited or dictionary entries become unavailable; disabling only the visual button is insufficient.

This is a Practice **source eligibility requirement**, not a minimum size for creating or storing Word Sets, and not a claim that all ten words must appear in every question. A source with ten distinct entries allows the learner to practise; it does **not** guarantee ten qualifying observations for any one word. Other vocabulary sources and exercise-specific minimums remain separate unless explicitly revised.

## Future /stats experience

The proposed `/stats` route reports per-word/Hanzi evidence transparently: qualifying encounters, distinct sessions, distinct active days, per-skill measured/needs-evidence/needs-review status, category and HSK association, and relevant grammar points. Expose why an item is not proficient; do not show only an unexplained percentage. A character's observed skill state and a word's observed skill state must remain distinguishable. Current does not implement this route or its durable backing ledger.

## Grammar learning and irreversible completion

The future [Courses mosaic](../courses/courses-mosaic.md) is built against the **HSK grammar syllabus**, with an explicit mapping from each authoritative grammar point to taught course, questions, assessments and stable IDs. Do not assert complete official coverage before item-by-item verification. Courses use authored explanations, worked examples, guided exercises (image-to-Hanzi, Hanzi writing, Character Builder, Sentence Builder and word-bank Sentence Transformation), and individually scored grammar-point assessments.

Instruction may intentionally reveal an answer, e.g. a Sentence Builder's correct-sentence label with playable audio below the builder. Such scaffolding is **not equivalent to a correct independent assessment**. Per-point assessment requires at least five scored questions and 80% in one attempt by default, as specified in the Courses contract. Passing every required point makes **course completion permanent** and reveals that course's large mosaic region. Vocabulary proficiency remains dynamic and separately determines small vocabulary-region opacity; grammar-point completion never implicitly marks associated words known.

## Storage/privacy gates

Use the personal DuckDB for authoritative session and derived evidence records once durability is verified; implement a clear Settings recording/retention control before collection. A final decision on opt-in default, raw audio/text retention, local/export/erase behavior, and handling of model-provider transfer is still required. The existing temporary Practice record must not be silently treated as a history database. Plan versioned schema and migrations, dictionary-identity continuity, idempotent commits, cross-tab coordination, quota/corruption recovery, export/import and user deletion.

## Verification, including time travel

Use an injected clock interface for both domain computation and timestamp generation. Production uses real time; tests use a deterministic fake clock with **explicit date/time and timezone**, advanced between sessions. Never change the operating-system clock, monkey-patch browser `Date` globally, or trust mutable DOM timestamps for proficiency. The Rust domain clock and browser persistence boundary must receive the **same simulated time**. Record timestamps immutably when attempts are scored; altering the test clock cannot rewrite history. See [E2E scenarios](../../testing-quality/e2e/learning-evidence-e2e.md).

Tests must cover seven distinct dates, ten capped scored encounters over at least three sessions, all four skill categories, session replay, duplicates, failure-driven regression, disabled recording, successful durable saves, failed writes, cross-session reload, and Stats reading the same persisted facts. Test both the boundary just before eligibility and the first genuinely eligible state. When per-skill success thresholds remain undecided, test *eligibility evidence* and a clearly pending overall status, not a fabricated proficiency pass.

## Open decisions (only these remain policy-dependent)

- The maximum qualifying encounters for one identity in one session; counting of immediate retries and partial answers.
- Per-skill success sample sizes/thresholds, remediation, and reliable listening, speaking and sentence-use assessment rules. Selecting only Matching must never satisfy all four modalities.
- Learner timezone policy when travelling, recording opt-in default, and retention/export/deletion of raw responses and microphone audio.
- Stable vocabulary/character identity across dictionary updates and the distinction between a word's compositional evidence and its constituent characters.

Do not convert these unresolved details into undocumented hard-coded defaults.

## Hanzi recognition award versus vocabulary proficiency

The separate [Hanzi recognition acquisition contract](../../dictionary-data/schema/pedagogy.md) is approved for future Dragon Progression: ten valid correct recognitions in at least three completed sessions per qualifying day, at most four credits per session, over seven consecutive dates separated by at least 24 elapsed hours; a per-day 0/1/2 mistake allowance defaults to zero. A failed day resets that acquisition streak, and a successful day locks when it qualifies. Earlier specification passages above describe the pre-existing the historical source vocabulary and full multi-skill proficiency design; they must not be used as the Hanzi Dragon awarding algorithm. Recognition acquisition is a distinct historical milestone, not proof of listening, speech, writing or sentence-use proficiency. The the historical source engine is in-memory only and is not integrated into production event capture or `/stats`.

## Approved 2026-11-17 grammar observation window

For grammar visualization, the selected target rule is seven qualifying local days within a rolling fourteen-day window, per canonical grammar-pattern ID. On each qualifying day, ten independent correct and verified attempts must use that pattern in Translate Sentence, Sentence Builder or Sentence Transformation. Merely generating an AI sentence, revealing a solution or matching a transcript without a validated assessment is insufficient. This is not implemented or verified and does not revise the D52 Hanzi recognition streak or the existing per-point course assessment contract without separate reconciliation.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/learning-practice-practice-learning-evidence.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.


## Prospective Knowledge Points policy supersession

The older seven-day recognition/proficiency criteria described above are **legacy approved requirements**, not the new active scoring implementation. The later approved R608 [Knowledge Points specification](../pedagogy/knowledge-points.md) describes a prospective replacement model with five fixed 0.2 dimensions, distinct-context successes, debt, relapse and evaluator attribution. R608 is **not live**; the R609 pure-Rust module remains an uncompiled candidate. Until integration, distinguish historical policy, prospective design and actual saved Practice outcome history. Grammar scoring, exact numerical debt defaults and policy-day/identity boundaries remain undecided; do not silently reconcile them here.

# Practice outcomes and session lifecycle

## Authority and implementation boundary

This document states approved target behavior. It does not assert that the current application implements or passes every requirement. Individual implementation and verification gaps are recorded in [open tasks](../../project-management/tasks.md) and the [issue library](../../issues/OPEN.md).

## Exercise verdicts

A completed scored exercise reports one of three outcomes: **Correct**, **Partially correct**, or **Incorrect**. Keep the meaning of these outcomes explicit for each exercise type. Do not manufacture a percentage, a binary success, or a universal pair-based count for mixed exercises. Not all exercise types can produce partial credit; those types report only meaningful outcomes.

Display an accessible stacked horizontal bar and textual counts for the three verdicts in the session summary. Use distinct colors and text labels. An empty outcome category has a count of zero. Do not use a Chart.js doughnut or require an additional charting dependency. The summary does not report a single universal percentage. Provide exercise-specific supplementary details only when meaningful, such as matching attempts, writing mistakes and assisted strokes.

Pair counts and streaks remain available within matching games where they have a clear meaning. Translation uses the three verdicts, and handwriting may record accepted, rejected and assisted strokes. A hint or assistance does not automatically confer independent success or mastery.

## Completion and progression

Session progress counts completed exercise slots against the configured session length. The dragon represents durable evidence of acquisition, not completion or exposure, and must be derived from persisted pedagogical evidence rather than an independent counter. Render progress and the dragon as separate, clearly labelled concepts.

There is **no Reset exercise** action. Skip discards the current unfinished exercise and generates a replacement of the same exercise type in the same slot, retaining that type's saved configuration. A session configured for five translation exercises still requires five completed translation exercises even after skips. A skipped item does not receive a scored verdict or mastery evidence. Previously submitted attempts and mistakes remain recorded where an evidence contract supports them. A replacement should avoid immediately repeating skipped material where eligible alternatives exist. Count skipped attempts separately from completed exercise verdicts.

Continue advances only after the required submission or completion. Resume restores the locally persisted session. A new session reuses its saved profile configuration and generates fresh content, respecting vocabulary eligibility, history and the configured pool exhaustion policy. Retain local persistence rather than encoding learner state, filters, exclusions or random offsets into URLs.

If an exercise is retried, previously recorded attempt evidence must not be erased. The exact per-exercise retry scoring contract remains an implementation-specific acceptance topic; do not infer success or mastery from a retry alone.

## Accessibility and summary content

Use real DOM text for verdict counts and progress. The stacked bar is supplementary. Follow the contextual copy policy: clear instructional feedback during exercises and restrained encouragement on achievement screens. Explain why an answer was correct, partially correct or incorrect when the evaluator has defensible reasons. Respect reduced motion, avoid layout jumps, and keep actions operable by keyboard.

See [vocabulary selection](../../dictionary-data/vocabulary/vocabulary-selection.md), [learning evidence](learning-evidence.md), and [acceptance criteria](../../testing-quality/acceptance/approved-behavior-acceptance.md).

## Word mosaics: selection and pair feedback

Word mosaics is an interactive Chinese-to-meaning matching exercise. This section specifies approved target behavior, not verified current behavior. The shared Practice exercise frame owns session position, exercise instructions, navigation, common feedback presentation and persisted outcome reporting. Active exercise headers do not repeat the exercise type name, and an additional Exit practice button must not duplicate the session's top-right leave control. The game retains its own matched-pair count as an exercise-specific metric.

- **First selection:** The chosen tile remains unmistakably selected until the second selection, cancellation or a state transition. Use a prominent outline and elevated/contrasting treatment. The state must also be communicated without relying only on color. A second selection makes both tiles identifiable while their pairing is evaluated.
- **Correct pair:** Both selected tiles receive immediate, clearly visible green confirmation, after which they leave the interactive pool or become clearly locked as matched. Update the matched-pair count only once per successful pair, and prevent repeated scoring. Any optional Chinese audio is governed by the shared audio preferences.
- **Incorrect pair:** Briefly emphasize both selected tiles in red, show concise text that identifies the attempted pairing when helpful, record one incorrect submitted pairing, then automatically clear the selection so the learner can try again. The tiles remain available. Use visible error indicators beyond color. The feedback must not consist solely of the generic message `Not a match. Try again.`
- **Progressive hints:** The first mistake may receive concise error feedback without disclosing the answer. Repeated mistakes involving a tile progressively provide a meaningful semantic clue, and eventually may gently emphasize an appropriate candidate when the system has reliable mapping information. Do not invent a meaning or disclose the complete solution immediately on the first wrong selection. Hints and eventual correct matching must retain prior mistake/assistance evidence and must not automatically count as independent mastery.
- **Input and transitions:** Mouse, touch and keyboard users can make and change selections. Feedback timing is long enough to perceive, but does not leave the grid stuck in a feedback state. Respect reduced-motion preferences by retaining state, outline and text feedback without requiring flashing animation. Announce results accessibly and return focus predictably. Prevent double clicks and stale timers from resolving a different later selection.
- **Shared design:** Preserve the application's existing dark-violet card and immersive Practice view. Reuse shared selection, progress, feedback and actions conventions where possible, while keeping pair logic in the Word mosaics component. Avoid putting a separate custom header or redundant Exit practice control in this exercise.

An actual browser run is required to verify timings, semantic hints, screen-reader announcements, input handling, persistence and result scoring. Screenshot evidence of the current generic message does not establish that these requirements are implemented.
title: Practice outcomes and session lifecycle

# Practice profile portability

## Product contract

Saved Practice profiles are local-first. Provide **Export JSON** on each profile and **Import JSON** in the saved-profile workspace. Export produces a readable, versioned configuration document; import validates before presenting a preview and saving a new profile. This is configuration portability, not a means of copying an active session or sending a seeded session URL.

The export includes the profile name, exercise types, exercise-specific configuration, eligible vocabulary source and relevant selection settings. It must **not** include progress, session results, attempts, mastery, global exclusions, visitation history, AI service credentials or unrelated personal settings.

Use an explicit export envelope with a schema version independent from the internal local-storage shape. Validate file type, size, parsed structure, exercise options, identifiers, source references and unexpected fields before importing. Imported profiles receive a new local identifier and should permit renaming to resolve duplicates. Never execute or trust user-supplied file content.

A reference to a personal Word Set is not itself a copy of that Word Set. If the destination does not contain the referenced set, show a clear missing-source error and require explicit replacement or cancellation. Do not silently switch to a public HSK source. AI-dependent options must respect the recipient's configured provider availability and cannot carry credentials.

Profile actions belong in the **Saved Practice profiles** workspace: Rename, Duplicate, Export JSON and Delete on the profile menu; Import JSON next to Create profile. Preserve accessible labels, focus order, useful errors, and confirmation before destructive operations. See [Practice outcomes](practice-outcomes.md) and [acceptance](../../testing-quality/acceptance/approved-behavior-acceptance.md).
title: Practice profile portability

# Practice setup and session execution

## Four-step setup

The learner follows **Path -> Exercises -> Vocabulary -> Summary**. The setup remains a coherent wizard; Back and Continue never discard configured settings inadvertently. Continue requires the current step to be valid. Selected and unselected controls must be visibly and accessibly distinct.

### Path

Present the supported Practice paths without empty spacer panels. A route that cannot create a valid session explains the reason before launch.

### Exercises

Start without implicitly preselecting exercise types. Provide **Select all** and **Clear all** actions with accessible icon labels. Select all only includes supported, currently available activities; AI-dependent exercises are disabled when their required service is unavailable. Preserve exercise configuration while temporarily deselected. The Configure tab exposes each supported exercise's applicable settings; exercises with none have a truthful no-settings state, not an unexplained blank panel.

Use the same visual controls for equivalent option types: segmented controls for short exclusive options, full-width radio rows for descriptive alternatives, checkboxes for independent flags and clear multi-selection patterns. Exercise-specific differences in available settings are permitted. See [shared exercise foundation](shared-exercise-foundation.md).

### Vocabulary

Select HSK/dictionary filters or personal Word Sets, honoring exact-entry exclusions for every exercise and replacement. Display the global excluded count and a link to Word Sets > Excluded. Eligibility counting is a separate cancellable, nonblocking operation, not a synchronous filter triggered by every keystroke. Do not interpret a calculation failure as zero eligible words. The global pool-exhaustion policy is configured in Settings, not in this wizard. See [vocabulary selection](../../dictionary-data/vocabulary/vocabulary-selection.md) and [counting](../../dictionary-data/vocabulary/eligibility-counting.md).

### Summary

Show selected exercise types, source filters, count and effective global policy. Save a named configuration as a Practice profile without including learner results or credentials. Profile management and versioned JSON export/import belong in Saved Practice profiles; see [profile portability](practice-profile-portability.md). Validate the session's eligible source before starting without blocking the UI thread.

## Execution contract

A dedicated Practice session workspace persists unfinished progress and can be resumed. The top-right leave control is the sole leave action. It does not silently end or discard the session. Active exercise cards do not repeat exercise names. Session progress counts completed slots, while exercise-local metrics and long-term learning evidence remain distinct. Skip and Replace preserves the configured slot and past submitted mistakes; results use three verdicts rather than a universal percentage.

The [outcome contract](practice-outcomes.md), [shared foundation](shared-exercise-foundation.md) and [acceptance checklist](../../testing-quality/acceptance/approved-behavior-acceptance.md) own those behaviors. The source's translation-specific session host must not be assumed to support all heterogeneous activities merely because the same setup wizard exposes them.

## Implementation and verification pointers

Inspect `crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/practice/setup/`, `crates/zipeek-web/src/components/practice/setup/`, `crates/zipeek-exercises/src/practice_draft/` and session persistence services before changing code. This specification is the target behavior, not proof of current implementation.

Earlier implementation snapshots and checkpoint details are preserved in [archived setup source](../../archive-history/audits/superseded-maintained/learning-practice--practice--practice-session-builder-source.md).
title: Practice setup and session execution

# Settings workspace: implemented behavior

The Settings route is [`#/settings`](../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/route.rs). The active panel is managed by [`pages/system/settings/mod.rs`](../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/system/settings/mod.rs) and its seven-tab [`navigation.rs`](../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/system/settings/navigation.rs). This is the current layout, not the earlier five-section the historical source proposal.

| Tab | Current ownership |
| --- | --- |
| Appearance | Preset, light/dark and layout density via the shared preferences/theme state |
| Chinese Characters | Hanzi font preference and Character Builder sizes (Standard, Large, Extra large) |
| AI Translation | OpenAI-compatible endpoint, model ID, memory-only optional API key |
| Image Generation | Local image server configuration and test controls |
| Practice | Practice/matching audio preference |
| Learning | Practice history preference/status, saved outcome inspection, grouped backup/restore and deletion, and diagnostic worker check |


## Preferences and credentials

[`preferences.rs`](../../../crates/zipeek-web/src/preferences.rs) stores a JSON document at `zipeek.preferences.v1` with ten fields: `preset`, `density`, `dark`, `font`, `character_size`, `matching_autoplay`, `image_server_url`, `ai_url`, `ai_model`, `learning_history_enabled`. The source supplies defaults for omitted fields. The saved model and endpoint are shared with both the public translator and Practice generated translation; neither question should expose another editable model/URL form. [`zipeek-browser/src/ai_configuration.rs`](../../../crates/zipeek-browser/src/ai_configuration.rs) keeps an optional API key in thread-local browser module memory, not in the JSON preferences. It may be lost on reload.

Selecting a palette does not itself change dark/light mode. Font preference does not install a missing host font. Character Builder tiles share the selected font and size; pinyin labels are separate.

## Practice learning-history recording (unverified)

The Personal Data tab now exposes an explicit opt-in for saving completed Practice outcomes to a dedicated OPFS-backed personal DuckDB file (`zipeek-personal-learning-v1.duckdb`). The preference is off by default and stored as `learning_history_enabled` in the existing `zipeek.preferences.v1` JSON document. The former standalone consent key is no longer read or migrated; existing users who opted in using only that key must opt in again. The record includes session/step IDs, exercise IDs and outcomes only, not typed answers, AI-generated sentences, microphone audio or handwriting strokes. Completed temporary sessions are retained until a successful checkpoint, close and readback verification, with a retry control on failure. With recording off, the existing temporary cleanup remains the default.

The tab also offers a separately confirmed erase-history action. The existing portable JSON backup does **not** export or restore the personal DuckDB history. The database writer, Settings control, deletion flow and associated Rust code have not yet been browser/WASM tested; do not represent the checkpoint as a verified storage service. Authoritative progress aggregation remains unimplemented; the `/stats` page is currently a non-authoritative empty-state dashboard.

## worker availability diagnostics

The Pedagogy tab offers an explicit, one-shot health probe through the read-only the historical source monitor. The JavaScript bridge resolves `pedagogy-worker/` from `document.baseURI`, preserving `/` and `/zipeek/` deployment paths. The monitor starts an isolated worker for the probe and terminates it in `finally`. A missing generated worker WASM bundle is displayed as an error rather than a healthy or running engine. This diagnostic cannot enable tracking, read DuckDB history, enqueue analysis, or write mastery records. A successful probe confirms worker availability only. Live browser verification is pending.

## Test evidence and limitations

Rust browser suites for Settings, font persistence, Debug and panel navigation exist under [`crates/zipeek-e2e/tests/`](../../../crates/zipeek-e2e/tests). Tests authored in source are not the same as test runs: current Windows confirmation is listed in [CURRENT](../../project-management/current.md). Browser/screen-reader keyboard behavior and OPFS durability require their own acceptance evidence.

## Future storage work

Add verified portable history export/import, retention policy, schema migrations, user-data deletion integration, concurrency and quota recovery coverage before the personal database is considered fully production-ready. See [learning evidence](learning-evidence.md).

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/learning-practice-practice-settings-workspace.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.

## R596 Learning Data clarity checkpoint

The current settings UI displays the persisted `learning_history_enabled` preference as Practice history saving: On, Off or Unavailable. This preference is not a pedagogy-analysis enablement switch. A separate Pedagogical assessment status explicitly says the analysis is not connected to saved Practice evidence. The worker check remains a one-shot availability diagnostic under Technical diagnostics and cannot record or award proficiency. Backup/restore and deletion are grouped under collapsed sections, with separate history inspection and irreversible-history confirmation. Source changes are unverified by Rust/WASM/Chrome.

The approved long evidence-driven dragon in `docs/product-ux/foundation/header-and-dragon.md` is still open. Current `AppShell` uses a small conditional SVG and redundant centered route title; this does not satisfy the artwork or authoritative evidence contract.

## R600 Learning controls and ownership

The Settings > Learning page is limited to the persisted Practice recording preference, the current absence of authoritative pedagogical assessment, personal data backup/restore, deletion, and technical diagnostics. Counts, summaries, and activity history inspection belong to Statistics rather than Settings.

`settings/learning/recording.rs` owns the sole recording toggle and listens to the existing same-tab change event and cross-tab storage event. Persistence remains in `services/practice_history.rs`; a failed write does not display the requested value as saved. `settings/learning/progress.rs` presents no fictional proficiency or activity totals. `settings/learning/diagnostics.rs` owns only a local worker availability request. `personal_storage/` retains backup and deletion workflows; deleting Practice outcome history is a separate confirmation because the portable JSON backup excludes it.

R600 is source-only until Rust/WASM and browser accessibility tests pass.


## Recording preference versus assessed knowledge

The `learning_history_enabled` setting is a default-off preference to save completed Practice outcomes to personal DuckDB/OPFS. It is **not** a proficiency engine switch. A successful diagnostic worker health probe only confirms a reachable worker, not evidence ingestion, persisted assessment or active mastery. Recording status is refreshed through same-tab `zipeek-recording-change` and cross-tab `storage` events in the R596 source review, pending current browser verification. Backup/Restore, Delete and technical worker diagnostics are distinct settings responsibilities. The proposed R608 [Knowledge Points](../pedagogy/knowledge-points.md) model requires a dedicated policy/reset contract and durable validated evidence; it is not enabled by the recording toggle.
title: Settings workspace: implemented behavior

# Shared Practice exercise foundation

## Purpose and scope

All active Practice exercise types share a coherent Rust/Yew presentation and lifecycle foundation. The foundation supplies consistent accessibility, instructions, session status, feedback and navigation, while domain-specific components retain their own gameplay logic, input method and evaluation. This is an approved architectural target, not a claim that a shared implementation already exists.

## Component responsibilities

| Logical component | Owner and responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Practice session host | Session identity, configured slots, durable persistence, scheduling and resumption, global progress and exit behavior |
| Exercise frame | Consistent content hierarchy, accessible instruction, common feedback region and shared action placement |
| Exercise progress | Exercise-local counts (pairs, strokes, rounds) independent of session position |
| Exercise content | Typed task state, interaction and evaluation for the concrete exercise type |
| Outcome/attempt adapter | Typed correctness, hint/assistance evidence, attempt counts and session reporting |
| Shared audio control | Manual playback, user preferences, availability and safe audio lifecycle |

Use composition and typed props/actions rather than a large conditional component that owns every exercise's local fields. Shared UI components may be flexible about geometry: a writing canvas, matching grid, word bank or speech exercise must retain enough space to work.

## Common visible layout

- In-session exercise cards **do not display the exercise type name as their header**. Names remain appropriate in setup, profiles and detailed results.
- Display session position, such as `Exercise 2 of 5`, consistently. Distinguish it from exercise-local `3 of 8 pairs matched` or `Stroke 4 of 7`.
- Display instructions close to the activity; show mistake counts only when meaningful and comprehensible.
- A single top-right **Leave Practice** control saves progress for resumption. Do not duplicate an Exit practice button in the card. Ending or discarding a session is a separate explicit action.
- Use shared rules for selected, incorrect, partial, correct, assisted, waiting, completed and disabled states. Each state needs text or shape signals in addition to color.
- Preserve current Zipeek dark-violet visual identity and scenic immersive Practice layout; responsive and reduced-motion modes must remain operable.

## Lifecycle and evidence contracts

The common lifecycle distinguishes preparing, active input, submitted feedback, completed and skipped/replaced. Each type may have additional internal states but must not bypass the host's durability and outcomes contract.

A submitted attempt retains its evidence, even when a later attempt is successful. Outcomes use **Correct**, **Partially correct** and **Incorrect** where semantically valid. Skip and Replace generates a new item of the same type/configuration within the same session slot, records the skipped attempt separately and does not award mastery. Successful completion alone is not sufficient for acquisition evidence.

Feedback should explain the actual error when determinable, avoiding invented grammar or unsupported certainty. Do not produce an immediate full solution where correction and progressively helpful hints are pedagogically appropriate. Keyboard users and screen readers must be able to understand selection, feedback and next actions without color or motion.

## Exercise-specific adapters

- Word mosaics: two-tile selection visibility, red/green pair feedback, deselection and progressive semantic hints; see [outcomes](practice-outcomes.md).
- Character builder: indicate misplaced or wrong characters, allow correction where permitted and distinguish assisted final outcomes.
- Multiple Choice: balanced variants, pinyin visible by default only when non-revealing, automatic pronunciation enabled by default where a Chinese pronunciation target exists, manual replay whenever supported. Respect autoplay restrictions.
- Write Hanzi: maintain canvas transforms, cancellation, assisted-stroke evidence and playback reliability; see [writing activity](../hanzi/write-hanzi-activity.md).
- Matching and Listening: unify equivalent configuration controls and error/selection semantics without conflating their exercise-specific progress metrics.

## Acceptance and migration

Migrate existing exercises incrementally; each migrated type must retain its prior working gameplay and gain the shared shell, typed outcomes, input accessibility and persistence integration. Avoid an all-at-once replacement. E2E scenarios must assert session position, no duplicated titles/exit buttons, correct attempt accounting, focus transitions, mobile usability and resume behavior. Link concrete tests in the [E2E matrix](../../testing-quality/e2e/e2e-requirements-matrix.md); do not mark them passing without a browser run.
title: Shared Practice exercise foundation

# Sentence translation: utility and Practice exercise

Zipeek has **two different translation experiences**. They share Settings-owned AI endpoint and model configuration but do not share scoring semantics.

## Translate a supplied sentence

`#/translate-sentence` accepts text authored by the learner and provides a model-generated translation, including optional analysis where supported. It is a utility, not a scored Practice question. Source input limits, direction controls and cancellation/error handling are owned by the translator page and AI client. Do not count its requests as Practice results.

## Sentence Translation in Practice

Under Practice -> Advanced, select **Sentence Translation** as the only exercise, select a vocabulary source, translation direction (Chinese to English, English to Chinese, or Mixed) and five, ten or Endless questions. The launch creates a UUID-backed record at `#/practice/session/<id>`; it does not require AI model or endpoint fields inside the exercise.

Generated questions use a seeded sample of at most ten distinct eligible source words. The generation prompt requests only a Chinese sentence and an English translation. Zipeek validates the response, constructs the ordered answer and shuffled word bank, persists the generated instance, and exposes stable canonical tile-order attributes for tests. Repeated words are assigned occurrence-aware positions. These attributes are an E2E interaction seam, not proof the sentence is linguistically valid.

The learner assembles the translation, submits it for AI evaluation and sees feedback before advancing. Fixed runs stop at five or ten questions; Endless continues until explicitly finished. Reload and navigation can restore saved unfinished questions. Completion removes the temporary record and explains that results are not durably retained.

## AI and privacy

Settings -> AI stores the endpoint (`ai_url`) and model (`ai_model`) in the consolidated preferences document (`zipeek.preferences.v1`). The optional API key is held in tab memory, not persisted. Requests go from the learner's browser to the chosen provider and require compatible CORS and transport security. Do not place an administrator API secret in a public browser deployment.

The inspected but browser-unverified source includes an unverified opt-in Practice-outcome writer and recording preference; browser acceptance and portable export are pending. The personal OPFS/DuckDB facilities are not an exercise-outcome store. See [personal data](../../dictionary-data/personal/personal-data-storage.md) and [technical boundary](../../architecture/modules/sentence-exercises.md).

## Implementation and tests

- Translation utility: `crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/translation/sentence_translator/`.
- Standalone generated exercise: `crates/zipeek-web/src/pages/translation/sentence_practice/` (still independently routable).
- Persisted Practice: `crates/zipeek-web/src/services/practice_launch.rs`, `practice_generated.rs`, `practice_session_store/mod.rs`, and `pages/practice/local_session.rs`.
- AI config and request client: `crates/zipeek-web/src/services/ai/`, `crates/zipeek-ai/` and `crates/zipeek-ai-client/`.
- Deterministic and optional live Chrome tests: `crates/zipeek-e2e/tests/translation_fixture.rs` and `ai_learner.rs`.

See [current validation](../../project-management/current.md) before claiming the latest Practice integration is browser-verified.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/learning-practice-translation-translate-sentence.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.

# Word Discovery: AI examples and app notifications

The Random Word and Word of the Day cards share `WordSpotlight`. Copying Hanzi uses browser Clipboard, with visible success and error toasts provided by `ToastProvider` at app root. The toast automatically dismisses after 3.8 seconds, can be dismissed manually, and exposes accessible `status`/`alert` roles. This is an ephemeral notification; it is not persisted or exported.

**Example sentence** calls the configured OpenAI-compatible model only after the user presses the button. The request includes the displayed Hanzi, pinyin and dictionary display meaning, asks for one Chinese sentence and one English translation, and checks that the output contains the exact chosen Hanzi. It enforces a 1,200-character response cap. Successful output is explicitly **AI-generated and unverified**-not CC-CEDICT data or an authoritative pedagogical example. A missing model, endpoint failure, malformed response or absent target shows an error. Toggling the panel does not reissue the same request; choosing another random word clears the old example and invalidates an in-flight result. This functionality may incur provider fees.

The new Settings AI connection diagnostics show an inspectable bounded transcript of the test, including the exact fixed system/user prompts and returned text, without storing or rendering authentication credentials. A successful endpoint test is not a quality guarantee. The diagnostics are not exported with learning data.

The standalone About page retains licence and attribution information; Settings no longer duplicates that page. A legacy Themes deep link redirects to Settings. Debug is only rendered when `cfg!(debug_assertions)` is true and contains only non-secret runtime metadata. Release-build users see NotFound for the Debug route.

The next milestone still needs real Rust/Yew compilation and browser/LM Studio acceptance. The `scripts/` directory and root images are deferred in the historical review.

## Ordered meanings and metadata

Word Discovery and the daily spotlight now display one ordered dictionary sense at a time. The left and right controls are bounded and the selection resets on word changes. Topics and explicit qualifiers belong to each sense, not the entire word; the HSK and part-of-speech metadata remain at word level. AI examples use the currently selected sense and invalidate stale examples when that sense changes.

Generated databases must be rebuilt with the updated `sense_qualifiers` table. The importer preserves the source gloss in `word_senses`, removes only recognized leading annotations from `sense_display`, and stores explicit region, usage, and register labels with source provenance. The first supported tags are Taiwan, Loanword, Figurative, and Colloquial. Unknown annotations remain verbatim; the application does not infer regional or usage tags from arbitrary text. No database migration is supplied.

## Ordered meanings and source labels

Word Discovery and expanded Browse results use ordered `sense_display` records rather than reconstructing meanings from a combined English string. `sense_categories` provides the categories for an individual sense and `sense_qualifiers` stores strictly parsed leading source annotations. Only recognized markers are converted into structured labels; unrecognized tags remain visible as source gloss text. Example generation uses the currently selected sense and its response is invalidated when the sense changes. The generator requires a full database rebuild; there is no migration.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/learning-practice-translation-word-discovery-ai-examples.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.

| Chinese dictionary and HSK sources | [Dictionary sources](../dictionary-data/schema/sources.md), [import rules](../dictionary-data/schema/import-rules.md), [bundled source notices](../build-deployment/handoff.md) | Preserve the applicable CC-CEDICT, HSK and derived-data notices; confirm provenance of the installed generated database. |
| HSK source dataset | `crates/zipeek-web/static/notices/HSK-LICENSE.txt` and `HSK-SOURCE-README.txt` | Retain their full terms and source attribution as provided. |
| Province Quest geography | Local AreaCity-JsSpider-StatsGov generated map bundle (dataset revision `2025.251231.260403`); upstream references include AreaCity, National Geographical Names Database, Tencent Maps, and Amap | Upstream licensing and redistribution rights remain unresolved. Use only for local development pending review; include source and license notices before public distribution. |
| Shared artwork and UI assets | `crates/zipeek-web/static/ATTRIBUTION.md`, `static/courses/` and `static/practice/` | Verify provenance, generation rights, adaptation and any required attribution before publishing or claiming exclusive ownership. |
| Fonts, icons, JS/WASM and other Rust dependencies | Manifest and lockfile dependencies, bundled notices and generated frontend assets | Generate or review a complete distribution-specific notice inventory; do not assert that every package uses the same license. |

External sources relevant to verification include [Hanzi Writer Data](https://github.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data), [Hanzi Writer](https://github.com/chanind/hanzi-writer) and [CC-CEDICT](https://www.mdbg.net/chinese/dictionary?page=cedict). These links identify resources, not confirmation of all obligations in a particular distribution.

## Learning and design inspirations

- [Duolingo](https://www.duolingo.com/) is an example of a language-learning product whose structured exercises and progress feedback can inform design exploration.
- [Ninchanese](https://ninchanese.com/) is an example of a Chinese-learning product whose vocabulary and gamification approaches can inform exploration.

These are acknowledgements of inspiration only, not claims that Zipeek uses their code, artwork, trademarks or lesson content. Zipeek is not presented as affiliated with, authorized by or endorsed by these services.

## Maintenance and release requirements

Before a public distribution, compare actual bundled datasets and artwork with the attribution manifest. Include required full license texts, source details and any attribution of modified material in the appropriate shipped notices. Keep the in-app footer's Credits link discoverable and keep mandatory license access independent of an optional web connection. Track unresolved provenance questions as engineering tasks rather than inventing a license.
title: Credits and acknowledgements

# Global header and dragon-shaped learning progress

## Design intent

The current visual reference is the **long, detailed horizontal Chinese dragon** approved during the UI review. The dragon itself forms the progress indicator. Do not substitute a generic rectangular bar with an adjacent dragon icon, simple wave, emoji or unsupported percentage badge.

The header contains branding and navigation at the start, the long dragon across available space, and global appearance/settings controls at the end. Remove redundant centered page titles from the global header; each page owns its contextual title inside its main content. Active Practice exercise names are also omitted from their cards.

## Dragon artwork and progress

- Preserve intricate dragon-head details, horns, whiskers, scales, flowing body and tail, and the violet-and-gold visual direction established by the approved mockup.
- The dragon's body itself visualizes **persisted pedagogical evidence**, with brighter completed regions and a subdued unreached region. The source of progress is not merely completed sessions, visited words or independent counters.
- Show **no visible stage name, level, percentage or other labels above the dragon**. Explanatory details appear only on deliberate pointer/keyboard interaction.
- Progress transitions smoothly without distortion, scaling artifacts, stale renders or changing the header's height. The same artwork should align in the completed and incomplete layers.
- A detail panel on click/keyboard activation may show the relevant evidence categories, current developmental stage and next milestone. Do not invent numerical mastery measures until their actual mapping to persisted evidence is defined.
- Artwork should be as faithful to the agreed reference as feasible; an expedient vector approximation is not acceptance. Rendering technique and asset form should be chosen based on fidelity, sharpness and sustainable performance.

## Responsive behavior

The dragon uses remaining horizontal space but must not crowd or overlap the navigation menu, branding, user controls or focus rings. On narrow screens, show a recognizable compact portion and provide progress details on interaction. Mobile collapse must not imply different scoring. Use semantic controls with focus-visible styling and an accurate accessible progress description derived from real data.

## Animation and reliability

Animate only meaningful progress changes and occasional stage transitions, never continuous distracting motion. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. Cancel stale animation tasks during route changes, data refresh and unmount; delayed frames must not present a newer learning record with an older fill state. Treat a missing or failed evidence store as an error, not `0% mastery`.

## Verification

Test actual artwork at the target desktop header width, intermediate breakpoints and narrow mobile layouts. Verify detail panel mouse/keyboard/focus behavior, persistent evidence consistency, theme contrast, reduced-motion behavior and loading/error states. Compare the rendered implementation to the approved mockup and actual app screenshots; do not claim visual fidelity from a source-code inspection alone.


## Implemented unassessed state and future scoring

The current header source uses `components/shell/app_shell/header/dragon.rs` and the unassessed artwork at `static/practice/header-dragon-unassessed.webp`. The illustration is shown independently of the Practice recording preference and explicitly reports unavailable/unassessed evidence, not a completion percentage. The diagnostic pedagogy worker and optional Practice outcome records do not authorize a dragon progress projection. Connect only validated, durable, policy-approved R608 scoring after the evidence journal, canonical denominator, access and UI states are established. Visual fidelity, responsive and reduced-motion acceptance remain open.
title: Global header and dragon-shaped learning progress

# Interface and platform policy

## Copy, feedback and formatting

Zipeek uses **contextual** language: concise and instructional during exercises, modestly encouraging for genuine achievements. Use sentence case for titles, controls and messages. Give specific, actionable explanations for correct, partially correct and incorrect verdicts where the evaluator can justify them. Do not show unsupported evaluation confidence. Avoid redundant headings and repeated instructions. Use consistent plurals, time formats and numeric presentation.

Use `HSK 7-9` as the advanced-band label. Traditional Hanzi is a secondary display, not a change to dictionary identity or matching keys. Follow existing approved character display rules in their owning feature specifications. Honor keyboard, screen reader, responsive and reduced-motion behavior.

## Progressive disclosure and useful interface copy

Show text when it helps a person make a decision or recover from a problem, not merely to describe the current implementation state. A visible label must earn its place by explaining an unfamiliar action, identifying data, or communicating important information that cannot be inferred from the interface. Prefer discoverable, theme-integrated controls, clear grouping and progressive disclosure to permanent instructional paragraphs.

- Do not expose internal state names such as `Empty`, `Drawing`, or `Image added` as badges when the current content already communicates that state. Keep such state in typed application logic.
- Do not repeat a page title as a card heading or repeat the same instruction in the page subtitle, action panel and footer. A simple drawing workspace needs the canvas, meaningful actions and results, not prose explaining each step.
- Use disabled affordances for unavailable actions when the cause is obvious, rather than permanently showing messages like `Add input before submitting`. If an unavailable action needs a non-obvious explanation, place it contextually near that action.
- Prefer concise icon-only controls for familiar secondary actions such as Undo and Clear when supported by an understandable icon. Give them accessible names, visible keyboard focus, descriptive tooltips and appropriately sized touch targets. Do not rely on icon shape alone for unfamiliar or high-impact actions.
- Use visible loading feedback during actual waits, a clear empty state only when it helps orientation, and actionable error or recovery text only when a failure occurs. Do not render status chatter or success narration after routine edits.
- Present recognition uncertainty where it changes a decision, such as an unverified candidate; do not surround every result with repeated disclaimers. Keep verified dictionary facts distinguishable from AI suggestions.
- Privacy and consent information must remain accessible and timely. Preserve necessary disclosures at the point of consequential sharing or in a linked contextual explanation, rather than repeating long privacy paragraphs throughout the workspace. Explicit user-triggered uploads and existing privacy protections remain mandatory.
- Audit copy in desktop, mobile, light and dark layouts. Remove redundant text before shrinking fonts or tightening spacing; reduced reading burden is a design goal, not merely a vertical-height optimization.

These rules do not remove accessible names, validation messages, meaningful empty states, setup prerequisites, security disclosures, or error diagnostics. Screen-reader labels and programmatic state remain available even when redundant visible copy is removed.

## Form controls and shared interaction design

Zipeek must not expose unstyled browser-default selects, checkboxes, radios or pagination that clash with the active theme. Use one consistent, reusable control vocabulary for sizing, color tokens, disabled/hover/focus states and pointer/touch targets. Preserve native HTML semantics whenever possible while styling their presentation; a custom-painted surface is not permission to lose keyboard, label, focus, screen-reader or form behavior.

- Prefer semantic native input elements with theme-integrated appearance where their behavior is sufficient. For application-specific selection patterns, reusable Yew button-based checkbox or switch controls may be used only with complete accessible state and keyboard operation.
- Put reusable controls in the relevant shared UI layer when multiple features need them; avoid independently inventing one-off toggles and dropdowns per route. For prototypes that do not yet have consumers outside a feature, a focused feature-local reusable component is acceptable.
- For custom listboxes or select menus, support Escape, arrow keys, Enter/Space, focus restoration, selection announcement, click-away behavior and mobile touch before replacing a native select. Prefer a styled native select if that full interaction contract is not justified.
- Keep filter values, pagination selection and checkbox state in typed reducer state when they affect multiple panels. Users should never need to infer a persistent selection from hover color alone.
- Test in Light, Dark, System, reduced motion, keyboard-only and narrow viewport states. Use design tokens rather than hard-coded colors.

## Appearance

Default theme preference is **System** and follows operating system light/dark changes live. Explicit Light and Dark overrides persist across sessions. Preserve existing saved user selections as feasible while respecting the project's development compatibility policy. Theme colors, including empty and disabled states, must remain legible.

## Startup and database recovery

If essential dictionary initialization or DuckDB loading fails, show a **blocking recovery screen** with a human-readable cause, Retry and optionally expandable diagnostic details. Do not enter the normal application with fabricated empty data. Retry must actually rerun initialization without erasing local settings, Word Sets or learning history. Genuine successful queries returning no matching words are ordinary empty states, not startup failures.

## Public discovery

Zipeek is a publicly indexed application. Maintain descriptive titles and descriptions, canonical URLs, appropriate indexing rules and Open Graph previews. Avoid exposing, indexing or sharing private session state, local learner data or temporary routes. Respect hosted `/zipeek/` paths and any development root-path routing differences.

## Engineering policy

Rust implementation code has **no comments**, including explanatory comments, doc comments, TODO comments and lint-allowance justifications. Prefer clear identifiers, types and module boundaries; document architecture rationale here in maintained documents instead. Dependencies should prefer current stable releases, but **any** addition or update, including transitive updates through `cargo update`, requires explicit user approval. Keep the root lockfile and locked checks. Never perform dependency upgrades incidentally.

## Reset app

The user approved a Settings Reset app section on 2026-11-26. Its destructive action is labeled **Clear all data and start over**, explains permanent deletion and retained dictionary/model/exported files, and requires explicit confirmation. Reset must clear the browser/WebView and native personal stores that actually hold learner state; navigating to Home alone is insufficient. On full success, reload the deployment's landing page with onboarding restored. On partial failure, retain a visible error and Retry, without a success message or automatic transition to landing. Close other Zipeek tabs/windows before reset; active sessions block cleanup. See [personal storage](../../dictionary-data/personal/personal-data-storage.md#confirmed-app-reset-2026-11-26).
title: Interface and platform policy

# Ux Accessibility

## Accessibility

Pragmatic accessibility (UX-A11Y01): implement the rules below without claiming
formal WCAG conformance. Practice feedback announcements are deliberately
omitted; a future summary canvas must have its numeric stats in adjacent DOM text.

- All actions support keyboard use: Tab, Enter/Space, plus documented shortcuts.
  This includes cards, answers, navigation, theme/drawer toggles, pronunciation,
  GitHub and progression actions. No mouse-only elements.
- Every focusable element has a visible focus ring/outline with at least 3:1
  contrast against its surroundings; never remove outlines without replacement.
- Prefer native buttons, links, nav, main and aside. Avoid redundant roles,
  unnecessary ARIA or tabindex; use tabindex only for a specific focus target.
- Correct/wrong feedback includes visible ✓/✗ alongside green/red, independent
  of hover. This applies to match cards and MCQ answers.
- Text contrast is at least 4.5:1; UI boundaries, focus rings and icon strokes
  at least 3:1. Check muted traditional hanzi, dimmed answers, theme control,
  footer and feedback states in both themes.
- Touch targets are at least 24×24 CSS px or sufficiently spaced for a 24px
  circle not to overlap another target. Aim for 44×44px on mobile controls.
  The footer's icon-only GitHub link must meet the 24×24px minimum.
- Committed route navigation moves focus to the new main or heading and updates
  `document.title` so routes are distinguishable, e.g. "Practice - Zipeek".
- A mobile overlay drawer contains focus with a close action returning it to
  the toggle, or uses an inline/nonmodal arrangement without moving focus.
  Never strand focus, expose obscured content through Tab, or trap the user.
- Retain the existing skip link: focus main without changing the route.
- Keep `<html lang="en">`; standalone hanzi uses `lang="zh-CN"` where practical.
- Search/future inputs need a visible label or aria-label, not only a placeholder.
- Reduced motion disables nonessential motion and keeps semantic colour changes.
  Practice selection, correctness and score updates have no live announcements.
title: Ux Accessibility

# Appearance and theme behavior

## Theme preference

The default is **System**, which follows operating-system light and dark appearance changes without a reload. A user-selected Light or Dark preference overrides System and persists. Preserve a previously saved explicit preference where feasible without requiring backwards-compatibility readers that conflict with the active-development policy.

The loading shell, database error recovery screen, route content, cards, header and footer must use a coherent theme; no avoidable flashing of the opposite theme. Contrast, selected-state clarity and focus-visible affordances remain usable in both themes. The landscape art can be retained with translucent overlays when text remains legible.

## Global header and footer

The top panel owns navigation, Zipeek branding, the [long evidence-based dragon](header-and-dragon.md) and global controls. It does not repeat page titles. The footer is centered within the main content region, excludes sidebar width and wraps accessibly on narrow viewports without overlapping the Practice reminder. Preserve mandatory legal attribution, Credits link and the repository link with appropriate accessible names and safe external-link behavior.

## Motion

Reduced-motion preference disables nonessential progress shimmers, tile movement and transition effects without removing state feedback. Themes, layout and status must be accessible even when motion is suppressed.

See [platform policy](interface-and-platform-policy.md), [global UX](../ux.md) and [acceptance](../../testing-quality/acceptance/approved-behavior-acceptance.md). A prior dark-default theme contract is preserved in [historical source](../../archive-history/audits/superseded-maintained/product-ux--foundation--ux-appearance-source.md) only.
title: Appearance and theme behavior

# Landing Page

## Purpose and scope

Only new visitors to the root Home route receive a short first-visit landing experience. The current application Home, Word of the Day, navigation drawer and all functional routes are unchanged after entry. This is not a mandatory account sign-in or a wizard.

## Entry and persistence

- On root `#/`, show the landing if `zipeek.preferences.v1` is absent and the browser has no existing personal Word Sets, Pinyin course progress, or excluded-vocabulary record.
- Clicking **Enter Zipeek** initializes `zipeek.preferences.v1` with default settings only if it does not already exist. No independent welcome marker is stored.
- Existing users with preferences or learning records bypass the landing.
- Direct links such as `#/browse`, `#/write-hanzi`, and `#/games/cloud-match` bypass the welcome screen.
- App startup does not write default appearance preferences merely to render the initial theme; user actions persist preferences explicitly.
- localStorage is a required application environment dependency. If browser policy denies access, startup reports an explicit initialization failure instead of silently treating the visitor as new.

## UI contract

- Full-height introductory hero with a concise proposition, a single prominent Enter action using the Yew Lucide play icon, and a theme-aware, static product preview. The preview includes a 16:9 media slot and feature labels for Practice, Browse, and Word Sets; it must not imply that a video is playable until a trailer exists.
- No drawer, application header, promotional tagline badge or footer on the first-visit landing. Normal shell appears immediately after entry.
- Keyboard-operable button and reduced-motion behavior. The layout stacks on narrow displays.
- Do not initialize the dictionary for the landing itself. The preview is static and does not require data or network requests. A future trailer may replace its media slot without changing the first-visit entry contract.

## Verification

Source contract tests are not equivalent to a compiled/browser pass. Run Windows Rust/WASM checks, then verify first root visit, entry and reload, existing-user bypass, direct deep links, theme colors, touch/keyboard navigation and the explicit startup failure when localStorage is blocked. Do not reset actual learning data to test onboarding; use a clean browser profile or an isolated origin.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/product-ux-pages-landing-page.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.
title: Landing Page
