# Documentation quality and remaining reconciliation

## Organization and authoritative ownership

The twelve top-level documentation sections correspond to the twelve sections in the application Docs reader. Maintained articles use lowercase kebab-case filenames, except conventional README entry points. Topic subfolders are preferred when they separate substantially different subjects; folder depth should not exceed three levels below the repository root for normal articles.

- Product and UX owns application-wide interaction policy, page-level behavior and accessibility.
- Learning and Practice owns exercise behavior, outcomes, pedagogy, course requirements and profile portability.
- Games owns game mechanics and feedback.
- Dictionary and Data owns data generation, storage, vocabulary selection and eligibility.
- Architecture owns module boundaries, state ownership and runtime contracts.
- Engineering owns coding standards and contributor workflows.
- Testing and Quality owns acceptance, browser scenarios and evidence policy.
- Build and Deployment owns CI, packaging, build tasks and optional services.
- Project Management owns active work, technical debt and approved decisions.
- Archive and History owns historical implementation narratives and superseded proposals.
- Issues owns defect reproductions and screenshots.
- Getting Started owns onboarding and first-run navigation.

The [credits](../product-ux/credits.md), [shared Practice foundation](../learning-practice/practice/shared-exercise-foundation.md), [header and dragon](../product-ux/foundation/header-and-dragon.md), and [eligibility counting](../dictionary-data/vocabulary/eligibility-counting.md) are maintained requirements, not implementation evidence.

The [current UX overview](../product-ux/ux.md), [Practice overview](../learning-practice/practice/practice-overview.md), and [browser E2E overview](../testing-quality/e2e/overview.md) are reader entry points. They link to authoritative topic contracts rather than duplicating them. The original dated narrative compilations were retained under [historical audits](../archive-history/audits/).

## Verification boundary

A passing Docs index and link check verifies path consistency, not editorial accuracy, browser rendering, or Rust compilation. Changes to the Docs reader need a Rust/WASM build and browser navigation test before being marked verified.

## Editorial reconciliation status

The former inventory of 55 maintained files was an estimate. The source-specific scan identified 53 files with numbered development references. All 53 have historical source snapshots, and their current-document disposition is tracked in the [editorial reconciliation inventory](editorial-reconciliation.md).

Twelve historical review pages were reduced to references linking the preserved source and current subject owner. The remaining 41 files retain implementation and technical detail with release chronology separated into the source archive. This resolves the identified release-marker cleanup task, not every possible factual disagreement between old documentation and the present code.

## Remaining verification work

- [Source-accuracy audit](source-accuracy-audit.md) has reconciled the workspace, database manifest, generator policy and selected startup boundaries. Continue verifying unsampled technical descriptions and the absent binary artifact in a running browser before asserting runtime completion.
- Inspect the Docs reader in real Chrome after the folder moves, including deep links, search, images and all twelve sections.
- Verify third-party licenses and asset provenance using shipped files, not merely aspirational Credits text.
- Align the E2E coverage matrix with executable Rust scenarios and run strict evidence capture on the supported browser environment.

One link in a frozen completed record still targets a removed source-contract script. Preserve that historical record; treat its warning separately from maintained-document validation.


## Release-review prevention and canonical-document workflow

A release must update the existing subject owner before treating a new design or implementation narrative as current documentation. Root-level R-numbered working notes and R-numbered reviews under `docs/engineering/` are not allowed as ongoing subject documentation. If a genuinely new subject lacks an owner, create a lowercase-kebab-case maintained article under the appropriate existing category and link it from `docs/README.md`.

Release-specific implementation narratives are reconciled into (a) current product/architecture/testing contracts, (b) still-open stable tasks/debt, and (c) a single historical review archive or release history. Date-specific checks and compiler/test claims remain historical and must never be promoted to current verification by relocation. Before removing old files, update maintained links, Docs index and browser-route fixtures. New `R...` Markdown documents under `docs/engineering/` require historical classification instead of creating a parallel authority.

The R610 documentation consolidation placed release-review source text into [one historical collection](../archive-history/audits/release-engineering-review-history.md) and linked the new [knowledge specification](../learning-practice/pedagogy/knowledge-points.md) and [scoring architecture](../architecture/modules/knowledge-scoring.md). This is an editorial ownership change only; no Rust tests or behavioural acceptance follow from it.

## Review limitations

- Marker removal and provenance separation are not equivalent to a source-level technical audit. Assertions about package ownership, stored data, dependencies, route behavior, current content totals and browser availability must still be checked against current source and live tests.
- The records in the historical audit collection are frozen source evidence. Historical tests and release claims do not count as current passing verification.
- The maintained source-archive naming specification necessarily includes an abstract filename pattern. It does not cite a past numbered release as product behavior.
- Documentation validation checks link targets and the generated search index, but not Rust compilation, browser rendering, pedagogical correctness or licensing.

# Source-to-documentation accuracy audit

## Scope and evidence

This review compares maintained documentation with the source snapshot in the same project archive. It is **not** a Rust compilation, a DuckDB data-file integrity test, a Chrome observation, or an exhaustive audit of every page. No dependencies or Rust application logic were changed. The current source manifest and manifest/policy code are authoritative for what this snapshot declares; approved UX documents define intended future behavior.

## Verified source facts and corrections

| Subject | Source evidence | Reconciled fact | Verification limit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cargo workspace | [`Cargo.toml`](../../Cargo.toml) | 22 member crates, Rust 2024 workspace, resolver 2, root lockfile | Crates not compiled in this review |
| Dictionary rows | [`hanzi.manifest.json`](../../crates/zipeek-web/static/hanzi.manifest.json) | **120,970 `words` rows**, not 12,188 | Manifest declaration only |
| Dictionary identity candidates | Same manifest | **120,970** | Manifest declaration only |
| Dictionary source entries | Same manifest | **11,494** HSK source entries | Source count, not database rows |
| Character occurrences | Same manifest | **312,649** | Manifest declaration only |
| Explicit character readings | Same manifest | **11,846** | Manifest declaration only |
| Diagnostics | Same manifest and [`hanzi.diagnostics.json`](../../crates/zipeek-web/static/hanzi.diagnostics.json) | **10,187** events | Not independently replayed |
| Engine and storage | [`policy.rs`](../../crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/policy.rs), [`writer.rs`](../../crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/artifact/writer.rs), manifest | Native engine `v2.0.0`, explicit storage `v2.0.0` | Browser engine version still requires a live query |
| WASM package | [`package.json`](../../crates/zipeek-web/package.json), generator policy, manifest | `@duckdb/duckdb-wasm@1.33.1-dev114.0` | Package lock and runtime not executed |
| Generated file name | Manifest | `hanzi-20261115-215819.duckdb` and `.gz` | **Neither database binary is included in this source archive** |
| Dictionary tables | Manifest `tables`, [`schema.sql`](../../crates/zipeek-db-gen/src/schema.sql) | `character_readings` **is listed** in the checked-in manifest | Physical database still needs open/query verification |
| Browser startup | [`database_provider.rs`](../../crates/zipeek-web/src/components/providers/database_provider.rs), [`database_boundary.rs`](../../crates/zipeek-web/src/components/providers/database_boundary.rs), [`route.rs`](../../crates/zipeek-web/src/route.rs) | Loading/ready/failure/retry boundary exists, but several routes bypass it | Approved whole-app failure blocking is not implemented |
| Other-tab coordination | [`coordinator.rs`](../../crates/zipeek-web/src/components/shell/app_shell/other_tab/coordinator.rs), [`mod.rs`](../../crates/zipeek-web/src/components/shell/app_shell/other_tab/mod.rs) | BroadcastChannel heartbeats and a **bottom-right warning**, not exclusive first-tab ownership | Browser behavior and crash recovery unverified |
| Header | [`app_shell/mod.rs`](../../crates/zipeek-web/src/components/shell/app_shell/mod.rs) | Centered route title remains part of the general header | Approved dragon-shaped evidence header not implemented |
| Learner storage | [`preferences.rs`](../../crates/zipeek-web/src/preferences.rs), [`word_sets.rs`](../../crates/zipeek-web/src/services/word_sets.rs), [`exclusions.rs`](../../crates/zipeek-web/src/services/exclusions.rs), [`practice_session_store/mod.rs`](../../crates/zipeek-web/src/services/practice_session_store/mod.rs) | Separate browser keys exist for preferences, Word Sets, exclusions and Practice sessions | Persistence not browser-verified |

## Important distinctions

- **12,188** describes distinct reading keys in a historical HSK source grouping and can remain in clearly labeled source-coverage documents. It must not be used as the count of the current expanded `words` table.
- The manifest contains checksums for the generated `.duckdb` and `.gz` assets, but the source ZIP does not include those files. Their absence prevents inspection of actual on-disk rows, FTS index usability, `character_readings` queryability and hash agreement.
- Historical approved decisions may describe a previous storage format. They remain preserved as history; the current checked-in generator and manifest use `v2.0.0`. Any future change to dependencies, generator pins or format requires explicit approval.
- The UI specification's full-screen duplicate-tab block, original-tab ownership and long dragon progress are approved **requirements**, not behaviors shown by the inspected Rust source.
- The database provider already has a retryable failure state, but the route-level boundary is not whole-application blocking. Do not report compliance with the approved startup policy until implemented and browser-tested.

## Remaining gates

1. On the user's Windows toolchain, compile the workspace and WASM target with `--locked`; address compiler errors separately from this documentation audit.
2. Prepare the generated dictionary through the approved explicit workflow, verify manifest hashes, open the real database and inspect `words`, `character_readings`, normalized relations and FTS queries.
3. Test dictionary initialization, failure/retry and route gating in Chrome at root and `/zipeek/`.
4. Test multiple tabs, abrupt termination, stale ownership and write exclusion with actual browser sessions.
5. Verify browser storage round trips, personal OPFS persistence and session recovery in browser E2E before treating source presence as successful data durability.
6. Review remaining specialist implementation documents and E2E assertions beyond this focused architecture/data/runtime inventory.

## Audit discipline

Maintain source truth and approved future requirements separately. A source file proves that code or a manifest declaration exists, not that the deployed application performs correctly. A passed documentation validator proves links and index consistency, not runtime behavior.
title: Source-to-documentation accuracy audit

# Technical debt register

Track implementation and verification liabilities here. [Tasks](tasks.md) is the active open-task triage index, and [historical acceptance ledger](../archive-history/LEGACY_ACCEPTANCE_LEDGER.md) preserves the unresolved historical checkpoint gates; [Current](current.md) records active checkpoint state. An item is resolved only when its acceptance evidence is recorded; source-contract tests alone do not prove Rust compilation or browser behavior.

| ID | Priority | Area | Evidence and impact | Resolution / acceptance gate | State |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TD-001 | P0 | Rust/WASM and browser acceptance | A complete current-tree native/WASM build and managed Chrome acceptance have not been established in this archive. | `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, affected native tests, locked WASM check and Chrome E2E all pass on pinned Windows toolchain; attach diagnostics. | Open |
| TD-003 | P1 | Grammar assessment authoring quality | 24 draft MCQs and five construction challenges require qualified Mandarin review; plausible, unambiguous distractors and coverage cannot be proven by automatic syntax checks. | Language review, item revision record, semantic rationale checks, validated item provenance and independent assessment policy before mastery eligibility. | Open |
| TD-004 | P1 | Grammar assessment model | Authored content integrity and stable scoring snapshots require verification against the current implementation. | Bind scoring to complete immutable authored items, reject orthographically duplicate choices, verify wrong-answer/restart flows, and run native/WASM/Chrome checks. | Source hardening reported historically; native/WASM/Chrome verification open |
| TD-005 | P1 | Pedagogical evidence and worker | Opt-in UI is not activated; `snapshot_verified` is caller-provided, and application-level verified DuckDB readback / single-tab ownership are absent. | Approved consent/provenance contract, transaction/readback confirmation, single-tab exclusion, restart and browser failure tests. | Open |
| TD-006 | P1 | Docs Markdown | Parser migration and safe Markdown link rendering are implemented; cross-document heading targets previously conflicted with the Yew hash-router syntax. | Verify Rust fixtures, locked WASM build, Chrome navigation (including reload/history) under root and `/zipeek/`, and scroll-to-heading behavior. | Source-level fixes are documented; Rust/WASM and Chrome acceptance remain open. Compilation and Chrome acceptance remain open |
| TD-007 | P1 | Courses mosaic and curriculum | Grammar and vocabulary curriculum completeness, qualification rules, geometry and official HSK mappings require current source and browser verification. | Source-backed HSK mapping, content review, geometry screenshots and independently verified reveal predicates. | Open |
| TD-008 | P1 | E2E full journeys | Standard journey and pedagogical seven-day endurance journey have not been run successfully in managed Chrome; enabled variant depends on the unfinished evidence pipeline. | Run reproducible seeded journeys with screenshots, genuine scored interactions and explicit no-pedagogy/Dragon assertions. | Open |
| TD-009 | P2 | Generated static assets | Source archives require generated-asset preflight and cross-target verification; ZIP integrity alone does not establish deployability. Node source/deploy preflight and offline tests now exist, and Rust source preflight permits a not-yet-generated Worker. | Native build asset preflight that checks generated index, bootstrap, WASM and artwork against manifest; ZIP integrity alone is insufficient. | Partially addressed: static integrity gate authored and Node tests executed; real deploy, Rust, WASM and browser acceptance open |


## Review procedure

When modifying a feature, inspect its relevant debt IDs and update source/tests together. Report newly discovered debt, addressed debt, and remaining acceptance evidence in [Current](current.md) and release notes. Do not close a debt entry solely because a draft test was added.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/project-management-technical-debt.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.

## R581 Statistics Grammar debt review

- **TD-STATS-GRAMMAR-001, P1, open:** All source teaching entries have pending editorial review; teaching-region IDs must not become invented course IDs or assessed grammar point identities. Gate: verified curriculum/canonical mapping and distinct assessment provenance.
- **TD-STATS-GRAMMAR-002, P1, open:** The Grammar UI now uses two bounded async source queries (table and six-item suggestion page), but suggestions have no request debounce or complete combobox keyboard/focus contract. Gate: browser test Arrow/Escape/Enter behavior, accessible active descendant, request-burst measurement and a dedicated source suggestion API if required.
- **TD-STATS-GRAMMAR-003, P1, open:** Source-level typed filtering/sorting does not equal validated backend pagination. Gate: production adapter tests for stable snapshot order, filter semantics and request cancellation under concurrent edits.
- **TD-STATS-GRAMMAR-004, P0, open:** Rust/WASM compile, Chrome E2E, responsive/theme checks and 5,000/10,000-record performance still require actual execution. Gate: Windows toolchain and browser evidence in the acceptance ledger.

## R601 module-boundary review

Ten approved source targets were refactored into responsibility-oriented modules. Source-level extraction is recorded in [component and state refactor review](../engineering/component-state-refactor-review.md). Do not close TD-001 or any affected workflow debt until the locked compiler and browser gates pass. Large Practice controllers, AI test lifecycle, exercise runtimes and DuckDB transaction handling remain open for follow-up.


## Consolidated architecture candidates and remaining gates

The historical ten-target R600 shortlist has been reconciled against the current R609 source at a **module existence and review-summary level**, not a successful compiler acceptance. Practice local-session and generated-session directories, Statistics reducer/query split, AI Settings directory, crossword and time-weaver work, exercise session transitions, and personal/recognition DuckDB modules were subjects of R601-R607 remediation. The R600 source paths and line counts are historical, not current navigation guidance.

**Open:** (1) locked Rust/WASM/Chrome acceptance for all touched modules (TD-001); (2) external AI-generation transport cancellation and stale response browser races; (3) genuinely atomic cross-tab Practice writes; (4) DuckDB partial-commit/quota/recovery and single-writer semantics; (5) Statistics stable selection/query IDs and performance, Grammar keyboard/debounce semantics; (6) R608 evidence journal, independent-context certification and evaluator schema. The existence of split `mod.rs` files does **not** close any behavioural debt without tested invariants. The original R600 candidate rationale remains preserved in [historical review](../archive-history/audits/release-engineering-review-history.md).

# Acceptance for approved product behavior

These are acceptance contracts, not recorded test passes. Source implementation must be assessed separately from actual Rust, WASM and Chrome execution.

## Practice outcomes and progression

- [ ] A mixed session displays Correct, Partially correct and Incorrect counts using accessible text and a stacked distribution without a universal percent.
- [ ] An exercise without partial scoring does not invent a partial verdict.
- [ ] Matching retains pair-specific attempts; handwriting retains rejected and assisted strokes without falsely awarding unassisted success.
- [ ] Session progress advances for completed slots; dragon acquisition responds only to persisted qualifying learning evidence.
- [ ] Skip replaces the same exercise type and slot without consuming the configured completion count.
- [ ] Multiple skips cannot spin forever or immediately repeat identical content where alternatives exist.
- [ ] Prior submitted attempts remain accounted for; skipped content produces no new mastery event.
- [ ] Resume restores the current session; new session reuses configuration and selects new eligible content without URL-encoded state.

## Vocabulary policies

- [ ] Pedagogical mode prioritizes rare recently failed words ahead of unseen entries and reduces priority after repeated successful evidence.
- [ ] Pedagogical mode off rotates less recently visited words without creating mastery evidence.
- [ ] Enabled multiple-choice formats are approximately balanced and do not override eligible vocabulary constraints.
- [ ] Excluding a standalone character entry does not exclude longer entries containing it.
- [ ] Global exact-entry exclusions apply across HSK and personal Word Set sources; there is no setup bypass.
- [ ] Word Sets can add, search and restore exclusions; Practice Setup displays the applicable excluded count.
- [ ] Global pool exhaustion preference is reused or finish early, defaults to reuse and is snapshotted per session.
- [ ] Zero eligible vocabulary stops generation with an informative error and never silently expands source filters.

## Profile portability

- [ ] Export JSON contains versioned configuration only, no learner history, service keys or exclusions.
- [ ] Import validates malformed, oversized and unsupported files before saving a new profile.
- [ ] Missing personal Word Set references require explicit resolution, not implicit fallback.

## Hanzi recognition and clipboard

- [ ] Draw, paste and file upload share one canvas on desktop and mobile.
- [ ] Paste works without persistent permission where browser allows and permission is not requested automatically on mount.
- [ ] Focus and paste listeners are cleaned up; old recognition responses cannot overwrite newer content.
- [ ] No clipboard image is uploaded without pressing Recognize.
- [ ] Single-character and multi-character candidates are validated against the dictionary; uncertain matches are clearly labelled.
- [ ] Clearing or navigating discards input and results; no recognition history is written to browser storage.
- [ ] Unsupported or absent vision services disable recognition with actionable explanation.

## Interface and platform

- [ ] System theme follows OS changes until an explicit persistent Light or Dark selection is made.
- [ ] Database initialization failure blocks normal navigation, supports retry and preserves local data.
- [ ] Genuine empty dictionary results remain accessible as empty results.
- [ ] Public metadata includes canonical URLs and appropriate Open Graph fields, without private learner state.
- [ ] Checked-in Docs index, image links and Markdown pass documentation validation, and the Docs reader works at `/` and `/zipeek/`.

## Sentence Relay

- [ ] Setup, explicit Start, preparation with cancel, gameplay and results are visibly distinct; generation does not start implicitly while choosing settings.
- [ ] The configured sentence count controls generation and completion; shortages produce clear feedback rather than a silent count change.
- [ ] Punctuation is not a selectable word-bank token; appropriate Chinese punctuation is rendered and validated.
- [ ] Clicking, dragging, in-answer reordering and equivalent keyboard operations work; selected tokens leave the word bank and return after Undo.
- [ ] Optional pronunciation plays on token selection or drop, reuses shared audio, and does not overlap or fire repeatedly while dragging.
- [ ] Incorrect submitted word order highlights a meaningful misplaced token or phrase while preserving a fully editable answer.
- [ ] For 他 在 吃 饭 正, a reliable validator identifies the displaced 正 rather than incorrectly highlighting all subsequent words.
- [ ] Missing, extra and multiply misplaced tokens receive contextual, progressively helpful feedback; uncertain grammar is never explained with invented certainty.
- [ ] Valid alternate Chinese word orders are not rejected solely for differing from one expected string.
- [ ] Accessible non-color error indicators, announcements, mistake counts per submission and a compact, distinguishable purple completion bar are verified.
- [ ] The setup settings icon exposes an accessible name; leaving an in-progress game warns before discarding progress.

## Application-shell and screenshot-reviewed UX

- [ ] Footer attribution is centered in the main content area and does not overlap floating reminders at narrow widths.
- [ ] Practice reminder shows concise icon actions, omits duplicate progress, preserves sessions on dismiss and synchronizes across local updates and storage changes.
- [ ] A second tab has a full-screen, non-dismissible blocking state while the original retains exclusive write ownership.
- [ ] A closed or crashed original tab cannot leave permanent stale ownership; at most one waiting tab acquires ownership.
- [ ] Word Sets removes redundant explanatory copy and offers a concise Practice this set action that preselects the vocabulary in Practice Setup.
- [ ] Write Hanzi suggestion-source labels truthfully distinguish a selected empty set from broader dictionary suggestions.
- [ ] Third-party Credits identify verified resources, applicable licenses and separate inspiration acknowledgements without implying endorsement.

## Word mosaics feedback

- [ ] A first tile selection remains visibly identifiable and screen-reader detectable until the second selection or cancellation; keyboard and touch selection behave consistently.
- [ ] The two attempted tiles remain identifiable during evaluation, including when the pair is incorrect.
- [ ] Correct pairs receive visible green and textual confirmation, then are removed or locked, with matched-pair progress incremented exactly once.
- [ ] Incorrect pairs receive visible red and textual feedback, then automatically deselect without removing tiles; each submitted wrong pair increments mistakes once.
- [ ] Selection, correct and incorrect states remain understandable without color, with reduced motion enabled and with a screen reader.
- [ ] Repeated wrong matches progressively reveal truthful semantic hints and, when reliable, candidate emphasis; the first error does not reveal the full solution.
- [ ] Earlier mistakes and assistance remain in the outcome evidence even if a pair is subsequently completed; no incorrect attempt is overwritten as independent mastery.
- [ ] Rapid clicks, interrupted feedback, navigation and session resume do not create stale selections, duplicate scoring or stuck feedback.
- [ ] Active exercise header does not repeat the exercise name; no redundant Exit practice action appears inside the Word mosaics card.
- [ ] Browser validation checks the accessible, responsive match grid and verifies matched-pair counts at completion.

## Shared Practice layout and header

- [ ] Every active exercise type uses a common session-position and feedback hierarchy without repeating its exercise-type name as a card header.
- [ ] Leaving uses one top-right control that preserves resumable state; no duplicate bottom-card Exit practice button appears.
- [ ] Session progress, exercise-specific progress and dragon acquisition evidence are independently understandable, persistent where required, and never conflated.
- [ ] Shared actions, focus handling, announcement behavior and error states remain consistent across Matching, Multiple Choice, Listening, Character builder, Word mosaics and Write Hanzi.
- [ ] The global header has no redundant centered page title; the long detailed dragon itself is the progress shape with no labels above it. Visual comparison, keyboard detail panel, evidence-backed fill and reduced-motion behavior pass on desktop and mobile.

## Practice vocabulary counting and setup

- [ ] Exercise selection offers accessible Select all and Clear all; only available exercises may be selected; configuration persists on temporary deselection.
- [ ] Short exclusive options, descriptive radio options and independent checkboxes follow shared patterns. An exercise without extra configuration has a truthful no-settings state.
- [ ] Eligibility calculations never monopolize the main browser thread; show measured or indeterminate progress and keep controls responsive.
- [ ] Filter changes invalidate older results; cancelling, navigating away or changing exclusions cannot cause stale counts or stuck loading UI.
- [ ] Zero eligible, failed count and exhausted-but-valid pool are different states, and only a validated nonempty pool can start a session.

## Multiple Choice pronunciation

- [ ] Pinyin defaults to Always for non-revealing displays; meaning-to-Pinyin questions do not leak the answer.
- [ ] Automatic question audio is enabled by default only where a Chinese target exists; blocked autoplay remains recoverable, and manual replay is available.
- [ ] Pinyin and audio settings survive saved profile and session round trips and preserve keyboard accessibility.

## Credits and legal notices

- [ ] The Credits page distinguishes bundled resources and applicable notices from design inspirations, without implying endorsement.
- [ ] Referenced license files and attribution statements match what is actually shipped.

# Exercise E2E coverage audit (2026-11-10)

This inventory was checked against the 16 selectable exercise IDs in `crates/zipeek-web/src/components/practice/setup/practice_builder/exercise_selector.rs`, the six `ExerciseVariant` values in `zipeek-core`, and actual Rust E2E test code. It records evidence, not an assertion of successful Chrome execution.

| Exercise | Existing browser coverage in source | Remaining acceptance gap |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Matching (3 variants) | `tests/suites/practice/matching.rs` exercises all three variants, recovery and fixed summaries | Run in managed Chrome |
| Multiple choice (3 variants) | `tests/suites/practice/mcq.rs` and `fixed_mcq.rs` cover all variants | Run in managed Chrome |
| Sentence translation | `tests/translation_fixture.rs` exercises deterministic AI fixture and browser learning flow | Real `zipeek-ai-server` browser integration |
| Speaking | `tests/speaking_interactions.rs` covers configuration and selection | Fake-device capture, stop, browser blob playback, discard/revoke, track cleanup and retry scenarios authored; Chrome run and physical-device verification pending |
| Listening choice | `tests/suites/practice/setup.rs` covers session and restoration | Replay of the same Mandarin phrase now asserted; run in managed Chrome |
| Type pinyin | `tests/practice_answer_options.rs` covers incorrect-answer retry and progression | Run in managed Chrome |
| Character builder | `tests/practice_answer_options.rs` covers automatic answer feedback | Run in managed Chrome |
| Word mosaics | `tests/suites/practice/setup.rs` exercises setup selection | Full eight-pair and wrong-answer scenario authored in `tests/suites/practice/word_mosaics.rs`; additionally verify visible selection, pair-specific red/green feedback, automatic deselection, progressive hints, accessible announcements, and reduced-motion behavior in Chrome against [Word mosaics requirements](../../learning-practice/practice/practice-outcomes.md) |
| Character hunt | `tests/exercise_interactions.rs` and setup scenarios cover hint and restoration | Run in managed Chrome |
| Fill in the blank | `tests/suites/practice/setup.rs` exercises answer, feedback, reload and continue | Run in managed Chrome |
| Audio dictation | `tests/suites/practice/setup.rs` checks play gating, reload, answer, feedback and continue | Run in managed Chrome; add audio failure/retry fixture |
| Sentence builder | `tests/suites/practice/setup.rs` checks answer, feedback and continue | Run in managed Chrome |
| Sentence transformation | `tests/suites/practice/setup.rs` exercises answer gating, reload, feedback and continue | Run in managed Chrome |
| Spot the mistake | `tests/suites/practice/setup.rs` checks repair, feedback and continue | Run in managed Chrome |
| Handwriting recall | `tests/suites/practice/setup.rs` checks reveal, canvas and continue | Run in managed Chrome |
| Image vocabulary | `tests/exercise_interactions.rs` checks selection modes, generation via both AI/image fixture servers, approval, answer grading and regeneration | Deterministic AI scene composition, image-server loading, approval, answer grading and regeneration authored; run in managed Chrome |

`tests/practice_coverage_pending.rs` retains legacy ignored placeholders until the newly authored browser journeys pass on Windows. The non-ignored Image Vocabulary and fake-microphone scenarios are implemented in `exercise_interactions.rs` and `speaking_interactions.rs`. No current-source Chrome results have been supplied for them; authoring a test does not prove successful audio capture or generated-image completion.

## AI server

`crates/zipeek-ai-server/src/http_tests.rs` contains six `#[tokio::test]` HTTP-level integration cases that start an in-process Axum router with a deterministic `FixtureBackend`. They cover model listing, model ID validation, JSON completion, SSE delta/DONE framing, untrusted browser origin rejection and permitted localhost preflight. These are meaningful HTTP integration tests, not proof that the packaged server executable runs with an actual model. `crates/zipeek-e2e/tests/translation_fixture.rs` tests a separate browser translation fixture; `tests/ai_learner.rs` is an ignored external LM Studio scenario, not an AI-server scenario.

`tests/ai_server_live_pending.rs` contains two ignored, deliberately unimplemented cases: running the real AI-server process and routing browser translation through it. Implement with a controlled model fixture and explicit opt-in environment rather than assuming a model is available in CI.

## Additional source-only acceptance findings

The Word Mosaics browser scenario verifies wrong-pair feedback, disabling matched pairs, eight-pair progress, and completion through the standalone route. The Speaking browser suite adds a deterministic microphone-permission denial with retry and target change. Both are authored but have not been executed in Chrome. Picture Vocabulary now prevents approval until its image loads and rejects invalid vocabulary source parameters. Its full browser completion scenario still requires an AI and image-server fixture.

The native AI-server executable supports an explicitly selected loopback-only fixture mode for real-process lifecycle and HTTP streaming tests. It is not a production model runtime; model-backed integration and a browser-to-server test remain pending.

# Testing and validation

> **Current approved target behavior:** [Approved behavior acceptance](approved-behavior-acceptance.md). Older implementation descriptions below record prior contracts and may not match the latest approved behavior or verified source.


Rust unit/integration tests and real Chrome runs answer different questions. JavaScript source-contract tests under `scripts/` were retired by decision in the historical source. A test appearing in the repository is not proof that it has run successfully. Current acceptance state is maintained in [CURRENT](../../project-management/current.md); open gates are in [TASKS](../../project-management/tasks.md). Historical evidence belongs in [release history](../../archive-history/RELEASE_HISTORY.md).

## Commands from the workspace root

```powershell
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo check --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p zipeek-web
cargo check --locked -p zipeek-e2e --tests
```

Run affected Rust tests first for routine work. For comprehensive release acceptance use:

```powershell
cargo make e2e-full
cargo make pack-e2e
```

`e2e-full` first checks WASM, compiles all release E2E targets, then runs the managed Rust/Chrome suites serially. The pack task prepares evidence for review. Browser suites use a managed server, an isolated Chrome profile and scenario-specific artifacts; see [E2E](../../archive-history/audits/e2e.md) and [E2E architecture](../e2e/e2e-architecture.md).

## Native Qwen3-TTS synthesis acceptance

The real `/v1/tts` endpoint prefers the local Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-CustomVoice model under `models/speech/` over eSpeak, while preserving eSpeak as an optional fallback when the neural checkpoint is absent. This pathway executes the talker, code predictor and neural codec decoder to produce PCM WAV, not test-tone audio. `ZIPEEK_QWEN_TTS_MODEL` overrides the checkpoint path, and `ZIPEEK_TTS_DEVICE` selects `cuda` (default) or `cpu` in the current Candle-native build; `ZIPEEK_STT_DEVICE` defaults to `cpu`. Do not mistake asset preflight for successful inference.

The new dependency requires lockfile resolution and review before accepted use. After that, run:

```powershell
cargo test --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt --test neural_tts -- --ignored --nocapture
cargo test --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt --test speech_tts_stt_roundtrip -- --ignored --nocapture
```

The first test saves `target/speech-e2e/mandarin_nihao_shijie.wav` and `target/speech-e2e/mandarin_nihao_shijie.opus` when neural inference succeeds. Listen to this output before accepting exact STT text comparison. Neural outputs must be non-silent and at 24 kHz; compilation alone does not establish model accuracy. Kokoro remains future work.

## R662 speech worker reliability and performance acceptance

The native speech service uses one persistent TTS worker and one independent STT worker. A request holds its backend permit through worker completion even when the caller abandons it. Cancellation is cooperative, not a forced CUDA interruption. `/v1/capabilities` reports `neural_tts_status`, `neural_stt_status`, and non-sensitive `neural_tts_failure`/`neural_stt_failure` categories (`none`, `model_load`, `inference`). Explicit shutdown transitions workers to `stopped`. Internal diagnostics are logged, not exposed in HTTP bodies.

Run the checkpoint-free unit and HTTP checks and then the ignored model-backed acceptance tests on Windows with the actual installed checkpoints. The 20-request tests print warm latency observations; compare measured p50/p95, VRAM usage and transcripts with the R661 baseline before attempting KV-cache or CUDA kernel optimizations. Stochastic TTS output has no fixed duration. The generated neural reference WAV is 24 kHz, while direct WAV STT input must be mono 16 kHz PCM16; the speech worker acceptance test resamples its reference fixture before transcription. This fixture conversion does not relax production input validation.

```powershell
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo check --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt
cargo clippy --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt
cargo test --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt --test speech_worker_acceptance -- --ignored --nocapture
```

Additionally verify timeout during active CUDA inference, prompt cancellation, shutdown while a request is executing, failed-load retry, worker-thread exit after all runtime clones drop, and correct audio playback using the Windows runtime. A passed synthetic permit test alone does not establish those end-to-end behaviours.

## Native speech Rust integration and end-to-end tests

The canonical native speech integration suite lives under `crates/zipeek-tts-stt/tests/`. Its shared `common/` harness launches the **actual compiled Rust server** on an ephemeral loopback port, sends HTTP requests, checks responses and kills/reaps the process on test completion. It requires no additional dependencies. Unit tests remain in `src/` for internal functions; Rust integration tests validate the binary and public boundaries.

From the workspace root, run the non-model-dependent suite:

```powershell
cargo test --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt --test speech_http_e2e --test speech_security --test model_loading
```

`model_loading` has one fast missing-file test and one ignored checkpoint-backed test. The baseline HTTP test can accept an explicit `503` when eSpeak is absent, but never mistakes this for synthesized speech. Baseline HTTP/security tests explicitly launch the server with an absent STT checkpoint path so they can verify a deterministic `503` regardless of local assets.

Run real eSpeak synthesis acceptance (requires a working installed eSpeak NG executable and a parent directory containing `espeak-ng-data`):

```powershell
$env:ZIPEEK_ESPEAK_BIN = 'C:\path\to\espeak-ng.exe'
$env:ZIPEEK_ESPEAK_DATA = 'C:\path\to\resources'
cargo test --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt --test tts_inference -- --ignored --nocapture
```

Run full Qwen3-ASR checkpoint and spoken-Mandarin HTTP acceptance separately. The test embeds the checked-in 16 kHz mono PCM16 Mandarin audio fixture with `include_bytes!` and compares the transcript to the fixed text `你好世界`. It is generated with eSpeak and must be listened to for Mandarin pronunciation verification; the local synthesis tool reported a missing full Chinese dictionary. Unlike a sine wave, it contains a speech synthesis signal, but this does not independently prove accurate speech content:

```powershell
$env:ZIPEEK_CANDLE_STT_MODEL = (Resolve-Path .\models\speech\Qwen3-ASR-0.6B\model.safetensors).Path
cargo test --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt --test model_loading -- --ignored --nocapture
cargo test --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt --test stt_inference -- --ignored --nocapture
```

A successful HTTP 200 and nonempty text are insufficient: the strict STT test compares the normalized transcript with the provided reference. Model-backed tests are ignored by default because the safetensors are not included in source archives and can require substantial memory/time. Passing a test is evidence only of that specific check; it does not establish numerical model parity, multiple-speaker accuracy, or full product/browser acceptance. The Rust toolchain and model files must exist on the testing machine.

### Optional external client probe


The dependency-free Node harness `scripts/speech-api-e2e.cjs` builds the locked `zipeek-tts-stt` binary, starts the actual speech server on a temporary loopback port, polls `/health`, and calls `/v1/capabilities`, `/v1/tts` and `/v1/stt`. It also checks payload validation and browser origin restrictions. The server is stopped after the run. Run from the repository root:

```powershell
node scripts/speech-api-e2e.cjs
```

This baseline mode accepts a truthful HTTP 503 for an unavailable backend and prints readiness separately. It is a server/transport check, not proof that neural STT or TTS works. To require operational eSpeak synthesis, supply its binary/data paths and require the WAV response:

```powershell
$env:ZIPEEK_ESPEAK_BIN = 'C:\path\to\espeak-ng.exe'
$env:ZIPEEK_ESPEAK_DATA = 'C:\path\to\resources'
node scripts/speech-api-e2e.cjs --require-tts
```

The `ZIPEEK_ESPEAK_DATA` directory must contain `espeak-ng-data`. To require both speech directions, use `--require-tts --require-stt`. STT now activates when Qwen3-ASR checkpoint assets pass preflight; the experimental environment toggle has been removed. Set `ZIPEEK_CANDLE_STT_MODEL` to the existing safetensors. The checked-in eSpeak-synthesized 16 kHz Mandarin fixture and `你好世界` reference string are used by both Rust and Node acceptance tests, without external audio-path or transcript variables. A tone is reserved for negative-path tests. The checkpoint decoder and transcription accuracy are not yet verified. The separate `scripts/tests/speech-api-e2e.test.cjs` checks the WAV fixture without starting the server. Use `--no-build` only if the debug executable has already been compiled with `cargo build --locked -p zipeek-tts-stt`. Neither the binary nor downloaded model weights are included in the source archive.

## Current browser coverage

- Shared catalog: 34 concrete route cases under root and the `/zipeek/` deployment base, plus separate accessibility and 320/390/768px responsive checks.
- Behavioral suites: Browse/Word Sets, Settings/Debug, Practice setup and persistence, courses, games, speaking, translation, writing, shell navigation and errors. See test targets under `crates/zipeek-e2e/tests/`.
- Sentence Translation: deterministic Rust AI fixture and optional live provider journey through Settings, Practice setup and the UUID-backed generated exercise. Fixture tests cover canonical tiles, finite completion, restore and Endless behavior.
- AI fixture: `crates/zipeek-e2e/src/harness/ai_fixture.rs`; the old Node `ai-server.cjs` is removed.

**Acceptance limitation:** The user reported successful Windows accessibility, Browse and an earlier live translation test. The newest UUID translation implementation and full suite still need their own execution. An ignored test is not a pass; route presence is not equivalent to complete interaction or WCAG compliance.

## Live AI test

Provide a running OpenAI-compatible endpoint and exact model ID, then run:

```powershell
$env:ZIPEEK_E2E_AI_ENDPOINT = 'http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1/'
$env:ZIPEEK_E2E_AI_MODEL = 'your-loaded-model-id'
cargo test --release --locked -p zipeek-e2e --test ai_learner -- --ignored --nocapture
```

The live test is intentionally excluded from deterministic CI. It sends actual requests to the locally configured provider; it is not a general assertion of model correctness.

## Related focused guides

[Browser database](../e2e/browser-db.md), [matching](../e2e/matching.md), [MCQ](../e2e/mcq.md), [startup](../e2e/startup.md), [shell](../e2e/shell.md), [E2E recording](../e2e/e2e-recording.md), [evidence](../e2e/evidence.md), [UI acceptance](ui-acceptance.md).

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/testing-quality-acceptance-testing.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.

## Record automatic microphone termination (R673)

Record route microphone capture may end automatically after sustained speech and a trailing silent interval. Its adaptive energy detector uses browser Web Audio analyser PCM with an 80 ms sampling callback. Speech must be sustained for at least 200 ms to arm stop detection; use 900 ms trailing silence for HSK words and 1500 ms for custom sentences. Maximum capture duration is 9 seconds for words and 28 seconds for sentences. The detector does not perform neural voice classification or know whether the target word has been completed. Manual stop and cancellation must remain functional. Recording bytes remain in browser memory and STT is called only after capture completes.

Acceptance requires noisy and quiet microphones, starting speech immediately or after silence, naturally spaced sentences, no-speech recordings, manually stopped recordings, permission refusal, service failure, target switching during capture, cancellation after stop and repeated recording/replay. Verify that no STT request is made when automatic capture ends without confirmed speech. Run the pure Rust `zipeek-browser` unit tests as well as the locked WASM build and actual Chrome interaction tests.

## Tauri frontend/database separation checks

After staging the native dictionary and sidecars with `cargo make desktop-sidecars`, run:

```powershell
cargo test --locked -p zipeek-db --lib
cargo test --locked -p zipeek-cli desktop_frontend
cargo test --locked -p zipeek-cli native_selection_uses_verified_manifest_without_a_browser_gzip
cargo check --locked -p zipeek-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
cargo check --locked -p zipeek-app
cargo test --locked -p zipeek-app --lib
cargo run --locked -p zipeek-cli -- desktop-frontend
```

Native tests require the pinned DuckDB DLL on PATH. Desktop output must omit database preload links, manifest/download files and DuckDB-WASM/Arrow vendor files, while retaining shared worker/assets and notices. A missing native bridge or failed native open must surface an error without requesting browser database assets. Browser builds must still load the dictionary at both `/` and `/zipeek/`. Local Chrome with an injected IPC fixture establishes frontend behavior only; actual WebView/installed acceptance still requires `cargo make desktop-dev` and `cargo make desktop-build` on Windows.

## Settings reset regression

`cargo test --locked -p zipeek-app --lib` covers native personal-file/WAL removal, reopen with empty history, dictionary preservation, repeat reset and invalid/removal-failure paths. The focused browser suite is:

```powershell
cargo test --locked -p zipeek-e2e --test app_reset -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture
```

It uses fresh managed Chrome profiles and the existing screenshot/video harness. Both root and Pages suites cover cancellation, full owned-storage cleanup, retention of unrelated data, fresh landing, unconfirmed reset URL, another active app tab, and mocked native failure/retry. The harness reinjects its silent-speech session flag on each document; reset assertions account for this test-only reinjection while verifying all seeded user data is gone. Native frontend fixture checks are not actual installed WebView acceptance. No tests clear the developer's real app profile.

# UI feature acceptance - Cloud Match, CSS, Write Hanzi

This document consolidates the current non-crossword UI checks. Previous release-specific checklists are superseded; versioned evidence remains in [Release history](../../archive-history/RELEASE_HISTORY.md).

## Cloud Match

1. Setup has a shared Back/Cloud Match title row and a compact **Start** action with a play icon. Verify both HSK and Word Set sources, three matching formats and all difficulty settings.
2. During a wave, clouds have varied silhouettes and individual movement speeds, remain visible/selectable throughout their bounded motion, and do not shift lanes when a match is removed.
3. Selection highlights the cloud silhouette, not a detached oval. Correct/incorrect feedback updates the score/lives HUD, not a bottom notification. Announcements remain accessible.
4. Match, miss, time out, pause, resume and stop: assert the pure engine score/lives/wave transitions still agree with the HUD and no pair can score twice.
5. Hide the browser tab during a wave; return to a **paused** round with its score, wave and remaining time intact. Resume explicitly. Test keyboard and touch, small screens, zoom, and `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Styles and shared shell

1. `crates/zipeek-web/styles/main.css` stays a Tailwind entry point, not a feature-style dumping ground. Tokens, base, accessibility, shared layout and feature-specific CSS retain their separate ownership.
2. Run asset preparation and the normal Trunk build to confirm Tailwind expands all local imports and scans Rust `@source` declarations.
3. Check light/dark and preset themes, button/action classes, focus/contrast, scrollbar styling and Chinese fonts. Verify shell fullscreen routes do not inherit an unwanted sidebar grid.
4. Visually compare Crossword, Cloud Match, Write Hanzi and landing layouts at desktop, mobile and high zoom. Source checks cannot establish pixel equivalence.

## Write Hanzi

1. Change between My Word Sets and English search; changing source or set resets selection and pagination as intended.
2. Search with fast successive edits and verify the latest submitted query wins. Page through more than five results and select a different word.
3. Navigate via a deep-linked word ID, including missing/unsupported entries; confirm explicit statuses and no stale selection.
4. Change characters inside a chosen word; prevent out-of-range indices. Verify the drawing workspace, stroke interactions and responsive sizing are unchanged.
5. Shared `Dictionary` and `WordSetsContext` remain providers. Route-local query/source/loading/selection/character state belongs in one typed workflow reducer; presentation children receive typed props and callbacks.

## Verification

Run `cargo make release-check` and the focused Rust/web tests appropriate to the change. Check behavior in Chrome with real browser data. Node source-contract successes are not build proof. Historical test counts and known missing gates are documented in [Release history](../../archive-history/RELEASE_HISTORY.md).

## Practice setupacceptance)

1. At `/practice`, traverse Path → Exercises → Vocabulary → Summary and back. Verify the single top action bar does not jump below the panels, including on narrow screens and with a large font; Start is followed by the play icon.
2. Toggle ten then zero then all fifteen exercise cards. The selected-count badge must always match the draft, including when moving to Configure and back; test keyboard and screen reader announcements.
3. In Categories & filters, confirm suggestions load before typing, filter immediately, prevent stale response overwrite, and allow selection/removal. With dictionary unavailable, no fabricated category options should appear.
4. Review the Summary icons, HSK and category chips, Word Set alternative, chosen session mode, and truthful practice-only limitations. Test zero and multiple selected filters.
5. Verify initial and per-session loading statuses, screen-reader announcements, light/dark contrast and `prefers-reduced-motion`; confirm no Animato transition is being claimed for this release.

## Source provenance

A full pre-reconciliation copy is retained in [historical source evidence](../../archive-history/audits/maintained-source-snapshots/testing-quality-acceptance-ui-acceptance.md). Dated implementation claims in that snapshot are not current build or browser verification.

# Hanzi Crosswords - testing and acceptance

This is the **current** acceptance checklist for `#/games/crosswords`. It replaces release-specific checklists that described intermediate implementations; historical results remain in [Release history](../../archive-history/RELEASE_HISTORY.md).

## Source and state contracts

- HSK 2.0/3.0 bands are selected in the initial setup. Gameplay and results **do not** offer a Change HSK levels action; Play again retains the original bands.
- Eligible crossword words come from browser-local DuckDB for the selected bands; no 13-word fallback. The generator targets at least six connected words, four crossings, and ten occupied cells. If it cannot produce a valid puzzle, report a generation failure rather than displaying a two-word puzzle or claiming the dictionary lacks words.
- A generated layout uses canonical vocabulary ordering and a seed so that refreshing restores the same board, filled characters, score and selected bands. New game uses a different seed and retains the bands. Generated clue coordinates remain consistent with rendered cropped board geometry.
- Each newly started game records its distinct Hanzi answer words in a browser-local 100-word least-recently-used rotation list and its vocabulary fingerprint in the last 10 game signatures. New game evaluates eight deterministic seed candidates and prefers valid puzzles with less recent vocabulary overlap; this is a preference, not an exclusion, so small pools remain playable. Restoring a saved session does not count the same session twice. This rotation is independent of learning-history consent and Word Sets.
- The `Crossword` domain owns legal placement, intersections, next-unfilled-cell selection, scoring and completion; Yew owns database loading, keyboard/focus and rendering. Setup/loading/errors use the workflow reducer; game actions use the gameplay reducer.

## Browser acceptance

1. Start from a fresh route and choose HSK 3.0 level 1; repeat with HSK 3.0 levels 4-6, HSK 2.0 level 1, and a cross-standard selection. Confirm clues come from the chosen vocabulary. If the generator fails, the error must be accurate and the preceding playable board must not be replaced with an undersized puzzle.
2. At desktop (1366×768, 1440×900), narrow (390×844) and 125% zoom, confirm the desktop viewport is not unnecessarily scrolling, the crossword cells are legible, the tile tray scrolls horizontally, and clue scrolling is independent. No global app bar or duplicate headings should appear in fullscreen gameplay.
3. Clues show gloss and Pinyin only (no numbering/direction prefix or checkmark). Click or keyboard-activate an unfinished clue: highlight its next unanswered cell. Hover must not change selection. Tapping a tile fills the next empty cell; already-filled crossing cells are skipped. Direct square placement and drag/drop remain functional.
4. Complete a clue: it becomes muted and disabled. Stale clicks or keyboard activation must not reactivate it. Correctly filled squares are subdued but legible, including intersections; unfinished clues remain actionable.
5. Type Pinyin without focusing a field: a floating suggestion widget opens. Enter selects a unique reading; number keys 1-5 distinguish tone; multiple characters with the same reading and tone still require explicit choice. Escape closes the widget. Input inside other forms and modified browser shortcuts must not trigger the widget. No permanent Pinyin field or instructional label belongs in the tray.
6. Place a wrong character, test bank depletion, change active clues, refresh halfway through, and verify consistent scoring and persisted selections. Confirm the progress and HUD are updated from one authoritative gameplay state.
7. Start several new games in the same HSK selection, inspect varying word sets where the pool permits, refresh midway and confirm the current puzzle and rotation history persist. Check that small vocabulary pools fall back to playable previously used words, that rotation history is capped, and that a repeated save does not increase usage. Complete the crossword: results replace the board and show points, completed words, mistakes, **Play again** and **All games** only. Play again retains the same HSK selections.
8. Check loading and generation feedback, slow/failed DuckDB queries, unavailable worker, keyboard focus, reduced motion, accessibility labels and browser console diagnostics.

## Validation commands

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo check --workspace --locked
cargo check -p zipeek-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --locked
cargo test -p zipeek-exercises --locked crossword
cargo test -p zipeek-web --locked
node --test scripts/*.test.cjs
```

`cargo make release-check` runs the configured gates. Source-text Node tests do not certify Rust compilation, DuckDB integration or rendered Chrome behaviour. See [Testing](../acceptance/testing.md) and [UI architecture](../../architecture/ui-architecture.md).
title: Hanzi Crosswords - testing and acceptance

# E2E architecture and evidence contract

## Goals

- One independent Chrome WebDriver session per scenario. The servers and deterministic AI fixture may be shared per suite, not the browser state.
- Capture and preserve a video and named screenshots for every scenario, including application initialization failures.
- Write all runs beneath the repository root `target/e2e`, not `crates/target/e2e`.
- Collect evidence before browser shutdown. Failure details must not be replaced by recorder or cleanup errors.
- Continue executing subsequent scenarios after an individual failure, then report aggregate suite failure.
- Keep existing `HarnessError`, `HarnessResult`, `Harness`, `ScenarioContext`, and Thirtyfour 0.38.1 with `cdp-events`.

## Runtime flow

1. Start the test suite's HTTP and fixture servers and create `target/e2e/<suite>-<pid>-<timestamp>`.
2. For each scenario, start a fresh Chrome session and a unique artifact directory.
3. Connect a CDP event stream and start screencasting **before** initializing browser state, navigating to the application, or awaiting dictionary readiness.
4. Reset the fresh browser and initialize diagnostic instrumentation. Wait for one of the explicit database states. `failed` becomes a named initialization failure; absence of a terminal state is bounded by a 45-second deadline.
5. Capture a ready checkpoint, execute the scenario, then capture the final page and diagnostics, regardless of result. Scenario panics are reported without skipping teardown.
6. Stop screencast, drain frames, encode MP4 with FFmpeg when installed, then close that scenario's browser.
7. Write `scenario.json` with phase, result and evidence presence. Browser cleanup and strict recording errors receive their own failure phases. Run all remaining scenarios despite failures.
8. Write `suite.json` and `summary.txt` at the run root; fail the overall test target if any scenario failed. If server startup fails, still write a suite failure manifest.

CDP frame events must be acknowledged regardless of whether individual frames can be stored. The capture limits are for safety; the recorder must clearly signal incomplete capture if a limit is hit. Variable-duration frame timing is preferred. The recording is diagnostic evidence, not a guaranteed full-frame-rate video.

## Evidence layout

Each run is stored under the repository root `target/e2e` and has a `suite.json`, `summary.txt` and human-readable `review.md`. Each scenario has `scenario.json`, `agent-feedback.md`, a timeline of named checkpoints, and conditional browser, failure and video artifacts.

Chrome CDP JPEG frames stream directly to FFmpeg, rather than being retained as numbered image files. The recorder writes `video/recording.mp4` and `video/status.json`; FFprobe reports validation where available. See [video and feedback evidence](e2e-video-recording.md) for the exact current environment controls, file layout and limitations.

The scenario manifest explicitly distinguishes execution, assertions and recording. An otherwise successful test may still have incomplete video evidence. Strict evidence mode fails a passing scenario if the recorder or video validation fails; it never hides a prior application failure.

## Test tiers

| Tier | Dependency | When to run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rust unit and contract tests | None | Every code change |
| Browser fixture smoke | Local app, Chrome, bundled dictionary and deterministic AI fixture | Every release and CI |
| Full browser journey suite | Local app and deterministic fixture | Before acceptance |
| Live-model AI acceptance | Explicit local LM Studio endpoint and loaded model | Opt-in; report model/version |
| Fault injection | Local fixture with delayed/failing responses | CI and recovery changes |
| Visual evidence review | Video, checkpoint images and scenario metadata | After every failed run |

## Route and module regression coverage

The root route matrix executes registered routes in separate Core, Practice, and
other-feature Chrome scenarios, plus a redirect/404 scenario. The same matrix
also tests the GitHub Pages base path. The individual scenarios have separate
browser profiles and evidence, so a failure in Practice routes does not suppress
checks for Settings, Games, or the other groups. The pure Rust matrix tests
verify that every declared route is covered and that each registered route is
assigned to exactly one root scenario group.

The Pages suite registers all 21 existing scenarios directly with the harness.
`Harness::run` accumulates failures while isolating each browser session;
`Harness::finish` reports the aggregate outcome. Do not wrap calls in a
fail-fast result chain. Page-object helpers live in the E2E library
`src/page_objects/`, not under individual integration targets. The root Node
test `scripts/e2e-module-contract.test.cjs` checks that explicit Rust `#[path]`
module references resolve and that test targets do not duplicate shared page
objects. This is a static check, not a replacement for Cargo compilation.

## Stable DOM selector contract

Domain and workflow roots should expose an existing stable `data-*` marker. Add a
specific marker to a control only when an E2E journey must locate or assert it;
do not instrument decorative wrappers. Prefer stable domain IDs over user-visible
labels, CSS classes, or translated text. Keep domain values separate from action
names and observable state. Native accessibility roles, labels, `disabled`, and
`aria-pressed` remain the authoritative interaction/accessibility semantics.

- Expanded Grammar: `data-grammar-course-id`, `data-grammar-pattern-index`,
  `data-grammar-practice-phase` (`recall`/`recognition`), `data-grammar-reveal`,
  `data-grammar-choice` (index within the current authored question),
  `data-grammar-choice-state`, `data-grammar-practice-feedback` and
  `data-grammar-previous`/`data-grammar-continue`.
- Sentence Transformation: `data-item-id`, `data-transformation-method`,
  `data-transformation-status`, `data-transformation-bank-tile` (source-bank
  index), `data-transformation-selected-tile`, `data-transformation-tile-position`,
  `data-transformation-undo`/`data-transformation-reset`, and
  `data-transformation-feedback`. These indices are question-local, not stable
  syllabus identities.
- Transformation setup: `data-transformation-pattern-search`,
  `data-transformation-pattern-status` (`valid`/`unsupported`),
  `data-transformation-pattern-all`, `data-transformation-answer-mode`,
  and `data-transformation-answer-option`.
- Cloud Match: `data-cloud-match-setup`, `data-cloud-match-eligibility`,
  `data-cloud-match-start` and `data-cloud-match-start-state` with readiness
  values `loading`, `error`, `insufficient`, or `ready`.

These attributes are a public *test selector* contract, not an application state
transport. Do not read domain decisions back from DOM attributes, expose answers
through them, or use an E2E hook to imply a learning result is verified.

## Practice exercise viewport and service selectors

Practice setup uses `[data-practice-exercise-scroll]` as the one desktop vertical scroll owner when choosing or configuring exercise types. The wizard footer and Choose/Configure tabs remain above the list, outside its scrolling region. The enclosing `[data-component="main-content"]` does not scroll on desktop. Browser acceptance must assert that the list has overflow, can reach the last tile, and that the main scroll position remains zero. On mobile, keep natural page scrolling.

Exercise tiles expose `data-external-services` (`none`, `ai`, or `ai,image-generation`) and named `[data-exercise-service]` labels. These describe required external generation services, not their readiness or permission to send private data. The sentence-translation tile requires AI; picture vocabulary requires both AI and image generation. Do not mistake local browser speech/microphone features for external generation services.

## Coverage priorities

P0: initial database loading, explicit error state, retry, stale readiness, server exit and evidence of failures before scenario execution.

P0: deterministic Sentence Translation generated question, tile selection, check, navigation, reload, retry, invalid generation and absence of model configuration. Run the fixture path without access to external model accounts.

P0: session restoration and completion for Matching, Multiple Choice, Listening Choice and Character Hunt; input/keyboard equivalence and no false mastery publication.

P1: authenticated or private storage journeys with isolated browser profiles; OPFS failure and recovery; dictionary checksum/adapter error reporting.

P1: reduced motion, responsive widths, focus, semantics, keyboard navigation, and screen-reader labels across the Practice setup and game views.

P2: optional real AI model responses, image loading/approval and cross-platform Chrome/FFmpeg behavior.

## Acceptance gates

- The first failing database-initialization scenario produces `scenario.json`, `failure.txt`, screenshot when possible, and video or an explicit recording failure record.
- The following scenario still runs with a fresh profile and its own evidence directory.
- A deterministic AI fixture journey appears as a registered browser test, not merely an unused function. Run it with `cargo test -p zipeek-e2e --test smoke deterministic_ai_practice --locked -- --nocapture --test-threads=1`.
- An ordinary multi-scenario run produces separate recordings for each scenario, plus a suite-level summary.
- Artifact locations resolve under the repository root `target/e2e` on Windows and Linux.
- The default upload bundle includes MP4 when available and falls back to raw JPEG frames when encoding was unavailable. Raw AI requests remain opt-in; manually inspect screenshots, videos and text before sharing.
- `cargo check -p zipeek-e2e --tests --locked` and actual Chrome/FFmpeg runs pass before labeling the release verified.

## Limitations

The source-level improvements do not establish a successful Chrome/CDP/FFmpeg execution until the local environment runs them. The current frame recorder may reach its size/frame limits in long scenarios; incomplete video should be explicitly reported and the final failure screenshot retained. A CDP stream can omit unchanged frames, so frame timing is not equivalent to screen capture at fixed FPS.

## Scenario quality and review

- Treat E2E tests as production code. Use small domain-focused scenarios with observable acceptance assertions, intentional setup and independent browser state. Avoid giant catch-all tests or repeated raw selector chains.
- Reuse existing typed harness APIs, stable semantic selectors or minimal `data-testid` hooks. Do not expose private answer keys or serialized internal round state in the DOM solely for tests.
- Prefer explicit bounded waits on observable conditions to arbitrary sleeps; ensure independent fixtures and cleanup. Isolate any necessary injected JavaScript behind short typed helpers and validate dynamic script inputs.
- Verify success, failure, keyboard, focus, navigation and responsive cases when relevant. Keep screenshots, videos and diagnostics, but do not equate their creation with visual review.
- Report exact suites, environment, artifacts, failures, skipped checks and pre-existing failures. Do not weaken meaningful assertions to obtain a passing result.

## exercise-type and Pinyin course scenarios

`cargo make e2e-exercise-types-and-courses` runs the focused exercise and
course suites. `exercise_type_journeys.rs` checks that all sixteen authored
Practice exercise definitions are selectable in Advanced mode and have an
accessible, individually selectable configuration tab. It also verifies the
exact eight-exercise Quick subset and runs isolated authored interactions for
Fill in the Blank, Audio Dictation, Sentence Builder, Sentence Transformation,
and Spot the Mistake. These journeys assert input gates, answer feedback and
selection recovery; they do not constitute verified mastery evidence or
full writing-stroke/microphone acceptance. Other established exercise targets
continue to cover Matching, Multiple Choice, Character Hunt, Type Pinyin,
Character Builder, Word Mosaics, Speaking, Picture Vocabulary, and translation.

`course_interactions.rs` validates the six Pinyin lesson identities, links,
sequential completion and persisted overview state. Grammar courses retain
their assessment, guided-tile, incorrect-answer and review assertions.
The Chrome suites remain pending execution until the supported toolchain and
browser fixtures are available.

## deterministic game completion and authored feedback

`cargo make e2e-ai-games-and-exercise-completion` runs the fixture-backed
`ai_game_journeys.rs` and expanded `exercise_type_journeys.rs` suites. The
shared Rust fixture recognizes the actual Sentence Relay and Dialogue Quest
completion prompts and returns four stable, validated game rounds. The browser
journeys test wrong-answer feedback, corrected answers, all four completions,
restart, and a visible server failure. AI requests remain bound to the local
loopback fixture and contain no real learner records.

Authored Practice checks now include traditional-character cloze answers,
incorrect-answer feedback and continuation, a full silent-TTS dictation
playback/check/continue flow, tile reconstruction and review for Sentence
Builder and Sentence Transformation, and detection-versus-repair feedback
for Spot the Mistake. These tests do not grant mastery or claim coverage of
Hanzi stroke tracing, physical microphones, or real AI inference.

All these tests are source-authored pending an actual locked Rust build and
Chrome execution; fixture unit checks do not replace browser acceptance.

## authored Practice session completion

`cargo make e2e-authored-session-completion` runs five isolated end-to-end journeys through the saved UUID Practice session lifecycle for Fill in the Blank, Audio Dictation, Sentence Builder, Sentence Transformation and Spot the Mistake. The test checks the actual number of scheduled rounds, accepted answers for four formats, intentional rejected dictation input and the playback prerequisite on each round. It then validates the final local-session completion count, skipped count, completion percentage and learning-history notice. After the history operation removes the temporary session, reloading its URL must show `[data-component="practice-session-unavailable"]` with a `not-found` error state and provide navigation back to Practice setup. It must not resurrect finished steps. This differs deliberately from standalone legacy MCQ summary/restart behavior.

These journeys do not provide evidence for Mandarin microphone transcription accuracy, handwriting gesture matching or browser audio audibility. The existing speaking and writing suites cover those boundaries to the extent that test fixtures permit. Rust compilation and Chrome runs are required before these scenarios count as passing.

## Dictionary preflight and deep-link readiness (R531 WIP)

The E2E startup checks the installed `static/hanzi.manifest.json` and verifies that its single compressed DuckDB file exists with the declared positive byte size, before launching Trunk. Once Trunk completes, it checks the corresponding output file in `dist`. This is a fast presence/size gate, not a replacement for the separately maintained SHA-256 asset-integrity audit or browser dictionary initialization. Generated dictionary binaries remain excluded from source handoffs.

Registered deep links wait for their route-specific marker; unregistered deep links retain the app-shell readiness fallback. Full-screen sessions and lessons need not render a global app shell. The Time Weaver entry route initially presents its setup screen, while gameplay tests separately assert the game marker.


## Shared WebDriver driver and selector contract

Import `zipeek_e2e::page_objects::WebDriverActions` at the call site to use `driver.click(css).await?` or `driver.element(css).await?`. These convenience methods preserve ordinary Thirtyfour `WebDriverResult` errors and `single()` element lookup. Shared selectors are in `zipeek_e2e::page_objects::selectors::{practice,image_review}`. The recorder-button contract includes required dispatch metadata; Image Review uses stable `data-image-review` markers on container, status, error and approval elements. Confirm these source contracts against the current Rust source before modifying driver APIs. Historical R310 validation totals (842 source contracts, 729 passes, 113 previously failing, and four focused passes) are **not current test results**; see [historical review](../../archive-history/audits/release-engineering-review-history.md).

## Native speech server integration

The native speech crate exports `server::SpeechServer`. An E2E caller binds `tokio::net::TcpListener` to `127.0.0.1:0`, then passes the owned listener and `Speech` configuration to `SpeechServer::start`. The server returns the assigned address and base URL. Use `shutdown().await` on successful completion; `Drop` aborts its task if a test unwinds or exits early. Graceful shutdown has a five-second bound and reports timeout as an error. The server rejects non-loopback listeners.

`crates/zipeek-e2e/tests/speech_server_lifecycle.rs` verifies live HTTP health/capabilities and listener release without Chrome or downloaded weights. This is an in-process lifecycle contract test, not an executable launch test or evidence of neural inference. The separate real-binary speech HTTP suite remains the process-boundary check. The API does not change the browser fixture's default speech mode.
